title: 'CIMB wins Malaysia’s Best Retail, Investment and SME Banking Awards from Euromoney
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: CIMB Bank Berhad and CIMB Investment Bank (collectively “CIMB”) have been recognised for strong performance, innovation and customer impact, winning three key awards at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026. CIMB was named Malaysia’s Best Retail Bank, Malaysia’s Best Digital Bank for SMEs and Malaysia’s Best Investment Bank.  These recognitions reflect CIMB’s continued focus on delivering customer-centric solutions through innovation, digital capabilities and deep market expertise across its retail, SME and investment banking businesses.  Novan Amirudin, Group Chief Executive Officer, CIMB Group, said, “These recognitions are a testament to the trust of our customers and the dedication of our teams across the Bank. They reaffirm CIMB’s purpose of advancing customers and society by making financial solutions more accessible, relevant and impactful for the people and businesses we serve.  We thank our clients and customers for the confidence they have placed in us over the years. As their needs continue to evolve, we remain committed to being a trusted partner supporting individuals in realising their aspirations and helping businesses achieve their growth ambitions through meaningful and lasting value creation."  In retail banking, the Bank continued to deepen its diversified franchise through personalised propositions, digitally enabled journeys and stronger engagement across key customer segments. Revenue and profitability advanced during the year, supported by market share gains across auto finance, credit cards and retail deposits, alongside continued progress in digital sales and customer cross-sell. The Bank also continued to strengthen its wealth proposition, underpinned by differentiated investment solutions, broader product diversity, CIO-led advisory capabilities and enhanced digital wealth platforms. Momentum was particularly strong within the Preferred segment, reflecting deeper affluent engagement and the Bank's continued focus on expanding advisory-led and relationship-based wealth capabilities.  For SMEs, CIMB continued to advance digital banking with the launch of CIMB OCTO Biz, connecting account opening, financing and transaction banking through a seamless end-to-end digital journey. The platform has onboarded more than 280,000 customers to date, offering real-time cash flow visibility, payments, foreign exchange, trade and financing services. The Bank also expanded financing access via embedded merchant financing with TNG eWallet, in addition to flexible financing through its SME FlexiCash, which uses account history and transaction behaviour to determine pre-qualified limits and link repayments to a proportion of revenue, better supporting businesses with uneven cashflows.  Meanwhile, CIMB Investment Bank’s leadership across Malaysia’s equity and debt capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, and bespoke financial advisory solutions, as well as its ability to execute complex transactions across multiple products, sectors and jurisdictions, further reinforced its position as a leading investment bank. In 2025, CIMB Investment Bank secured the #1 ranking in Malaysian equity and debt capital markets by deal value and share of wallet, while also capturing the top position in ASEAN equity and debt capital markets by deal value, with its execution of cross-border transactions reinforcing its position as a leading M&A and advisory house in ASEAN.  These three accolades reinforce CIMB’s brand promise, Moving You Forward, reflecting its continued focus on empowering customers and communities through accessible, inclusive and purpose-driven financial solutions.  For more than 30 years, Euromoney’s Awards for Excellence have recognised financial institutions that set the global standard in performance, innovation and client impact. The Awards for Excellence programme evaluates financial institutions through Euromoney’s benchmarking framework, using comparable metrics, structured submissions and a transparent research process to assess institutions against their peers.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Stays Higher At Midday Tracking Regional Markets
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 – Bursa Malaysia maintained its positive momentum at midday on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, tracking regional equity market gains following an overnight rally on Wall Street powered by megacap technology stocks and artificial intelligence (AI) investment optimism. At 12:30 PM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) advanced 5.49 points, or 0.34 per cent, to trade at 1,637.24 compared to Monday’s closing mark of 1,631.75. After opening 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38, the index fluctuated within a range of 1,635.21 to 1,641.20 during the morning trading session. Global Dynamics and Market Breadth Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) noted that strong earnings momentum and robust AI investments supported US markets despite rising Treasury yields. Key market factors and breadth metrics at midday include: - Global Commodity & Debt Markets: Brent crude oil eased below US$102 per barrel amid recovering West Asia exports, G7 emergency stockpile releases, and Saudi price cuts. Meanwhile, the US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.33 per cent amid persistent inflation concerns. - Market Breadth: Advancing counters outpaced decliners 524 to 428, with 520 counters remaining unchanged, 1,310 untraded, and 13 suspended. - Trading Volume: Total turnover reached 2.36 billion units valued at RM1.24 billion. Top Stock Movements and Sector Performance Gains across technology, consumer products, and plantation counters helped sustain the market’s upward drive. Key individual stock and sector highlights include: - Heavyweights: Maybank rose two sen to RM10.02 and IHH Healthcare gained seven sen to RM7.83. Public Bank fell five sen to RM4.66, CIMB shed two sen to RM7.71, and Tenaga Nasional traded flat at RM13.00. - Active Counters: Zetrix AI rose three sen to 9.5 sen, while ACE Market debutant SLGC fell three sen to 25 sen. V.S Industry dropped half a sen to 31.5 sen and Ramssol slipped two sen to 81.5 sen. - Top Gainers: Technology and plantation stocks posted sharp gains, led by Malaysian Pacific Industries (up 86 sen to RM44.26), Nestle (up 70 sen to RM90.70), Kuala Lumpur Kepong (up 48 sen to RM21.34), Mi Technovation (up 38 sen to RM5.79), and Batu Kawan (up 24 sen to RM19.22). - Top Decliners: Dutch Lady Milk Industries led losses, falling 40 sen to RM29.60, followed by BLD Plantation (down 18 sen to RM14.82), Ayer Holdings (down 15 sen to RM7.55), Samaiden (down 12 sen to RM3.07), and Kelington (down 10 sen to RM9.02). - Sectoral Indices: The Plantation Index surged 114.24 points to 9,045.27, the Energy Index gained 5.98 points to 835.92, and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.98 of a point to 179.95. The Financial Services Index declined 20.24 points to 19,119.90. On the broader index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index jumped 97.32 points to 17,640.81, the FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 74.37 points to 12,143.38, and the FBM ACE Index added 8.10 points to reach 5,614.71. –NMT

title: 'Bella Astillah, Syed Saddiq to release reality show documenting their love story
body: 'Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and Malaysian singer-actress Bella Astillah are offering fans a closer look at their relationship through their upcoming reality series, Walimatul Urus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq. At a press conference in Kuala Lumpur last week, the couple said the show would chronicle their love story, their journey towards marriage and what lies ahead for them. Bella, whose full name is Dayang Nabellah Awang Astillah, admitted that she was initially nervous when discussions about collaborating with Astro on the series began. However, she felt it was time for her and Syed Saddiq to give fans a more personal glimpse into their lives together. "Many fans already know that Syed Saddiq and I frequently do live streams together, but we have never talked in detail about how we first got acquainted and so on," Bella, 32, said. She added: "This journey is very meaningful to us, especially because we get to share these happy moments with our family, my two children, Ayden and Ara, and everyone who has supported us. "May this story become a sweet memory that we will cherish forever." Meanwhile, Syed Saddiq, 33, said he has always reminded Bella that happiness is something that should be shared with everyone. "Without their prayers, support and encouragement, our journey together might not be the same as it is today. Everyone has a role in making our journey a success," he said. The former youth and sports minister added that he is eagerly anticipating their wedding day on Oct 10 at Menara Merdeka Maybank in KL. "I cannot wait to share this happy day with everyone, especially my family and friends who have been waiting for a long time," he said. Walimatul Urus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq comprises eight episodes. The first two episodes, which document the couple's journey towards their wedding day, will premiere tomorrow (Oct 6) and Wednesday at 11pm, respectively, on Astro Ria (Ch 104), Astro Go and Sooka. The third episode will feature a live stream of Bella and Syed Saddiq's Oct 10 wedding ceremony, beginning at 9am on Astro Ria, Astro Prima (Ch 105), Astro Awani (Ch 501), Astro Go, Sooka and Astro Gempak. The fourth episode will feature a live stream of the pair's reception in Kuala Lumpur on Oct 18, beginning at 8pm on Astro Prima, Sooka, Astro Go and Astro Gempak. The remaining episodes, which will document the couple's life after marriage and preparations for their honeymoon, will premiere Tuesdays at 11pm from Oct 27 onwards on Astro Ria, Astro Go and Sooka.

title: 'Anak syarikat ES Sunlogy tuntut RM1.17 juta daripada Ecolectric, Maybank terlibat prosiding garnisi - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 2 Okt - Anak syarikat milik penuh ES Sunlogy Berhad, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd sedang mengambil tindakan untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman mahkamah bernilai RM1.17 juta terhadap Ecolectric Engineering Sdn Bhd selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan prosiding garnisi melibatkan Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank). Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membenarkan permohonan Savelite bagi Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab terhadap Maybank, yang dinamakan sebagai garnisi pertama Ecolectric, dalam pendengaran ex parte pada 30 September lalu, menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy kepada Bursa Malaysia. Mahkamah menetapkan 21 Oktober 2026 bagi pendengaran tunjuk sebab. Perintah Garnisi atau Garnishee Order merupakan proses undang-undang yang membolehkan pihak yang memperoleh penghakiman mahkamah memohon mendapatkan bayaran daripada wang milik pihak yang berhutang di bawah penghakiman tetapi dipegang oleh pihak ketiga, seperti bank. Dalam kes ini, Maybank dinamakan sebagai garnisi dan perlu menunjukkan sebab kepada mahkamah sebelum mahkamah memutuskan sama ada wang yang mungkin dipegang bagi pihak Ecolectric boleh digunakan untuk memenuhi penghakiman tersebut. Savelite akan mendapatkan Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab itu dan mengatur penyerahannya kepada Maybank mengikut arahan mahkamah. Prosiding itu menyusuli penghakiman ingkar pembelaan yang direkodkan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026 berhubung pertikaian kerja pemasangan elektrik bagi projek pembangunan kediaman di Damansara Heights. Pertikaian projek Damansara Heights Menerusi penghakiman itu, Ecolectric diperintahkan membayar RM1,174,327.72 kepada Savelite dalam tempoh 14 hari. Jumlah itu merupakan RM1,234,551.27 yang diputuskan mahkamah selepas ditolak wang tahanan RM60,223.55 yang dipegang Savelite. Pertikaian itu berpunca daripada surat anugerah bernilai kira-kira RM1.65 juta bertarikh 25 April 2022, apabila Savelite melantik Ecolectric sebagai subkontraktor untuk membekalkan tenaga kerja bagi pemasangan perkhidmatan elektrik untuk projek pembangunan kediaman 54 unit di Damansara Heights. Savelite mendakwa Ecolectric gagal atau enggan menempatkan tenaga kerja yang mencukupi atau berkemahiran di tapak, menyebabkan kerja tidak dapat dilaksanakan mengikut program yang dipersetujui. Savelite memfailkan writ saman dan penyata tuntutan terhadap Ecolectric pada Julai 2026. Menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy, Ecolectric tidak memasukkan kehadiran dalam tempoh 14 hari selepas writ saman dan penyata tuntutan diserahkan serta gagal memfail dan menyerahkan pembelaannya dalam tempoh ditetapkan. Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian merekodkan penghakiman ingkar pembelaan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026. Selain bayaran RM1.17 juta, mahkamah memerintahkan ganti rugi am ditaksir dan kos RM528 dibayar oleh Ecolectric kepada Savelite. ES Sunlogy sebelum ini berkata Savelite telah membuat rosot nilai penuh sebanyak RM3.17 juta ke atas jumlah terhutang daripada Ecolectric berkaitan projek Damansara Heights dan Old Klang Road, mencerminkan penilaian kumpulan terhadap kebolehkutipan jumlah tersebut. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Marginally Higher on Easing US Treasury Yields, Fed Tone
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – Bursa Malaysia rebounded to open marginally higher on Friday morning, October 2, 2026, supported by easing US Treasury yields and a measured tone from the Federal Reserve, which provided temporary relief to investor sentiment. At 9:10 AM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.49 points, or 0.09 per cent, to 1,631.85, up from Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The index initially opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87. Overall market sentiment was mildly positive, with gainers outpacing decliners 239 to 137, while 270 counters traded unchanged, 2,127 untraded, and 24 suspended. Total turnover stood at 173.94 million shares valued at RM95.98 million, with analysts anticipating cautious trading within the 1,625–1,640 range throughout the day. Heavyweights and Active Stocks Key heavyweights presented a mixed performance during early trade: - Tenaga Nasional added four sen to RM12.94. - IHH Healthcare rose one sen to RM7.71. - Maybank traded flat at RM9.95. - Public Bank and CIMB shed one sen each to RM4.66 and RM7.68, respectively. In active trading, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources, and Genetec remained unchanged at 16.5 sen, 18 sen, and 32.5 sen, respectively. V.S Industry gained one sen to 28 sen, while Kinergy Advancement lost half a sen to 39.5 sen. Technology and oil-related counters led the early gainers: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Advanced 58 sen to RM41.70. - Hengyuan Refining: Inched up 19 sen to RM3.83. - Petronas Chemicals: Perked up 15 sen to RM4.28. - UWC & MI Technovation: Both firmed 10 sen to RM7.20 and RM5.36, respectively. Decliners were led by MISC, which dropped 14 sen to RM7.54. Meanwhile, LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB, and RHB Bank shed four sen each to RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78, and RM7.43, respectively. title: '2026 Mazda CX-5 – third-gen secures over 600 bookings before launch; Maybank reports circa RM160k price tag
body: 'According to a market insight report by Maybank Investment Bank, Bermaz Auto has secured over 600 bookings for the third-generation Mazda CX-5 ahead of the SUV’s launch on October 8 this year. Bermaz Motor, the official distributor of Mazda vehicles here, previously said the latest CX-5 will initially arrive as a fully-imported (CBU) model before local assembly (CKD) starts “about 12-16 months” later. Estimated pricing for the SUV is said to be from RM170k. In its report, the investment back states that CKD production of the CX-5 will start in mid-2027, with pricing below said estimate at circa RM160k. The report also revealed a new B-segment SUV arriving in either 2027 or 2028, likely priced at around RM120k. This likely points towards the second-generation CX-3, which was confirmed by Mazda last month. As per the Japanese carmaker’s mid-year financial report, the next generation of the CX-3 will be introduced in phases in ASEAN, Japan and other markets from 2027, with Thailand being the production base for the model. Both the current CX-3 and Mazda 2 – the latter sharing the same underlying vehicle platform – have already been dropped from Bermaz Motor’s line-up.

title: 'Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. “In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said. Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide. He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony. — Bernama

title: 'Opinion: When audit opinions meet uncertain numbers
body: 'Two lawsuits filed within days of each other in late July and early August have renewed a question that matters to every investor. When financial statements rest on estimates that could go either way, what does a “clean” audit opinion actually guarantee? The liquidators of Serba Dinamik Holdings Bhd are seeking at least RM1.56 billion from KPMG, alleging that unqualified opinions between FY2016 and FY2019 failed to detect revenue overstatements of up to 87%. The suit claims the misstatements would have been uncovered earlier, before the group paid RM1.795 billion in dividends, which the claim links to the alleged audit failures. Around the same time, the Sabah government, together with other plaintiffs, sued Ernst & Young for RM2.4 billion over its audits of Sabah Development Bank, alleging that EY issued unqualified opinions for years even though, according to the claim, 85.94% of the bank’s loan portfolio had been recorded as non-performing loans by FY2018. Both claims remain before the courts, and the allegations have not been tested at trial. The cases will turn on negligence and evidence. But they expose a deeper structural tension that the courts cannot resolve. There is a gap between what an audit opinion actually asserts and what investors assume it guarantees. The lawsuits concern alleged audit failures. The broader issue, however, exists even where there is no allegation of failure. To see that tension clearly, it helps to separate alleged audit failure from the routine judgements in every set of audited accounts. Serba Dinamik and Sabah Development Bank are outlier cases. The structural issue is visible in ordinary audits of Malaysia’s largest companies, whose auditors have not been accused of anything. Maybank’s FY2025 audited accounts provide one illustration. The auditors identified expected credit losses on loans, advances and financing as a Key Audit Matter (KAM). These assets represent 64.3% of the group’s total assets. The auditors stated that measuring expected credit losses (ECL) “requires the application of significant judgement and increased complexity”, involving forward looking factors, probability weighted scenarios and management overlays. They tested models, challenged assumptions and engaged credit modelling specialists. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s FY2025 statements offer another. Post employment benefit liabilities of RM13.3 billion at group level were valued using actuarial assumptions on salary increases, medical cost inflation and discount rates. The auditors “focused on this area because of the significant estimates made by management”, checked assumptions against historical data and compared discount rates to market yields with valuation experts. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. These are not presented as cases of audit failure. The system is working as designed. Yet TNB reports that a one percentage point movement in the discount rate can change its defined benefit obligation by more than RM1 billion. Maybank’s KAM similarly describes extensive audit procedures without showing investors the range of possible outcomes. The KAM explains the judgement, but not how sensitive the number may be. International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 701 requires auditors to communicate KAMs and allow them to highlight matters requiring significant auditor attention, while the opinion remains on the financial statements as a whole. But the framework is binary while uncertainty is not. Two competent valuers may reach different estimates, and a figure can be reasonable without being the only supportable answer. KAMs can therefore become lists of procedures rather than explanations of risk. Estimation uncertainty exists on a continuum while audit reporting remains categorical. The question is not whether KAMs should exist, but whether they tell investors enough about how uncertain the most consequential numbers really are. Malaysia’s Audit Oversight Board has identified “failure to sufficiently review significant risk areas and significant judgements” as a recurring enforcement concern. The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) highlighted in its November 2025 statement the importance of high-quality valuation practices, appropriate use of valuation experts and rigorous audit assessment. The International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR) has likewise identified accounting estimates, including fair value measurement, as an area where audit regulators have consistently found deficiencies. When auditors use KAMs to flag a valuation without qualifying the opinion, they are telling investors that the matter involved significant judgement but that the financial statements nevertheless met the requirements for an unmodified opinion. That may be technically correct for Maybank and TNB. But the Serba Dinamik case illustrates how insufficient that signal can be for investors. The concern is not simply whether auditors get the judgement wrong. Even a sound audit can leave investors unable to see how fragile a reasonable estimate may be. That is the gap the current reporting model should address. Four reforms would help. First, require sensitivity disclosure in the KAM. Auditors should disclose the reasonable range of outcomes and its impact on the financial statements. TNB’s statements already include sensitivity analysis on discount rate assumptions. This information should be connected directly to the KAM, rather than leaving investors to piece the implications together from different sections of the annual report. Second, consider graduated reporting for significant estimation uncertainty. Such reporting could signal that an estimate falls within an acceptable range but remains highly sensitive, without implying that there is a material misstatement. The existing Emphasis of Matter framework under ISA 706 could provide a starting point. Third, require independent valuation review for specified material Level 3 assets. A second valuation would provide an additional check on management bias. The auditor could assess the divergence as evidence and consider the additional data point when applying professional scepticism. Fourth, strengthen audit committee disclosure. Audit committees should disclose how they challenged management’s fair value assumptions. If the committee accepted management’s numbers without meaningful scrutiny, that should be visible to shareholders. None of these solutions are radical. Each builds on existing frameworks, including Malaysian Financial Reporting Standard 13 (MFRS 13), ISA 701, ISA 540 and Malaysia’s corporate governance code. They require recognition that the current approach to fair value auditing, while technically sound, is insufficiently transparent for the risks involved. Judgement is unavoidable. Opacity is not. A KAM should do more than say, “we looked at this”. It should help investors understand what drove the estimate, how sensitive it is and what could change the auditor’s assessment. A “clean” audit opinion was never meant to guarantee that every number is right. But as financial statements rely increasingly on complex estimates, audit reporting should show more clearly how uncertain the most consequential numbers are. Hijat A Jabbar and Siti Zabedah Saidin are professors of accounting at Universiti Utara Malaysia.

title: 'TNB Moving Higher Up The ESG Ladder
body: 'Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) is strengthening its environmental, social and governance (ESG) profile through major renewable energy and hydroelectric upgrades that align with Malaysia’s national energy transition agenda.  Following an investor webinar held by TNB on Oct 1, it was highlighted that the utility group’s Hybrid Hydro Floating Solar (HHFS) project at Tasik Kenyir and the Sungai Perak Hydro Life Extension Programme (HLEP) as two initiatives supporting the transition towards a lower-carbon electricity system.  Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) targets renewable energy accounting for 70% of installed power capacity by 2050, a target reaffirmed by the government as recently as September.  The first phase of the Kenyir project, known as Kenyir #1, will comprise 595MWac of floating solar capacity integrated with a 297.5MW battery energy storage system (BESS).  The engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning contract has been awarded to the Cypark-Sunview consortium, with commercial operations targeted for the fourth quarter of 2028.  TNB expects the project to generate a high single-digit equity internal rate of return, despite floating solar requiring around 10% to 15% higher capital expenditure than conventional ground-mounted solar.  The economics are supported by a 21-year Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) offtake agreement with DayOne Data Centers, CIMB said.  From an ESG perspective, TNB highlighted several advantages of the floating solar project. These include higher power output from the cooling effect of the water body, the avoidance of land clearing and an estimated reduction of 650,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.  The project is also expected to have limited impact on Tasik Kenyir’s biodiversity as the installation will occupy only about 1.4% of the lake’s surface area.  Alongside new solar capacity, TNB is investing RM5.8 billion in rehabilitating and upgrading its ageing Sungai Perak Hydroelectric Plant network.  The HLEP covers five hydroelectric stations with a combined installed capacity of 648MW. Progress had reached 36% as of June 2026, with commissioning scheduled progressively between 2026 and 2033.  Once completed, the plants are expected to operate for another 40 years under a new power purchase agreement, allowing TNB to preserve existing renewable generation assets while extending their productive lifespan.  CIMB said both initiatives fit with the NETR’s emphasis on expanding renewable generation and energy storage capacity. The roadmap identifies renewable energy as one of Malaysia’s core energy-transition levers.  The research house maintained its BUY call and RM15.90 target price on TNB, while keeping its FY2026-FY2028 core earnings forecasts unchanged.  CIMB does not expect the projects to provide a meaningful earnings boost over the next three years, given their development timelines, but views them positively for TNB’s longer-term sustainability positioning and said they could contribute to further improvements in the group’s ESG ratings.

title: 'BernamaBiz - Malaysia Entering More Supportive Water Investment Cycle  -- CIMB Securities
body: 'Malaysia Entering More Supportive Water Investment Cycle -- CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 (Bernama) -- Malaysia is entering a more supportive water investment cycle as ageing infrastructure, high water losses and rising industrial and data centre demand, as well as greater climate variability are increasing the urgency to improve water efficiency, reliability, and resilience. In a note today, CIMB Securities said the federal government had approved RM1.7 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800 kilometres of critical pipes from 2026 to 2030, alongside a multi-year National Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Programme. It said sizeable projects including Langat 2 Phase 2, Rasau Phase 2, and the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme should further strengthen water security and provide a visible pipeline for contractors, pipe manufacturers and ancillary solution providers. CIMB Securities said Malaysia’s NRW rate stood at 37.1 per cent in 2024. “Persistently high NRW, ageing distribution networks, and rising climate variability result in unnecessary raw water extraction, higher treatment and pumping requirements, weaker utility economics, and supply disruption risks. “Concurrently, population growth, industrialisation, and rapid data centre development are driving structural water demand, particularly across economic corridors in Selangor, Johor, and Penang,” it added. The stockbroking company said Malaysia’s water transition is seen broadening from purely building new infrastructure towards using existing water resources and assets more efficiently. It said sustainable NRW reduction requires physical rehabilitation alongside smart metering, leak detection, pressure management, telemetry, analytics, and intelligent asset-management systems. “These technologies can make water networks more visible, measurable, and manageable, improving the effectiveness of every ringgit spent on water infrastructure. “This is aligned with the Water Sector Transformation 2040 (WST2040), which promotes digitalisation, climate resilience, integrated water-resource management, and stronger sector governance,” it said. From an investment perspective, CIMB Securities said it favours companies positioned at either the efficiency or infrastructure-enablement layers of Malaysia’s water transition. “Insight Analytics Bhd is among the most direct listed proxies to water digitalisation and NRW management, while Gamuda Bhd offers exposure to large-scale treatment, transmission, and water security projects. “The key near-term risk remains the pace at which funding and policy commitments translate into tenders, project awards, and, ultimately, earnings,” it said. -- BERNAMA

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 25): Malaysian plantation companies with sizeable operations in Indonesia face greater regulatory uncertainty following the country’s new agrarian reform law, with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG), Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KL:KLK) among those with the largest exposure, according to CIMB Securities.

The potential impact, however, remains unclear as key details — including maximum landholding limits for companies and affiliated entities, and how a provision requiring at least 20% of certain land to be made available for agrarian reform and redistribution — have yet to be finalised through implementing regulations.

As such, CIMB has not made any adjustments to its earnings forecasts or the land banks of plantation companies under its coverage, saying it sees higher regulatory uncertainty rather than an immediate loss of land or earnings.

“We do not expect an across-the-board 20% cut in existing land,” the research house said in a note on Friday.

Indonesia’s parliament approved the Agrarian Reform Law on Tuesday, creating a broader framework to address land ownership concentration, redistribution and longstanding agrarian conflicts. The law also provides for a dedicated body under the president to oversee implementation, supervision and conflict resolution.

However, the Indonesian government still needs to draw up implementing rules that will, among other matters, determine minimum and maximum landholding limits. Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning Minister Nusron Wahid said such details would be provided through subsequent regulations.

The development was reported earlier this week, including by Bloomberg, which highlighted broader risks to Indonesia’s plantation and property sectors. CIMB’s latest assessment focuses on the potential implications for Malaysian-listed plantation companies.

Among CIMB’s Malaysian plantation coverage, SD Guthrie, Genting Plantations and KLK have the largest absolute plantation exposure to Indonesia. IOI Corp Bhd (KL:IOICORP) has a smaller relative exposure, while Johor Plantations Group Bhd (KL:JPG), Ta Ann Holdings Bhd (KL:TAANN) and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd (KL:HSPLANT) have plantation operations entirely in Malaysia.

CIMB said the impact will depend on the final land limits, whether the 20% rule applies to existing plantations and how it will be implemented.

Bloomberg consensus as at Friday showed analysts remaining broadly positive on SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations, while views on KLK were more mixed.

For SD Guthrie, 17 analysts had "buy" calls and three had "hold" calls, with a 12-month target price of RM7.68. Genting Plantations had 10 "buy" calls and two "hold" calls, with a target price of RM6.81. KLK had nine "buy" calls, 10 "hold" calls, and one "sell", with a target price of RM24.57.

Separately, India’s decision to lower import duties on major edible oils could provide some support for crude palm oil (CPO) demand, although CIMB expects the benefit to Malaysian planters to be modest.

India cut the basic customs duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil to 5% from 10%, while eliminating the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil, effective Thursday. The Indian government said the move was aimed at reducing import costs and easing domestic edible oil prices.

CIMB said the lower CPO duty should reduce landed costs and support Indian palm oil imports, although the larger tariff reduction for sunflower oil could make it more competitive against palm oil and limit the increase in demand.

India accounted for about 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025. CIMB said the main benefit for Malaysian planters would likely come through firmer CPO prices rather than a significant direct increase in export volumes.

CIMB maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 per tonne for 2027.

title: 'Maybank, Hong Leong Win Best CEO and CFO Honours at Bursa Malaysia Awards
body: 'Bursa Malaysia awarded its top CEO and CFO honours to Maybank’s Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli and Hong Leong Bank’s Malkit Singh Maan. The inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026 took place on 4 September. Maybank received four honours, including Best CEO in Investor Relations for its President and Group CEO Khairussaleh. The bank also won Best Company in Investor Relations overall, Best Financial Reporting and Best Large-cap Company in Investor Relations for Financial Services. Malkit won Best CFO in Investor Relations. Hong Leong Bank also ranked among the top three performers in the large-cap financial services category, according to the bank. Malkit said, “As we execute our bankwide strategic transformation, our focus in Investor Relations is to maintain open, continuous dialogue with analysts, fund managers and shareholders, ensuring that our drive for efficiency and new growth opportunities is always backed by strong governance and clear financial disclosures. We remain deeply grateful for the continued trust and strong support of our investment community, shareholders, and valued partners throughout this journey.” The awards recognised 32 winners across eight main categories for investor engagement, market communication and corporate transparency. Local and international investors and analysts participated in the evaluation, supported by independent verification and Bursa Malaysia’s due diligence review. title: 'FBM KLCI charts slight gain at midday
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's benchmark index lagged enthusiasm, weighed down by persistent fears over geopolitical risk, inflation risks and a weak sentiment for equities. At noon, the FBM KLCI was up 1.84 points to 1,632.71, with heavyweight banks helping to shore up the market. AMMB rose 11 sen to RM6.50, Hong Leong Bank jumped 26 sen to RM22.90 and Public Bank was up three sen to RM7.46. On the broader market, the sentiment remained weak with 560 decliners compared to 477 gainers. There were 2.93 billion shares traded for a value of RM1.39bil. The technology sector was the biggest gainer, jumping 1.69%, while financial services rose 0.4% Telcos dove 2.12%, utilities dropped 0.51%, property shed 0.43% and energy slid 0.37%. Meanwhile, Zetrix AI continued its fall after the trading halt was lifted at 10am. The share hit limit down after falling 3.5 sen to eight sen, after news broke last Friday it owed over RM200mil in collections. VS Industry rose four sen to 33 sen and Cuscapi slid 0.5 sne ot 4.5 sen. In regional markets, Japan's Nikkei was up 2.08% to 69,730 while South Korea's Kospi gained 0.46% to 7,003. China's Shanghai Composite index added 0.31% to 3,842. Hong Kong's Hang Seng was nearly flat at 23,952.

title: 'ASB Disposes 13 Million Shares In Maybank
body: 'AmanahRaya Trustees Bhd, as trustee for Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB), disposed of 13 million shares in Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) on Sept 29, 2026.  In a filing, Maybank said the disposal was made through a sale of shares and involved ASB’s direct interest in the banking group.  Following the transaction, ASB’s direct shareholding in Maybank stood at 3.418 billion shares, representing 28.261% of the bank’s issued shares.  The notice of the change in substantial shareholding was dated Sept 29 and received by Maybank on Oct 1.  Maybank shares closed lower at 9.95, the stock has come down 14% over the last 6 months.

title: 'Hannah: 88 More Open-space Lots Gazetted in KL, Bringing Total to 582
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): A total of 88 open-space lots in the federal capital have been gazetted in the first nine months of this year, bringing the number of legally protected lots to 582, covering 476.17 hectares. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the latest gazettement involved 26 lots covering 7.33 hectares, equivalent to about 10 football fields. “The gazettement provides clearer legal protection for open spaces and helps ensure they are preserved for public benefit. “Open spaces also play an important role in the urban environment by helping to absorb rainwater runoff, reduce the effects of urban heat and provide recreational areas for the community,” she said in a Facebook post on Tuesday. Hannah said the latest 26 lots were located across eight parliamentary constituencies: Bandar Tun Razak (six lots), Segambut (five), Seputeh and Cheras (four each), Wangsa Maju, Lembah Pantai and Batu (two each), and Setiawangsa (one). In Bandar Tun Razak, the areas are Alam Damai, Taman Damai Jaya and Taman Connaught, while in Segambut, they include Taman Segambut Indah, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Taman Sri Hartamas, Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Sri Bintang. In Seputeh, the lots are in Taman LTAT, Taman Shanghai, Bandar Bukit Jalil and Taman Esplanad, while Cheras involves Taman Midah, Taman Connaught and Taman Bukit Ria. The other areas are: Taman Desa Melawati and Taman Setapak (Wangsa Maju); Bukit Persekutuan/Jalan Travers (Lembah Pantai); Taman Kok Lian (Batu); and Taman Keramat AU3 (Setiawangsa). The public can check the list, gazettement status and locations of all 582 open spaces via the MyHijau link on the official Federal Territories Land and Mines Office (PPTGWP) website at www.ptgwp.gov.my. The facility allows Kuala Lumpur residents and residents’ associations to check the status of open spaces in their neighbourhoods and help monitor and preserve them. title: 'The Ladies 2026: 42 pemain mulakan saingan pusingan pertama - Portal Berita RTM
body: 'SERI KEMBANGAN, 1 Oktober – Pusingan pertama Kejohanan Golf Wanita The Ladies 2026 menyaksikan 42 pemain mula beraksi seawal pukul 7.30 pagi tadi. Saingan kali ini turut menampilkan gandingan pemain profesional serta amatur seperti Allycia Gan, Liyana Durisic, Durriyah Damian dan Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan tersebut adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan. Kejohanan tersebut juga sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja di The Mines Resort and Golf Club, kelmarin. Kejohanan tersebut kembali buat kali kedua dengan menyasarkan visi menjadi antara kejohanan wanita berprestij di rantau ini, sebelum melangkah ke pentas antarabangsa. Kejohanan yang berlangsung di Kelab Golf The Mines dari 1 hingga 3 Oktober itu menawarkan jumlah hadiah wang tunai sehingga RM100,000.

title: '‘Ibu Janji Ambil Kami Di Sekolah, Tapi Dia Pergi Buat Selamanya’ | Medialahmy
body: 'GUA MUSANG – Hancur hati dua beradik apabila ibu yang dinanti untuk menjemput mereka pulang dari sekolah tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya mereka menerima berita duka apabila insan tersayang itu meninggal dunia akibat kemalangan. Nur Arissa Najla Mohd Shazuam, 13, dan Nur Amani Nuwairah Mohd Shazuam, 15, menanti penuh sabar selepas ibunya, Nor Hasyikim Daud, 34, berjanji mengambil mereka pulang dari Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bandar Chiku. Nur Arissa Najla berkata, dia menerima berita kemalangan itu daripada seorang rakan ketika menunggu pada 1.40 tengah hari. “Ibu ada maklumkan akan ke Gua Musang dengan rakannya dan berjanji mengambil saya serta kakak dari sekolah. “Pada hari kejadian, saya menduduki tiga kertas peperiksaan dan sangat teruja untuk memberitahu ibu yang saya boleh jawab semua soalan subjek Sejarah. “Lebih setengah jam menanti ibu, namun tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya saya terima berita ibu kemalangan. “Saya nampak bapa saudara datang menjemput kami,” katanya ketika ditemui di Felda Chiku 5 di sini. Dalam kejadian Ahad lalu, Nor Hasyikim maut di lokasi kejadian apabila kenderaan dipandunya bertembung dengan lori 10 tan di Kilometer 40 Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Krai. Mangsa meninggal dunia akibat tersepit, manakala rakannya di tempat duduk penumpang hadapan cedera parah. Allahyarham turut meninggalkan seorang bayi Nur Aireen Nisrina berusia 11 bulan. Sementara itu, kakak kepada Nor Hasyikim, Siti Noraeshah Daud, 39, berkata, tiga beradik itu akan dijaga ibunya dengan bantuan adik-beradik lain. “Sejak setahun lalu arwah membesarkan tiga anaknya dengan bekerja di kantin asrama SMK Bandar Chiku. “Selepas ini kami akan bersama-sama menjaga dan membesarkan tiga anak perempuan arwah,” katanya. Orang ramai yang ingin memberi sumbangan boleh menyalurkan ke akaun Bank CIMB milik Siti Noraeshah Daud bernombor 7601845122. Sumber – Berita Harian

“Kalau kita gunakan kontena, ada masalah termasuk kemungkinan terpaksa menunggu lama untuk masuk sehingga menyebabkan barangan terutama makanan rosak.

“Kalau RM5 juta itu dikira berdasarkan kontena, jumlahnya tidak kurang daripada 20 kontena,” katanya.

Beliau berkata, MAPIM juga bersedia menggunakan laluan kemasukan yang dijangka tersedia pada November sekiranya ia berjaya dibuka.

Katanya, usaha itu memerlukan kerjasama kerajaan Malaysia dan Mesir terutama bagi mendapatkan kebenaran supaya bantuan dapat dibawa masuk ke Gaza.

Kempen berkenaan menyasarkan kira-kira 66,000 penerima di Khan Younis, Rafah, Deir Al-Balah, Jabalia dan Gaza City.

title: 'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says
body: 'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says KUALA LUMPUR — Tenaga Nasional Bhd could absorb an additional RM120 million to RM150 million in costs between September and December 2026 following the expansion of government exemptions covering electricity-related charges for residential consumers, according to CIMB Securities. The brokerage said nearly one million additional households are expected to benefit after the monthly electricity consumption threshold for the exemptions was raised to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) from 600 kWh. The change brings the total number of residential consumers covered to more than eight million. The exemptions involve the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charges and sales and service tax, reducing the immediate impact of electricity costs on a wider group of households. However, CIMB Securities said the arrangement means TNB is expected to absorb additional costs during the September-to-December protection period. The eventual financial impact will depend on the level of AFA charges during that period, which in turn is influenced by fuel costs. Unexpected cost for utility CIMB Securities described the development as a negative surprise because it had previously expected TNB to recover any government-sanctioned AFA subsidies through the Kumpulan Wang Industri Elektrik fund. The latest arrangement instead places an estimated RM120 million to RM150 million of additional costs on the national utility during the final four months of 2026. The research house noted that TNB had previously made a voluntary RM150 million corporate contribution towards the government’s tiered electricity rebate initiative between April and September 2020. That programme was introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic. CIMB Securities said it regarded the 2020 contribution differently because it was made in response to what it described as a severe and unprecedented crisis. The latest cost absorption therefore raises a broader question for investors over whether TNB could be required to shoulder similar costs beyond 2026. 2026 profit forecast trimmed Despite the additional burden, CIMB Securities maintained its “buy” recommendation on TNB and kept its discounted cash flow-based target price unchanged at RM15.90. The brokerage reduced its core net profit forecast for TNB’s full 2026 financial year by two per cent to account for the additional costs. Its core net profit forecasts for the 2027 and 2028 financial years were left largely unchanged. CIMB Securities said the immediate effect on TNB’s core earnings remained relatively small and was insufficient to change its valuation. Its longer-term concern centres instead on what could happen if fuel prices remain elevated and the expanded AFA exemptions continue beyond the end of 2026. Regulatory predictability in focus The research house warned that requiring TNB to absorb further subsidies could affect investor perceptions of the predictability of the utility’s regulated returns. TNB operates under Malaysia’s Incentive Based Regulation framework, which is intended to provide a structured mechanism governing electricity tariffs, costs and regulated returns. For investors, the issue therefore extends beyond the RM120 million to RM150 million estimated impact this year. CIMB Securities said continued cost absorption beyond 2026 could raise concerns about how consistently costs and returns would be treated under the regulatory framework. For households, meanwhile, the higher 800 kWh threshold extends protection from the specified electricity charges to almost one million more residential users. The balance between shielding consumers from higher electricity costs and maintaining the financial predictability of the regulated utility could consequently remain an important issue if fuel costs stay elevated into 2027.

title: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah to hold wedding receptions in Muar & Kota Kinabalu, public invited to 'Kenduri Rakyat'
body: 'Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and Malaysian singer-actress Bella Astillah, who are set to marry on Oct 10, will celebrate their special occasion with the public through two receptions themed “Kenduri Rakyat”.  The couple, who got engaged on March 28, will first exchange vows at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur.  The celebrations will then continue in Muar, Johor, on Oct 25, before the couple heads to Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on Oct 31.  At a press conference in Kuala Lumpur today (Oct 2), Syed Saddiq said preparations for the receptions had been challenging, as the events were organised within a span of two months.  Much of the difficulty came from finding enough vendors and a suitable venue within the limited timeframe.  “We are expecting around 20,000 to 30,000 guests. We will do our best to accommodate everyone,” the former youth and sports minister said.  Bella said about 10,000 special souvenirs would be prepared for guests attending the two public receptions, with the items distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.  She clarified that the Sabah reception would be held in Kota Kinabalu instead of in her hometown of Sandakan due to certain limitations.  Bella then went on to share more about her relationship with Syed Saddiq, revealing that it was the simple things he did that gave her the confidence to trust him.  “Everything he does is big in my eyes. Just little things like opening the door for me, reminding me to sleep early and eat my meals or just telling me to exercise … Even though it’s basic stuff, I’m happy,” she said.  Bella previously married Singaporean actor Aliff Aziz in 2016, but the relationship ended in divorce twice – once in 2019 and the second time in 2024.  She has two children from her former marriage: Ayden, nine; and Ara, six.

title: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, construction stocks seen as key beneficiaries of Budget 2027
body: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, construction stocks seen as key beneficiaries of Budget 2027 KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday. In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion. It believes the higher allocation “could provide a modest boost to mass-market consumption, particularly benefitting companies exposed to lower- and middle-income households”. Among the counters poised to benefit are 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (KL:99SMART), Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd (KL:ECOSHOP) and MR DIY Group (M) Bhd (KL:MRDIY), as well as food and beverage manufacturers Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:NESTLE), Life Water Bhd (KL:LWSABAH) and QL Resources Bhd (KL:QL). CIMB Securities also expects gross development expenditure to rise to RM83 billion in 2027, with higher spending on water infrastructure among the potential areas of focus. Among the counters it sees as well positioned to benefit are Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM), Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT) and Insight Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB). Healthcare sector seen supported Separately, Maybank Investment Bank expects Budget 2027 to remain supportive of the healthcare sector. Potential measures include tax relief for healthcare and medical insurance, support for the nationwide MediAsas rollout, continued medical-tourism incentives and greater public-private collaboration to ease congestion at public hospitals, it said. Local pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturers may also benefit from continued government support for manufacturing, procurement, research and development, Maybank IB said. title: 'Stock Today: Maybank Dips 0.2% Despite New Wealth Advisory Initiative
body: 'Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) shares fell 0.19% to RM10.40 as of 12.35 pm, after the bank and Asian Banking School (ABS) signed an agreement to explore a professional certification framework for wealth advisory in Malaysia.  The stock opened at RM10.44 and moved between an intraday high of RM10.48 and a low of RM10.38. Some 4.77 million shares changed hands.  Maybank had closed at RM10.42 in the previous trading session, putting the latest price two sen lower.  The proposed ABS Wealth Advisory & Management Certification Programme is intended to establish an industry-recognised benchmark for wealth advisory professionals in banking.  If launched, the programme would be Malaysia’s first industry-wide professional certification framework dedicated to wealth advisory, with the first intake expected in the second half of 2027.  Maybank will serve as the founding industry partner while ABS will oversee the standards, assessment and certification process.  Maybank plans to incorporate the programme into its Maybank Wealth Academy, linking the certification with structured learning and workplace development.  The two parties will also explore extending relevant certification pathways to wealth professionals across the region

title: 'Nelly Korda's Deliberate Golf Break Costs Her as She Becomes Ineligible for LPGA Award - Report
body: 'Nelly Korda's Deliberate Golf Break Costs Her as She Becomes Ineligible for LPGA Award - Report Nelly Korda had a chance to settle her LPGA Hall of Fame future on the course this year. Victories at the Chevron Championship and U.S. Women's Open left her at 25 points, two short of induction. Given her early-season form, she was widely expected to earn those two points by the end of 2026. A single major win would have done it, but she has not won another major since June. Now, despite leading the tour in scoring average, Korda is set to miss another Hall of Fame point. This time, it has nothing to do with her performance or scores. Korda is ineligible for the Vare Trophy, the LPGA's award for lowest scoring average, due to insufficient rounds played, though she remains on track for Player of the Year. Golfweek's senior writer Beth Ann Nichols notes that the World No. 1 "currently leads the Vare Trophy race for low scoring at 69.38." However, she is not playing enough golf to win it. Had she earned the Vare Trophy, she would have received a Hall of Fame point. Paired with the Player of the Year award, which is worth one more point, that would have put her at 27. But the Vare Trophy has two key eligibility requirements. First, the golfer must play at least 60 individual-scoring rounds, or 60% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. If Nelly Korda makes the cut at The ANNIKA and plays all four rounds of the CME Group Tour Championship, she will have played 61 rounds. However, she won't meet the second eligibility criterion, which is playing at least 70 rounds, or 70% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. Counting the four rounds of the Dow Championship she played this summer, Korda finishes at 65 rounds. Thus, she falls five rounds shy of the eligibility criterion. She missed out on the Vare Trophy and the Hall of Fame point for the same reason in 2021. She could have become eligible if she had played two more events during the season. Her last event was the Solheim Cup, which Charley Hull & co. won. In total, she has made only 15 starts so far in 2026. She is now on a break that includes the ongoing Lotte Championship, which she is not playing. Golfweek reports that she will also be skipping the Asia swing, which includes the Buick LPGA Shanghai, the BMW Ladies Championship, the Maybank Championship, and the TOTO Japan Classic. This brings her total break to around two months. This isn't the first time she has missed the Asia swing. In fact, some fans have been outraged by her habit of skipping it. Korda has not played a fall Asian event since 2023. She skipped the 2024 stops after a neck injury sustained in practice. "I'm disappointed to miss these events and am especially sorry to my fans who were looking forward to seeing me play," she wrote in 2024. She also skipped last year's swing because of injury. After a top-five finish in Hawaii, Korda withdrew from the International Crown in October 2025 with an unspecified injury, and she was expected to sit out the Asia swing that followed. It came in a winless 2025 in which neck problems cost her time. Korda said after the Hawaii event that her body is "definitely worn down" by that point in the year, and she has stressed the need to be as close to 100 percent as possible before teeing it up. But despite the reduced schedule, the 28-year-old has a chance to win the remaining two points by the end of the season. She leads Haeran Ryu in the Player of the Year race by 75 points. So that is one possible point. In addition, she can win either The ANNIKA or the CME Group Tour Championship to earn the last point. Korda is a three-time winner at The ANNIKA and can do it again this year. Nelly Korda's shortened schedule has cost her another opportunity to add an LPGA Hall of Fame point, but her season is far from over. 'Nelly Korda's Deliberate Golf Break Costs Her as She Becomes Ineligible for LPGA Award - Report Nelly Korda had a chance to settle her LPGA Hall of Fame future on the course this year. Victories at the Chevron Championship and U.S. Women's Open left her at 25 points, two short of induction. Given her early-season form, she was widely expected to earn those two points by the end of 2026. A single major win would have done it, but she has not won another major since June. Now, despite leading the tour in scoring average, Korda is set to miss another Hall of Fame point. This time, it has nothing to do with her performance or scores. Korda is ineligible for the Vare Trophy, the LPGA's award for lowest scoring average, due to insufficient rounds played, though she remains on track for Player of the Year. Golfweek's senior writer Beth Ann Nichols notes that the World No. 1 "currently leads the Vare Trophy race for low scoring at 69.38." However, she is not playing enough golf to win it. Had she earned the Vare Trophy, she would have received a Hall of Fame point. Paired with the Player of the Year award, which is worth one more point, that would have put her at 27. But the Vare Trophy has two key eligibility requirements. First, the golfer must play at least 60 individual-scoring rounds, or 60% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. If Nelly Korda makes the cut at The ANNIKA and plays all four rounds of the CME Group Tour Championship, she will have played 61 rounds. However, she won't meet the second eligibility criterion, which is playing at least 70 rounds, or 70% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. Counting the four rounds of the Dow Championship she played this summer, Korda finishes at 65 rounds. Thus, she falls five rounds shy of the eligibility criterion. She missed out on the Vare Trophy and the Hall of Fame point for the same reason in 2021. She could have become eligible if she had played two more events during the season. Her last event was the Solheim Cup, which Charley Hull & co. won. In total, she has made only 15 starts so far in 2026. She is now on a break that includes the ongoing Lotte Championship, which she is not playing. Golfweek reports that she will also be skipping the Asia swing, which includes the Buick LPGA Shanghai, the BMW Ladies Championship, the Maybank Championship, and the TOTO Japan Classic. This brings her total break to around two months. This isn't the first time she has missed the Asia swing. In fact, some fans have been outraged by her habit of skipping it. Korda has not played a fall Asian event since 2023. She skipped the 2024 stops after a neck injury sustained in practice. "I'm disappointed to miss these events and am especially sorry to my fans who were looking forward to seeing me play," she wrote in 2024. She also skipped last year's swing because of injury. After a top-five finish in Hawaii, Korda withdrew from the International Crown in October 2025 with an unspecified injury, and she was expected to sit out the Asia swing that followed. It came in a winless 2025 in which neck problems cost her time. Korda said after the Hawaii event that her body is "definitely worn down" by that point in the year, and she has stressed the need to be as close to 100 percent as possible before teeing it up. But despite the reduced schedule, the 28-year-old has a chance to win the remaining two points by the end of the season. She leads Haeran Ryu in the Player of the Year race by 75 points. So that is one possible point. In addition, she can win either The ANNIKA or the CME Group Tour Championship to earn the last point. title: 'Ryt Bank Now Malaysia’s First Digital Bank to Support Apple Pay
body: 'Ryt Bank has become the first licensed digital bank in Malaysia to support Apple Pay, allowing cardholders to pay in stores, online and in apps. The bank also added Google Pay support in January 2026. Customers can add their Ryt Card through the bank’s app by selecting the Cards tab, tapping “Add to Apple Wallet” and following the on-screen instructions. Once they add the card to Apple Wallet on an iPhone, they have the option to add it to their other compatible Apple devices. According to the bank, transactions require authentication through the device’s built-in security features, including Face ID, Touch ID or a passcode. Card numbers are not shared with merchants or stored on Apple servers. Customers who misplace their iPhone can mark it as lost through Find My to suspend their card on the device. Other banks supporting Apple Pay in Malaysia include AmBank, CIMB, Hong Leong Bank, HSBC, Maybank, RHB and Standard Chartered. Apple also lists Wise Payments Malaysia as a participating card issuer, with support varying by issuer and card type. title: 'HLB Meezani Account-i Offers Cash, Gold, And Cars In New Prize Draws
body: 'HLB Meezani Account-i holders stand a chance to win cash, gold bars, holiday packages, a Proton e.MAS 5, and a Porsche Cayenne in HLB Islamic’s second year of prize draws, which runs from 30 July 2026 to 29 July 2027. There are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws, with minimum balances ranging from RM100 to RM60,000 depending on the prize. HLB Islamic announced this year’s prizes at a rewards ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on 29 September 2026, held to mark the account’s first year. The bank said 43% of those who opened the account in its first year were new HLB Islamic customers. The Minimum Balance For Each Prize Each prize has its own minimum balance, and you get one entry for every full multiple of that amount. For example, keeping RM1,000 in the account when the day ends gives 10 entries in the daily draw, since the minimum balance is RM100. For the weekly draw, you get one entry for every RM200. Keeping RM2,500 at the end of the week gives 12 entries, and the extra RM100 doesn’t count. For quarterly and yearly prizes, entries are counted from each month-end balance and added up until the draw. Keeping RM2,000 in the account at the end of each month for a three-month quarter, for example, gives three entries for the 10g gold bar draw. Since the monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws all use your month-end balance, withdrawing money on the last day of the month can reduce your entries for that month, even if you put the money back a few days later. Some Payments And Deposits Can Earn Extra Entries The monthly and quarterly prizes also offer extra entries if you’ve already met the minimum balance for the relevant prize. You can earn additional entries by making at least 10 eligible QR or online payments from the account in a month, or by depositing at least RM2,000 in a single transaction. Doing both in the same month earns one more combo entry. Making 10 payments earns extra entries for the RM500 cash and Touch ‘n Go prizes. A deposit of RM2,000 or more earns extra entries for every prize in the table except the Proton e.MAS 5, which only gets the combo entry when you do both in the same month. The daily, weekly, and yearly draws don’t offer extra entries. Win Limits And Claiming Your Prize You can win the daily prize once a week at most, and the weekly prize once every two weeks. If your name is selected for more than one monthly prize in the same month, you’ll only receive the highest-value prize. The same applies to the quarterly and yearly draws. To qualify for the draws, you need to actively use HLB Connect from the start of each draw period until any prize is handed over. Winners are selected within 30 working days after each draw period ends and notified through the HLB Connect app within 14 working days after that. You have 30 working days from the announcement to claim your prize, after which the bank may award it to another winner. Cash prizes are credited directly into the winner’s HLB Meezani Account-i. Winners are responsible for any taxes or fees related to their prizes, and HLB Islamic may publish winners’ names with part of their IC numbers concealed. Non-cash prizes are handed over within 90 working days. Winners will need their winning letter and IC to collect them. Prizes can’t be exchanged for cash or transferred to someone else. Opening An HLB Meezani Account-i The account is Shariah-compliant and open to individuals who live in Malaysia. You need RM100 to open it and RM50 to keep it open. The account currently has an indicative profit rate of 0.05% p.a., calculated daily and paid monthly, as of 30 September 2026. You can deposit or withdraw money through HLB Islamic branches, ATMs, cash deposit machines, and online channels. Because it’s an investment account rather than a savings account or fixed deposit, HLB Islamic states that the money and returns aren’t guaranteed and the account isn’t protected by Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM). The prize draws come on top of the account’s profit rate, so look at both when deciding where to keep your money. You can also compare the latest savings account and fixed deposit rates on RinggitPlus. You can open the account at an HLB Islamic branch or book an appointment through the HLB Islamic website. The full rules are set out in the campaign’s terms and conditions [PDF]. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates. title: 'Budget 2027 may bring SST exemptions, income tax relief for middle-income earners — CIMB Securities
body: 'Budget 2027 may bring SST exemptions, income tax relief for middle-income earners — CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 18): Budget 2027 could see further sales and service tax (SST) exemptions to reduce costs embedded in businesses, alongside possible personal income tax relief for middle-income taxpayers, according to CIMB Securities. CIMB Securities said there is scope for the government to broaden SST exemptions for production-related inputs, as businesses continue to face elevated energy, logistics and other operating costs. It expects further SST relief to reduce government collections by about RM1 billion, although underlying growth should still lift SST revenue by 5.5% to RM72 billion in 2027. Unlike the goods and services tax (GST), the SST does not have a general input tax credit mechanism, meaning businesses may pay tax on inputs without being able to deduct it against tax charged on their own sales. This can result in tax costs being embedded through the supply chain, CIMB noted. CIMB said in a note extending selected exemptions is likely to be the more immediate option in Budget 2027, while a broader input tax credit mechanism could be introduced from 2028 or later because of the additional administrative and refund framework required. At the same time, CIMB sees room for targeted personal income tax relief for middle-income taxpayers, particularly households facing higher living costs but receiving less direct cash assistance. As an illustration, the research house said tax rates for chargeable income of RM50,001 to RM70,000 and RM70,001 to RM100,000 could each be reduced by one percentage point to 10% and 18% respectively. The current 25% tax bracket could also be split, with a 24% rate applied to chargeable income between RM100,001 and RM150,000. Such a package could provide annual tax savings of RM200 for those with RM70,000 in chargeable income, RM500 at RM100,000 and as much as RM1,000 for those earning RM150,000 and above, CIMB estimated. It said the illustrative package would cost the government about RM800 million annually. More broadly, CIMB expects Budget 2027 to continue providing household support while maintaining fiscal consolidation, forecasting the fiscal deficit to narrow slightly to 3.4% of gross domestic product in 2027 from an estimated 3.5% in 2026. The research house also expects cash assistance under Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah to increase by RM2 billion to RM17 billion, supported partly by lower fuel subsidy spending. CIMB forecasts petrol and diesel subsidies to fall to RM32 billion in 2027 from RM41 billion, creating room for higher household assistance and development spending while keeping the government on its fiscal consolidation path. Budget 2027, the fifth Madani Budget and the second under the 13th Malaysia Plan, is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The Ministry of Finance has said the budget will focus on areas including cost-of-living pressures, business competitiveness and productivity, while maintaining fiscal discipline.
