title: 'Maybank Foundation marks a decade of empowering weavers with third regional natural dye workshop and gallery launch in Cambodia | Maybank
body: 'Workshop and gallery launch strengthens natural dyeing knowledge and Cambodia's silk weaving heritage, building on a decade of empowering 2,617 women weavers and supporting 3,024 farmers across ASEAN Maybank Foundation, the social impact arm of Maybank Group, together with Maybank Cambodia and local programme implementation partner, Color Silk, recently marked the conclusion of the third Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) Regional Natural Dye Workshop and officially launched the MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery at the Maybank Silk Weaving Training Centre in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia. Held from 25 to 28 September 2026, the four-day workshop brought together women weavers and MWEW programme partners from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines to exchange traditional natural dyeing knowledge, strengthen technical skills and advance sustainable textile practices across ASEAN. The workshop and gallery launch form part of MWEW’s tenth anniversary milestones, celebrating a decade of preserving traditional woven textile heritage, strengthening women’s economic independence and supporting sustainable livelihoods across the region. The closing ceremony and gallery launch brought together 80 guests, including Her Excellency Srey Siyut, Advisor to the Governor, National Bank of Cambodia; Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women's Affairs Cambodia; His Excellency Prem Rotha, Deputy Governor of Siem Reap Province; Mr Me Sambo, Deputy Director of Department of Culture and Fine Arts in Siem Reap, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts; Mr Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia; Ms Qazreen Chan, Chief Operating Officer of Maybank Cambodia; Ms Noor Fadzlin Ariffin, Head, Community Empowerment of Maybank Foundation; Ms Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk, representatives from Maybank Cambodia, Maybank Foundation, regional MWEW programme partners and weavers, and Color Silk weavers. The ceremony also featured the presentation of certificates to workshop participants, a sharing session with three Cambodian graduate weavers and a gathering of representatives from all 10 MWEW programme batches in Cambodia. Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women’s Affairs, Cambodia, tries her hand at the traditional loom, as other attendees look on. As part of the MWEW programme, looms are provided by Color Silk to weavers upon completion of their training, enabling them to continue weaving from home and generate income towards greater financial independence. Ten years of strengthening women’s livelihoods and Cambodia’s weaving heritage Cambodia has been an integral part of MWEW since its introduction in 2016. Through its longstanding partnership with Color Silk, Maybank Foundation has supported the preservation of traditional Cambodian silk weaving while equipping women from underserved communities with skills and opportunities to build sustainable livelihoods and greater economic independence. As of 30 June 2026, MWEW in Cambodia has trained 852 women weavers, supported 1,584 farmers and facilitated the planting of approximately 220,700 mulberry trees to sustain local sericulture and silk production. Beneficiaries have also recorded monthly income increases of up to USD350, demonstrating how traditional craftsmanship can create tangible economic opportunities for women and their communities. Izlyn Ramli, CEO of Maybank Foundation and Head of Group Corporate Affairs, Maybank said, “Over the past decade, Maybank Women Eco-Weavers has shown that preserving traditional weaving heritage can go hand in hand with strengthening women’s economic independence and creating sustainable livelihoods. What began as an initiative for women weavers has grown into a livelihood and value-chain ecosystem connecting women, farmers and communities across five ASEAN countries through shared knowledge, skills and opportunities. “The third Regional Natural Dye Workshop and launch of the Natural Dye Gallery in Cambodia build on this journey. It is especially meaningful that the gallery was funded and developed through the eMpowering Youths Across ASEAN (eYAA) Cohort 4 programme with Color Silk, bringing together youth volunteers and communities to create a lasting resource for women weavers and farmers. This reflects the kind of lasting impact we seek to create through Maybank Foundation, where collaboration creates opportunities for communities to thrive while preserving ASEAN’s cultural and environmental heritage for generations to come,” she added. Advancing regional collaboration through natural dyeing The third MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop builds on a regional knowledge-sharing platform established in 2024 to strengthen traditional natural dyeing expertise and promote more sustainable textile production across MWEW communities. The first workshop in Sarawak, Malaysia in 2024 brought together 47 programme partners and weavers from four countries, resulting in 69 natural hues. In 2025, the second edition expanded participation to all five MWEW countries, with 77 women weavers developing 158 natural hues through exchanges on natural dyeing, local biodiversity and sustainable community practices. Hosted by Color Silk, the 2026 workshop brought together 50 participants to explore locally sourced botanical materials and traditional techniques for working with silk and cotton. The workshop culminated in more than 18 natural hues, while strengthening connections between women artisans, farmers and communities involved in the cultivation and supply of natural dye materials. From ASEAN youth initiative to a lasting resource for Cambodian communities The MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery builds on the Natural Dye Laboratory and Planting (NDLP) project launched in 2024 under Cohort 4 of eMpowering Youths Across ASEAN (eYAA), jointly implemented by Maybank Foundation and ASEAN Foundation. Through the project, Color Silk worked with 10 ASEAN youth volunteers and the local community in Siem Reap to promote sustainable dyeing practices and create economic opportunities for women weavers and farmers. The initiative benefited 215 community members, engaged 38 students in tree planting, provided 40 households with dye trees, supported the planting of 420 dye trees and engaged 17 local community members in constructing the gallery. Sixteen women weavers from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines completed the 3rd MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop, unlocking 18 colours through natural dyeing techniques. The hands-on exchange strengthens practical knowledge and sustainable weaving practices across MWEW’s ASEAN community. Officially launched two years after its establishment, the gallery is equipped with natural dye processing facilities and will serve as a hub for Color Silk’s weavers and wider community, supporting hands-on learning, experimentation, knowledge-sharing and the showcasing of locally developed natural dye products. The facility connects the outcomes of an ASEAN youth-led initiative with MWEW’s longer-term commitment to strengthening women’s livelihoods and sustainable weaving practices in Cambodia. Ms Vanntha Ngorn, Founder of Color Silk, said, “For our women weavers, traditional silk weaving is more than a craft. It is a source of livelihood, cultural identity and knowledge passed down through generations. Natural dyeing is an important part of this heritage, and the gallery provides a space for our community to continue learning, experimenting and strengthening these traditional skills. “What makes this facility particularly meaningful is how it was developed through the collective efforts of ASEAN youth volunteers and our local community. Their contributions have helped establish a resource that can continue supporting our women weavers and farmers, while encouraging younger generations to appreciate and preserve Cambodia’s traditional textile heritage,” she added. Ms Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk (with microphone), explains to distinguished guests on the natural dyeing process which uses locally sourced materials such as coconut husks, seeds and neem leaves to extract natural colours at the newly launched gallery. The space of the MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery is designed to facilitate hands-on learning and the continued sharing of traditional dyeing knowledge. Mr Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia, “Cambodia’s silk weaving heritage is an important part of our cultural identity, and preserving this tradition means continuing to invest in the women, farmers and communities who sustain it. Through our longstanding collaboration with Maybank Foundation and Color Silk, we have seen how traditional skills can create meaningful economic opportunities while keeping an important part of Cambodia’s heritage alive. “The Natural Dye Gallery represents another step forward in this journey. By bringing together traditional craftsmanship, sustainable practices and the contributions of ASEAN youth, we are creating opportunities for our weaving communities to continue developing their skills while preserving this valuable knowledge for future generations.” Celebrating a decade of growing together across ASEAN Since its launch in 2016, MWEW has grown into a regional economic ecosystem spanning Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines. As of 30 June 2026, it has trained 2,617 women weavers and supported 3,024 farmers, with USD5.6 million (RM22.9 million) invested across traditional weaving, natural fibre cultivation, natural dyeing, skills development, sustainable production and market access. Participants received their certificates at the completion ceremony of the 3rd MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop, joined by representatives from the Cambodian government, Maybank Cambodia, Maybank Foundation and Color Silk. The workshop reflects MWEW’s continued commitment to connecting communities through shared knowledge and sustainable craft practices. Witnessing the certificate presentation ceremony are (Back row); His Excellency Prem Rotha, Deputy Governor of Siem Reap Province (in dark blue suit with glasses); Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women's Affairs Cambodia (in teal blue dress); Her Excellency Srey Siyut, Advisor to the Governor, National Bank of Cambodia (in dark brown dress); Mr. Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia (in yellow and black shirt); Mr. Me Sambo, Deputy Director of Department of Culture and Fine Arts in Siem Reap, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts (in black suit with white shirt and light blue neck tie); Ms. Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk (in light brown dress); Ms. Qazreen Chan, Chief Operating Officer of Maybank Cambodia (in black and white blazer jacket); Ms. Noor Fadzlin Ariffin, Head, Community Empowerment of Maybank Foundation (in black cardigan) and Mr. Johann Nawawi, MWEW Architect Benefactor (in light brown batik shirt). Following its tenth anniversary celebration in Bali in August 2026, the third Regional Natural Dye Workshop carries this milestone into Cambodia, bringing regional knowledge and collaboration directly to its weaving communities. MWEW also advances Maybank Group’s ROAR30 sustainability ambitions by supporting inclusive economic participation, sustainable livelihoods and resilient communities while preserving ASEAN’s cultural heritage.

full_text: 'Maybank Foundation marks a decade of empowering weavers with third regional natural dye workshop and gallery launch in Cambodia | Maybank. 'Workshop and gallery launch strengthens natural dyeing knowledge and Cambodia's silk weaving heritage, building on a decade of empowering 2,617 women weavers and supporting 3,024 farmers across ASEAN Maybank Foundation, the social impact arm of Maybank Group, together with Maybank Cambodia and local programme implementation partner, Color Silk, recently marked the conclusion of the third Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) Regional Natural Dye Workshop and officially launched the MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery at the Maybank Silk Weaving Training Centre in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia. Held from 25 to 28 September 2026, the four-day workshop brought together women weavers and MWEW programme partners from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines to exchange traditional natural dyeing knowledge, strengthen technical skills and advance sustainable textile practices across ASEAN. The workshop and gallery launch form part of MWEW’s tenth anniversary milestones, celebrating a decade of preserving traditional woven textile heritage, strengthening women’s economic independence and supporting sustainable livelihoods across the region. The closing ceremony and gallery launch brought together 80 guests, including Her Excellency Srey Siyut, Advisor to the Governor, National Bank of Cambodia; Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women's Affairs Cambodia; His Excellency Prem Rotha, Deputy Governor of Siem Reap Province; Mr Me Sambo, Deputy Director of Department of Culture and Fine Arts in Siem Reap, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts; Mr Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia; Ms Qazreen Chan, Chief Operating Officer of Maybank Cambodia; Ms Noor Fadzlin Ariffin, Head, Community Empowerment of Maybank Foundation; Ms Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk, representatives from Maybank Cambodia, Maybank Foundation, regional MWEW programme partners and weavers, and Color Silk weavers. The ceremony also featured the presentation of certificates to workshop participants, a sharing session with three Cambodian graduate weavers and a gathering of representatives from all 10 MWEW programme batches in Cambodia. Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women’s Affairs, Cambodia, tries her hand at the traditional loom, as other attendees look on. As part of the MWEW programme, looms are provided by Color Silk to weavers upon completion of their training, enabling them to continue weaving from home and generate income towards greater financial independence. Ten years of strengthening women’s livelihoods and Cambodia’s weaving heritage Cambodia has been an integral part of MWEW since its introduction in 2016. Through its longstanding partnership with Color Silk, Maybank Foundation has supported the preservation of traditional Cambodian silk weaving while equipping women from underserved communities with skills and opportunities to build sustainable livelihoods and greater economic independence. As of 30 June 2026, MWEW in Cambodia has trained 852 women weavers, supported 1,584 farmers and facilitated the planting of approximately 220,700 mulberry trees to sustain local sericulture and silk production. Beneficiaries have also recorded monthly income increases of up to USD350, demonstrating how traditional craftsmanship can create tangible economic opportunities for women and their communities. Izlyn Ramli, CEO of Maybank Foundation and Head of Group Corporate Affairs, Maybank said, “Over the past decade, Maybank Women Eco-Weavers has shown that preserving traditional weaving heritage can go hand in hand with strengthening women’s economic independence and creating sustainable livelihoods. What began as an initiative for women weavers has grown into a livelihood and value-chain ecosystem connecting women, farmers and communities across five ASEAN countries through shared knowledge, skills and opportunities. “The third Regional Natural Dye Workshop and launch of the Natural Dye Gallery in Cambodia build on this journey. It is especially meaningful that the gallery was funded and developed through the eMpowering Youths Across ASEAN (eYAA) Cohort 4 programme with Color Silk, bringing together youth volunteers and communities to create a lasting resource for women weavers and farmers. This reflects the kind of lasting impact we seek to create through Maybank Foundation, where collaboration creates opportunities for communities to thrive while preserving ASEAN’s cultural and environmental heritage for generations to come,” she added. Advancing regional collaboration through natural dyeing The third MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop builds on a regional knowledge-sharing platform established in 2024 to strengthen traditional natural dyeing expertise and promote more sustainable textile production across MWEW communities. The first workshop in Sarawak, Malaysia in 2024 brought together 47 programme partners and weavers from four countries, resulting in 69 natural hues. In 2025, the second edition expanded participation to all five MWEW countries, with 77 women weavers developing 158 natural hues through exchanges on natural dyeing, local biodiversity and sustainable community practices. Hosted by Color Silk, the 2026 workshop brought together 50 participants to explore locally sourced botanical materials and traditional techniques for working with silk and cotton. The workshop culminated in more than 18 natural hues, while strengthening connections between women artisans, farmers and communities involved in the cultivation and supply of natural dye materials. From ASEAN youth initiative to a lasting resource for Cambodian communities The MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery builds on the Natural Dye Laboratory and Planting (NDLP) project launched in 2024 under Cohort 4 of eMpowering Youths Across ASEAN (eYAA), jointly implemented by Maybank Foundation and ASEAN Foundation. Through the project, Color Silk worked with 10 ASEAN youth volunteers and the local community in Siem Reap to promote sustainable dyeing practices and create economic opportunities for women weavers and farmers. The initiative benefited 215 community members, engaged 38 students in tree planting, provided 40 households with dye trees, supported the planting of 420 dye trees and engaged 17 local community members in constructing the gallery. Sixteen women weavers from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines completed the 3rd MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop, unlocking 18 colours through natural dyeing techniques. The hands-on exchange strengthens practical knowledge and sustainable weaving practices across MWEW’s ASEAN community. Officially launched two years after its establishment, the gallery is equipped with natural dye processing facilities and will serve as a hub for Color Silk’s weavers and wider community, supporting hands-on learning, experimentation, knowledge-sharing and the showcasing of locally developed natural dye products. The facility connects the outcomes of an ASEAN youth-led initiative with MWEW’s longer-term commitment to strengthening women’s livelihoods and sustainable weaving practices in Cambodia. Ms Vanntha Ngorn, Founder of Color Silk, said, “For our women weavers, traditional silk weaving is more than a craft. It is a source of livelihood, cultural identity and knowledge passed down through generations. Natural dyeing is an important part of this heritage, and the gallery provides a space for our community to continue learning, experimenting and strengthening these traditional skills. “What makes this facility particularly meaningful is how it was developed through the collective efforts of ASEAN youth volunteers and our local community. Their contributions have helped establish a resource that can continue supporting our women weavers and farmers, while encouraging younger generations to appreciate and preserve Cambodia’s traditional textile heritage,” she added. Ms Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk (with microphone), explains to distinguished guests on the natural dyeing process which uses locally sourced materials such as coconut husks, seeds and neem leaves to extract natural colours at the newly launched gallery. The space of the MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery is designed to facilitate hands-on learning and the continued sharing of traditional dyeing knowledge. Mr Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia, “Cambodia’s silk weaving heritage is an important part of our cultural identity, and preserving this tradition means continuing to invest in the women, farmers and communities who sustain it. Through our longstanding collaboration with Maybank Foundation and Color Silk, we have seen how traditional skills can create meaningful economic opportunities while keeping an important part of Cambodia’s heritage alive. “The Natural Dye Gallery represents another step forward in this journey. By bringing together traditional craftsmanship, sustainable practices and the contributions of ASEAN youth, we are creating opportunities for our weaving communities to continue developing their skills while preserving this valuable knowledge for future generations.” Celebrating a decade of growing together across ASEAN Since its launch in 2016, MWEW has grown into a regional economic ecosystem spanning Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines. As of 30 June 2026, it has trained 2,617 women weavers and supported 3,024 farmers, with USD5.6 million (RM22.9 million) invested across traditional weaving, natural fibre cultivation, natural dyeing, skills development, sustainable production and market access. Participants received their certificates at the completion ceremony of the 3rd MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop, joined by representatives from the Cambodian government, Maybank Cambodia, Maybank Foundation and Color Silk. The workshop reflects MWEW’s continued commitment to connecting communities through shared knowledge and sustainable craft practices. Witnessing the certificate presentation ceremony are (Back row); His Excellency Prem Rotha, Deputy Governor of Siem Reap Province (in dark blue suit with glasses); Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women's Affairs Cambodia (in teal blue dress); Her Excellency Srey Siyut, Advisor to the Governor, National Bank of Cambodia (in dark brown dress); Mr. Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia (in yellow and black shirt); Mr. Me Sambo, Deputy Director of Department of Culture and Fine Arts in Siem Reap, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts (in black suit with white shirt and light blue neck tie); Ms. Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk (in light brown dress); Ms. Qazreen Chan, Chief Operating Officer of Maybank Cambodia (in black and white blazer jacket); Ms. Noor Fadzlin Ariffin, Head, Community Empowerment of Maybank Foundation (in black cardigan) and Mr. Johann Nawawi, MWEW Architect Benefactor (in light brown batik shirt). Following its tenth anniversary celebration in Bali in August 2026, the third Regional Natural Dye Workshop carries this milestone into Cambodia, bringing regional knowledge and collaboration directly to its weaving communities. MWEW also advances Maybank Group’s ROAR30 sustainability ambitions by supporting inclusive economic participation, sustainable livelihoods and resilient communities while preserving ASEAN’s cultural heritage.

title: 'Maybank completes RM2.5bil AT1 sukuk mudharabah issuance | KLSE Screener
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively. The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033. Meanwhile, the RM650 million tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036. ...

title: 'Best Study Loans in Malaysia: PTPTN vs Banks
body: 'What Are Your Study Loan Options in Malaysia? When it comes to funding your higher education, you generally have four paths to choose from. It is always wise to look at them in this specific order: 1. The "Bank of Mom and Dad" (Family Support) If your parents or family members have an education fund set aside for you, this is your best option. It is interest-free, comes with zero debt stress, and requires no complicated paperwork. 2. Scholarships and Government Grants Scholarships do not require monetary repayment. However, they are highly competitive and often come with "bonding periods," requiring you to work for the sponsoring company or government body for a set number of years after graduating. 3. PTPTN Study Loans The default choice for the majority of Malaysian students. It is highly accessible, easy to apply for, and charges an incredibly low flat administrative rate (Kos Upah). 4. Commercial Bank Education Loans Banks like Maybank, Bank Rakyat, and Affin Bank offer dedicated education financing. While they can cover higher tuition fees (especially for expensive courses like medicine or overseas pilot programs), they come with much higher interest rates and stricter eligibility criteria. PTPTN vs. Bank Education Loans: How Do They Compare? To help you visualise the difference, here is a quick comparison of what you can expect: (Please verify the latest rates and terms on the official bank or PTPTN websites before applying.) Can You Combine PTPTN with a Scholarship? This is a very common question. The short answer is: it depends on the type of scholarship. If your university offers a partial tuition fee waiver or a merit discount directly on your semester fees, you are usually still eligible to apply for PTPTN to cover the remaining balance or your cost of living. This helps ease your overall financial burden. However, if you have secured a full, third-party sponsorship (from corporate giants like Yayasan Petronas, JPA, or Sime Darby), their terms and conditions will almost certainly prohibit you from taking a PTPTN loan simultaneously. Always check with your university’s student affairs department before signing any agreements. The Million-Ringgit Question: Should You Pay Off PTPTN Early? A PTPTN loan charges a flat administrative rate of 1% per annum. In the world of finance, this is virtually free money. A 1% flat rate translates to a very low effective interest rate (roughly 1.8% to 1.9%). Imagine you have a RM50,000 PTPTN loan with a 15-year repayment period. Your minimum monthly repayment is roughly RM319.44. If you have extra cash on hand after graduating, you have two choices: - Option 1: Pay off the loan as slowly as possible and put your extra cash into high-yield savings accounts, digital banks (which offer up to 3% to 4% p.a.), or low-risk investments like ASB or EPF (which historical data shows yield 4.5% to 6% p.a.). - Option 2: Pay off the loan quickly in 5 to 10 years to live a debt-free life. Scientifically speaking, Option 1 makes more financial sense. Because the interest rate of PTPTN (1%) is significantly lower than the dividend rates of ASB or digital banks, your money grows faster in an investment account than the debt accumulates. However, Option 2 gives you peace of mind and improves your Debt Service Ratio (DSR). This makes it much easier to apply for home loans and car loans later in life. The Real Consequences of Ignoring Your PTPTN Repayments During our interviews with university graduates, we noticed a worrying trend: many do not take PTPTN repayment seriously. Some assume that because they are "government loans," they can simply be ignored. This is a massive mistake. If you fail to repay your PTPTN loan, you will face severe long-term financial consequences. Your CCRIS Score Will Be Ruined PTPTN is linked directly to the Central Credit Reference Information System (CCRIS) managed by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). If you default on your payments, your CCRIS report will show black marks. When you apply for a credit card, a car loan for your first Axia, or a home loan, banks will pull your CCRIS report. If they see unpaid PTPTN dues, your application will be instantly rejected. Legal Action and Debt Collectors PTPTN has the right to take legal action against you. You will be issued letters of demand, and in worst-case scenarios, your bank accounts or salary could be subject to garnishment. Travel Bans (An Ongoing Possibility) While the blanket immigration travel ban was suspended a few years ago to ease the burden on young graduates, PTPTN reserves the right to re-enact travel restrictions for chronic defaulters. Don't risk getting stopped at KLIA on your way to a holiday or an overseas work trip. FAQs About PTPTN Q: Can I get my PTPTN loan waived if I graduate with First Class Honours? A: Yes! PTPTN still offers a loan-to-scholarship conversion (exemption from repayment) for students who graduate with First Class Honours. However, this is subject to specific criteria, such as graduating within the prospective time frame and applying within 12 months of your graduation date. Q: Can I use my EPF savings to pay off my PTPTN loan? A: Yes, you can. Under the revised EPF structure, you can make withdrawals from your Akaun Sejahtera (Account 2) to pay off your own PTPTN loan or even your children's PTPTN loans. This is a great way to settle your debt without affecting your monthly cash flow. Q: Is there a grace period before I have to start paying back? A: Yes. PTPTN gives you a 12-month grace period after you complete your studies before you are required to start making repayments. This timeline gives you enough buffer to secure a stable job first. Q: How do I easily manage and track my PTPTN repayments? A: You can download the official MyPTPTN app on your smartphone. It allows you to check your outstanding balance, make direct payments via FPX, set up direct debits, and even open or top up your SSPN savings accounts. Summary: The TL;DR on PTPTN - Unbeatable Interest Rates: At a 1% flat rate, PTPTN is still the cheapest and most accessible study loan in Malaysia. - CCRIS is Real: Failing to pay back your PTPTN loan will ruin your credit score, making it impossible to buy a car or a home in the future. - Repayment is Flexible: You can use your EPF Akaun Sejahtera to make lump-sum payments. - Strive for the Best: Aiming for a First Class Honours degree can completely wipe out your debt. Conclusion Is PTPTN still the best study loan for Malaysian students? Yes, absolutely. No commercial bank in Malaysia can match its 1% administrative fee, nor do they offer loan waivers for high-achieving students. Just remember: PTPTN is a revolving fund. When you pay back your loan, you are directly funding the education of the next generation of Malaysian students. Take charge of your finances, make your repayments on time, and build a strong financial foundation for your adult life. Taking proactive steps now will set you up for a much brighter financial future.

title: 'Batu Kawan’s Takeover of MKH Crosses 95%
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 30): Batu Kawan Bhd’s (KL:BKAWAN) unconditional mandatory takeover of MKH Bhd (KL:MKH) has crossed the 95% threshold, paving the way for the property developer’s delisting. As at market close on Wednesday, Batu Kawan and its wholly owned unit Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd, together with parties acting in concert, held 548.85 million MKH shares, representing a 95.16% stake, according to a statement issued on their behalf by Maybank Investment Bank Bhd. With the offeror having received valid acceptances of not less than nine-tenths in the nominal value of the offer shares, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will invoke Section 222(1) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 to compulsorily acquire the remaining MKH shares from dissenting shareholders, the statement said. The takeover offer, it said, will remain open until Oct 8, following an extension from the original Sept 17 closing date. Bursa Malaysia Securities will suspend trading of MKH shares upon the expiry of five market days from Oct 8. Thereafter, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will procure MKH to take the necessary steps to withdraw its listing status from Bursa Malaysia. Two weeks ago, minority shareholders of MKH and its separately listed plantation arm, MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd (KL:MKHOP), were given contrasting recommendations regarding Batu Kawan's dual takeover play. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, the independent adviser appointed by MKH, deemed the RM2 cash buyout “not fair but reasonable”, noting that the offer price undervalues the property developer’s fair asset worth. On the other hand, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd urged MKH Oil Palm shareholders to reject the related 66.26 sen per share buyout offer, labelling it "not fair and not reasonable". Mainstreet emphasised that the offer represents a steep 47% discount to MKH Oil Palm's net asset value, and noted that Batu Kawan intends to maintain the plantation unit's listing. The takeover was initiated in May, when Batu Kawan, through Whitmore, agreed to acquire a combined 47.7% stake in MKH from members of the Chen family for RM549.8 million, or RM2 per share. The RM2 offer valued the total cost of taking MKH private at up to RM1.15 billion, including the initial stake purchase. Batu Kawan's share price closed unchanged at RM20.52 on Wednesday, with a market capitalisation of RM8.2 billion. MKH also settled unchanged at RM1.99 with a market value of RM1.17 billion, while MKH Oil Palm closed unchanged at 64.5 sen, valuing the group at RM660 million. full_text: 'Batu Kawan’s Takeover of MKH Crosses 95%. 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 30): Batu Kawan Bhd’s (KL:BKAWAN) unconditional mandatory takeover of MKH Bhd (KL:MKH) has crossed the 95% threshold, paving the way for the property developer’s delisting. As at market close on Wednesday, Batu Kawan and its wholly owned unit Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd, together with parties acting in concert, held 548.85 million MKH shares, representing a 95.16% stake, according to a statement issued on their behalf by Maybank Investment Bank Bhd. With the offeror having received valid acceptances of not less than nine-tenths in the nominal value of the offer shares, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will invoke Section 222(1) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 to compulsorily acquire the remaining MKH shares from dissenting shareholders, the statement said. The takeover offer, it said, will remain open until Oct 8, following an extension from the original Sept 17 closing date. Bursa Malaysia Securities will suspend trading of MKH shares upon the expiry of five market days from Oct 8. Thereafter, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will procure MKH to take the necessary steps to withdraw its listing status from Bursa Malaysia. Two weeks ago, minority shareholders of MKH and its separately listed plantation arm, MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd (KL:MKHOP), were given contrasting recommendations regarding Batu Kawan's dual takeover play. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, the independent adviser appointed by MKH, deemed the RM2 cash buyout “not fair but reasonable”, noting that the offer price undervalues the property developer’s fair asset worth. On the other hand, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd urged MKH Oil Palm shareholders to reject the related 66.26 sen per share buyout offer, labelling it "not fair and not reasonable". Mainstreet emphasised that the offer represents a steep 47% discount to MKH Oil Palm's net asset value, and noted that Batu Kawan intends to maintain the plantation unit's listing. The takeover was initiated in May, when Batu Kawan, through Whitmore, agreed to acquire a combined 47.7% stake in MKH from members of the Chen family for RM549.8 million, or RM2 per share. The RM2 offer valued the total cost of taking MKH private at up to RM1.15 billion, including the initial stake purchase. Batu Kawan's share price closed unchanged at RM20.52 on Wednesday, with a market capitalisation of RM8.2 billion. MKH also settled unchanged at RM1.99 with a market value of RM1.17 billion, while MKH Oil Palm closed unchanged at 64.5 sen, valuing the group at RM660 million. title: 'Former UiTM Holdings CEO Charged With CBT of Misappropriating RM37 Mil
body: 'SHAH ALAM (Oct 1): A former chief executive officer of UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UHSB) has been charged with criminal breach of trust (CBT) for misappropriating RM37.4 million earmarked for solar power development. Azlizan Fadzil, who was in court in a wheelchair due to his stroke, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial before Sessions Court judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. The 52-year-old is accused of misappropriating RM37.4 million by making payments other than for the specified purpose of investment in a large-scale 50MW solar photovoltaic power generation development in Gambang, Pahang. The alleged offence took place between February and October 2017. The single charge is framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code and carries a penalty of imprisonment for a term between two to 20 years, whipping and a fine. UHSB is the wholly owned investment holding company of Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), generating wealth and creating commercial investment opportunities for the institute of higher learning. The court set bail at RM50,000 with two sureties, with additional conditions for the accused to report to authorities once every three months and not to disturb potential prosecution witnesses. Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Law Chin How proposed RM100,000 bail, citing the large sum involved, UiTM's reputation at stake and its high-profile nature which involves leakages of public funds. Defence counsel Hasshahari Johari Mawi asked for a lower bail of RM20,000 as his client has no independent income and is fully dependent on his wife and family. The lawyer added that the wife has to also care for seven children aged between 14 and 21 years old, who are all still schooling. Hasshahari also added that his client suffers from cognitive impairment and is not a flight risk. He added that his client has also been cooperative with authorities in their investigations. The case comes up for mention on Nov 3. title: 'TNB share price up on Kenyir project's outlook
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd's share price rose in early trading on Friday with its Kenyir Hydrogen Hybrid Fuel System (HHFS) project expected to generate a high single-digit equity internal rate of return. As at 9.57 am, TNB's share price rose eight sen to RM12.98 with 889,300 shares traded. According to MBSB Investment Bank (MBSB IB), electricity demand is also expected to remain strong, with growth projected at 5.4 per cent in calendar year 2026. "We continue to view TNB as a key beneficiary and enabler of Malaysia's energy transition, supported by rising regulated grid capex, growing battery energy storage system requirements and sizeable renewable energy opportunities through initiatives such as HHFS. As such, MBSB IB has maintained its "Buy" recommendation on TNB, with an unchanged discounted cash flow (DCF)-derived target price of RM16.31. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has also maintained its "Buy" recommendation, with an unchanged DCF-based target price of RM15.90.

title: 'DNB completes RM5.2bil financing to support next phase of 5G growth
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2bil syndicated Islamic term financing, strengthening its long-term funding position as Malaysia moves into the next phase of its dual 5G network framework. In a statement, DNB said the financing will facilitate the planned exit of Minister of Finance Inc (MOF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder and the transition to equal ownership among its mobile network operator shareholders, namely CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd. The ownership transition is expected in the early fourth quarter of 2026, while MOF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests. The syndicated financing also includes the refinancing of DNB's government-guaranteed revolving credit facility, which expired on Sept 29, and establishes a longer-term funding structure to support the company's growth. DNB said the completion of the financing coincided with the award of the full 100 MHz of the 3.3–3.4 GHz spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240 MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. The assignment by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) takes effect from Oct 1. DNB said the 240 MHz spectrum block would enhance network capacity, efficiency and performance and support technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and artificial intelligence-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said the financing would provide DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently while continuing to invest in network enhancement and capacity expansion. “The successful completion of this RM5.2bil financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy,” he said. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger for the financing. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd were joint mandated lead arrangers, while AmInvestment Bank was DNB's financial adviser.

title: 'DNB lengkapkan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion bagi menyokong fasa seterusnya pertumbuhan 5G | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) melengkapkan pembiayaan berjangka Islam secara sindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan pembiayaan jangka panjang syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa pertumbuhan seterusnya dwirangkaian 5G . DNB dalam kenyataan berkata pembiayaan itu akan memudahkan perancangan keluar Menteri Kewangan Diperbadankan (MOF Inc) sebagai pemegang saham biasa dan peralihan kepada pemilikan sama rata dalam kalangan pemegang saham pengendali rangkaian mudah alihnya, iaitu CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd. Peralihan pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026, manakala MOF Inc akan mengekalkan saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan negara. Pembiayaan berkenaan turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula kemudahan kredit pusingan DNB yang dijamin kerajaan dan tamat tempoh pada 29 September, selain mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang bagi menyokong pertumbuhan syarikat. Penyempurnaan pembiayaan itu bertepatan dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100MHz dalam jalur 3.3–3.4GHz serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum 240MHz DNB kepada penetapan spektrum. Penetapan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober. Menurut DNB, blok spektrum 240MHz tersebut akan meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, selain menyokong teknologi termasuk Massive MIMO, pengagregatan pembawa, 5G Advanced dan keupayaan rangkaian dipacu kecerdasan buatan. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif DNB, Datuk Azman Ismail berkata pembiayaan berkenaan menyediakan platform mampan untuk syarikat beroperasi secara bebas sambil meneruskan pelaburan dalam peningkatan rangkaian dan peluasan kapasiti. “Penyempurnaan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion ini merupakan pencapaian penting bagi DNB dan mencerminkan keyakinan kukuh terhadap asas perniagaan, rekod operasi serta peranan jangka panjang kami dalam ekonomi digital Malaysia,” katanya. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bertindak sebagai pengatur utama yang diberi mandat, pengurus buku dan pengatur penyelaras bagi pembiayaan itu. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd dan United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd pula merupakan pengatur utama bersama yang diberi mandat, manakala AmInvestment Bank bertindak sebagai penasihat kewangan DNB. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Banking Sectors Funding Conundrum
body: 'The local banking sector remains fundamentally sound, supported by robust business lending, comfortable liquidity and healthy asset quality, but a widening gap between loan and deposit growth is beginning to put pressure on funding costs and could slow the recovery in net interest margins, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest banking sector review, CIMB maintained its Overweight stance, saying system loan growth accelerated to 5.7% year-on-year in August 2026, while deposit growth lagged at 4.2%.  The divergence reflects increasingly strong corporate credit demand as Malaysia’s investment cycle gathers momentum. Business loans expanded 6.8% year-on-year, compared with 5% growth in household lending, while business lending including development financial institutions grew 8%.  CIMB said the pattern suggests credit growth is increasingly being driven by investment, corporate expansion and working-capital requirements rather than household leverage.  Business loan applications rose 5.5% year-on-year in August while approvals jumped 30.9%, contrasting with declines of 5.1% and 10.4%, respectively, for household applications and approvals.  Funding Costs Becoming The Key Constraint  While credit demand remains healthy, CIMB said banks are increasingly contending with more expensive funding.  The ex-foreign currency loan-to-deposit ratio stood at 100.8%, while wider interbank money-market spreads and recent tightening in system liquidity are keeping marginal funding costs elevated.  This could limit the extent to which banks can rebuild net interest margins (NIMs) despite continued loan growth.  The composition of deposit growth also points to pressure beneath the surface. Islamic Tawarruq fixed deposits and wholesale deposits are becoming more important funding sources, but CIMB estimates these can cost 130 to 170 basis points more than conventional fixed deposits.  CASA deposits remained a positive factor, rising 7.9% year-on-year, helped by a 12% increase in business CASA. However, conventional fixed deposits declined 1.4%.  Liquidity, Asset Quality Still Healthy  Despite tighter funding conditions, CIMB said the banking system is not facing an immediate liquidity problem.  The system liquidity coverage ratio remained comfortable at 145.9% in August, although it eased from 148.7% in July. Islamic banks recorded a lower average of about 134%, a trend CIMB said warrants monitoring rather than representing an immediate concern.  Asset quality also remains broadly sound.  The gross impaired loan ratio edged up to 1.44% from 1.43%, while household and business impaired loan ratios remained relatively low at 1.11% and 1.92%, respectively. Loan-loss reserve coverage stood at 125.1%.  CIMB nevertheless observed rising impaired balances in selected segments including passenger vehicles, wholesale trade, retail and services, and transportation and storage.  It does not yet view those increases as evidence of broad deterioration, citing stable employment, contained inflation and ongoing investment as supportive of repayment conditions.  Capital Strength Offers Buffer  CIMB said Malaysian banks remain well positioned to withstand a more volatile global rate environment, backed by a Common Equity Tier 1 ratio of 14.1%, adequate liquidity, strong reserves and earnings visibility.  The research house also expects stronger capital positions, Basel 3.1-related benefits and balance-sheet optimisation to create greater scope for dividends and other capital returns.  For 2026, 2027 and 2028, CIMB forecasts domestic loan growth of 5.1%, 5.2% and 5.2%, respectively, while sector NIM is expected to remain broadly flat at around 2%. It projects banking sector core net profit growth of 2.9% in 2026, 5.5% in 2027 and 5.3% in 2028.  Its preferred banking stocks are Public Bank, RHB Bank and Hong Leong Bank, citing their capital return potential, dividend prospects and earnings resilience.  Overall, CIMB sees a banking system that remains healthy and profitable, but where the challenge is shifting from credit demand to funding economics: loan growth is strong, asset quality remains manageable and capital is ample, but competition for deposits and greater reliance on higher-cost funding are increasingly constraining margin expansion.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia gains on Wall Street lead as weak US payrolls temper Fed rate hike expectations - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday, tracking Wall Street’s gains after softer US payroll growth eased expectations of an immediate Federal Reserve rate increase. At 9.10 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 5.01 points, or 0.31 per cent, to 1,635.88 from last Friday’s close of 1,630.87. The index opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42. On the broader market, gainers surpassed losers 224 to 158, with 337 counters unchanged, 2,054 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover stood at 206.30 million shares worth RM98.78 million. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year yield remained elevated at 5.28 per cent and Brent crude oil settled at US$102.25 per barrel, keeping sentiment sensitive to interest rates and West Asia developments. “Over in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index slipped below 24,000 as financial and technology shares weakened. “Back home, following FBM KLCI’s higher close last Friday, we anticipate tentative stabilisation within 1,625-1,635 today, with bargain hunting offering some support amid a cautious market undertone,” he told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB and Tenaga Nasional gained four sen each to RM10.06, RN4.70, RM7.69, and RM13.00, while IHH Healthcare decreased six sen to RM7.74. In active trade, VS Industry added three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTec increased four sen to 74.5 sen, GB Bond inched up half-a-sen to 23.5 sen, SFP Tech gained a sen to 28.5 sen, while Dagang NeXchange was flat at 51.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Samaiden put on 19 sen to RM3.03, UWC was 16 sen firmer at RM7.73, Critical Holdings perked up 15 sen to RM2.61, Mi Technovation strengthened nine sen to RM5.30, and Solarvest advanced eight sen to RM4.25. Nestle led the decliners, falling 32 sen to RM89.20, while Vitrox eased 14 sen to RM10.32, Kobay Technology was 12 sen lower at RM2.18, Kelington shed five sen to RM8.58, and YTL Power International edged down four sen to RM5.64. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 28.14 points to 17,510.07, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 33.81 points to 12,204.38, the FBM Top 100 Index widened 32.24 points to 11,989.92, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 22.28 points to 12,082.60, and the FBM ACE Index improved 31.41 points to 5,560.87. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index inched up 0.59 of-a-point to 179.11, the Energy Index gained 2.57 points to 835.60, the Financial Services Index jumped 97.59 points to 19,138.10, and the Plantation Index gained 2.23 points to 9,058.78. — Bernama

title: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp
body: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Asteel Group Bhd (KL:ASTEEL) has appointed former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman and new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong as executive deputy chairman. The boardroom reshuffle follows Clifford securing a 53.08% stake in Asteel at the closing of a mandatory offer on Monday via investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd. Clifford emerged as Asteel’s controlling shareholder in August with the acquisition of an initial 52.94% stake in the company via a RM20.75 million cash deal at 7.5 sen apiece. This triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06% stake in Asteel, also at 7.5 sen apiece. Clifford, 43, the son of the journalist-turned-businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, who is the founder and executive chairman of property developer HCK Capital Group Bhd (KL:HCK) and group managing director and major shareholder of private education group SEG International. Clement is also the founder of Gambit Group Sdn Bhd, whose subsidiaries are involved in information technology services, investment, business management consultancy and is a registered digital asset custodian under the Securities Commission Malaysia. Clifford, a former non-independent, non-executive director at HCK Capital, has more than 20 years of experience in the education, property and financial technology sectors. He had held senior management and board positions covering corporate strategy, business development, corporate deals and investments, corporate governance and project management. Razarudin, 63, who is also independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd (KL:ADVCON), brings more than four decades of experience in national security and law enforcement. He was Malaysia’s 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. His previous positions include independent director of Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, chief executive officer and executive director of Canadia Bank PLC in Cambodia, group CEO of EON Bank Bhd, director of banking solutions at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, group head of consumer banking at RHB Bank Bhd and managing director of consumer banking at DBS Bank Ltd. At Tuesday's market close, Asteel shares rose a sen or 10.5% to 10.5 sen, valuing the group at RM50.9 million. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth.  In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding.  The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL: CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL: YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026.  Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters.  DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment.  The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.  DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities.  Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets.  DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider.  In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026.  Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing.

title: 'MARC Ratings Affirms PNB Merdeka Ventures’ Sukuk Rating - MARC
body: 'MARC Ratings has affirmed the rating of AAAIS on PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Berhad’s (PNBMV) Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah Programme of up to RM6.0 billion with a stable outlook. The affirmed rating is equalised with the AAA/Stable corporate credit rating of Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) which is based on publicly available information. The rating equalisation is premised on the unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee from PNB to cover any shortfall in principal repayments and profit payments on the Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah. PNBMV is wholly owned by PNB and was set up to undertake the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in the vicinity of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara in Kuala Lumpur. The development comprises several components, chiefly the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank (formerly known as Menara Merdeka 118), a single tower with 84 floors of office space, a 17-floor luxury hotel and a three-floor observation deck. Adjacent to the tower are a seven-floor retail mall which is expected to open in November 2026, and sites earmarked for the future construction of two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. PNBMV has leased the entire 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement. PNB undertakes all property-related expenses, including quit rent, insurance and repair costs, in addition to the monthly net rental and service charge. PNBMV is therefore not exposed to the occupancy risks or other risks associated with the office component of the tower. As at date, about 70% of the 1.6 million sq ft of net lettable area (NLA) of the office tower has been sub-leased: 40% or 33 floors to Maybank, 20% to PNB, and about 10% to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to increase to approximately 90% over the next five years. The office tower is expected to generate an annual net property income of around RM137.0 million. The rating equalisation is premised on the unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee from PNB to cover any shortfall in principal repayments and profit payments on the Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah. PNBMV is wholly owned by PNB and was set up to undertake the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in the vicinity of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara in Kuala Lumpur. The development comprises several components, chiefly the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank (formerly known as Menara Merdeka 118), a single tower with 84 floors of office space, a 17-floor luxury hotel and a three-floor observation deck. Adjacent to the tower are a seven-floor retail mall which is expected to open in November 2026, and sites earmarked for the future construction of two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. PNBMV has leased the entire 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement. PNB undertakes all property-related expenses, including quit rent, insurance and repair costs, in addition to the monthly net rental and service charge. title: 'MGS sell-off set to hit RHB's Q3 earnings: HLIB
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd's near-term earnings are likely to come under pressure from higher Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields, said Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research. Analyst Raymond Ng said the recent spike in MGS yields would likely hurt trading income in the third quarter of financial year 2026 (Q3 FY26), with limited time left in the quarter for a recovery. He said stronger contributions from wealth management, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, broking and loan-related fees should provide some cushion but are unlikely to fully offset the trading income weakness. "The impact should be viewed more as foregone trading upside rather than outsized losses, given RHB's relatively small trading book," he said in a note. Ng said RHB's treasury division had also been tactically unwinding securities positions, crystallising gains where possible while reducing exposure. However, the bank's management remained more positive on the fourth quarter, with scope to reposition the portfolio and capture opportunities if bond yields stabilise or retreat. Despite the near-term earnings pressure, management maintained its return on equity (ROE) target of 10.8 per cent to 11 per cent, supported by about six per cent loan growth, cost growth of no more than one per cent and benign credit costs. Ng said the target remained within reach, although RHB was more likely to end up at the lower end of the range. Credit costs are tracking at around 13 basis points, at the lower end of management's 13 to 14 basis points guidance, while wealth sales rose 35 per cent year-on-year as of June 2026. On asset quality, Ng said there were no major red flags, with deterioration in the small and medium enterprise (SME) segment remaining gradual and manageable. "Gross impaired loan formation continues to stem largely from SME and community banking, although management has not seen a meaningful acceleration in stress," he said. He added that RHB remained selective in mortgage and SME lending and was not chasing growth through aggressive pricing where risk-adjusted returns were unattractive. Meanwhile, capital management remains a medium-term catalyst, with management targeting greater clarity on its capital and dividend policy by the first quarter of 2027. Ng said a potential 100-basis-point uplift in RHB's common equity tier-one ratio following the Basel III reforms in January 2028 could translate into about RM2 billion of additional capital. However, any excess capital return would depend on the group's growth requirements and ability to maintain its CET1 ratio at around current levels. HLIB maintained its "Hold" call on RHB with an unchanged target price of RM8, based on an implied 1.0 times the calendar year 2027 price-to-book ratio. RHB currently offers a projected FY27 dividend yield of more than 6.5 per cent, while a potential increase in the overnight policy rate from 2.75 per cent to three per cent in 2027 could provide another earnings boost.

title: 'Import Duty On Minted Gold Bars Drops To 0% From 1 November 2026
body: 'Small gold bars of 1g, 5g, or 10g have become a common way for people to put money aside a little at a time. Since 8 June 2026, though, anyone buying imported minted bars may have been paying for a 10% import duty included in the price. The Customs Duties (Amendment) Order 2026, P.U. (A) 350, cuts that duty from 10% to 0% from 1 November 2026. Gold Bars Covered By The Cut The cut applies to minted (stamped) gold bars, the small bars people buy to save. The most common sizes are 1g to 50g. The duty only ever applied to imported bars, so bars minted in Malaysia were never taxed and their prices have no duty to lose. Bank Muamalat sells imported bars, and it told customers in May that these bars would cost more once the duty applied. According to Tomei Consolidated group managing director Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, large cast bars, which weigh 1kg and up and are used by manufacturers, are classed differently and were already duty-free. Jewellery isn’t affected either. So this matters to you if you buy imported minted bars, or if you convert gold in your account into an imported physical bar. Possible Savings On An Imported Bar The duty is 10% of what a bar is worth when it arrives in Malaysia. So a bar worth RM100 costs the seller RM110 once the duty is added. When the duty is removed, RM110 drops back to RM100. That’s a saving of RM10 out of RM110, or about 9.1% off what the seller paid for the bar. On 5 October, Bank Muamalat sold a gold bar at RM605.02 a gram and gold in its account at RM584.53 a gram, according to its own price board. If the account price has no duty in it, the RM20.49 difference is the most the duty could be adding to each gram of the bar. The table below shows what that means for each bar size Bank Muamalat sells. RinggitPlus worked out these amounts using Bank Muamalat’s bar and account prices on 5 October 2026. Prices will change with the gold price. The real saving will be less than this, because part of the difference pays for making and packaging the bar, and that cost stays. Buying Now Or Waiting Until November If you buy gold every month through a gold account or gold savings plan, you probably don’t need to change anything. The Malaysia Gold Association’s president, Datuk Seri Louis Ng, said in September that the duty applies to minted bars in finished, packaged form, and not to kilobars and cast bars. So gold held in an account may not be affected, but check with your bank. If you’re planning to buy an imported minted bar in October, ask the seller two things. Did they pay the import duty on this bar, and will the price change after 1 November? Then work out how much more the bar costs than the seller’s gold account price, per gram. Do this now, and then again in the first week of November. If that difference shrinks, the duty removal has made the bar cheaper. If it doesn’t, any price drop is just the gold price moving. Do note that some sellers have already paid the duty on bars they have in stock now. They may keep their prices the same until those bars are sold, so prices may not drop straight away on 1 November. The gold price also changes every day. If the gold price goes up in November, it could cancel out what you save from the duty removal. Waiting makes the most sense if you were already planning to buy a 50g or 100g bar, and the seller confirms the duty is included in its price. Gold doesn’t earn interest, and gold accounts aren’t protected by PIDM the way savings accounts are. If you’re looking at gold accounts, see how Maybank Islamic’s MIGA-i works.
