description: 'FBM KLCI hits a 42-week low amid foreign outflows and oil pressures as markets cautiously await Budget 2027, global inflation data, and Fed policy updates.
full_text: 'Weekly Strategy - 5 Oct 2026. 'The FBM KLCI came under significant selling pressure last week, falling to a 42-week low of 1,630 and marking a fresh 2026 low amid persistent foreign fund outflows. Investor sentiment was further weighed down by rising U.S. Treasury yields and concerns over higher borrowing costs, while heightened geopolitical uncertainty surrounding the U.S.-Iran conflict raised concerns over its potential inflationary impact. Although bargain hunting provided intermittent support following the sharp sell-off, recovery attempts lacked momentum and proved short-lived amid continued caution. Consequently, the benchmark index ended the week firmly in negative territory. Week-on-week, the FBM KLCI plunged 40.75 points, or 2.44 percent to 1,630.87, as falls on Sunway Bhd (-33sen), KLK (-RM1.52), Petronas Chemicals (-28sen), RHB Bank (-36sen) and 99 Speed Mart (-14sen) offset gains on Gamuda (+22sen), Axiata (+1sen) and Tenaga (+7sen). Average daily traded volume last week declined to 3.48 billion shares versus the 3.52 billion shares the previous week, while average daily traded value rose marginally to RM2.89 billion, from the RM2.88 billion average the previous week. Foreign Selling Drags the FBMKLCI Further Below Its August Peak The FBMKLCI enters the week on a fragile footing after closing 7.0% below its August high of 1,753.22 on broad-based selling. Foreign investors remained the main source of pressure. They sold a net RM799.9mn in the week ended 2 October, extending YTD outflows beyond RM6.4bn. However, the coming week carries an unusually dense set of catalysts. Budget 2027 will be tabled on Friday, 9 October. U.S. Treasury yields sit at their highest in more than two decades, and crude oil hovers above USD 100 per barrel. President Trump has said the war will not end before the 3 November midterm elections. The U.S. is also reportedly deploying up to 10,000 troops, along with ships and aircraft carriers, to the region. As such, pressure on oil prices is unlikely to ease soon. Budget 2027 and Melaka Polls Dominate Domestic News Flow Budget 2027 on 9 October is the week's key domestic catalyst. We forecast another expansionary Budget of RM438.9bn (+3.7%), with development expenditure directed towards infrastructure, renewable energy and digitalisation. Revenue is projected at RM363.5bn (+4.9%), lowering the fiscal deficit to 3.3%, which continues the narrowing trend from 3.7% of GDP in 2025 and 3.5% in 2026. Investors will look for three things. First, a credible consolidation path despite higher oil-linked subsidy costs. Second, the scale of development spending, which drives contract flow. Third, any changes to targeted fuel subsidies under BUDI95, or new revenue measures. Politics also return to focus. The Election Commission meets on 7 October to set nomination and polling dates for the Melaka state election, following the assembly's dissolution on 18 September. The result will be read as an early test of voter sentiment ahead of GE16. Meanwhile, the 3Q26 results season is approaching. Pre-results positioning is likely to favour companies with pricing power, given the gap between elevated producer prices and tame consumer inflation. We expect the FBMKLCI to trade cautiously in the first half of the week, before Budget positioning lends support. Valuations remain undemanding. The index trades at 13.7x consensus CY27 PER, about 13% below its 15.8x long-term average. Our end-2026 target of 1,730 implies 6.1% upside from the 2 October close. Hence, we view the pullback as an opportunity rather than a warning. Investors should favour defensive and quality names, complemented by growth exposure to Budget themes. Our preferred picks include GAMUDA (BUY, TP:RM5.65), TM (BUY, TP:RM8.80), SIMEPROP (BUY, TP:RM2.10) and NESTLE (BUY, TP:RM128.80). Any weakness around Budget Day or the late-October FOMC meeting should be used to build positions selectively. (Please refer to our Preview of Budget 2027 report “Strengthening Resilience, Sustaining Growth”, which was released on 9 September for details). Industrial Output Data to Test the Export Boom Budget and politics aside, domestic data are light but relevant. The key release is August industrial production (IPI), due at 12.30pm on 9 October, hours before the Budget speech. IPI growth moderated to 4.7% YoY in July from 6.5% in June. Manufacturing (+6.4%) offset a 3.2% contraction in mining, where crude oil output fell 13.1%. We expect August output to firm from July's pace. Exports surged 45.5% YoY to RM191.05bn in August, led by E&E, petroleum products and LNG. Shipments to the U.S. and China also reached record monthly highs. An IPI print above 5% would therefore reinforce our 2026 GDP forecast of 5.1%. Conversely, a print below July's 4.7% would suggest that export strength reflects prices more than volumes. That risk deserves attention, as the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing PMI slipped to 49.9 in September from 50.2. Weak Payrolls Cool Hike Bets; FOMC Minutes Next U.S. data will shape how far the Federal Reserve tightens. The Fed raised rates by 25bps to 3.75–4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, and 16 of 19 policymakers project at least one further hike this year. However, the case for an October move has weakened sharply. August core PCE inflation came in at 3.0% YoY (consensus 3.3%), and several Fed officials struck a dovish tone. Last Friday's payrolls report reinforced that shift. The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September, well short of the Bloomberg survey of 90,000 and below the bottom of the 60,000 to 130,000 forecast range. Revisions also cut a combined 60,000 jobs from July and August, leaving July in contraction (-10,000). Unemployment edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%. Wage pressure eased as well, with average hourly earnings up just 0.1% MoM (3.0% YoY, from 3.1% in August). October hike odds now stand at about 22%, against roughly 70% in late September. With the labour market losing momentum, this week's data will test whether inflation allows the Fed to pause. ISM Services opens the week on 5 October, with Bloomberg forecasts pointing to an easing to about 55.2 from 55.4. Still, the prices component matters more. ISM Manufacturing prices surged to 77.9 in September from 71.1, even as the headline missed (54.5 vs 55.0 expected). The FOMC minutes on 7 October will show how many members favoured a faster pace. Finally, the University of Michigan survey on 9 October will be watched for inflation expectations, after the one-year gauge rose to 4.6% in September. A firm reading on prices would keep a further hike in play before year-end. Conversely, softer prices would support the view that September marked the last move of this cycle. China Returns From Golden Week With Firmer PMIs China's mainland markets are closed from 1 to 7 October for the National Day holiday and reopen on 8 October. No major Chinese data are scheduled this week, as September CPI and PPI follow on 14 October. Still, investors will digest the September PMIs released before the break. The official manufacturing PMI returned to expansion at 50.1 (consensus 50.1; August 49.8). The non-manufacturing PMI beat expectations at 50.2 (consensus 49.3; August 49.0), while the private RatingDog manufacturing PMI rose to a five-month high of 52.1 (consensus 51.6). This is encouraging after 2Q26 GDP growth eased to 4.3% YoY. However, the gap between the official and private readings leaves the strength of the recovery open to debate. Early Golden Week figures point to firm travel demand. Rail trips hit a record 25.2mn on 1 October, and Macau visitor arrivals rose 22.3% YoY on the first day. Spending data will matter more. Soft spending would revive concern over China's 4.5– 5.0% growth target. Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) said its wholly-owned Indonesian unit, PT Perindustrian Sawit Synergi (PT PSS), has received the arbitral award in a dispute involving the termination of a gas supply agreement. The award is not expected to have any material impact on the group’s earnings, net assets or gearing for FY26. KLK said that while the arbitration proceeding was ongoing, PT PSS and PT GN concurrently engaged in mediation process to explore an amicable resolution of the dispute. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Gas Malaysia Bhd (Not Rated) aims to make a final investment decision on plans for its first regasification terminal by the 2HCY27. The facility to be built in Yan, Kedah, is due to come online by the end of 2030. The proposed terminal, announced in March, is being jointly developed with Japan's Tokyo Gas and Dutch group VTTI at an estimated cost of between RM2.0bn and RM3.0bn (US$490.0mn to US$735.0mn). (The Edge) Mah Sing Group Bhd has signed a collaboration term sheet with Kinergy Advancement Bhd (Not Rated) to provide technical advisory and evaluate power infrastructure for its proposed data centre developments. Mah Sing entered into the non-binding and nonexclusive agreement with Kinergy to assess captive power plant options and Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme frameworks for its sites at Southville City in Bangi, Selangor, and Meridin East in Pasir Gudang, Johor. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Samaiden Group Bhd’s wholly owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd has secured contracts from Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd to undertake engineering, construction and commissioning works, including the supply of solar components, for a 99.99 megawatts alternating current (MWac) large-scale solar photovoltaic plant. The contracts’ value or location of the proposed facility was not disclosed. (Bursa Malaysia/The Star) Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd, part of Berjaya Corporation Bhd (Not Rated), said the enforcement on its properties by Pahang authorities was “unconscionable and totally unacceptable”. The action, taken amid dispute over a sharp jump in quit rent, was also “unreasonable” and impinges on Berjaya Hills’ legitimate expectation to carry on its business and operations in a peaceful manner. The group has secured an interim stay from the court and is seeking leave from the Federal Court to argue its case. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will suspend MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd (Not Rated), both under MYEG Group, as its collection agents effective 12.01am next Monday. JPJ said the decision was made after taking into account the group’ compliance with the terms and conditions of their agreements, as well as outstanding obligations that have yet to be fulfilled or settled. (Bursa Malaysia/New Straits Times) Seal Incorporated Bhd’s (Not Rated) non-interested shareholders are advised to vote in favour of providing associate company MSR Green Energy Sdn Bhd (MSRGE) a corporate guarantee of RM58.7mn to help it complete several solar projects. UOB Kay Hian, its independent adviser, highlighted that the corporate guarantee allows MSRGE to obtain and utilise vital banking facilities without direct cash or equity injections from Seal, thereby preserving the group's working capital. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Inta Bina Bhd has launched its second property development project, a 499-unit serviced apartment project in Bukit Jelutong, Shah Alam, with a projected gross development value of RM291.0mn. The development will comprise two residential blocks, commercial space and supporting facilities. Construction will take 36 months to complete. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Adnex Group Bhd's (Not Rated) has secured a contract from Bursa Malaysia Bhd for refurbishment works at its Exchange Square main building. The RM14.2mn contract, accepted on 2 October 2026, covers refurbishment works at levels six, 14 and 15 of the building. The works are expected to take three months and are targeted for completion in 4QCY26. (Bursa Malaysia/New Straits Times) PMCK Bhd (Not Rated) has proposed to diversify into the import and supply of medical consumable products by acquiring Derberg Sdn Bhd and Marpoliq Sdn Bhd for RM52.8m in cash. PMCK will fund the purchase through a combination of bank borrowings and internal funds. This includes a RM5.3mn deposit, RM41.5mn payable upon completion, and a further RM6.0mn that will only be paid if the companies meet the agreed profit targets for FY27 and FY28. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) TXCD Bhd (Not Rated) has secured a RM110.0mn subcontract from Vestland Bhd (Not Rated) to build a 62-storey Sovo commercial development in Section 44, Kuala Lumpur. The contract's value is about 1.8x TXCD’s market capitalisation of RM62.3mn as at Friday’s close. Work has commenced and is slated to end by 31 December 2028. (Bursa Malaysia) DPI Holdings Bhd’s (Not Rated) subsidiary Eastern Forever (Sabah) Sdn Bhd is acquiring a 2.05-acre industrial land in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, for RM7.6mn cash. The vacant industrial lot has a 99-year lease expiring on 31 December 2098. The acquisition is in line with the group’s strategic plans to expand its fast-moving consumer goods distribution network and warehousing capacity in Sabah and East Malaysia, thereby enhancing operational efficiency and market presence in the region. (Bursa Malaysia/The Star) Country Heights Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) said its 80.9%-owned subsidiary Golden Horse Palace Bhd has been served with a winding-up petition over two outstanding Industrial Court awards involving RM312,653. GHPB operates the luxury Palace of the Golden Horses hotel at The Mines. It is a major subsidiary of Country Heights, in which the group’s total investment stands at about RM219.0mn. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Meridian Bhd's (Not Rated) auditors are doubting survival of the group, drawing attention to multiple material uncertainties and missing accounting records. UHY Malaysia PLT issued a ‘disclaimer of opinion’ in its report on Meridian, meaning that they refused to vouch for the accuracy of the financial statements prepared, and flagged the group’s ability to continue as a ‘going concern’ and to remain afloat. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) The Securities Commission Malaysia has approved construction firm Lim Seong Hai Capital Bhd’s (Not Rated) transfer of its listing to the Main Market from the ACE Market. The slated transfer comes a year and a half after LSH transitioned from the LEAP Market in March 2025. It was listed on the LEAP Market in July 2021. (The Edge) PETRONAS Chemicals Group Bhd announced on 2 October 2026 that its chief executive officer Mazuin Ismail will retire effective 1 January 2027. Izwan Ismail, 51, has been appointed to replace him. Mazuin, 58, who also serves as the company’s managing director, assumed the role in January 2024. He has spent his entire 35‑year career within the PETRONAS Group. (The Edge) Malaysia’s semiconductor industry has asked Putrajaya to up reinvestment and research incentives, ease access to skilled foreign talent as well as reduce friction of doing business in Budget 2027 to enable the next phase of growth, as competition for investment intensifies globally. While Malaysia continues to attract significant investments — with RM16.9bn approved investments in the semiconductor subsector in 2025 — the Malaysia Semiconductor Industry Association (MSIA) said rapid developments in artificial intelligence, geopolitical tensions, changing supply chains and competition for investment and talent were increasing pressure on Malaysia to strengthen its semiconductor policies. Malaysia “must respond by strengthening the policy enablers that support long-term industry competitiveness” given rapid advances in artificial intelligence, geopolitical developments, changing global supply chains and intensifying competition for investment and talent are reshaping the global semiconductor landscape, it said. (The Edge) Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain and is ready to expand cooperation in various fields, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said the cooperation would cover healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and smart manufacturing. He said the areas were among those discussed during his meeting with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, who is visiting Malaysia in conjunction with the 2026 Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. “Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain, while Malaysian companies are ready to leverage Bahrain as a gateway to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) market, for the prosperity and well-being of the people of both countries. We also used the meeting to discuss efforts to strengthen Malaysia-Bahrain ties, including expediting senior officials’ consultations to activate the High-Level Joint Committee and strategically advance the bilateral agenda. In line with the aspirations of the Madani Economy and Bahrain Economic Vision 2030, we are committed to expanding cooperation in healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and smart manufacturing,” he said. (The Edge, Bernama) The SME Association of Malaysia (SMEAM) has called on the government to place greater emphasis on the outcomes of its assistance to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Budget 2027, rather than on the amount allocated for various programmes. SMEAM national president Dr Chin Chee Seong said the effectiveness of SME support should be assessed based on whether it leads to measurable improvements in productivity, investment, business growth and competitiveness. At a joint press conference with the Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) on Friday, Chin said grants should be tied to results, such as demonstrable gains in automation or business performance. Instead of providing assistance based solely on eligibility, he suggested that businesses demonstrate improvements in areas such as automation, competitiveness or business performance before receiving support. (The Edge) Malaysian manufacturers must accelerate the adoption of automation to boost productivity and reduce their dependence on foreign labour, said Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin. He said the government has gradually reduced the foreign workforce quota from about 20% previously to 15%. Foreign workers currently account for 13% of the total workforce. The government targets to further reduce this to 10% by 2030. This gradual reduction will give businesses time to do so but it is happening too slowly, he said. “Every sector is being informed about it. Everyone knows it’s going to be difficult. Businesses understand this; we are not reducing it overnight but gradually,” he told reporters after launching the Malaysia Smart Manufacturing Awards (MSMA) 2027. (The Edge, Bernama) Malaysia is still far from achieving its target of transforming 3,000 manufacturers into smart factories by 2030, with only 93 having successfully completed the transformation so far. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said 161 more manufacturers were currently in the process of transformation and were expected to do so by December 2026. “Under our New Industrial Master Plan 2030, we want to achieve 3,000 smart factories, but unfortunately, our take-up rate is still very low. Only 93 have successfully transformed, and 161 on the way by December 2026. So, we are still very far away from 3,000,” he told reporters after the launch of the Malaysia Smart Manufacturing Awards (MSMA) 2027. He said the government was focusing on helping manufacturers that lacked the financial capacity and capabilities to adopt smart manufacturing technologies. (The Star) US manufacturers in Malaysia shift to local suppliers, cut Chinese inputs amid tariffs, survey shows American manufacturers operating in Malaysia are reducing their reliance on Chinese inputs and turning to local suppliers as they adapt to pressure from US tariffs, according to a survey. The American Malaysian Chamber of Commerce’s (AMCHAM) latest Economic Impact Survey found that companies responded to tariff pressure by reorganising their procurement, repricing products and reshaping their workforce, rather than simply absorbing higher costs or pulling out of Malaysia. Of the 21 manufacturers that source inputs from China, none increased their reliance on Chinese suppliers after the tariffs took effect. Meanwhile, nine companies, or 43% of the 21, reduced their reliance on China. These companies are concentrated in electronics manufacturing services and hightechnology hardware, sectors with historically deep supplier linkages to China. Separately, AMCHAM said 15 of the 44 manufacturers surveyed, or 34%, increased the share of their inputs sourced from Malaysia in response to tariff pressure. (The Edge) Japan is no longer experiencing deflation so does not need excessively loose monetary policy for the pursuit of a higher inflation rate, Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said on Friday. Monetary policy decisions are the jurisdiction of the Bank of Japan (BOJ), Kiuchi added, declining to comment on whether the government opposed further central bank interest rate hikes. "Japan has emerged from an era where it needed the kind of reflationist policies taken under Abenomics," Kiuchi said at a regular news conference, adding that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's policies were different from the massive stimulus introduced by the late former prime minister Shinzo Abe in 2013. Kiuchi made the remarks in response to reporters asking about a summary of opinions of the BOJ's September policy meeting, which showed a government representative called for caution over further interest rate hikes. The remarks add to commentary from the government dismissing the viewpoint that it was pursuing reflationist policies to bolster demand through expansionary fiscal and monetary steps. (Reuters) US job growth slowed more than expected in September, but that likely does not signal a material shift in the labour market, with the weakness likely related to a calendar quirk. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs last month after a downwardly revised 133,000 rise in August, the Labour Department's closely watched employment report showed on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls advancing 90,000 after a previously reported 162,000 surge in August. Estimates ranged from as low as 35,000 to as high as 180,000. Volatility linked to seasonal adjustment factors, the model the government uses to strip out seasonal fluctuations from the data, probably accounted for both the meagre payroll gains last month and the downward revision to August's count. (Reuters) Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the recent rise in US Treasury yields was in line with global trends and didn’t warrant consternation, even as worries about persisting price pressures pushed some benchmark rates to their highest in more than two decades. “I would be concerned if we were having some kind of idiosyncratic rise,” Bessent said during an interview with Axios published on Saturday. “We’re not seeing people selling treasuries to buy German bonds or Japanese bonds I can’t control the bond market. What I can do is get people to slow down and think,” he said. Bessent also touted the US financial intervention to rescue Argentina and left the door open to similar rescues in the future. The Trump administration last year bought the peso and provided the government of Javier Milei — a Trump ally — with a US$20bn (RM81.7bn) swap line, which helped Argentina defend its currency and ward off a full-blown economic crisis. (Bloomberg) President Donald Trump said he won’t ban US diesel exports, after Group of Seven nations and their partners agreed to release some of their emergency fuel stockpiles in a bid to bring down soaring prices. “Europe has a lot of diesel and they’re going to be making a major world contribution — and so are we,” Trump told reporters Friday at the White House. “And we’re not going to be doing the export ban.” The bloc, which includes major economies from Europe, North America and Asia, agreed to release as much as 100mn barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks, after an intense pressure campaign from the Trump administration. “I did ask them, and we’re going to have a lot of oil,” Trump added. Trump’s declaration comes amid a record surge in prices for diesel, which fuels much of the modern economy, powering farm equipment, propelling US shipping and supplying heat and power to rural communities. (Bloomberg) New orders for US factory goods barely rose in August as strong demand for electrical equipment, appliances and components was offset by weakness in commercial aircraft orders. Factory orders edged up 0.1% after a downwardly revised 0.8% jump in July, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast orders gaining 0.1% after a previously reported 0.9% rise in July. Orders increased 6.8% on a year-over-year basis in August. Factory orders in August were restrained by a 4.3% drop in orders for civilian aircraft and parts. Orders for motor vehicle bodies, parts and trailers rose 0.8%. Machinery orders soared 1.1%. Orders for computers and electronic products were unchanged but were up 14.7% year over year. Orders for electrical equipment, appliances and components surged 1.1%. (Reuters) President Donald Trump said on Friday that a US trade deal with South Korea now includes US$8.4bn for an oil recovery project. "The Republic of Korea Deal keeps getting BETTER! 8.4bn Dollars for an enhanced Oil Recovery Project. Producing more Oil and Gas means American Energy Dominance and Energy Security in the World for the Future!" Trump wrote on Truth Social. The announcement is the latest in a series of economic and investment deals Trump is highlighting ahead of November's midterm elections, as he seeks to reinforce his economic record amid voter concerns over the Iran war and high gasoline prices. Trump unveiled plans on Wednesday for South Korea to invest some US$200bn in US projects, but Seoul quickly suggested one key element, a US$54bn pipeline for an LNG project in Alaska, was not yet set in stone. Trump said the investment would include the construction of eight large-scale nuclear power plants, a natural gas pipeline and a 6-gigawatt power Generation Facility in Texas. (Reuters) Eurozone inflation surged more than expected in September and is likely to increase further in the coming months on soaring energy costs, keeping pressure on the European Central Bank to raise interest rates and governments to help struggling consumers. Inflation in the 21 nations sharing the euro currency jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2% a month earlier, exceeding expectations for 3.6% in a Reuters poll, driven primarily by fuel, natural gas, and to a lesser extent, food costs. A closely watched 'core' figure, which excludes volatile food and fuel prices and signals underlying trends, accelerated to 2.5% from 2.4%, on a pick-up in services prices, data from Eurostat, the EU's statistics agency, showed on Friday. (Reuters) Opec+ has agreed in principle to keep oil production targets steady for November, three sources close to the matter said ahead of the group's meeting on Sunday. Gulf Opec+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran, with exports fluctuating at 60-80% of normal levels in recent months. The war has also delayed the group's output capacity review — crucial to determine members’ 2027 output quotas — because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources have said. The seven core Opec+ members pumped 25mn barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly five million bpd below prewar levels in February, Opec data shows. (Reuters) World food prices rose in September to their highest in nearly four years as logistics disruptions and weather concerns affected crop markets, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization said. Fears about a severe El Niño weather pattern have pushed international sugar prices to an 18-month high, while a war-related collapse in Black Sea trade pushed wheat futures to a three-year peak early last month. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in international prices for a basket of food commodities, averaged 136.0 points, up from a revised 134.0 for August and the highest reading since November 2022. FAO's benchmarks for cereal, sugar and vegetable oil prices all rose last month, though meat and dairy quotations fell. (Reuters) Governments around the world are running out of room to shield consumers from higher energy prices resulting from the Iran war and other crises, with fuel subsidies potentially costing more than US$1tn this year, a United Nations study found. Global policy interventions to cushion the impact of rising food and energy prices will become more difficult to sustain as a result of higher borrowing costs and what’s on track to be the strongest El Niño on record, according to a UN Development Programme report released Friday. The UNDP warned the next couple of months will be particularly important for governments that have deployed price caps, subsidies and tax rebates as oil near US$100-abarrel and elevated borrowing costs squeeze already strained budgets. “The horizon over the next few weeks and months is uncertain because we don’t see a very clear pathway out of the three-pronged crisis,” said UNDP’s chief economist George Gray Molina, pointing to the Iran war, borrowing costs and the weather phenomenon El Niño. title: 'Markets brace for tighter Fed path: CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Financial markets are pricing a more hawkish US Federal Reserve interest rate path than the latest forecasts from policymakers and economists: This could keep the US dollar supported into 2027, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The firm said markets are pricing about 80 basis points of additional Fed tightening in 2027, equivalent to roughly 3.2 rate hikes. This is in comparison with the latest Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) projections for a 25-basis-point increase in the fourth quarter of 2026 and no further hikes in 2027. The FOMC's latest projection puts the policy rate at 4.25 per cent after the expected fourth-quarter move. CIMB Securities said market forecasts for end-2027 rates remain widely dispersed, ranging from 3.25 per cent to 4.50 per cent, with a median of 3.50 per cent. The firm said near-term upside risks to global energy prices and potential price shocks could keep markets positioned for tighter US monetary policy in the fourth quarter of 2026. It also revised higher its forecasts for US Treasury yields relative to German and Japanese government bonds. CIMB Securities raised its end-2027 two-year US Treasury-Bund and US Treasury-JGB spread assumptions by eight basis points and 15 basis points to about 160 basis points and 270 basis points respectively. title: 'CIMB sees rising odds of BNM rate hike in 1H27
body: 'BANK Negara Malaysia (BNM) is expected to keep the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75% in November, although the probability of a rate hike in the first half of 2027 is increasing if economic growth remains firm and inflation pressures broaden, according to CIMB Treasury and Markets Research.   “We expect a hold in November, but see rising odds of a 25bps rate hike in 1H27 if growth stays firm and inflation broadens,” CIMB said in a report released today. title: 'CARSOME Academy Marks 5 Years with more than RM2 Million in Support to Build Malaysia’s Automotive Talent
body: 'Selangor State Government to continue supporting CARSOME Academy with more than RM350,000 in scholarships for Asnaf and B40 students Partnerships with Maybank Islamic Berhad and JETOUR Automobile Malaysia connect automotive training with industry experience and employment opportunities The Academy launches two new TVET programmes, the first known industry-led programmes of their kind in Malaysia, combining automotive sales expertise with nationally recognised SKM certification  Kuala Lumpur, 24 September 2026 – CARSOME Academy marked its fifth anniversary with more than RM2 million in combined financial support, scholarships and development funding, alongside new partnerships and programmes aimed at preparing Malaysians for careers across the automotive industry.  The milestone brings together support from the Selangor State Government, Maybank Islamic Berhad and industry partner JETOUR Automobile Malaysia, expanding opportunities for Malaysians to gain industry-relevant skills, practical experiences, and access to careers in the automotive industry.  The RM1.65 million Accelerate with TVET Programme, anchored by Maybank Islamic Berhad, alongside matching contributions from Bank Negara Malaysia, CARSOME Academy and Etiqa General Takaful, will provide greater access to industry-relevant technical and vocational education and training.  “TVET is a powerful pathway to equip Malaysians with the practical skills and opportunities they need for the future. To us, Maybank’s Humanising Financial Services means creating opportunities that make a meaningful difference to people and communities. We are proud to partner with CARSOME Academy to expand access to industry-relevant training and strengthen pathways from education to employment. By investing in skills and talent development, we can help build a more inclusive, capable and future-ready workforce, while contributing to a positive and lasting impact for Malaysian society,” said Mohamad Yasin Abdullah, CEO, Maybank Islamic Berhad.  CARSOME Academy and Maybank Islamic Berhad mark their partnership with an MoU, supporting scholarships and greater access to automotive TVET education for aspiring talent. From L-R: ● Eric Cheng, Co-Founder & Group Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME ● Teoh Jiun Ee, CARSOME Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy ● Mohamad Yasin Abdullah, CEO, Maybank Islamic Berhad ● Nur Hidayah Salim, Head, Group Values-Based Centre of Excellence  This is further supported by more than RM350,000 in scholarships from the Selangor State Government through IKTISASS and Yayasan MBI, benefiting Asnaf and B40 students from Selangor.  Speaking at the Academy’s fifth anniversary celebration, Yang Berhormat Tuan Mohd Najwan Bin Halimi, Selangor State Exco for Youth, Sports, and Entrepreneurship, said the Selangor Government would continue to support CARSOME Academy as a homegrown company contributing to the state’s automotive talent and economic development.  Y.B. Tuan Mohd Najwan bin Halimi, Selangor State Exco for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship, delivers his speech at CARSOME Academy’s 5th anniversary celebration and graduation ceremony.  “Selangor will continue to stand with CARSOME Academy. As a company that was born in Selangor, headquartered in Petaling Jaya and committed to training young people in the automotive sector, CARSOME Academy is an important partner in developing the talent that contributes to our state’s economy. The Selangor State Government looks forward to expanding this collaboration,” he said.  CARSOME Group is also contributing an additional RM150,000 towards scholarships, with other funding and development commitments bringing the Academy’s total support to more than RM2 million.  JETOUR Partnership Expands Industry Pathways  Complementing the TVET initiative, CARSOME Academy has signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with JETOUR Automobile Malaysia to create work placement and practical job opportunities for its students and graduates across various areas of the industry, including vehicle inspection, sales, and aftersales.  Through the partnership, CARSOME Academy and JETOUR will work together to structure and develop trainee programmes that give learners hands-on industry experience and opportunities to build their technical skills in real-world automotive settings.  CARSOME Academy and JETOUR Automobile Malaysia formalise their partnership through an MoU to connect automotive TVET training with industry exposure and employment opportunities. From L-R: ● Eric Cheng, Co-Founder & Group Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME ● Teoh Jiun Ee, CARSOME Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy ● Nicholas Ng, Vice President, Jetour Malaysia ● Mohd Azhar, Sales Director, Jetour Malaysia  “Industry exposure is essential in preparing the next generation of automotive talent. As the automotive industry continues to evolve, stronger collaboration between industry and TVET institutions play our part in bridging the gap between education and industry, while providing students with meaningful opportunities to gain real-world experience and insights into the automotive industry,” said Nicholas Ng, Vice President of Jetour Malaysia.  Five Years of Impact and The Road Ahead  Since 2021, 593 students have registered with CARSOME Academy, with 90% securing employment within three months. The Academy has also trained more than 8,000 employees, developed more than 500 leaders and supported 280 scholarship recipients.  Building on this foundation, the Academy is growing its role across the automotive ecosystem through five key pillars spanning vehicle inspection, TVET, corporate training, talent and job matching, and industry partnerships.  This includes two new automotive sales TVET programmes, Certified Sales Professional and Certified Sales Excellence, the first known industry-led TVET programmes of their kind in Malaysia, combining practical automotive sales expertise with nationally recognised SKM certification.  “Five years on, the impact of CARSOME Academy is clear, from building technical capabilities to creating real opportunities for employment. With 593 students trained and 90% securing employment within three months, we have seen first hand how industry-led training can translate into a meaningful career,” said Teoh Jiun Ee, Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy and Co-founder of CARSOME Group.  Teoh Jiun Ee, Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy and Co-founder of CARSOME Group, at CARSOME Academy’s 5th anniversary celebration and first graduation ceremony, shared that since 2021, 593 students have registered with the Academy, with 90% securing employment within three months. The Academy has also trained more than 8,000 employees, developed over 500 leaders and supported 280 scholarship recipients.  “Now, we are taking that further. By expanding into automotive sales and working with partners such as Maybank Islamic and JETOUR, we are connecting more people to the skills, experience and opportunities they need to succeed. As we look to the next five years, our ambition is to keep building a stronger, more future-ready automotive workforce,” he added.  The new programmes mark the Academy’s continued expansion beyond technical training, opening up recognised opportunities in automotive sales while helping employers develop job-ready talent. As it enters its next five years, CARSOME Academy will continue strengthening training and employment initiatives across the automotive ecosystem, connecting people, skills and opportunity to the industry’s evolving talent needs.  Distinguished guests and industry partners join CARSOME Academy in commemorating its 5th anniversary and celebrating the achievements of its graduating students. From L-R: ● Puan Siti Kamariah Ahmad Sukri, Pengarah Urusan Yayasan Hasanah ● Mohamad Yasin Abdullah, CEO, Maybank Islamic Berhad ● Nicholas Ng, Vice President, Jetour Malaysia  ● Y.B. Tuan Mohd Najwan Bin Halimi, Selangor State Exco for Youth, Sports, and Entrepreneurship ● Teoh Jiun Ee, CARSOME Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy ● Eric Cheng, Co-Founder & Group Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME ● Ts. Dr. Wan Nasarudin Bin Wan Jalal, Pengarah Jabatan Pembangunan Kemahiran Wilayah Tengah  For more information please visit CARSOME Academy’s website.  About CARSOME Academy  CARSOME Academy is the automotive education arm of CARSOME and one of Southeast Asia’s leading accredited training institutions for future automotive talent. Accredited by the Department of Skills Development (DSD) and recognised as an HRD Corp training provider, CARSOME Academy offers Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) programmes in Automotive Technology and a variety of upskilling opportunities to support talent development in the automotive sector.  Since its establishment in 2021, CARSOME Academy has trained more than 8,000 students and achieved a 95% job placement rate within three months. Beyond classroom training, CARSOME Academy emphasises holistic development by equipping learners with both technical expertise and essential soft skills to prepare them for long-term success in the automotive industry.  Through collaborations with foundations, government agencies, and community organisations, CARSOME Academy supports accessible education for B40 and underserved communities, with over 90% graduates coming from these backgrounds. By developing skilled, future-ready professionals, CARSOME Academy continues to strengthen the region’s automotive ecosystem.  CARSOME is Southeast Asia’s largest integrated car e-commerce platform. With operations across Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Singapore, CARSOME aims to digitize the region’s used car industry by reshaping and elevating the car transaction and ownership experience.

title: 'Awards offer SMEs a benchmark for growth
body: 'GEORGE TOWN: Business awards can serve as more than recognition, giving small and medium enterprises (SMEs) a benchmark to measure their progress, identify areas for improvement and set targets for the year ahead, said fourth-generation entrepreneur Jonathan Chan Heng Liang. Chan, 34, the fourth-generation successor of Sin Boon Kee Coffee, said the guidelines under the Star Outstanding Business Awards (SOBA) categories provided companies with an indication of where they stood and what they could work towards next. “Joining SOBA is actually kind of one indicator for us, whether we improved since last year, what we are doing in the future and what we are aiming to hit next year. “Winning awards could also generate publicity and give customers greater confidence in a brand,” he said during SOBA Connect Penang at The Ship Campus in Batu Kawan on Sept 29. Organised by Star Media Group (SMG) and themed “Connections That Matter, Strategies That Scale”, the event attracted over 100 business owners, entrepreneurs and industry representatives for discussions on business growth, financing, technology and cybersecurity. Chan’s company, SBK Concept Store Sdn Bhd, received five recognitions at SOBA 2025, including Platinum awards for Best Employer, Best in CSR and Best in Halal Product/Service, Gold for Best Use of Technology and a Meritorious Achievement for Young Entrepreneur of the Year. He was among three speakers in the “Funding Growth: Unlocking Capital” panel, together with RHB Bank Bhd (RHB) SME Product and Programme Lending Management (PLM) development head Ian Chua and National Association of Women Entrepreneurs of Malaysia (Nawem) Penang chairman Bharati Suresh Chand. “Businesses should maintain cash reserves equivalent to three to six months of operating expenses. “This provides an important buffer to help them navigate periods of cash-flow pressure and manage their day-to-day obligations with greater confidence,” said Chua. He added that RHB views itself as a partner to SMEs, offering financing solutions tailored to their evolving business needs, whether to support short-term working capital requirements or longer-term expansion plans. “We see ourselves not just as a financier, but as a partner to SMEs. Whether businesses require short-term working capital to bridge temporary cash-flow gaps or financing to support expansion and asset acquisition, we are committed to providing solutions that meet their specific needs,” he said. The event also covered cybersecurity and data protection, an area increasingly tied to business growth. Titled “Cybersecurity & Data Protection for Business Growth”, the panel featured BitRanger Sdn Bhd chief executive officer and founder as well as Universiti Sains Malaysia Cybersecurity Research Centre (Cyres) deputy director Assoc Prof Dr Shankar Karuppayah, EY Consulting association partner Jerry Ng and Crest Asia Council chairman BK Soon and examined cybersecurity and data protection from a business perspective, as companies increasingly relied on digital systems for operations, customer engagement and growth. The programme subsequently moved to an Alumni Spotlight featuring business growth stories, with speakers sharing practical examples from their own companies. Berry Group founder and managing director Victor Tan presented his session on “Tech-Driven Growth: Turning Digital Tools into Business Advantage”, highlighting how the education group expanded from 200 students in 2020 to 10,500 in 2026. The 50-fold growth was achieved with a lean core team of 30 full-time staff while the group managed 147 tutors. He explained how the company connected six systems covering operations and culture, workforce accountability, virtual classrooms, customer engagement, enrolment automation and AI-supported teaching. Solar House business development director Ong Yong Qiang, who presented Cash Flow Mastery: Strengthening Business Stability & Growth, highlighted three factors putting pressure on business margins – the impact of the Sales and Service Tax (SST), rising material costs and changes in industry policies. He cited the July 2025 electricity tariff restructuring for medium-voltage users as an example, with lower charges per kilowatt-hour but higher charges based on maximum demand. Collaborative Excellence Sdn Bhd founder and managing partner Chong Li Ken, who presented “Future-Ready Workforce: Building Agile & Adaptive Teams”, highlighted the importance of turning individual expertise into organisational capability by capturing knowledge, processes and data, enabling businesses to build more adaptive teams and retain critical know-how as people and technology evolve. The event also saw services business pitches by the four main SOBA sponsors: Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) Prai branch manager Nori Harni Juhari, U Mobile Sdn Bhd (U Mobile) head of SME Caroline Chin, RHB regional sales head SME Darren Lau and The Ship Campus chief executive officer Jasmon Lim, representing PKT Logistics Group Sdn Bhd (PKT). Lim said The Ship Campus’ role in Batu Kawan went beyond providing space for events, with the campus focused on developing an ecosystem linking businesses, education and entrepreneurship. “Our core and primary role being located in Batu Kawan was to ensure that we could build an effective ecosystem. The campus, established in 2020, engaged businesses and potential clients to understand their needs and connect them with potential suppliers, customers and other business opportunities. “The ecosystem also included Peninsula College, which offers certificates, diplomas and degrees, and Penn Skills, an accredited training centre focused on skilling, upskilling and reskilling. “Having the campus in Batu Kawan’s industrial area also placed it close to manufacturers and other companies, allowing it to understand their talent requirements and connect industry with education and skills training,” he said. SOBA 2026 is organised by SMG with CGC, PKT, RHB and U Mobile as main sponsors, while Great Wall Motor is co-sponsor, with the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) being the official trade promotion partner. It is audited by BDO while radio stations 988 and Suria are official media partners. For more information, call the SOBA Hotline at 017-231 1789or visit www.soba.com.my

Berry Group founder and managing director Victor Tan presented his session on “Tech-Driven Growth: Turning Digital Tools into Business Advantage”, highlighting how the education group expanded from 200 students in 2020 to 10,500 in 2026. The 50-fold growth was achieved with a lean core team of 30 full-time staff while the group managed 147 tutors. He explained how the company connected six systems covering operations and culture, workforce accountability, virtual classrooms, customer engagement, enrolment automation and AI-supported teaching. Solar House business development director Ong Yong Qiang, who presented Cash Flow Mastery: Strengthening Business Stability & Growth, highlighted three factors putting pressure on business margins – the impact of the Sales and Service Tax (SST), rising material costs and changes in industry policies. He cited the July 2025 electricity tariff restructuring for medium-voltage users as an example, with lower charges per kilowatt-hour but higher charges based on maximum demand. Collaborative Excellence Sdn Bhd founder and managing partner Chong Li Ken, who presented “Future-Ready Workforce: Building Agile & Adaptive Teams”, highlighted the importance of turning individual expertise into organisational capability by capturing knowledge, processes and data, enabling businesses to build more adaptive teams and retain critical know-how as people and technology evolve. The event also saw services business pitches by the four main SOBA sponsors: Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) Prai branch manager Nori Harni Juhari, U Mobile Sdn Bhd (U Mobile) head of SME Caroline Chin, RHB regional sales head SME Darren Lau and The Ship Campus chief executive officer Jasmon Lim, representing PKT Logistics Group Sdn Bhd (PKT). Lim said The Ship Campus’ role in Batu Kawan went beyond providing space for events, with the campus focused on developing an ecosystem linking businesses, education and entrepreneurship. “Our core and primary role being located in Batu Kawan was to ensure that we could build an effective ecosystem. The campus, established in 2020, engaged businesses and potential clients to understand their needs and connect them with potential suppliers, customers and other business opportunities. “The ecosystem also included Peninsula College, which offers certificates, diplomas and degrees, and Penn Skills, an accredited training centre focused on skilling, upskilling and reskilling. “Having the campus in Batu Kawan’s industrial area also placed it close to manufacturers and other companies, allowing it to understand their talent requirements and connect industry with education and skills training,” he said. title: 'Maybank emerges as top winner at inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026
body: 'Maybank emerges as top winner at inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026 KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 7): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) emerged as the biggest winner at the inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026 that was held last Friday, sweeping home three awards including Best Financial Reporting and the flagship Best Company in IR. Capping the hattrick win for the company was its sectoral win as Best Large-Cap company in IR for Financial Services while its president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli was named Best CEO in IR. The awards honoured a total of 32 winners across eight main categories, celebrating public listed companies (PLCs) and investor relations professionals who have demonstrated a strong commitment to investor engagement, market communication and corporate transparency, Bursa said in a statement on Monday. The eight categories are: - Best Company in IR (overall) tor (across 13 sectors) - Best Mid/Small-cap Company in IR by Sector (across 13 sectors) Other notable winners include Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA), which took home twin awards for Best Sustainability Communications and Best Large-cap Company in IR for Utilities, and Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd (KL:KOPI), which was named Best IPO Company in IR. The other individual award — the Best CFO in IR — went to Malkit Singh Maan of Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK). Effective investor relations is important in strengthening the quality and competitiveness of Malaysia's listed companies, said Treasury secretary general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican when delivering the keynote address at the awards celebrations. “By communicating openly and consistently with investors, public listed companies enable better-informed investment decisions and demonstrate their commitment to transparency and accountability. As we continue enhancing the competitiveness and quality of Malaysia’s listed companies, effective investor engagement will remain an enabler of long-term value creation and sustainable market growth,” Johan said. The inaugural awards aimed to recognise companies and professionals who are setting a high standard for transparency, engagement and market communication, said Bursa CEO Datuk Fad'l Mohamed. "By spotlighting these practices, we hope to encourage more listed companies to strengthen their investor relations capabilities and help raise standards of investor engagement across the market," he said. He also noted that there is considerable opportunity to strengthen IR capabilities across the market and enhance issuer-investor engagement across the market. Based on Bursa's research, only 32% of listed companies have a dedicated internal IR function while 17% outsource the function and 51% operate without any formal IR structure. The exchange operator and regulator said it has been building IR capabilities in the capital market through IR4U by providing practical guidance and learning opportunities for PLCs, which saw the participation of about 690 listed companies throughout 2024 and 2025. These efforts are complemented by MY Value Up, the national capital market initiative jointly launched by the Securities Commission Malaysia and Bursa to encourage companies to strengthen fundamentals while articulating their strategies and priorities more clearly to the market. The complete list of award winners will be featured in a special pullout in The Edge Malaysia weekly. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. Refer to the original content for accurate info. title: 'AHB Maintains Five Sen Income Distribution For FY2026
body: 'Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) has maintained its income distribution at five sen per unit for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026, benefiting more than 82,000 unit holders.  The final distribution for the six months ended Sept 30 was set at 2.1 sen per unit, alongside a 0.4 sen bonus distribution declared by fund sponsor Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB).  Together with the 2.5 sen interim distribution declared in April, the total distribution for FY2026 comes to five sen per unit.  PHB said RM120.13 million will be paid in the final round, bringing the total annual distribution to RM236.41 million.  The bonus distribution applies to the first 1,000,000 units held by each unit holder.  PHB Group Managing Director Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad said the full-year distribution reflected the resilience of AHB and its underlying property portfolio.  “AHB’s performance this year demonstrates our commitment to continue providing competitive returns to unit holders. At the same time, we remain focused on strengthening AHB’s position as an investment instrument of choice for Bumiputera investors through prudent capital management, dynamic investment strategies and continuous portfolio optimisation to ensure sustainable growth and long-term value creation,” he said.  PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM) Chief Executive Officer Zulkifli Ishak said the fund manager would continue managing AHB responsibly to ensure it remained accessible to Bumiputera investors.  The distribution will be paid in the form of AHB units and credited directly into unit holders’ AHB accounts by Oct 13. The units will be automatically reinvested, allowing holders to increase their holdings.  Bumiputera investors can subscribe to AHB at a fixed price of RM1 per unit, with a minimum investment of RM100 and maximum of RM1 million. Subscriptions are available through authorised distributors including Maybank, AmBank, AmBank Islamic, Bank Islam Malaysia and Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia.

title: 'UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking and Maybank execute landmark MYOR-based transaction - Newswav
body: 'PETALING JAYA: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking Group and Malayan Banking (Maybank) recently executed the first Malaysia Overnight Rate-based three-month interbank money market transaction in the country, incorporating a two-day lookback calculation convention through an interbank money market broker. The landmark transaction was anchored by UOB Malaysia and executed with RHB and Maybank, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of Malaysia’s money market and supporting industry efforts towards the adoption of risk-free rate-based market conventions. The transaction enhances transparency and price discovery by making funding levels and spreads visible to a broader network of market participants. This contrasts with bilateral transactions, where pricing information is limited to the counterparties involved. By helping establish a transparent Malaysia Overnight Rate (MYOR) funding curve and an observable reference point for three-month interbank funding, the transaction improves visibility into funding spreads over MYOR and banks’ cost of borrowing, supporting more efficient pricing across the wider market. UOB Malayia corporate and investment banking country head Christina Cheah said, “The successful execution of this money market transaction reflects the strong collaboration between UOB Malaysia, RHB and Maybank in supporting the evolution of the country’s financial markets. By establishing a transparent benchmark for MYOR-based funding, we are contributing to greater price discovery and helping to build confidence in the adoption of risk-free rate conventions. “As a leading foreign bank in the country, UOB Malaysia remains committed to partnering local market participants, sharing regional expertise and supporting initiatives that strengthen market resilience and align the domestic financial ecosystem with global standards.” The transaction references MYOR compounded in arrears with a two-day lookback mechanism, providing operational certainty in interest calculations while remaining anchored to actual market transactions. RHB Banking Group wholesale banking managing director Nurjesmi Mohd Nashir said, “This transaction demonstrates how market participants can work together to put MYOR-based conventions into practice and support the continued development of Malaysia’s money market. “As the industry progresses towards the transition from KLIBOR to MYOR, it is important that we build practical market experience and develop conventions that can be adopted more widely. RHB is committed to supporting Bank Negara Malaysia’s efforts to develop a deeper and more efficient MYOR market, and to playing an active role in the continued development of Malaysia’s financial markets.” Farid Kairi, deputy group CEO of global banking and managing director of global markets said: “Maybank is pleased to have played an integral role in this inaugural MYOR-based money market transaction. It marks an important first step in establishing the foundation for deeper liquidity, while setting the stage for widening the aperture for more MYOR-linked solutions and supporting robust price discovery for market participants. “This achievement reflects the collective efforts of industry participants and Bank Negara Malaysia in strengthening Malaysia’s financial market infrastructure.” Bank Negara Malaysia introduced MYOR in September 2021 as Malaysia’s Alternative Reference Rate (ARR). MYOR is calculated as the volume-weighted average rate of actual unsecured overnight ringgit interbank transactions, providing a robust benchmark grounded in deep and liquid overnight funding markets. The transition towards MYOR aligns Malaysia with other major financial markets that have adopted overnight risk-free rates including Singapore, Japan, Switzerland, the United States and the United Kingdom.

title: 'Malaysia-Myanmar: The repatriation question
body: 'A group of 1,476 people have been returned to Myanmar from Malaysia earlier this week, as part of a wider repatriation programme that could eventually involve up to 5,000 people. The government says the returns are voluntary, however the UN refugee agency has questioned whether people held in immigration detention can make a genuinely free and informed decision to return to a country still under ongoing conflict. Astro Awani’s Melisa Idris talks to with Sharifah Shakirah, the founder and director of the Rohingya Women Development Network, and Dr Moe Thuzar, a senior fellow and co-ordinator of the the Myanmar studies programme at Iseas-Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore. body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme.   In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively.   The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033.

title: 'Saudi, UAE to Cooperate in Building Crude Stockpile in Asia — Report
body: 'TOKYO (Oct 5): A framework for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to cooperate with Asian countries on oil stockpiling is set to be launched, with Japan supporting the initiative through financial assistance and stockpiling expertise, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday. Saudi, UAE to cooperate in building crude stockpile in Asia, Nikkei reports The Japan-led Asia Zero-Emission Community (Azec), a grouping of 11 countries including Southeast Asian nations, will hold a ministerial meeting in the Philippines on Thursday, where senior Saudi and UAE officials are expected to announce their intention to cooperate on oil stockpiling, the Nikkei said. The framework is expected to be included in a joint statement from the meeting, providing a basis for member countries to discuss expanding oil reserves with Middle Eastern producers, it said Specific details and the scale of cooperation will be worked out through bilateral discussions with Saudi Arabia and the UAE possibly expanding exports to participating countries or providing priority supplies in an emergency, Nikkei said Japan already leases domestic private storage tanks to state-owned oil companies in countries such as Saudi Arabia under a joint stockpiling scheme, which Japanese companies can access in an emergency Japan is expected to share the framework at a ministerial dialogue of the International Energy Forum in Saudi Arabia on Oct 11, the report said. A Japanese industry ministry official who spoke on condition of anonymity confirmed there will be dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the UAE and oil-consuming countries in Asia on the sidelines of the Azec ministerial meeting, although no concrete projects will be discussed. title: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Asteel Group Bhd (KL:ASTEEL) has appointed former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman and new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong as executive deputy chairman. The boardroom reshuffle follows Clifford securing a 53.08% stake in Asteel at the closing of a mandatory offer on Monday via investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd. Clifford emerged as Asteel’s controlling shareholder in August with the acquisition of an initial 52.94% stake in the company via a RM20.75 million cash deal at 7.5 sen apiece. This triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06% stake in Asteel, also at 7.5 sen apiece. Clifford, 43, the son of the journalist-turned-businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, who is the founder and executive chairman of property developer HCK Capital Group Bhd (KL:HCK) and group managing director and major shareholder of private education group SEG International. Clement is also the founder of Gambit Group Sdn Bhd, whose subsidiaries are involved in information technology services, investment, business management consultancy and is a registered digital asset custodian under the Securities Commission Malaysia. Clifford, a former non-independent, non-executive director at HCK Capital, has more than 20 years of experience in the education, property and financial technology sectors. He had held senior management and board positions covering corporate strategy, business development, corporate deals and investments, corporate governance and project management. Razarudin, 63, who is also independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd (KL:ADVCON), brings more than four decades of experience in national security and law enforcement. He was Malaysia’s 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. title: 'Monday wrap: Young architects rise, insurers rethink adequacy, AI trust gaps widen
body: 'Architecture's young talent, a shift in insurance strategy, AI trust gaps, and rising bank margins mark the week.  Last week in Singapore Business Review, eight architects under 40 were named for their work on hospitals, civic infrastructure, and heritage projects. Etiqa Insurance said the industry's challenge is shifting from expanding coverage to ensuring adequacy as customers plan for retirement and wealth transfer. Nearly all IT leaders reported artificial intelligence (AI) tools accessing sensitive data without permission, whilst AI shopping adoption climbed even as checkout trust lagged. Banks, meanwhile, are expected to see margins rise as SORA climbs toward 1.4% by year-end.  Singapore Business Review's list of notable architecture professionals under 40 for 2026 features eight honourees—five women and three men—from DP Architects, SAA Architects, RSP Architects Planners & Engineers, CPG Consultants, and Chang Architects. Their combined portfolio spans a $790m hotel (the largest Mercure property worldwide), Singapore's first fully integrated healthcare campus at Woodlands Hospital, and civic landmarks including One Punggol's Regional Library and the Goh Keng Swee Centre for Education, a 30-storey office tower under active construction.  Standout work included Kelvin Ng Si Hoa's role delivering Woodlands Hospital despite expressway noise and rocky terrain constraints, and Loh Zhu Ping's contributions to the $450m Funan Redevelopment and the $790m Mercure ICON Singapore City Centre.  Singapore insurers should shift focus from expanding coverage to ensuring policy adequacy, according to Etiqa Insurance Singapore CEO Claudia Soh, as customers increasingly treat insurance as part of long-term financial planning rather than pure protection against loss. Singapore's insurance penetration stood at 7.6% of GDP as of May 2026, ranking fourth among selected Asian markets behind South Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong.  A May CIMB report found 52.6% of residents viewed insurance as supporting financial independence, up from 45% in 2025, with customers increasingly looking at retirement, wealth-building, and inheritance planning. Soh said AI can help insurers tailor services but cautioned that "trust, human judgement, and meaningful customer relationships remain just as important."  Nearly all Singaporean IT leaders (98.9%) reported an AI tool or agent accessing sensitive data beyond its intended scope in the past year, the second-highest rate among eight markets surveyed in Delinea's 2026 Identity Security Report.  Despite 99.6% of organisations having a formal AI data access policy, only 14% of IT leaders can detect a scope violation as it happens, and 72% take a full day or longer to catch one—the highest globally. Employee behaviour compounds the risk: 84% of Singaporean employees said they have bypassed required approval processes for AI use, and just 38% of IT leaders said they can always trace a sensitive access event back to a named human authoriser.  Singapore consumers are increasingly shopping with AI, but remain wary of letting it complete purchases, according to Adyen's 2026 Singapore Retail Report. Whilst 72% of consumers use AI assistants for shopping, only 29% are comfortable letting AI complete a purchase, and 49% of existing AI shopping users hesitate at the payment stage.  Still, AI-referred visitors generate 53% more revenue per visit and convert 54% more than non-AI traffic. Separately, Salesforce's State of Commerce report found 82% of Singapore commerce leaders expect large language models to become essential to product discovery within the year, with agentic search usage as a shopping-journey starting point up 200% year-over-year.  Singapore's three-month benchmark borrowing rate is expected to climb to 1.4% by year-end, supporting bank margins into 2027, according to UOB Kay Hian. The three-month compounded SORA rose to 1.22% in the third quarter after falling to 1.02% in April, reflecting MAS's tighter monetary policy stance amid slowing money supply growth.  UOB Kay Hian raised its 2027 net profit forecasts for DBS and OCBC by 5.7% and 4.7% respectively, citing expected margin gains, whilst flagging risks from elevated US rates and potential Red Sea shipping disruptions that could push freight and oil costs higher.

title: 'RHB Group maintains Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast at 5.4pct
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026 is projected at 5.4 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electric and electronic (E&E) exports, according to RHB Group. In RHB's Global Economics Outlook for Q4 2026, group chief economist and head of market research, Barnabas Gan said the bank revised the headline inflation forecast to 1.9 per cent for 2026 from 2.1 per cent previously, reflecting softer-than-expected price pressures. For the first eight months of the year, inflation averaged 1.8 per cent, alongside the restoration of the BUDI95 monthly quota and an increase in the diesel subsidy quota from September. "For the rest of 2026, the inflation trajectory will be shaped by global commodity price movements, changes in domestic policies, as well as potential upside from food inflation," he said. Gan added that domestic policy measures, such as RON95 and diesel subsidy, stable food prices, stable demand conditions and a relatively stable ringgit, as well as gradual pass-through to consumer prices should help keep inflation contained. Meanwhile, he said the overnight policy rate is expected to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the upcoming November Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting amid manageable inflation. Moving forward, Gan said RHB Bank expects Bank Negara Malaysia to deliver a token 25 basis points (bps) hike in the first half of 2027 (1H 2027) as a normalisation move towards a more neutral policy setting rather than a response to significant inflationary pressures. He also expects the 2026 fiscal deficit to remain broadly on track towards the government's 3.5 per cent of GDP target, although risks are tilted towards a modest overshoot given the relatively high deficit in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) and uncertainties surrounding fuel subsidy expenditure. At the same time, the bank is maintaining its current account surplus forecast at 2.4 per cent of GDP for 2026, versus a 2.5 per cent surplus in 1H 2026. "The goods surplus should remain supported by resilient E&E exports amid the global technology cycle, while robust tourism receipts and information and communication technology services exports should underpin the services account. "Together, these should sustain Malaysia's current account surplus," added Gan.

title: 'Rights-based approach needed to support longer, dignified lives for older people – Suhakam
body: 'The Malaysian human rights commission, Suhakam, commemorates the International Day of Older Persons 2026 under the theme ‘The age of longevity: Rethinking systems for longer lives’. The theme highlights the need to rethink policies, institutions and systems in response to longer life expectancy and ensure that older people can continue to enjoy their rights with dignity, equality and independence. Malaysia is experiencing a significant demographic shift. According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia, people aged 60 years and above accounted for an estimated 4.1 million people or 12% of Malaysia’s population in 2025, compared with 3.9 million or 11.6% in 2024. The DoS projects that Malaysia will become an ageing nation by 2036, when the proportion of people aged 60 years and above is expected to exceed 15% of the total population. This demographic change underscores the need for Malaysia to strengthen its preparedness for an ageing society and ensure that policies, services and systems remain responsive to the changing needs of its population. Suhakam stresses that preparing for an ageing society requires more than providing care and welfare assistance. Older people must have meaningful access to economic security, employment, affordable and accessible healthcare, adequate housing and social protection. They must also be protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation and discrimination and have access to public spaces and services. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member As digitalisation increasingly shapes access to information and essential public services, efforts towards digital inclusion should also be strengthened to ensure that older people are not left behind by technological changes. Meaningful participation must remain central to policies and decisions affecting older people. Their experiences, knowledge and contributions should be recognised and valued, with opportunities for them to participate in family, community, economic and social life according to their abilities and choices. The protection and wellbeing of older people also form part of Malaysia’s broader human rights commitments, including recommendations made during Malaysia’s fourth universal periodic review in 2024 to enhance the rights, protection and wellbeing of older people. Suhakam has continued to advance discussions on the rights of older people through forums and engagements focusing on economic, social and cultural rights, including social protection, healthcare, housing, employment and other aspects of wellbeing. These engagements have also examined the implications of an ageing population and Malaysia’s preparedness to respond to the needs and rights of older people at the national and state levels. At the regional level, Suhakam in its capacity as chair of the South East Asia National Human Rights Institutions Forum for 2026, has also brought the rights of older people into regional discussions as an emerging and cross-cutting human rights issue. Suhakam also reiterates its long-standing support for the development of specific legislation to protect the rights of older people in Malaysia. As early as 2018, Suhakam fully supported the development of an older people’s bill following efforts by the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development to address gaps in existing laws, including in relation to elder abuse and neglect. Suhakam maintains that a dedicated legal framework would strengthen the protection of older people and help ensure that their rights, dignity and wellbeing are upheld as Malaysia transitions towards an ageing society. In conjunction with the International Day of Older Persons 2026, Suhakam will also commemorate Older Persons’ Day on 7 October at Rumah Seri Kenangan Cheras under the theme ‘Celebrating our older persons!’. This will honour the wisdom, experience and contributions of older people to our communities and nation. The programme reflects Suhakam’s commitment not only to advocate for the rights of older people but also to engage with them meaningfully, recognise their contributions and affirm their place as valued members of society. On this International Day of Older Persons, Suhakam calls on the government, relevant institutions, civil society, communities and families to strengthen collective efforts towards an inclusive society where people can age with dignity, remain active and independent according to their abilities and choices, participate meaningfully in decisions and communities, and continue to enjoy their human rights throughout all stages of life. – Suhakam The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.
