title: 'RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26
body: 'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank Bhd’s management has shared that there is sufficient runway to reposition the bank’s portfolio and capitalise on market opportunities for the fourth quarter ending Dec 31, 2026 (4Q26) after surging Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields weigh on non- interest income (NOII) in 3Q26. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research said the bank’s near-term outlook faces pressure from elevated MGS yields, which could weigh on its 3Q26 NOII, but that management appears less downbeat on the 4Q26 outlook should MGS yields stabilise or retrace. The research house, which recently met with the bank’s management, maintained a “hold” call and target price of RM8 based on implied one time 2027 price to book, as most near-term drivers have been baked in, with no stronger immediate catalyst. “We came away from a recent meeting with RHB’s management feeling neutral on its earnings trajectory and asset quality outlook,” it said, with weaker trading income largely inevitable given the limited runway for recovery during 3Q26. “While stronger wealth, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, brokerage and loan-related fees should provide some cushion, these are unlikely to fully offset the trading-income shortfall.” The research firm said the impact on 3Q26 should be viewed more as a foregone trading upside rather than outsized losses, given RHB’s relatively small trading book. The Treasury has been tactically unwinding securities positions, crystallising gains where possible while reducing exposure. The bank’s return on equity (ROE) target range of 10.8% to 11% appears within reach despite the NOII headwinds, but only towards the lower end as the burden increasingly shifts to core operations, with loan growth of 6% and management having reset cost growth to less than or equal to 1%, providing scope for better operating leverage. “Credit cost is tracking around the lower end of its 13 basis points (bps) to 14bps guidance, with management comfortable at 13bps and hopeful of achieving 12bps should recoveries materialise,” HLIB Research said. Wealth sales have also risen 35% year-on-year as of June 2026, while bancassurance/takaful, brokerage and loan-related fees continue to gain traction. Taken together, these levers should partially cushion the NOII drag, although the path towards the upper end of management’s ROE ambition has become more challenging amid elevated bond yields. Capital management remains an important medium-term catalyst, with management targeting more clarity on its capital/dividend policy by 1Q27. The priority would be to ensure operations and targeted growth trajectory can be adequately funded while sustaining Common Equity Tier 1 around current levels. Should these growth requirements be met without absorbing the existing surplus, the excess capital could potentially be fully returned to shareholders. The existing dividend remains respectable, with projected dividend yield of 6.5% for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2027.

title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat.

title: 'Construction Firm SLGC Ends First Trading Day Below IPO Price
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm’s shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intraday low of 24 sen as more than 83 million shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140 million. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. “Now that SLGC is a listed company, the priority for us is to continue strengthening the business while staying disciplined in how we grow and we intend to keep improving on how we deliver,” managing director Yong Zheng Lin said in his speech at the listing ceremony. SLGC is a building construction contractor with G7 grade and got its start in 2009 under the name SLG Construction Sdn Bhd before being incorporated in 2024. The company also has an operations office in Taman Gembira, Kuala Lumpur. The company is mainly involved in design and building construction services for residential and non-residential works. SLGC's customers include property developers and building owners in Malaysia. The IPO raised about RM29.4 million for the company and another RM17.64 million for four selling shareholders that include Yong and his wife Chew Ka Yan. Liong Yang Herng, the company’s project director, and contract director Loo Chun Kok are also cashing out part of their stake in SLGC. The company has allocated RM9.2 million of the IPO proceeds towards acquisition of construction machinery and equipment, RM7.6 million to repay bank borrowings, and RM7.5 million for general working capital. The rest will cover software upgrades and listing expenses. M&A Securities Sdn Bhd acted as the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter, and placement agent for the IPO. title: 'Maybank to acquire rest of Maybank Ageas for RM4.83 billion
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has entered into an unconditional share purchase agreement (SPA) with Belgium-based Ageas Insurance International NV to acquire the remaining 30.95% equity interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd (MAHB) for RM4.83 billion. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Maybank said the agreement involves acquiring 78 million MAHB shares from Ageas. The banking group said it signed the SPA today after receiving approval from Bank Negara Malaysia on Sept 1 and that the purchase consideration will be funded entirely through internally generated funds. Maybank said the proposed acquisition is intended to enable it to wholly own MAHB and provide the group with greater strategic flexibility. “The acquisition is also aimed at strengthening MAHB’s position as a national insurance and takaful player, supporting expansion across Southeast Asia, enhancing sustainable and resilient long-term value for the Maybank group, and improving capital management efficiency across its insurance and takaful franchises. “Full ownership of MAHB is expected to provide both Maybank and MAHB with greater strategic agility to accelerate product innovation, deepen bancassurance penetration, expand takaful propositions, and enhance capital and operational efficiency across the insurance and takaful franchises,” it said. Barring unforeseen circumstances, Maybank said that the proposed acquisition is expected to be completed on Sept 11. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd has been appointed as the principal adviser, while Morgan Stanley Asia (Singapore) Pte has been appointed as its international financial adviser.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower Amid US Yield Increase and Regional Tensions
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia began the trading day on a lower note, reflecting Wall Street's mixed performance as higher US Treasury yields and ongoing tensions in West Asia affected investor sentiment. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 3.74 points, or 0.22 percent, to 1,647.43 at 9.10 am on Thursday, down from the previous day's close of 1,651.17. The index had opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. The broader market saw 200 decliners outpacing 142 gainers, with 307 counters unchanged, 2,124 untraded, and 12 suspended. The turnover was 246.59 million shares, valued at RM118.14 million. Thong Pak Leng, Vice-President of Equity Research at Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, noted that Wall Street's mixed close was influenced by softer inflation, which eased the expectations of another US Federal Reserve rate hike, although elevated bond yields still weighed on market sentiment. Domestically, Thong indicated that the market may trade cautiously due to weak market breadth and recent foreign selling, suggesting continued investor caution. He anticipates the index to consolidate within the 1,640-1,660 range, with bargain hunting providing some support. Among the heavyweights, Maybank and IHH Healthcare remained unchanged at RM9.90 and RM7.83, respectively. Public Bank decreased by three sen to RM4.67, CIMB fell one sen to RM7.78, and Tenaga Nasional dropped two sen to RM12.94. In more active trading, new ACE Market entrant GB Bond fell half a sen to 24.5 sen, while VS Industry remained steady at 28 sen. Astro Malaysia increased by half a sen to six sen, Jaks Resources gained one sen to 21.5 sen, and Divfex rose two sen to 11 sen. Top gainers included Keck Seng, which advanced 11 sen to RM5.14, and Petron Malaysia, which rose seven sen to RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining and Spritzer each gained six sen to RM3.62 and RM3.67, respectively, while Jati Tinggi strengthened five sen to RM1.44. Leading the decliners, Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 18 sen to RM22.02, UWC decreased 15 sen to RM6.92, and both Insights Analytics and MISC fell nine sen to RM1.20 and RM7.55, respectively. Petronas Dagangan lost eight sen to RM19.20. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 42.26 points to 17,532.41, the FBM Emas Index declined 26.32 points to 12,265.69, and the FBM Top 100 Index shed 27.82 points to 12,056.62. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 22.09 points to 12,154.26, while the FBM ACE Index decreased by 6.31 points to 5,527.97. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 0.10 point to 180.31, the Energy Index gained 1.41 points to 847.11, the Financial Services Index fell 27.47 points to 19,189.02, and the Plantation Index retreated 33.34 points to 9,163.33.

title: 'FBM KLCI Slips At Open As Budget 2027 Looms
body: 'The FBM KLCI opened slightly lower on Wednesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, with the market continuing to search for fresh catalysts.  At 9.05am, the benchmark index fell 3.22 points to 1,630.13, remaining rangebound amid continued uncertainty.  Apex Securities said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 could provide some support to the local market, although a stronger recovery would likely require fresh foreign fund inflows and clearer direction on bond yields and geopolitical developments.  “We stay cautious on the local bourse this week, as easing crude oil prices and Budget 2027 expectations may offer some support, but a stronger recovery will likely require fresh catalysts such as foreign fund inflows and clearer direction on bond yields and geopolitical developments,” it said in a note.  The research firm also remained cautious on near-term global risk appetite, noting that the current rally was narrowly led by technology stocks while bond yields remained near multi-decade highs.  It said equities could remain vulnerable if the US Federal Reserve adopts a more hawkish tone.  Banking counters were among the early decliners, with CIMB falling seven sen to RM7.63 and Hong Leong Bank losing eight sen to RM22.  Press Metal shed six sen to RM7.13.  Among actively traded stocks, Metronic was unchanged at 0.5 sen and Zetrix AI remained at nine sen, while Top Glove jumped five sen to 92.5 sen.  Glove makers also gained amid renewed optimism in the sector, with Supermax rising two sen to 48 sen, Hartalega adding five sen to RM1.17 and Kossan gaining two sen to RM1.27.

body: '户头解冻遭速提1165万 投资者迎追讨曙光 轰动全国的黄金投资骗局金玉华（Genneva Gold）私人有限公司，已被高庭正式颁布清盘令！ 马来西亚高庭于2026年9月30日正式批准清盘申请，此举为数以千计的受害投资者通过法律清盘程序、向该公司追讨多年血汗钱铺平了道路。法庭也同时确认黄荣富（译音）正式担任该公司的清盘人。 高庭法官旺法蒂拉诺在宣读判词时指出，法庭下令清盘基于三大理由：第一，该公司此前因非法吸收存款被定罪，证明其曾被用于非法用途；第二，公司停运多年，目前缺乏合法执照和准证恢复业务；第三，公司管理极度混乱，不仅未妥善保存秘书记录，更没有一个正常运作的董事会。 户头刚解冻 1165万遭“闪电”转移 此项清盘申请是由持有金玉华75万股的董事黄婉瑜（译音）于2024年8月提出。而促使她急切向法庭申请清盘的导火线，正是涉及一笔高达1165万令吉的银行资金被迅速提走的惊人内幕。 根据法庭文件，地庭于2024年6月下令撤销国家银行此前的资产扣押令，解冻了金玉华在马银行（Maybank）及大众银行（Public Bank）的户头资金。然而，款项解冻后，金玉华董事局随即批准将1165万9661令吉20仙的款项，迅速转入其长期法律顾问律师楼的客户托管账户。 更令人震惊的是，黄婉瑜声称，在资金移至律师楼账户后，其中竟有高达到1026万令吉，以“专业服务费（律师费）”的名义被转出。由于担心公司剩余资产沦为某些人的“私人利益”而非用于偿还投资者，她决定通过法律清盘，由独立清盘人介入展开深入调查。 清盘人接管 全面追查非法资产转移 已被法庭正式确认为清盘人的黄荣富表示，初步调查显示，金玉华的资产在过去确实曾被不当且违法地转移。 随着高庭正式下达清盘令，清盘人现已获得法律授权，全面接管并清查金玉华遗留的所有资产。接下来的核心工作将包括追查这笔被“速提”的千万资金去向、追讨不当转移的资产，并在稍后开放受害者索赔登记程序。受害投资者受促密切关注官方清盘资产申报流程，以保障自身权益。 清盘是投资者的“迟来正义”，但“能拿回多少”仍是残酷的未知数 虽然高庭颁布清盘令、委任独立清盘人全面追查是法律的胜利，但受害者切勿盲目乐观： 金玉华当年席卷的资金高达数十亿令吉，涉及数万名受害者。如今独立清盘人去追查的，只是这区区一千多万令吉的冰山一角。 清盘人黄荣富虽然誓言追讨，但要从律师楼的口袋里、从已定罪的高层资产中把钱“吐出来”，还需要经历无数轮的法律诉讼与资产清算。即便最终追回，在扣除清盘行政费、法律费及优先债权后，普通投资者能分到的数额恐怕也只是象征性的巴仙率（%）。 金玉华案跨越十余年，从高调吸金、国行取缔、漫长诉讼，到如今解冻后的“临终分赃”与强行清盘，它是一部活生生的大马金融血泪史。它再次敲响警钟：在崩盘的庞氏骗局面前，不仅骗子的承诺不可信，连高喊合法合规的“内部人”也随时准备在废墟上刮骨吸髓。 【金玉华案前因后果：从吸金数十亿到内部“闪电分赃”】 高调吸金（2009—2012年）： 金玉华打着“伊斯兰合规黄金买卖”旗号，以高于市价20%卖金并承诺每月给2%至3%高额回扣，吸引全马数万名投资者砸入数十亿令吉棺材本。 国行取缔（2012—2020年）： 2012年10月，国家银行突击查封该公司，大盘轰然倒塌。历经多年诉讼，上诉庭于2020年做出终审定罪，判定多名核心高层非法吸收存款及洗黑钱罪成，判监并重罚4.5亿令吉。 解冻速提（2024年）： 2024年6月，地庭撤销当年的资产扣押令，其银行户头重新解冻。不料，控制权派系董事随即采取“闪电操作”，将1165万令吉现金转入合作的律师楼户头，更将其中1026万令吉以“律师费”名义转出分赃。 内讧清盘（2026年9月30日）： 另一名董事黄婉瑜因不满千万资金被内部蚕食，愤而“掀桌子”申请清盘。高庭最终宣判金玉华正式破产清盘，由独立清盘人接管。 图取自中国报 【免责声明】 《风采》网站欢迎读者/网民留言，创造友好交流空间；唯网民留言皆不代表本网站立场。本网站有权删除任何人身攻击、鼓吹种族宗教隔阂、诽谤造谣、网络霸凌等煽动性留言。 想要买《风采》，网购最方便！ 👉 https://s.lazada.com.my/s.xqJTn (西马) 👉 https://s.lazada.com.my/s.xqJ58 (东马) 👉 https://my.shp.ee/urmN2pCX (西马) 👉 https://my.shp.ee/K9R1Es9m (东马) 👉订阅《风采》纸本杂志： https://shop.enanyang.my/product/feminine/

title: 'One of Top Plantation Analysts Turns Cautious as Indonesia’s Land Reform Clouds Sector Outlook
body: 'Maybank Investment Bank analyst Ong Chee Ting downgraded his three-month view on regional plantations to “Neutral” from “Positive” after Indonesia passed a new agrarian reform law on September 22. The law seeks to address unequal land ownership and agrarian disputes. Ong believes unresolved questions over future landholding limits and whether the 20% land-provision requirement or an alternative profit-sharing arrangement applies to existing concessions could weigh on plantation share prices. He stressed that the law does not automatically require companies to surrender productive plantation land and has left his earnings forecasts unchanged pending implementation rules. Ong considers Malaysian plantation companies with little or no Indonesian estate exposure relatively safer from this regulatory risk. Sarawak Oil Palms and Ta Ann Holdings have all their planted area in Malaysia, while TH Plantations has only 3% in Indonesia. Separately, Maybank’s preferred “Buy” list now comprises SD Guthrie, Sarawak Oil Palms and Genting Plantations, with SD Guthrie replacing Kuala Lumpur Kepong on that list. Ong remains constructive on 2027 crude-palm-oil (CPO) prices, although strong current production and weak exports may limit near-term gains. Ong Chee Ting is currently ranked No.2 among 15 analysts covering the plantation sector on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 76% expert rating, with a 17% average return and an 85% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. Public Investment Bank analyst Chong Hoe Leong takes a less cautious near-term view. He maintained the plantation sector at “Overweight”, arguing that the new law is unlikely to cause immediate earnings or asset losses while its rules remain unsettled. He expects firmer CPO prices to support second-half earnings and retains a 2026 CPO price forecast of RM4,500 per tonne. His preferred stocks are Sarawak Plantation and Ta Ann Holdings, citing their above-industry production growth, projected dividend yields of 7%–8% and lack of Indonesian plantation exposure. Chong Hoe Leong ranks No.2 among 12 Public Investment Bank analysts tracked by StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He has a 45% expert rating and a 39% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. As of 11:26 a.m. on September 28, the Bursa Malaysia Plantation Index dropped 0.4% to 9,294.3 points. title: 'Bursa opens marginally higher on easing US Treasury yields, Fed tone
body: 'At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.49 points, or 0.09%, to 1,631.85 from Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The index opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87. On the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 239 to 137, with 270 counters unchanged, 2,127 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover stood at 173.94 million shares worth RM95.98 million. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the latest decline had pushed the index back into oversold territory, which could have encouraged bargain hunting following the sharp correction. “Against the reported foreign-selling backdrop, however, we believe any initial rebound may remain modest. “Nonetheless, the weakness presents opportunities to selectively accumulate fundamentally sound stocks, particularly among established banks, utilities and semiconductor counters,” he noted. Thong said a more sustainable recovery would require stronger participation from heavyweight counters and an improvement in market breadth. Thus, he expects cautious trading today within the 1,625-1,640 range. Among the heavyweights, Maybank was flat at RM9.95, while Public Bank and CIMB fell one sen to RM4.66 and RM7.68, respectively. Tenaga Nasional added four sen to RM12.94 and IHH Healthcare rose one sen to RM7.71. In active trade, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources and Genetec all remained unchanged at 16.5 sen, 18 sen and 32.5 sen, respectively. V.S Industry gained one sen to 28 sen, but Kinergy Advancement lost half a sen to 39.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries advanced 58 sen to RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining inched up 19 sen to RM3.83, Petronas Chemicals perked up 15 sen to RM4.28, while UWC and MI Technovation both firmed 10 sen to RM7.20 and RM5.36, respectively. MISC led the decliners, falling 14 sen to RM7.54, while LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB and RHB Bank shed four sen each to RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78 and RM7.43, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index ticked up 75.93 points to 17,434.91, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 17.18 points to 12,160.71, and the FBM Top 100 Index widened 21.58 points to 11,954.73. The FBM Emas Shariah Index accumulated 34.76 points to 12,047.77, while the FBM ACE Index improved 18.61 points to 5,501.58. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index grew 1.10 points to 178.83, while the Energy Index gained 9.45 points to 844.46. The Financial Services Index fell 26.33 points to 19,034.58, while the Plantation Index ticked up 2.75 points to 9,029.32.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Ends Lower as It Tracks Cautious Wall Street Performance
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 – Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Thursday, October 1, 2026, under persistent selling pressure across major blue-chip counters, tracking a mixed and cautious overnight performance on Wall Street. The benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 20.81 points, or 1.26 per cent, to finish at 1,630.36, down from Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. After opening 1.30 points weaker at 1,649.87, the key index fluctuated between an intraday low of 1,630.10 and a high of 1,649.87 throughout the trading session. Market breadth was negative as decliners outpaced gainers 750 to 342, with 495 counters trading unchanged, 1,186 untraded, and 12 suspended. Total market turnover dropped to 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion, compared to 3.63 billion units worth RM3.62 billion recorded on Wednesday. Economic data released earlier in the day showed that the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) slipped into contraction territory, falling to 49.9 in September from 50.2 in August—marking the first downturn in operating conditions in four months. Regionally, the S&P Global ASEAN Manufacturing PMI also eased to 52.1 in September from 52.3 in August. Blue-Chip Heavyweights and Active Counters Financial, utility, and healthcare heavyweights experienced notable selling pressure: - CIMB dropped 10 sen to RM7.69. - IHH Healthcare erased 13 sen to RM7.70. - Tenaga Nasional lost 6 sen to RM12.90. - Maybank slipped 4 sen to RM9.95. - Public Bank fell 3 sen to RM4.67. In active trading, ACE Market debutant GB Bond slumped 4.5 sen to close at 20.5 sen. Jaks Resources dropped 2.5 sen to 18 sen, and VS Industry dipped 1 sen to 27 sen. Meanwhile, Zetrix AI and HHRG each added half a sen to close at 16.5 sen. Top gainers for the session were led by technology and consumer stocks: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Surged 72 sen to RM41.12. - Ayer Holdings: Advanced 20 sen to RM7.70. - Riverview Rubber Estates: Rose 12 sen to RM3.02. - Dutch Lady Malaysia Industries: Added 10 sen to RM30.00. - Vitrox: Gained 9 sen to RM10.00. Plantation and consumer-linked counters featured among the session’s major losers: - Kuala Lumpur Kepong: Led losses, dropping 78 sen to RM21.42. - Allianz Malaysia: Declined 62 sen to RM21.00. - United Plantations: Shed 60 sen to RM30.96. - Fraser & Neave & Hong Leong Industries: Each fell 32 sen to RM21.42 and RM16.14, respectively. –NMT

title: 'Hong Leong Bank Launches HLB opus Ceramic Card
body: 'Hong Leong Bank has launched HLB opus, an invitation-only payment card aimed at its most affluent clients. The new card is Southeast Asia’s first credit card made from exclusive ceramic material. It is also Malaysia’s first payment experience built around the Visa Infinite Privilege tier. HLB is positioning opus as more than another premium card. Instead, the bank wants it to act as a gateway to exclusive travel, dining, wellness and concierge services for selected clients. HLB opus Uses Ceramic Instead of Metal Premium credit cards have increasingly relied on metal construction to create a sense of exclusivity. HLB has taken a different approach. HLB opus uses Giesecke+Devrient’s Convego Ceramic technology. The card is produced using high heat and pressure before being finished through diamond refinement. HLB says the result is a scratch-resistant card with a smooth surface and reflective finish. The ceramic construction is also intended to give the card a distinctive physical and acoustic character. For HLB, that physical design reflects the broader positioning of opus as a statement product rather than simply another payment tool. Andrew Jong, Managing Director of Personal Financial Services at HLB, said the bank created opus to recognise the achievements and personal journeys of its clients. He described the card as a tribute to success built through ambition, resilience and long-term effort. Visa Infinite Privilege Brings Global Benefits The new card is anchored around Visa Infinite Privilege. That gives clients access to a collection of premium international services. Benefits include unlimited access to Plaza Premium Lounges worldwide. Clients can also receive selected immigration fast-track services and access to Visa private clubs. Status-matching benefits are available with several luxury and travel programmes. These include Harrods Gold, ALL Accor+ Explorer Gold and Banyan Voyager. The range of benefits reflects HLB’s focus on internationally mobile clients. Jason Phua, Head of Clients at Visa Malaysia, said affluent customers increasingly value personalised experiences over traditional expressions of luxury. He said the partnership combines Visa’s premium privileges with HLB’s understanding of its high-value clients. HLB opus Targets Frequent Travellers Travel rewards form another major part of the HLB opus proposition. The bank has expanded its existing relationship with Malaysia Airlines’ Enrich loyalty programme. HLB says opus provides the highest Enrich Points earning potential in the region. Clients receive 60,000 Enrich Points after paying the annual fee. They can then increase their points earnings through overseas spending. HLB opus clients can also earn one Elite Point for every RM10,000 spent overseas. Those rewards can support status progression and redemptions across Malaysia Airlines and the wider oneworld airline network. Phillip See, Chief Executive Officer of Loyalty & Travel Services at Malaysia Aviation Group, said premium travellers increasingly expect benefits throughout their entire journey. He added that the partnership is designed to provide more flexibility, rewards and travel privileges. HLB Builds a Broader Privilege Ecosystem The card is also tied to HLB’s wider banking relationships. The bank describes this approach as its “One Bank” client success model. Under that structure, Business & Corporate Banking supports business creation and enterprise growth. Private Banking then focuses on protecting and structuring wealth. Personal Financial Services adds lifestyle and rewards benefits through products such as HLB opus. The strategy is designed to keep clients within the HLB ecosystem across different stages of their business and personal financial journeys. That makes opus more than a standalone credit card launch. It also serves as a visible extension of the bank’s affluent and high-net-worth customer strategy. Physical Cards Still Matter in a Digital Banking Era The introduction of a ceramic payment card comes at a time when digital wallets and virtual payment methods continue to grow. However, premium banks still see value in physical cards as status objects. Farouk Musthafa, Managing Director at Giesecke+Devrient Singapore, said physical cards remain an important tangible expression of distinction. He said HLB approached opus as a privilege-first product rather than a conventional card programme. That positioning helps explain the decision to use ceramic instead of more common plastic or metal materials. The card itself becomes part of the luxury experience. HLB Deepens Focus on Wealth and Affluent Banking The launch also supports Hong Leong Bank’s wider transformation strategy. Business banking and wealth management remain important growth areas for the bank. HLB has been strengthening its offerings across corporate banking, private banking and affluent financial services. Its Private Bank already works with global wealth partners including Lombard Odier. HLB opus adds another layer to that strategy by connecting financial relationships with premium lifestyle benefits. For selected clients, the bank wants business banking, wealth management and personal privileges to operate as one connected experience. HLB opus is therefore positioned as both a payment card and a symbol of that broader relationship. With ceramic construction, Visa Infinite Privilege benefits and enhanced Enrich rewards, HLB is clearly aiming at the highest end of Malaysia’s premium banking market.

title: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, Construction Stocks Seen as Key Beneficiaries of Budget 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday. In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion. It believes the higher allocation “could provide a modest boost to mass-market consumption, particularly benefitting companies exposed to lower- and middle-income households”. Among the counters poised to benefit are 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (KL:99SMART), Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd (KL:ECOSHOP) and MR DIY Group (M) Bhd (KL:MRDIY), as well as food and beverage manufacturers Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:NESTLE), Life Water Bhd (KL:LWSABAH) and QL Resources Bhd (KL:QL). CIMB Securities also expects gross development expenditure to rise to RM83 billion in 2027, with higher spending on water infrastructure among the potential areas of focus. Among the counters it sees as well positioned to benefit are Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM), Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT) and Insight Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB). Separately, Maybank Investment Bank expects Budget 2027 to remain supportive of the healthcare sector. Potential measures include tax relief for healthcare and medical insurance, support for the nationwide MediAsas rollout, continued medical-tourism incentives and greater public-private collaboration to ease congestion at public hospitals, it said. Local pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturers may also benefit from continued government support for manufacturing, procurement, research and development, Maybank IB said. description: 'Malaysia Budget 2027 may boost consumer, construction and healthcare stocks through higher cash aid, infrastructure spending, healthcare incentives and public-private support.
full_text: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, Construction Stocks Seen as Key Beneficiaries of Budget 2027. 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday. In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion. It believes the higher allocation “could provide a modest boost to mass-market consumption, particularly benefitting companies exposed to lower- and middle-income households”. Among the counters poised to benefit are 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (KL:99SMART), Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd (KL:ECOSHOP) and MR DIY Group (M) Bhd (KL:MRDIY), as well as food and beverage manufacturers Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:NESTLE), Life Water Bhd (KL:LWSABAH) and QL Resources Bhd (KL:QL). CIMB Securities also expects gross development expenditure to rise to RM83 billion in 2027, with higher spending on water infrastructure among the potential areas of focus. Among the counters it sees as well positioned to benefit are Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM), Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT) and Insight Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB). Separately, Maybank Investment Bank expects Budget 2027 to remain supportive of the healthcare sector. Potential measures include tax relief for healthcare and medical insurance, support for the nationwide MediAsas rollout, continued medical-tourism incentives and greater public-private collaboration to ease congestion at public hospitals, it said. Local pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturers may also benefit from continued government support for manufacturing, procurement, research and development, Maybank IB said. Its top picks include IHH Healthcare Bhd (KL:IHH), KPJ Healthcare Bhd (KL:KPJ), Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd (KL:SUNMED), PMCK Bhd (KL:PMCK), Duopharma Biotech Bhd (KL:DPHARMA) and Pharmaniaga Bhd (KL:PHARMA). title: 'Stock Today: Maybank Gains 0.5% In Afternoon Trade
body: 'Shares in Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) rose 5 sen or 0.50% to RM10.04 as of 2.31pm, with 6.22 million shares traded.  The stock opened at RM10.00 and climbed to an intraday high of RM10.10 before easing to a low of RM9.99.  Maybank had 321,600 shares queued at the best buying price of RM10.02, while 533,500 shares were available at RM10.04 on the sell side.  The counter’s last adjusted closing price was RM9.99.  The share price movement comes after Maybank fully redeemed its RM1.56 billion Additional Tier 1 (AT1) Sukuk Mudharabah on Sept 25, its first call date seven years after the securities were issued.  The sukuk was originally issued on Sept 25, 2019 and formed part of Maybank’s AT1 capital instruments.  Meanwhile, Bank Negara Malaysia Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the central bank was reviewing whether financial institutions could be given greater flexibility to take on higher risks within acceptable limits to support Malaysia’s energy transition.  The move could have implications for how banks assess and finance green energy projects, particularly those that are technically feasible but not yet commercially viable.

title: 'Mplus Market Pulse - 07 Oct 2026
body: 'MY: Tracking positive regional performance, the local bourse continued to trade higher ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement. Market breadth turned positive, with 667 gainers against 456 losers. Sector-wise, both Technology and Healthcare outperformed with gains exceeding 3%, while Financial Services lagged the most. US: Wall Street logged solid gains with the Dow rising 0.5%, the S&P 500 gaining 0.6% to reach new record highs, and the Nasdaq jumping 0.5% higher as US 10-year Treasury yields slipped to 5.3%, while Brent crude hovered at USD100/bbl amid potential Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions. US: Wall Street may retain its constructive tone after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached fresh record highs, helped by easing Treasury yields and stabilising oil prices. AI remains a key earnings driver, with Marvell (MRVL) in focus after raising its FY2028 revenue target to USD20.0bn and guiding FY2031 revenue to USD70.0- 90.0bn, underpinned by strong demand for custom AI silicon and optical connectivity. Meanwhile, Salesforce (CRM) could benefit from renewed strength in enterprise software as concerns over AI disruption ease, while Meta (META) continues expanding its AI offerings to businesses through its Meta Enterprise Platform. MY: On the local front, the FBMKLCI is poised to track global tech strength, with sentiment supported by robust earnings and positioning ahead of Budget 2027 on 9 October. The semiconductor and automation space could remain in focus, with semiconductors, AI and high-value investments among the Government's key priorities. UWC stands out after 4QFY26 revenue jumped 71.1% to RM186.2m, while net profit surged 129.7%, reflecting stronger semiconductor demand and project execution. VITROX could also attract interest following a sharp improvement in 2QFY26 earnings. Meanwhile, TOPGLOV offers an earnings-driven play after 4QFY26 revenue rose 39.7% to RM1.25bn, with net profit surging 352.6%. Selective buying provided a minor lift to the local bourse on Tuesday, though the benchmark remains capped under key moving averages. Downside risk persists as the MACD histogram stays below zero while the RSI is oversold below 30. Key resistance is pegged at 1,648-1,663, while support is expected around 1,603-1,618. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200m (RM817m). (The Edge) Zetrix AI Bhd (ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314m in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. (The Edge) Top Glove Corporation Bhd (TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78bn pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72bn in FY2026. The group's net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63m in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83m in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25bn. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15. For the full FY2026, Top Glove's net profit nearly tripled to RM307.96m. Revenue increased 21% to RM4.23bn as volume grew close to 30%. (The Edge) Samaiden Group Bhd (SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99- megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238m. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. (The Edge) Mesiniaga Bhd (MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3m contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider's earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. (The Edge) Scientex Bhd (SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580m to boost the property developer's land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. (The Edge) Dialog Group Bhd (DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand's 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. (The Edge) Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (ELRIDGE) is investing RM45m to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45m in cash. (The Edge) Insights Analytics Bhd (IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44m subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. (The Edge) Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm's shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intra-day low of 24 sen as more than 83m shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140m. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. (The Edge) ZenaTech, Inc. (ZENA) advanced its ZenaDrone 2000 heavy-lift autonomous interceptor through prototype assembly in Sharjah, UAE, targeting Q1 2027 flight testing. Built with a 40 kg payload capacity and four-plus hours of hover endurance, the gasoline-powered platform will validate autonomous navigation and multi-target threat pursuit alongside its Interceptor P-1 system. (Investing.com) ONEOK, Inc. (OKE) completed its acquisition of Brazos Midstream's Permian Midland Basin natural gas gathering and processing assets for approximately USD 4.425 billion in cash. The transaction more than doubles ONEOK's Midland Basin processing capacity to roughly 2.3 billion cubic feet per day and adds 600,000 dedicated acres backed by long-term fixed-fee contracts averaging over 12 years. Market breadth turned positive, with 667 gainers against 456 losers. Sector-wise, both Technology and Healthcare outperformed with gains exceeding 3%, while Financial Services lagged the most. US: Wall Street logged solid gains with the Dow rising 0.5%, the S&P 500 gaining 0.6% to reach new record highs, and the Nasdaq jumping 0.5% higher as US 10-year Treasury yields slipped to 5.3%, while Brent crude hovered at USD100/bbl amid potential Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions. US: Wall Street may retain its constructive tone after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached fresh record highs, helped by easing Treasury yields and stabilising oil prices. AI remains a key earnings driver, with Marvell (MRVL) in focus after raising its FY2028 revenue target to USD20.0bn and guiding FY2031 revenue to USD70.0- 90.0bn, underpinned by strong demand for custom AI silicon and optical connectivity. Meanwhile, Salesforce (CRM) could benefit from renewed strength in enterprise software as concerns over AI disruption ease, while Meta (META) continues expanding its AI offerings to businesses through its Meta Enterprise Platform. MY: On the local front, the FBMKLCI is poised to track global tech strength, with sentiment supported by robust earnings and positioning ahead of Budget 2027 on 9 October. The semiconductor and automation space could remain in focus, with semiconductors, AI and high-value investments among the Government's key priorities. UWC stands out after 4QFY26 revenue jumped 71.1% to RM186.2m, while net profit surged 129.7%, reflecting stronger semiconductor demand and project execution. VITROX could also attract interest following a sharp improvement in 2QFY26 earnings. Meanwhile, TOPGLOV offers an earnings-driven play after 4QFY26 revenue rose 39.7% to RM1.25bn, with net profit surging 352.6%. Selective buying provided a minor lift to the local bourse on Tuesday, though the benchmark remains capped under key moving averages. Downside risk persists as the MACD histogram stays below zero while the RSI is oversold below 30. Key resistance is pegged at 1,648-1,663, while support is expected around 1,603-1,618. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200m (RM817m). (The Edge) Zetrix AI Bhd (ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314m in unpaid remittances. title: 'KLIA T2 Retail Occupancy Holds Steady Despite Airline Capacity Cuts
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 29): Visitors walking through Kuala Lumpur International Airport's Terminal 2 (KLIA T2) will notice hoardings — temporary boards and barricades put up around shops that are empty or under renovation — at several areas of its retail section. While these appear just as airlines trim flight capacity to counter soaring fuel costs, the boarded-up spaces do not necessarily signal a broader downturn in the terminal's retail performance. Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB), which operates KLIA and 38 other airports in the country, said tenant occupancy at KLIA T2 remained resilient despite a decline in passenger traffic. Commercial occupancy stood at 93% currently, up from 92% a year earlier. “Some of the hoardings currently visible within the terminal are part of a planned reconfiguration of space to improve passenger processing and circulation,” MAHB said in an email response to questions from The Edge Malaysia. The airport operator said some commercial areas were being repurposed for this purpose, with several outlets in the affected areas scheduled to be progressively phased out by the end of the year. MAHB declined to disclose tenant level sales or passenger spending, citing commercial sensitivity. It said commercial performance depended on factors beyond passenger volumes, including passenger profiles, outlet locations, retail categories and the performance of individual businesses. The clarification comes as airlines operating from KLIA T2 contend with a sharp rise in fuel costs and weaker capacity on some routes since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February. Global average jet fuel prices reached US$194.90 per barrel in the week ended Sept 18 — up 116.5% from a year earlier — according to data from Platts and S&P Global. Airlines have been particularly exposed to the increase because fuel typically accounts for between 30% and 50% of their operating costs. Budget carriers such as AirAsia Group Bhd (KL:AAGB) and Batik Air Malaysia, which remain largely unhedged, have been hit by the volatility in the jet fuel market. In response, some airlines have cut capacity by as much as 30% since April to limit fuel consumption and contain costs. AirAsia is the largest airline tenant at KLIA T2. Other carriers operating from the terminal include Scoot, Spring Airlines, Cebu Pacific Airways, Lucky Air, Qingdao Airlines and Shandong Airlines. On Sept 18, AirAsia said it had reduced capacity by 20% to 25% in the third quarter, traditionally a weaker travel period. It expects to restore capacity towards pre-Iran war levels in the fourth quarter, when year-end travel demand typically strengthens. The impact of the capacity cuts have been reflected in KLIA T2's footfall. While total passenger traffic across KLIA rose 2.1% year-on-year to 41.95 million between January and August this year, the headline growth masks a clear divergence between its two terminals. Traffic at Terminal 1 climbed roughly 8% y-o-y to 24.46 million passengers, but T2 saw numbers fall 5% y-o-y to 17.48 million over the same period. Still, MAHB said traffic had begun to recover from June. Total KLIA passenger movements increased from 4.7 million in June to five million in July and 5.2 million in August, with both terminals recording improvements. At T2, passenger numbers rose from 1.83 million in June to 1.86 million in July, and 1.98 million in August. “While T2 traffic remains below the corresponding period in 2025, the recent trend shows a gradual recovery following the capacity reductions experienced during the middle of the year,” MAHB said. The airport operator said it would continue to monitor airline capacity, passenger traffic and commercial performance. It added that the recent recovery in passenger movements provides a more balanced picture of conditions at both KLIA terminals than the weaker traffic figures recorded earlier in the year. For airlines, however, fuel remains a significant pressure point. In a Sept 21 report, Maybank Investment Bank Research estimated that every US$1 increase in the price of jet fuel could reduce AirAsia’s earnings by RM75 million. AirAsia shares closed half a sen or 0.94% lower at 52.5 sen on Monday, valuing the group at RM1.76 billion. The stock has fallen about 70% since the start of the year. title: 'DNB completes RM5.2 bil syndicated Islamic financing ahead of ownership transition
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth. In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding. The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL:CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL:YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026. Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment. The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission. DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets. DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider. In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing. AmInvestment Bank was the financial adviser to DNB. title: 'RHB Pay simplifies how businesses manage digital payments
body:
'
Launch partners of RHB Pay commemorate the launch of Malaysia's first bank-owned unified online payment gateway.

Malaysia’s first bank-owned unified payment platform helps businesses bring multiple payment channels together, with faster settlement and simpler reconciliation.

For businesses, getting paid is only one part of the equation. Knowing where the money is, when it will reach the bank account and how to reconcile transactions can be just as important, particularly for businesses handling high volumes of digital payments.

Launched by RHB Bank Berhad, RHB Pay is Malaysia’s first bank-owned unified online payment platform, bringing payment collection, settlement and reconciliation onto a single platform. Built on RHB’s banking infrastructure with bank-grade security, it is designed to give businesses greater control over their collections and cash flow.

Digital payments have established themselves as an integral part of modern commerce. Malaysia recorded more than 18 billion electronic payment transactions in 2025, highlighting the growing role of digital payments in how businesses collect and manage money.

For merchants, the proposition is straightforward: accept payments through cards, FPX, DuitNow and e-wallets through one integration, while having a consolidated view of transactions and settlement.

But the move to digital payments can also bring its own set of operational headaches, particularly for mid-sized corporates and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that have to manage separate systems, logins, settlement files and reconciliation processes across different payment methods. That fragmentation adds friction as businesses shift more volume away from cash handling and its associated costs.

RHB Pay is designed to reduce that fragmentation by bringing the different payment channels into one integration layer. This means merchants do not have to build and maintain separate integrations for each payment method they offer.

The unified platform also simplifies onboarding and verification across payment channels, reducing the time and effort required for merchants to get started. It is also designed to accommodate new digital payment channels as they emerge, without requiring merchants to build another integration each time.

Getting cash into the business faster

A payment platform’s value does not end when a customer completes a transaction. Settlement is where many merchants feel the biggest strain. How quickly funds reach their accounts can have a direct bearing on working capital and day-to-day cash flow.

With some third-party payment arrangements, funds can take one to five days to reach the merchant’s bank account, depending on the payment method and settlement arrangement. By comparison, RHB Pay is designed to provide real-time or next-day settlement directly into the merchant’s RHB account, giving them faster access to their collections.

For those operating on tight cash cycles, that can mean having funds available sooner for supplier payments, inventory replenishment and other operating expenses.

Less time spent matching transactions

Reconciliation is another area where payment fragmentation can create additional work. Traditionally, businesses spend considerable time and manual effort matching end-of-day sales across disparate e-wallet portals, card terminals and bank transfers. RHB Pay consolidates these transactions into a standardised report within its portal, which can be reconciled directly against the merchant's bank statement. This gives businesses a single view of their collections, rather than having to pull information from multiple payment platforms and match them manually.

A consolidated view becomes more useful as payment volumes grow, giving businesses greater visibility over their cash position while reducing the administrative work involved in reconciliation.

Built on banking infrastructure

Security and reliability become increasingly important as more payment collections move online. RHB Pay is built on RHB’s banking infrastructure, operating within the bank’s governance and regulatory framework. This gives merchants added assurance over the handling of their funds and payment data.

RHB Pay also leverages Malaysia’s wider payments infrastructure, including PayNet’s national payment rails such as FPX and DuitNow, alongside technology partners across the payments ecosystem.

The platform’s roadmap will see further use of AI and data analytics, including in areas such as reconciliation, fraud management, cash flow forecasting and financial planning.

More than a payment gateway

For RHB, the strategic opportunity extends beyond payment processing fees.

By bringing merchants’ payment collections into the bank, RHB can deepen its relationship with businesses through the transaction flows that run through their day-to-day operations. These flows can also support the bank’s broader transaction banking proposition, including deposits, working capital financing and other financial solutions.

According to research by CIMB Securities, RHB’s enhanced transaction banking capability could lift the Group’s net interest margin (NIM) by about five basis points over time, equivalent to an estimated RM170 million in additional net interest income.

Rather than focusing solely on generating payment gateway fees, RHB’s core strategy centres on capturing merchant transaction flows to build low-cost, sticky Current Account and Savings Account (CASA) deposits. These transaction-linked deposits are embedded in merchants’ daily cash flow cycles, which can make them stickier than deposits acquired primarily through interest rate pricing.

The ability to better understand businesses’ transaction flows could also support more targeted working capital financing and other banking solutions as businesses grow, while creating opportunities for broader fee income and cross-selling.

CIMB Securities maintains a “Buy” rating on RHB Bank with a target price of RM9.20, citing the potential for the bank to strengthen its CASA franchise and deliver capital-efficient earnings growth, alongside its dividend yield and Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital position.

Building for the next phase of digital payments

The immediate benefits are simpler payment collection, faster access to funds and less time spent on reconciliation.

RHB also sees scope to build on this with AI and data analytics, with potential applications in cost management, cash flow planning, fraud management and other operational areas.

The longer-term opportunity is to give businesses greater visibility into the money flowing through their operations, rather than simply providing another channel to accept payments.

title: 'Felda’s road ahead in the spotlight
body: 'Felda’s road ahead in the spotlight KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Seven years after Malaysians were made aware of the problems confronting the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), the institution is once again at a crossroads. Felda, which has the largest plantation footprint in the country and has helped improve the livelihoods of more than 100,000 original settlers and their families, is undergoing another strategic review amid concerns over its long-term sustainability. An interim report on the Felda Group Strategic Roadmap 2025-2030 (HTF 30) was submitted last month by the Special Committee on the Strategic Plan for Felda Group to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Among the proposals under consideration is a redefinition of Felda’s mandate, including a review of the Land Development Act that governs the agency, as the committee monitors actions taken following the 2019 Felda White Paper, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The review comes as the highly indebted entity grapples with crucial replanting costs that could reach RM900 million annually, on top of more than RM900 million in financing costs currently borne by the government. Felda oversees some 870,000 hectares (ha) of land, of which 490,000ha was allocated to settlers, 330,000ha to Felda’s commercial plantations — later placed under FGV Holdings Bhd — and another 50,000ha for village development. Fragmented and ineffective management of the land and operations, together with questionable transactions and investments, resulted in heavy losses despite Felda receiving billions of ringgit from the listing of its commercial arm, then known as Felda Global Ventures Holdings Bhd. By 2017, Felda’s borrowings had ballooned to RM12.1 billion from just RM100 million in 2007. In 2023, the government guaranteed and agreed to service Felda’s RM9.9 billion sukuk, issued to fund the RM3.7 billion privatisation of FGV to consolidate its estate operations, as well as Felda and settlers’ debt. But more needs to be done before those efforts bear fruit. Huge capital needed to become sustainable In 2012, Felda raised RM6 billion through the offer for sale of FGV shares during the latter’s initial public offering, while FGV itself raised RM4.5 billion from investors. In total, the exercise raised RM10.5 billion. Instead of directing more of those proceeds towards critical needs such as replanting, the 2019 Felda White Paper found that RM4.6 billion, or 76% of Felda’s IPO proceeds, went towards what it described as “unproductive spending”, while another RM1.4 billion was channelled into investments that failed to generate returns. The spending included RM1.69 billion in special payments to settlers, RM550 million in one-off contributions to state governments, RM400 million in loans for settlers’ house extensions, RM406 million to redeem FGV shares and RM177 million in listing expenses. FGV, meanwhile, spent RM3.3 billion, or 73% of its RM4.5 billion in IPO proceeds, on investments and developments that did not generate satisfactory returns. FGV, which leased Felda’s plantation land, also failed to achieve the yields Felda had projected, leaving the agency with an earnings shortfall. Following FGV’s privatisation, Felda is looking at consolidating the management of its commercial estates and settlers’ land. But that alone will not resolve the underlying balance-sheet problem, particularly the heavy capital requirements needed to keep the estates productive. The role of Felda Beyond its plantation operations, Felda bears significant social obligations to settlers, including spending on housing, infrastructure and income support for up to five years during the replanting cycle. Today, the families of Felda settlers span as many as six generations and number about 2.8 million people. In many respects, Felda has fulfilled its original mandate of opening up rural land and developing communities alongside settlers, about 95% of whom have received titles to their land. Without a clear framework for its future model, the institution’s role and the financial obligations that come with it risk continuing to be shaped by factors beyond its core mandate, particularly when political considerations intersect with policy during periods of adjustment. Any new roadmap will therefore have to define more clearly where Felda’s commercial responsibilities end and its social obligations begin, and how each should be funded. Felda’s troubled investments Felda was in better shape before the mismanagement that followed the windfall from FGV’s listing, when the institution was earning around RM3 billion a year. There are also arguments that greater provisions should have been made for replanting, which is central to sustaining its core operations. Poor investment decisions, however, turned Felda’s fortunes upside down in less than a decade. A forensic audit found RM2.2 billion in asset impairments from eight transactions undertaken by Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) between 2010 and 2018 — equivalent to half of their initial RM4.4 billion investment value. Among them were PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk, the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, and several London properties. One of the largest was Felda’s US$505.4 million acquisition of a 37% non-controlling stake in Eagle High Plantations in 2016 at a premium, resulting in an impairment loss of RM1.576 billion in 2017. Its London property purchases also came under scrutiny over discrepancies between reported acquisition prices and amounts received by vendors, while some properties saw their values fall sharply soon after acquisition. KLVC, meanwhile, remains the subject of a legal dispute between Felda and developer Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd (SPSB) over the development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak. Former FIC chief executive officer Mohd Zaid Abdul Jalil has also been charged with two counts of cheating the company’s board, which allegedly resulted in the ownership of 16 land parcels being transferred from Felda to SPSB. title: 'Daily Newswatch - 30 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI ended 1.6% lower at 1,644 points on Tuesday, hitting a ninemonth low as broad-based selling pressure weighed on the market. Sentiment was dampened by rising oil prices and bond yields hovering near multi-year highs, as investors braced for interest rates to remain elevated for longer. Financial Services (-1.7%), Transportation & Logistics (-1.5%) and Property (-1.4%) led sectoral declines, dragged by RHB Bank (-3.8%), Tenaga Nasional (-1.5%) and Nestle Malaysia (-1.2%). Market breadth remained weak, with 684 losers against 412 gainers, while 556 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Tuesday as elevated oil prices and US Treasury yields weighed on risk appetite. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 0.3% to 6,870.8, Taiwan’s TAIEX declined 0.8% to 47,632, Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.6% to 65,481.3, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng eased 0.5% to 24,523.6. In contrast, the Shanghai Composite gained 0.2% to 3,830.5. In South Korea, losses were recorded in LG Energy Solution (-3.30%), Hyundai Motor (-1.55%), Hanwha Aerospace (-2.22%), and Doosan Enerbility (-2.93%), while weaker domestic business sentiment added to the cautious tone as the BOK’s business sentiment index fell for the first time in three months in September. In China, gains were led by Guangzhou Automobile (+10.0%), Greenland Holdings (+6.4%) and China Fortune (+6.2%), supported by expectations of increased government bond issuance in 4Q26 as Beijing steps up fiscal support to shore up slowing economic growth and weak domestic demand. European equities edged higher on Tuesday as easing oil prices reduced inflation concerns and lowered expectations of an imminent ECB rate hike. The STOXX 50 gained 0.3%, while the STOXX 600 was little changed, with technology stocks leading gains. ASML jumped 4%, while energy stocks weakened as Brent crude eased toward USD104/barrel. Julius Baer surged 7%, while Lindt & Sprüngli fell 8.4% after cutting its sales-growth outlook. US stock indices closed mostly lower on Tuesday as rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices weighed on sentiment. The S&P 500 fell 0.2% and the Dow shed 130 points, while the Nasdaq gained 0.2%. The 10-year yield climbed to levels last seen in 2007, while the 30-year yield hovered near 2004 highs. Tech stocks were mixed, with Alphabet and Nvidia down 0.5% and 0.7%, respectively, while Meta, Oracle, Broadcom and Micron gained 3.2%, 4.0%, 1.6% and 1.0%, respectively, amid optimism following plans for an Anthropic IPO. US: 10 Year Treasury Note Yield to 5.28% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note resumed its climb to 5.28% on Tuesday, holding at 2007 highs, while the 30-year rate surpassed 5.6% to touch a 2002 dot-com bust level. Global government bonds have come under pressure as Middle East-driven oil price gains fuel expectations that central banks, including the Federal Reserve, will raise interest rates further.
