full_text: 'Daily Newswatch - 30 Sep 2026. 'The FBM KLCI ended 1.6% lower at 1,644 points on Tuesday, hitting a ninemonth low as broad-based selling pressure weighed on the market. Sentiment was dampened by rising oil prices and bond yields hovering near multi-year highs, as investors braced for interest rates to remain elevated for longer. Financial Services (-1.7%), Transportation & Logistics (-1.5%) and Property (-1.4%) led sectoral declines, dragged by RHB Bank (-3.8%), Tenaga Nasional (-1.5%) and Nestle Malaysia (-1.2%). Market breadth remained weak, with 684 losers against 412 gainers, while 556 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Tuesday as elevated oil prices and US Treasury yields weighed on risk appetite. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 0.3% to 6,870.8, Taiwan’s TAIEX declined 0.8% to 47,632, Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.6% to 65,481.3, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng eased 0.5% to 24,523.6. In contrast, the Shanghai Composite gained 0.2% to 3,830.5. In South Korea, losses were recorded in LG Energy Solution (-3.30%), Hyundai Motor (-1.55%), Hanwha Aerospace (-2.22%), and Doosan Enerbility (-2.93%), while weaker domestic business sentiment added to the cautious tone as the BOK’s business sentiment index fell for the first time in three months in September. In China, gains were led by Guangzhou Automobile (+10.0%), Greenland Holdings (+6.4%) and China Fortune (+6.2%), supported by expectations of increased government bond issuance in 4Q26 as Beijing steps up fiscal support to shore up slowing economic growth and weak domestic demand. European equities edged higher on Tuesday as easing oil prices reduced inflation concerns and lowered expectations of an imminent ECB rate hike. The STOXX 50 gained 0.3%, while the STOXX 600 was little changed, with technology stocks leading gains. ASML jumped 4%, while energy stocks weakened as Brent crude eased toward USD104/barrel. Julius Baer surged 7%, while Lindt & Sprüngli fell 8.4% after cutting its sales-growth outlook. US stock indices closed mostly lower on Tuesday as rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices weighed on sentiment. The S&P 500 fell 0.2% and the Dow shed 130 points, while the Nasdaq gained 0.2%. The 10-year yield climbed to levels last seen in 2007, while the 30-year yield hovered near 2004 highs. Tech stocks were mixed, with Alphabet and Nvidia down 0.5% and 0.7%, respectively, while Meta, Oracle, Broadcom and Micron gained 3.2%, 4.0%, 1.6% and 1.0%, respectively, amid optimism following plans for an Anthropic IPO. US: 10 Year Treasury Note Yield to 5.28% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note resumed its climb to 5.28% on Tuesday, holding at 2007 highs, while the 30-year rate surpassed 5.6% to touch a 2002 dot-com bust level. Global government bonds have come under pressure as Middle East-driven oil price gains fuel expectations that central banks, including the Federal Reserve, will raise interest rates further. Swaps traders are pricing in nearly a full percentage point of Fed rate hikes over the coming year. In the US, strong economic activity, along with concerns over large fiscal deficits and rising government debt, is also weighing on the bond market. (Trading Economics) US: Job openings fall in August; layoffs remain low US consumer confidence fell in September to the lowest level since 2014 as pessimism grew about the economy and the labour market. The Conference Board’s gauge of confidence decreased 6.7 points to 81.9 after a downward revision to the prior month, data released Tuesday showed. The median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists was 89. (Bloomberg) US: Consumer confidence plunges to lowest level since 2014 Job openings, a measure of labour demand, had dropped by 256,000 to 7.079 million by the last day of August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said in its Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or Jolts report, on Tuesday. Data for July was revised higher to show 7.335 million vacancies instead of the previously reported 7.271 million. (Reuters) US: Gold ticks up after hitting over seven-week low; US data in focus Gold prices edged higher on Tuesday after hitting a more-than-seven-week low in the previous session, as investors watch for US economic data that could offer clues on the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate outlook. Spot gold rose 0.6% to US$4,140.10 (RM16,899.89) per ounce, as of 0856 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since Aug 5 on Monday. US gold futures gained 0.1% to US$4,171.60. (Reuters) US: Bond market is getting closer to sounding alarm on US economy The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the sixmonth US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (Bloomberg) EU: Area Economic Sentiment Indicator The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the six-month US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (European Commission) UK: Set to pay highest yield since 1999 at 10-year bond auction The UK government is set to pay the highest yield since 1999 at an upcoming auction of 10-year debt, as investors demand additional premiums to compensate for persistent inflation and the prospect of spending increases in next month’s budget. Britain’s Debt Management Office is scheduled to sell up to £4.25 billion (US$5.6 billion or RM22.95 billion) of 4.875% coupon bonds maturing in July 2036 on Tuesday. (Bloomberg) UK: Mortgage approvals fall to 32-month low as loan costs bite Demand for home loans unexpectedly fell in August as higher borrowing costs triggered by the Iran war put off prospective homebuyers. The number of mortgage approvals fell for a second consecutive month to 54,918 from a downwardly revised 55,928 in July, the Bank of England said Tuesday. It was the lowest figure since December 2023. Economists expected no change. (Reuters) CN: Said to offer cheap loans to help state firms pay overdue bills China has started offering low-cost funding to help local government-affiliated firms settle unpaid bills, according to people familiar with the matter, expanding efforts to mend corporate balance sheets and remove one of the biggest bottlenecks for investment. The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) set up a new relending facility to provide cheap capital to commercial and policy banks, they said, asking not to be identified discussing a decision that hasn’t been made public. (Reuters) CN: Expands targeted lending to bolster economy, cuts PSL rate China announced several steps to encourage banks to lend to targeted sectors including infrastructure and technology, in an attempt to juice growth after a months-long slowdown in the economy. The People’s Bank of China increased the quota for a relending programme supporting technological innovation and equipment upgrades by 200 billion yuan (US$28 billion or RM114 billion), bringing the total to 1.4 trillion yuan, according to a statement Tuesday. (Bloomberg) CN: Offers mortgage subsidies to boost ailing property sector China will subsidise mortgage interest payments for first-time homebuyers nationwide, as policymakers step up efforts to revive the housing market amid a prolonged property downturn and slowing economic growth. First-home buyers will get subsidies worth an annualised rate of one percentage point of the mortgage principal, according to a Ministry of Finance statement late Tuesday. To qualify, homes must be 120 square meters or smaller and priced at 1.5 million yuan (US$224,000 or RM913,337) or less. (Bloomberg) CN: Signals economic stimulus to counter worsening slowdown China has given its strongest signal yet that it will move with greater urgency to counter a deepening slowdown, as the government promised to introduce new measures to support the economy and study policies to stabilise the reeling property market. The authorities will “put in place a package of practical and effective additional policies” as they seek to “strengthen counter-cyclical adjustments” to achieve this year’s economic and social development goals, according to a statement issued after a Monday meeting of the State Council, China’s cabinet chaired by Premier Li Qiang. (Bloomberg) SK: Monthly Industrial Statistics, August 2026 South Korea’s industrial production unexpectedly dropped 4.8% month-on-month in August 2026, falling well short of market expectations for a 0.5% increase and reversing an upwardly revised 0.5% rise in July. It was the first decline in industrial production in three months and the steepest decline since May 2020, with manufacturing contracting 5.1% (vs 0.4% in July), weighed down by the automobile industry. Manufacturing production contracted for both domestic (-5.5% vs 1.2%) and overseas (-0.2% vs 4.1%) demand. (Statistics Korea) JP: August factory output falls 1.7% month-on-month Japan's factory output fell 1.7% in August from the previous month, versus the median market forecast for a 1.7% rise, government dat showed on Wednesday. Manufacturers surveyed by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry expect seasonally adjusted output to increase 3.2% in September and grow 3.1% in October.(Reuters) JP: Retail Sales Growth Below Forecasts Retail sales in Japan increased 2.7% year-on-year in August 2026, below market expectations for a 3.3% rise and slowing from a downwardly revised 3.7% growth in the previous month. It was the sixth consecutive month of growth in retail activity, mainly boosted by a 17.7% surge in motor vehicle sales. (Ministry of Economy Trade & Industry (METI) MY: Set to land nearly RM90m in film, TV deals through Australia, South Korea co-productions - minister Malaysia is set to tap international opportunities in the creative industry through two co-production projects with industry partners in Australia and South Korea worth a combined US$22 million (about RM89.7 million) over the next two years. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the collaboration, spearheaded by OMG Studios, would involve Australia’s Madman Entertainment and South Korea’s Greenpatch Studio. (The Edge) MY: No decision yet on new minimum wage, says HR minister The government has yet to make a decision regarding the new minimum wage rate, including claims that it would be raised to RM2,000, RM2,100, or RM2,200, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan. He said any announcement concerning the new rate would only be made after obtaining approval from the Cabinet, including Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. (The Edge) MY: Palm oil may gain premium over soyoil in 2027 on supply risks, says industry official Palm oil could trade at a premium to soyoil in 2027 as El Niño threatens production and rising biodiesel demand in top exporter Indonesia tightens supplies, a senior industry official told Reuters on Tuesday. Palm oil supplies are expected to tighten in 2027 as El Niño-induced dry weather weighs on production, potentially lifting prices above rival soyoil, as happened in 2024, Eddy Martono, chairman of the Indonesian Palm Oil Association, said. (Reuters) MY: Needs 25,000 rail sector workers by 2030 - deputy HR minister Malaysia needs 25,000 workers in rail technology and operations by 2030, said Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan. He said the Human Resources Ministry, through the Manpower Department, is developing suitable Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) courses to meet this goal. (Bernama) MY: BNM considering greater risk-taking to support energy transition Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) is considering allowing financial institutions more room to take on higher risks responsibly as part of efforts to support the energy transition, governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said. He said the central bank is reviewing how regulations could be better calibrated to support the transition, including by giving financial institutions greater flexibility to take on higher risks within an acceptable risk appetite. (Bernama) MY: GLICs, GLCs to catalyse economy with RM120b investments under GEAR-uP over 2024-2028 - Amir Hamzah Government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) are stepping up their role in developing the domestic economy, backed by an additional RM120 billion under the GEAR-uP initiative over 2024-2028. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said more than RM20 billion was invested last year, with a similar level expected this year. (Bernama) CRESNDO: 2Q net profit surges over fourfold to RM70.6m, declares 2 sen dividend Crescendo Corp Bhd's net profit more than quadrupled in the second quarter due to the sale of two parcels of land in Johor to data centre developers. In its bourse filing on Tuesday, the property developer said the sale of the parcels in Kota Cemerlang Industrial Park (KCIP) and Nusa Cemerlang Industrial Park (NCIP) made up a bulk of its net profit for the quarter under review. (The Star) MNC: Wireless switches out advisers for RM83m capital reduction exercise MNC Wireless Bhd said on Tuesday it is terminating the services of its advisers for its proposed capital reduction exercise of RM83 million. In a circular on Bursa Malaysia, the mobile and digital solutions company said the termination of Sierac Corporate Advisers Sdn Bhd was based on a mutual agreement between the two parties. It did not elaborate on the reason for the termination. (The Edge) UMSINT: Seeks to raise RM450m via placement for Penang, Vietnam and Singapore expansion UMS Integration Ltd is seeking to raise up to RM450 million through a placement representing 5.63% of its enlarged share capital, to fund projects in Penang, Malaysia, as well as expansion in Vietnam and Singapore. It plans to issue up to 52.94 million new shares at RM8.50 each, the dual-listed integrated high-precision engineering and manufacturing firm said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday. (The Edge) UMSINT: Shares suspended on Bursa pending announcement Trading in the shares of integrated high-precision engineering and manufacturing firm UMS Integration Ltd (KL:UMSINT) was suspended on Tuesday pending an announcement. The trading suspension took effect from 9am to 5pm on Tuesday at the company’s request, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia. (The Edge) SNS: 2Q profit down 37% on higher costs and delivery delays, declares 0.25 sen dividend SNS Network Technology Bhd's second-quarter net profit declined 37.3%, weighed down by lower sales and higher expenses. The ICT solutions provider also saw its revenue slashed by half as supplier-side shortages hampered on-time delivery to customers — a trend also observed in the previous quarter (1QFY2027). (The Edge) GAMUDA: SD Guthrie consortium to build solar plant in Perak for US tech firm A consortium between Gamuda Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd and Gentari Sdn Bhd have inked an agreement with a US-based technology company for a proposed 680-megawatt renewable energy project in Perak. The project, which includes a four-hour battery energy storage system, will achieve commercial operation in 2029 and run for 21 years, according to an exchange filing. The project may generate more than RM10 billion in gross revenue over the offtake period, according to Gamuda’s estimates. (The Edge) SCIENTX: To acquire 70% stake in China plastic packaging maker for RM101.5m Scientex Bhd is acquiring a 70% stake in Hunan Changcheng Mint New Material Technology Co Ltd (Mintpack), a plastic packaging manufacturer in China’s Hunan province, for 167.3 million yuan (RM101.5 million), as it seeks to expand its footprint in China. The packaging manufacturer and property developer said its wholly owned unit Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd has entered into an equity interest sale and purchase agreement with Mintpack founder Tan Cui Fang and Hunan Changcheng Tianyi Information Technology Co Ltd (Tianyi) to acquire the stake. (The Edge) AEONCR: 2Q net profit drops 18% on higher impairment losses AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd reported a 18% drop in its net profit for the second quarter amid higher impairment losses on financing receivables. Net profit for the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (2QFY2027) fell to RM59.30 million from RM72.23 million a year earlier, according to the consumer financing provider's exchange filing on Tuesday. (The Edge) VS: Records first full year loss on lower orders VS Industry Bhd posted its first full-year loss since it was listed in 1998, dragged down by lower orders placed by key customers amid weak global consumer sentiment. The electronic manufacturing services provider registered a net loss of RM53.8 million for its financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY2026), compared with a net profit of RM36.7 million in the previous year, as revenue fell 3.62% to RM3.65 billion from RM3.79 billion. (The Edge) FAIRE: Johor-based Faire files ACE Market IPO to expand into industrial properties Johor-based property developer Faire Bhd is seeking to list on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia in order to raise funds for its expansion into industrial properties. According to its draft prospectus published on Tuesday, Faire said it intends to strengthen its presence in Johor by expanding its project portfolio and broadening into industrial properties. Its existing portfolio comprises terrace, cluster, semi-detached and detached houses, as well as shop units and shop houses. (The Edge) APOLLO: 1Q profit up nearly 10% on strong sales Confectioner Apollo Food Holdings Bhd posted a 9.5% increase in net profit for its first quarter as stronger sales helped offset higher costs. For the three months ended July 31, 2026 (1QFY2027), net profit rose to RM6.96 million from RM6.36 million the previous year, while revenue grew 13.36% to RM73.76 million from RM65.07 million, driven by higher export sales, particularly in its core Indonesian market. (The Edge) GAMUDA: Annual net profit tops RM1b for second straight year, order book hits RM61b Gamuda Bhd closed its financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY2026) with a net profit topping RM1 billion for the second straight year, as its construction order book reached a record high. Full-year net profit stood at RM1.05 billion, up 5% from RM1 billion a year earlier, Gamuda said in a bourse filing on Tuesday. Revenue rose 15% year on year to RM18.3 billion from RM16 billion. (The Edge) SUPERMX: Co-founders agree to wind up holding firm, to hold stakes directly Supermax Corp Bhd co-founders Datuk Seri Stanley Thai and wife Datuk Wira Cheryl Tan Bee Geok have resolved the legal wrangle over their company that holds their interests in the glove manufacturer. The settleent entitles the pair to a full disbursement of dividends from Supermax Holdings Sdn Bhd (SHSB) according to their shareholdings of 42.5% to Tan and 57.5% to Thai. SHSB holds 40.3% in Supermax Corp, the RM1.2 billion glove maker that the now estranged married couple founded in 1987. (The Edge) VITROX: Rides AI-fuelled complexity to new highs ViTrox Corp Bhd broke earnings record in its latest quarter and the growth momentum will continue. “This year, our numbers will double. We believe strong growth momentum will continue into the next few years,” co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng tells The Edge in an interview at its campus in Batu Kawan Industrial Park in Seberang Prai, Penang. (The Edge) VITROX: Planting the seeds for Malaysia's tech ecosystem FOR Datuk Chu Jenn Weng, solving Malaysia’s talent shortage in the technology sector means taking steps long before graduates enter the workforce. That conviction led ViTrox Corp Bhd to build an education arm designed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry needs, giving students early exposure to real-world manufacturing problems, advanced equipment and working engineers. (The Edge) AAGB: Needs no bailout, says Fernandes, as fuel shock puts liquidity under scrutiny AIRASIA Group Bhd, which is seeking to raise up to US$1 billion (RM4.08 billion) on the international debt market, has dismissed concerns about its liquidity, with co-founder and adviser Tan Sri Tony Fernandes insisting that the low-cost carrier remains financially resilient. “We do not need a rescue, bailout or whatever,” he said, adding that the group was “good at managing cash” and “strong in liquidity” and had more than RM1 billion available. (The Edge) VANTNRG: Stays in the black in 2Q on lower forex losses, finance costs Vantris Energy Bhd remained in the black for a fourth consecutive quarter, helped by lower foreign exchange losses and finance costs following the completion of its restructuring exercise, as well as the absence of a favourable insurance claim recorded a year earlier. These gains were partly offset by lower contributions from its engineering and construction, and drilling segments. (The Edge) NWE: To tap into changing health trends among younger consumers NWE Resources Group Bhd is looking to tap into changing health and wellness trends among younger consumers with six new health food formulations as part of its business expansion for its initial public offering (IPO). Speaking to reporters after the launch of its prospectus on Tuesday, executive director Tan Chor Han said the group had identified areas including sleep deprivation, stress, eye-care, joint health, colon care and gut health, for which younger people are increasingly turning to health food products in order to address these concerns. (The Edge) KGB: Bags RM172m engineering job for Sarawak manufacturing facility Kelington Group Bhd has secured a RM172 million contract for engineering and early-stage infrastructure development works for an advanced data storage manufacturing facility in Kuching, Sarawak. In a bourse filing on Tuesday, the engineering group said its unit, Kelington Technologies Sdn Bhd, accepted the letter of award on Sept 25 from a manufacturing company located at the Sama Jaya Free Industrial Zone. (The Edge) YINSON: Posts 27% rise in 2Q amid absence of refinancing charge Yinson Holdings Bhd said its net profit for the second quarter grew 26.7% year-on-year amid the absence of a one-off charge related to the refinancing of the floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) Maria Quitéria project financing loan. Net profit for the three months ended July 31, 2026 (2QFY2027) rose to RM128 million from RM101 million in the previous year’s corresponding quarter. (The Edge) JFTECH: Partner Shenzhen HFC surges more than eightfold on debut Shenzhen HFC Co Ltd, which operates an advanced thermal and shielding materials manufacturing facility in Malaysia in partnership with Main Market-listed JF Technology Bhd, saw its shares surge more than eightfold in their Shenzhen Stock Exchange debut. Shares of HFC jumped to around 600 yuan from their initial public offering (IPO) price of 76.86 yuan per share at the opening bell, before hitting an intraday high of 630.01 yuan. The stock then retreated to 613 yuan at Tuesday’s noon break. (The Edge) KLK: Coalfields Retail Park scheduled to reach 100% occupancy by 1Q2027 KLK Land Sdn Bhd's newly soft-opened Coalfields Retail Park in Sungai Buloh is scheduled to achieve 100% occupancy by 1Q2027, according to a press statement issued on Tuesday. The lifestyle retail hub, developed by the property development arm of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, spans 21 acres with approximately one million square feet of gross built-up area. (The Edge) SERNKOU: To wind down loss-making plywood manufacturing unit Sern Kou Resources Bud said on Tuesday that its will wind down its plywood manufacturing unit due to continuous quarterly losses since the financial year ended June 30, 2024 (FY2024). In its bourse filing on Tuesday, the wood products manufacturer said there was no reasonable expectation that the financial performance of Sern Kou Plywood Sdn Bhd (SKPW), its 51%-owned subsidiary, will improve in the foreseeable future. title: 'Maybank wins Best Company at Bursa Malaysia Investor Relations Awards 2026 | Maybank
body: 'Other achievements include Best Company in IR by Sector, Best Financial Reporting and Best CEO in IR Maybank, one of ASEAN’s leading financial services institutions, achieved a landmark recognition at Bursa Malaysia’s inaugural Investor Relations Awards 2026, securing four awards across company and leadership categories. The recognition reflects Maybank’s focus on long term shareholder value and the role of investor relations in advocating trust, transparency and market confidence, in line with Malaysia’s broader MYValueUp agenda. Leading the Group’s achievements is its recognition as Best Company in IR (Overall), setting a strong standard for investor relations excellence. It highlights Maybank’s clear equity story and consistent engagements with its stakeholders, underpinned by a strong track record of delivery. Maybank wins Best Company at Bursa Malaysia Investor Relations Awards 2026 Supporting this track record, Maybank’s investor relations function is positioned as a strategic role that connects the Group’s strategy, performance and value creation priorities with the expectations of the investment community. This two-way engagement enables investors to gain greater clarity on Maybank’s strategic direction, while helping management remain cognisant of shareholder expectations. At the sectoral level, Maybank was recognised as Best Company in IR by Sector (Large Cap). As Bursa Malaysia’s largest listed company and the nation's largest financial institution, Maybank recognises its responsibility to uphold high standards of market accessibility and investor engagement. This is reflected in a structured and differentiated engagement model, which includes thematic Investor Days, quarterly briefings, non‑deal roadshows, investor conferences and targeted sessions; enabling sustained dialogue and deeper understanding of the Group’s strategy, performance and outlook. Maybank also took home Best Financial Reporting, affirming its commitment to clarity, depth and consistency of its disclosures, going beyond mandatory filings to provide clear, data‑driven insights that support informed investor and analyst decision making. The Group’s integrated reporting suites provided a comprehensive view of financial performance, business drivers, capital and liquidity position, asset quality, dividends and outlook. title: 'FBM KLCI expansion to improve sector diversification: CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) to 50 constituents is expected to materially improve sector diversification. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said the expanded benchmark will have lower exposure to financial services and utilities, while increasing representation across industrials, technology, consumer discretionary, energy, real estate and consumer staples. This is consistent with CIMB Securities' previous simulation, which estimated that the 20 new constituents could account for around 15.6 per cent of the expanded index at full inclusion. "We remain positive on the structural change as it should create a more representative Malaysian benchmark and broaden institutional exposure beyond the existing large-cap sectors," it said in a note. Meanwhile, CIMB Securities said FTSE clarified that full market capitalisation determines final stock selection, while free float determines index weights. Since passive FBM KLCI-tracking assets under management are relatively small and inclusion is phased at 50 per cent in December 2026 and 100 per cent in June 2027, the firm expects the near-term flow impact to be more stock-specific than market-wide. "The FBM70 will be reduced to 50 constituents and renamed FBM Mid-cap Index on Dec 21 while the FBM100 remains unchanged. "Derivatives specifications remain unchanged, while FTSE Russell is reviewing a relaxation of the fast-entry threshold for large initial public offerings," it said. CIMB Securities expects details to be reflected in an updated FTSE Bursa Malaysia Index Series Ground Rules notice once finalised at the end of this month. "Key dates to watch are the Nov 23, 2026 ranking cut-off, Dec 3, 2026 constituent announcement and Dec 21, 2026 first-stage inclusion, with full inclusion on June 21, 2027," it added.

title: 'M’sians Camp Outside Maybank From 4am For BTS Card, Turning It Into Mini ‘Concert’ | WeirdKaya
body: 'What time would you wake up for a debit card? For some Malaysian BTS fans, apparently before the sun even comes up. Fans were seen gathering outside Maybank’s Shah Alam Main Branch in Seksyen 14 from the early hours of the morning after the Maybank Visa | BTS WORLD TOUR ‘ARIRANG’ Debit Card became available on Sept. 23. And judging from the crowd, you might have mistaken the bank for a BTS concert venue. Fans arrived as early as 4am A staff member shared photos of the situation on Threads, showing BTS fans waiting both inside and outside the Shah Alam branch. In one post, he jokingly asked: “Is this a bank or a BTS concert?” Speaking to WeirdKaya, Irfan confirmed that the scenes were taken at the Shah Alam Main Branch in Seksyen 14. According to him, customers had already begun showing up at around 3am to 4am. Day 2 also saw fans ‘camping’ outside In another update the following morning, Irfan shared a photo showing a group of customers sitting outside the bank while waiting for it to open. The photo showed fans sitting along the walkway with their bags and belongings, looking more like they were waiting for concert doors to open than preparing for a banking transaction. More photos shared by Irfan showed a packed banking hall, with customers holding BTS themed items while staff attended to the crowd. The atmosphere even prompted Irfan, who handles the branch’s speaker, to ask customers what songs they wanted him to play for the day.

title: 'Banned from Sarawak – but why?
body: 'Kua Kia Soong In August 2007, I arrived at Kuching airport to officiate at a graduation ceremony for teachers trained by New Era College, where I was then principal. I was not carrying drugs. I was not wanted by the police. I was not entering Sarawak to organise an insurrection. I was there to attend an educational ceremony. Yet I was stopped at immigration and told that I was not allowed to enter Sarawak. After I persistently asked why, I was apparently told that I was on a blacklist because of my “anti-logging activities”. I was then put on a flight back to Kuala Lumpur. The contemporary report of the incident records that I had been an active campaigner against the Bakun Dam and had participated in a fact-finding mission concerning Indigenous people displaced from the Bakun area. Think about that for a moment. A Malaysian citizen, travelling from one part of Malaysia to another, was effectively told: you are not welcome in this part of your own country because you opposed the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous communities. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Nearly 20 years later, the question remains: Sarawak may have the constitutional power to do this. But does it have the moral right? The legal argument is not the whole argument Let me be clear. I am not disputing that Sarawak possesses special immigration powers. These powers are rooted in the constitutional arrangements surrounding the formation of Malaysia. Article 161E protects certain constitutional safeguards for Sabah and Sarawak, while Part VII of the Immigration Act 1959/63 provides the statutory framework for immigration control. The Sarawak government itself describes immigration autonomy as an entrenched constitutional right. But there is a much more important question: what is that power for? The justification traditionally associated with Sarawak’s immigration safeguards was the protection of the state’s special interests – including its economy, employment, security, cultural identity and the interests of its people. The constitutional autonomy was not created as a blank cheque for excluding inconvenient Malaysians. There is a world of difference between immigration autonomy and political exclusion. If the purpose of the special powers is to protect Sarawak and Sarawakians, what exactly was Sarawak being protected from when I was turned away? A former Malaysian MP and college principal coming to officiate at a teachers’ graduation? Or an environmental campaigner who had criticised the Bakun Dam and logging? If the latter was the real reason, then the issue is no longer simply immigration administration. It becomes an issue of freedom of expression, political dissent and the abuse of administrative power. What exactly was my crime? My supposed offence was to oppose the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous people. During the 1990s, I was active in opposing the Bakun Dam project. I participated in a fact-finding mission to investigate the conditions of Indigenous people displaced to Sungai Asap. So apparently, in the strange political dictionary of the time, defending forests and Indigenous communities could make a Malaysian an undesirable person in Malaysia. What next? The irony is almost unbearable. Sarawak has every reason to be proud of its unique constitutional position. But autonomy should mean more democracy, not less. It should mean that Sarawakians have greater control over their land, resources, culture and political affairs. It should not mean that the state acquires a constitutional moat around itself so that environmentalists, human rights defenders, academics or political critics can be kept outside. Otherwise, autonomy becomes a very peculiar proposition: the more autonomous the government becomes, the less accountable it becomes to citizens exercising their democratic rights. That cannot be the meaning of Malaysia’s federal bargain. Apparently, the issue has not disappeared. Just last week, Sahabat Alam Malaysia president Meenakshi Raman was denied entry into Sarawak. A Sarawak deputy minister said the state is not required to give advance notice to people barred from entering and that the relevant immigration laws give the state authority to stop people from entering. Civil society groups have called for the reasons and basis for the restriction to be disclosed. Thus, nearly two decades after my own experience, environmental defenders are still encountering the same question: Who gets to decide who is sufficiently ‘Sarawakian’ in spirit to be allowed into Sarawak? But what about international human rights? Here, the distinction between legal authority and international legitimacy becomes crucial. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights states in Article 13(2) that everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights goes further in Article 12(4): “No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of the right to enter his own country.” There is, however, an important qualification: Malaysia has not ratified the covenant. Therefore, I would not argue that my exclusion in 2007 was automatically a violation of a treaty obligation binding Malaysia under the covenant. But that does not make the international human rights question disappear. The Universal Declaration remains one of the foundational statements of the international human rights system. And Malaysia has repeatedly presented itself internationally as a country committed to human rights, democracy and the rule of law. The question is therefore not merely was Sarawak legally entitled to do it? It is: was it consistent with the human rights values Malaysia claims to uphold? And that is a much harder question for the authorities to answer. Sarawak’s forests are not a Sarawak-only issue. There is another irony here. Logging, Indigenous rights, biodiversity and environmental destruction are not purely ‘state matters’ in any meaningful moral sense. The rainforest does not stop at the Kuching immigration counter. Neither does climate change. Nor does the destruction of biodiversity. Nor does the displacement of Indigenous peoples. A Malaysian citizen concerned about what happens to Sarawak’s forests is not a foreign agitator. He is a Malaysian citizen concerned about Malaysia. And if Sarawak’s forests are part of Malaysia’s natural heritage, why should Malaysians be treated as outsiders for expressing concern about them? Indeed, the more internationally connected environmental politics becomes, the more absurd such restrictions appear. Malaysia wants to attract international investment. It wants to promote Sarawak as an ecological and cultural destination. It wants to speak proudly about sustainable development and Indigenous communities. Yet an environmental campaigner can apparently arrive at an airport and be told: Turn around. Your concern for our forests is unwelcome here. What kind of message does that send to the world? A constitutional right should come with a constitutional conscience. That is a question of political morality. And it is a question that Sarawak – and Malaysia – still has to answer. Nearly 20 years after I was turned away at Kuching airport, I am still waiting for a convincing answer. – Suaram Dr Kua Kia Soong, a former MP and former director of the human rights group Suaram. title: 'DNB lengkapkan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion bagi menyokong fasa seterusnya pertumbuhan 5G - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) melengkapkan pembiayaan berjangka Islam secara sindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan pembiayaan jangka panjang syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa pertumbuhan seterusnya dwirangkaian 5G . DNB dalam kenyataan berkata pembiayaan itu akan memudahkan perancangan keluar Menteri Kewangan Diperbadankan (MOF Inc) sebagai pemegang saham biasa dan peralihan kepada pemilikan sama rata dalam kalangan pemegang saham pengendali rangkaian mudah alihnya, iaitu CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd. Peralihan pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026, manakala MOF Inc akan mengekalkan saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan negara. Pembiayaan berkenaan turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula kemudahan kredit pusingan DNB yang dijamin kerajaan dan tamat tempoh pada 29 September, selain mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang bagi menyokong pertumbuhan syarikat. Penyempurnaan pembiayaan itu bertepatan dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100MHz dalam jalur 3.3–3.4GHz serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum 240MHz DNB kepada penetapan spektrum. Penetapan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober. Menurut DNB, blok spektrum 240MHz tersebut akan meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, selain menyokong teknologi termasuk Massive MIMO, pengagregatan pembawa, 5G Advanced dan keupayaan rangkaian dipacu kecerdasan buatan. title: 'Life Water Poised for Further Growth as Capacity and Distribution Expand
body: 'Life Water Berhad (“Life Water”, Bursa: LWSABAH, 5328) is positioned for continued growth, backed by spare production capacity, an expanding distribution network in Sabah and rising demand for its bottled water and carbonated drinks. The Sabah-based beverage maker reported a 19.9% increase in revenue to RM207.31 million for the financial year ended 30 June 2026, while net profit grew 23.8% to RM37.15 million. Momentum strengthened towards the year-end, with fourth-quarter revenue up 28% year on year to RM57.01 million and net profit up 21% to RM10.95 million. The growth was driven by higher drinking water sales volumes, a price revision implemented in May 2026, seasonally stronger demand during hot weather and wider distribution. Gross margin reached 49.3% in the second quarter, supported by better operational efficiency and lower raw material costs. Life Water is the leading bottled water and carbonated drinks brand in Sabah and held about 11% of Malaysia’s bottled water market at the time of its Main Market listing in November 2024. Since then, its share price has risen from the IPO price of RM0.65 to around RM1.66, giving it a market capitalisation of about RM785 million. A key factor behind the group’s growth outlook is its available capacity. Following new production lines funded by its IPO, including the expansion of the Sandakan Sibuga Plant 1 completed in June 2025, annual drinking water capacity stands at about 626 million litres, with utilisation of around 60%. This allows the group to meet higher demand without major new investment. The group is also investing in reaching more customers. Its truck fleet has grown from 70 to 90 units, and new distribution centres are being established in Tawau, Lahad Datu and Keningau, extending coverage to Sabah’s east coast and interior. In December 2025, Life Water began supplying Sabah’s largest mini-market chain, which operates about 280 outlets. Its products are also included in the government’s Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programme. External conditions are supportive. Visit Malaysia Year 2026 is drawing more visitors to Sabah, lifting demand from hotels, food service outlets and retailers, while bottled water demand during the dry season typically runs about 30% above normal. Beyond Sabah, the group has been building its presence in Sarawak and Brunei through local distributors. CIMB Securities has a Buy call on Life Water with a target price of RM2.05, and forecasts core net profit to grow at a compound annual rate of 22.9% from FY2025 to FY2028.

title: 'Sabah Energy Corp raises RM350 mil in maiden sukuk, Maybank IB appointed as adviser
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 17): Sabah Energy Corporation Sdn Bhd (SEC) has raised RM350 million through its maiden sukuk issuance under a RM3 billion sukuk wakalah programme.

The issuance was announced in a joint statement with Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK). 

The sukuk was rated AAA with a stable outlook by RAM Rating Services Bhd and was priced through book-building, with demand reaching 2.2 times the amount offered.

Maybank Investment Bank Bhd was appointed as the sole principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager and sustainability structure adviser, as well as shariah adviser and facility agent. 

“This landmark issuance broadens and diversifies SEC's access to long-term ringgit funding while raising the profile of both SEC and Sabah among domestic and international institutional investors. The strong over-subscription reflects investors' confidence in SEC's credit strength and growth trajectory," said Maybank IB chief executive officer Michael Oh-Lau.

Maybank said the issuance gives the Sabah state-owned energy company a longer-term funding source as it plans investments across its energy businesses, including natural gas infrastructure, power generation and renewable energy.

SEC said the funding platform will support its strategic roadmap called PETA (Pelan Strategik dan Hala Tuju) 2030, which covers the expansion of its gas and infrastructure operations, power generation and renewable energy activities, as well as investments across Sabah's energy value chain.

“In turn, this supports the broader outcomes envisaged under SERAMP 2040: stronger energy security, a faster energy transition and more reliable supply for Sabah," said SEC group chief executive officer Datuk Adzmir Abd Rahman. 

SEC has been Sabah's sole natural gas aggregator, transporter and distributor since its corporatisation in 1997. 

It has since expanded into power generation, renewable energy and offshore oil and gas support services.

title: 'Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google
body: 'This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026  Transitioning from the entertainment industry to the food and beverage (F&B) sector is not easy, but when comedian Ajak Shiro heard his child express a desire to start a fried chicken business, he thought of making the idea a reality.  Ajak, whose real name is Mohd Hanaffi Razak, looked for a business partner. This ended up being Aliey Othman, an F&B industry veteran with 20 years of experience and involvement in many notable brands.  Starting with fried chicken as the foundation, their conversation gradually evolved into a discussion on nasi padang, a Minangkabau meal of steamed rice and a variety of side dishes.  “In Malaysia, nasi padang hasn’t become mainstream yet. Moreover, it is considered expensive, so we thought of coming up with a large-scale nasi padang brand, but with low prices,” says Ajak.  He went on to start Babah Ventures Sdn Bhd (BBV) and opened its first stall, named Bumbu Babah, at a food court in Giant Batu Caves in November 2024. There are now more than 50 outlets across Peninsular Malaysia and the company is on track to reaching 60 outlets this year.  Delivering affordable and accessible food is important to Ajak. So, a plate of nasi padang can be priced as low as RM9.90. The uncompromised value the company offers in terms of price point and flavour has become Bumbu Babah’s unique selling point, he says.  “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price,” says Ajak.  To accelerate its next stage of growth, BBV will launch an equity crowdfunding (ECF) campaign on pitchIN to attract institutional investors with its numbers, create a fundraising exercise with customer engagement and possibly look at fast-tracking to an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028 at the earliest. On the ECF platform itself, the company aims to raise between RM5 million and RM20 million, with shares issued at RM10 each.  BBV plans to allocate 40% of the funds from the ECF campaign to acquiring its top-performing licensed outlets. Two activities, the setting up of corporate-owned outlets in malls and supporting the rollout of the new concept, will be allocated 25% each, while the final 10% will go to enhancing technology and its working capital.  “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price.” - Ajak (Photo by BBV)  Behind the quick expansion  The business has been able to expand quickly because its licensees have shown interest in opening more outlets.  “We call it a licensed-and-managed concept because we are very mindful that we don’t want licensees or franchisees to run the outlets their own way and steer away from the standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, we came up with a structure where they provide the funding and become a passive investor in the outlet,” says BBV corporate finance manager Chan Eu-Jinn.  This is how the system works: the licensee fully owns the outlet, but BBV continues to run it as if it belonged to the company. BBV also charges a management fee based on a percentage of the licensed outlet’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) on a monthly basis. “If the outlet is not profitable, we do not charge the management fee, so we have to ensure that it is run properly,” he notes.  There are currently seven corporate-owned Bumbu Babah outlets. The remaining outlets are owned by licensees.  BBV aims to continue expanding, but with a strategy centred more on mall outlets.  “Our MyTown, Melawati Mall and IOI City Mall outlets are doing well, but we are still not in a lot of the major malls in the market yet. With the funds raised, we can then invest in this,” says Chan.  BBV acknowledges that F&B brands have a tendency to overexpand, and Chan says the company has addressed this by setting a target number of outlets for Bumbu Babah restaurants so as to retain operational quality. “When we hit our target number [we may look more into] maintenance, but we will not be growing for the sake of opening and then cannibalising ourselves.”  Bumbu Babah was also able to grow quickly with the introduction of a centralised kitchen to ensure the quality of the food across its licensed outlets remains consistent.  Chan says the curry, sambal, proteins and sides are prepared in advance and sent straight to the outlets. This contributes to the efficiency of its operations, as the staff are able to run the basic equipment at the outlets by following the SOPs.  Ajak plans to develop more offerings beyond Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang menu. Reflecting this resolve is BBV’s recent collaboration with local music group KRU to open a fine-casual-dining restaurant called KRU Cafe.  “We will also have stalls where we will have food menus that include Chinese and Indian food. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says.  On solid operational and financial ground  Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees.  For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million.  This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds.  The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak.  The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits.  Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%.  The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings.  “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says.  Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper.  “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says.  On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy.  The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says.  Zooming in on the numbers  Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low.  However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth.  BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027.  Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year.  “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says.  “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.”  Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met.  However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL: KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO.  “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low.  Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover.  This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders.  Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income.  “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan.  Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group.  Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up.  This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements.  “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan.  Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk.  Key-figure risk  Tan also cautions that BBV’s reliance on Ajak as a key figure of the company could potentially be a risk as the marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue can fluctuate depending on public sentiment on a celebrity’s status.  “A reputational event or attention shift affecting the founder would remove that structural cost advantage and force a step-up in marketing spend, compressing margins, and the concentration is compounded by reliance on a single brand and cuisine, as the newer concepts remain unproven,” he says.  Furthermore, the F&B space has a low barrier to entry and is fashion-sensitive, which can influence the performance of same-store sales over time.  Seasonality is another factor, with business during the Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidil Fitri festive periods running about 50% and 30% respectively below typical months. Tan indicates that the quarterly figures vary too much to be simply multiplied and predict the full year’s results.  Nevertheless, Chan says momentum is picking up, especially after the RON95 petrol subsidy cap was restored to 300 litres a month from 200 litres, improving sentiment and driving a spike in revenue.  Additionally, Bumbu Babah recently began listing on Grab exclusively and saw an increase of almost 20% at most of the outlets on the food delivery side without cannibalising dine-in traffic.  “Last year, we were focusing a lot on dine-in. We didn’t want to have an additional delivery business affect our operations. So we’re confident that even with all these challenges, we’re on track to hitting our target this year,” says Chan.  BBV’s ECF campaign is currently at the pre-live stage. Investors can visit pitchIN’s website to find out more information and make an investment.

There are now more than 50 outlets across Peninsular Malaysia and the company is on track to reaching 60 outlets this year.  Delivering affordable and accessible food is important to Ajak. So, a plate of nasi padang can be priced as low as RM9.90. The uncompromised value the company offers in terms of price point and flavour has become Bumbu Babah’s unique selling point, he says.  “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price,” says Ajak.  To accelerate its next stage of growth, BBV will launch an equity crowdfunding (ECF) campaign on pitchIN to attract institutional investors with its numbers, create a fundraising exercise with customer engagement and possibly look at fast-tracking to an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028 at the earliest. On the ECF platform itself, the company aims to raise between RM5 million and RM20 million, with shares issued at RM10 each.  BBV plans to allocate 40% of the funds from the ECF campaign to acquiring its top-performing licensed outlets. Two activities, the setting up of corporate-owned outlets in malls and supporting the rollout of the new concept, will be allocated 25% each, while the final 10% will go to enhancing technology and its working capital.  “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price.” - Ajak (Photo by BBV)  Behind the quick expansion  The business has been able to expand quickly because its licensees have shown interest in opening more outlets.  “We call it a licensed-and-managed concept because we are very mindful that we don’t want licensees or franchisees to run the outlets their own way and steer away from the standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, we came up with a structure where they provide the funding and become a passive investor in the outlet,” says BBV corporate finance manager Chan Eu-Jinn.  This is how the system works: the licensee fully owns the outlet, but BBV continues to run it as if it belonged to the company. BBV also charges a management fee based on a percentage of the licensed outlet’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) on a monthly basis. “If the outlet is not profitable, we do not charge the management fee, so we have to ensure that it is run properly,” he notes.  There are currently seven corporate-owned Bumbu Babah outlets. The remaining outlets are owned by licensees.  BBV aims to continue expanding, but with a strategy centred more on mall outlets.  “Our MyTown, Melawati Mall and IOI City Mall outlets are doing well, but we are still not in a lot of the major malls in the market yet. With the funds raised, we can then invest in this,” says Chan.  BBV acknowledges that F&B brands have a tendency to overexpand, and Chan says the company has addressed this by setting a target number of outlets for Bumbu Babah restaurants so as to retain operational quality. “When we hit our target number [we may look more into] maintenance, but we will not be growing for the sake of opening and then cannibalising ourselves.”  Bumbu Babah was also able to grow quickly with the introduction of a centralised kitchen to ensure the quality of the food across its licensed outlets remains consistent.  Chan says the curry, sambal, proteins and sides are prepared in advance and sent straight to the outlets. This contributes to the efficiency of its operations, as the staff are able to run the basic equipment at the outlets by following the SOPs.  Ajak plans to develop more offerings beyond Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang menu. Reflecting this resolve is BBV’s recent collaboration with local music group KRU to open a fine-casual-dining restaurant called KRU Cafe.  “We will also have stalls where we will have food menus that include Chinese and Indian food. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says.  On solid operational and financial ground  Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees.  For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million.  This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds.  The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak.  The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits.  Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%.  The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings.  “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says.  Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper.  “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says.  On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy.  The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says.  Zooming in on the numbers  Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low.  However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth.  BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027.  Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year.  “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says.  “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.”  Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met.  However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL: KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO.  “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low.  Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover.  This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders.  Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income.  “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan.  Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group.  Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up.  This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements.  “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan.  Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk.  Key-figure risk  Tan also cautions that BBV’s reliance on Ajak as a key figure of the company could potentially be a risk as the marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue can fluctuate depending on public sentiment on a celebrity’s status.  “A reputational event or attention shift affecting the founder would remove that structural cost advantage and force a step-up in marketing spend, compressing margins, and the concentration is compounded by reliance on a single brand and cuisine, as the newer concepts remain unproven,” he says.  Furthermore, the F&B space has a low barrier to entry and is fashion-sensitive, which can influence the performance of same-store sales over time.  Seasonality is another factor, with business during the Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidil Fitri festive periods running about 50% and 30% respectively below typical months. Tan indicates that the quarterly figures vary too much to be simply multiplied and predict the full year’s results.  Nevertheless, Chan says momentum is picking up, especially after the RON95 petrol subsidy cap was restored to 300 litres a month from 200 litres, improving sentiment and driving a spike in revenue.  Additionally, Bumbu Babah recently began listing on Grab exclusively and saw an increase of almost 20% at most of the outlets on the food delivery side without cannibalising dine-in traffic.  “Last year, we were focusing a lot on dine-in. We didn’t want to have an additional delivery business affect our operations. So we’re confident that even with all these challenges, we’re on track to hitting our target this year,” says Chan.  BBV’s ECF campaign is currently at the pre-live stage. Investors can visit pitchIN’s website to find out more information and make an investment.

title: 'RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26 | KLSE Screener
body: 'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank Bhd’s management has shared that there is sufficient runway to reposition the bank’s portfolio and capitalise on market opportunities for the fourth quarter ending Dec 31, 2026 (4Q26) after surging Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields weigh on non- interest income (NOII) in 3Q26. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research said the bank’s near-term outlook faces pressure from elevated MGS yields, which could weigh on its 3Q26 NOII, but that management appears less downbeat on the 4Q26 outlook should MGS yields stabilise or retrace. The research house, which recently met with the bank’s management, maintained a “hold” call and target price of RM8 based on implied one time 2027 price to book, as most near-term drivers have been baked in, with no stronger immediate catalyst. “We came away from a recent meeting with RHB’s management feeling neutral on its earnings trajectory and asset quality outlook,” it said, with weaker trading income largely inevitable given the limited runway for recovery during 3Q26. ...

title: 'Bursa ends higher on bargain-hunting
body: 'However, the rebound lacked momentum as broader Asian markets remained under pressure ahead of key US labour market data. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.51 points, or 0.03%, to 1,630.87 from yesterday’s close of 1,630.36. The benchmark index, which opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, moved between 1,630.63 and 1,640.78 throughout the trading session. Market breadth turned positive with gainers leading losers 585 to 541, while 558 counters were unchanged, 1,089 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover climbed to 4.23 billion units, worth RM2.70 billion, from 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion on Thursday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the recent sell-off had brought valuations of selected blue-chip stocks to more attractive levels, which could encourage gradual accumulation and provide some downside support. However, he said investors continued to adopt a defensive stance as bond yields and crude oil prices remained elevated. “As for the local bourse, we remain cautious despite today’s rebound, as external headwinds are likely to keep market volatility elevated,” Thong told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose seven sen to RM10.02, Public Bank fell one sen to RM4.66, CIMB eased four sen to RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional firmed up six sen to RM12.96, and IHH Healthcare added 10 sen to RM7.80. In active trade, Zetrix AI erased five sen to 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources remained unchanged at 18 sen, JCY International jumped 10.5 sen to 66 sen, VS Industry ticked up two sen to 29 sen, and PUC went up one sen to 4.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries rose from RM1.28 to RM42.40, UWC rallied 47 sen to RM7.57, Vitrox bounced 46 sen to RM10.46, United Plantations gained 42 sen to RM31.38, and UMS Integration improved 38 sen to RM9.03. Top losers were led by Nestle, which reduced 48 sen to RM89.52; Kuala Lumpur Kepong fell 42 sen to RM21; Enra trimmed 25.5 sen to 72.5 sen, while Allianz Malaysia and Hong Leong Bank both shaved off 20 sen to RM20.80 and RM22.64, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 122.94 points to 17,481.93, the FBM Emas Index added 27.04 points to 12,170.57, and the FBM Top 100 Index advanced 24.52 points to 11,957.68. The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 47.31 points to 12,060.32, and the FBM ACE Index improved 46.49 points to 5,529.46. Sector-wise, the industrial products and services index edged up 0.79 of a point to 178.52, while the energy index shaved off 1.98 points to 833.03. The financial services index eased 20.40 points to 19,040.51, and the plantation index grew 29.97 points to 9,056.55. The Main Market volume increased to 2.67 billion units worth RM2.34 billion from 1.82 billion units valued at RM2.42 billion on Thursday. Warrants turnover soared to 973.40 million units worth RM160.21 million from 618.78 million units valued at RM72.71 million previously. The ACE Market volume eased to 593.05 million units valued at RM205.21 million from 650.13 million units worth RM226.92 million yesterday. Meanwhile, consumer products and services counters accounted for 241.01 million shares traded on the Main Market, industrial products and services (266.57 million), construction (183.37 million), technology (1.41 billion), financial services (50.26 million), property (152.37 million), plantation (19.73 million), real estate investment trusts (15.78 million), closed-end fund (214,200), energy (99.69 million), healthcare (103.06 million), telecommunications and media (28.89 million), transportation and logistics (47.35 million), utilities (46.61 million), and business trusts (119,600).
