title: 'CIMB IB says Malaysia could widen corporate tax base for Budget 2027, cut old deductions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Malaysia could widen its corporate tax base by reviewing special and double deductions that have been in place for two to three decades, and remove deductions that no longer serve their original purpose, said CIMB Investment Bank. CIMB IB said, citing KPMG senior adviser on tax policy Dr Verrinderjeet Singh during a discussion, that the removal of selected deductions could lead to the government collecting more revenue while creating room for a lower headline corporate tax rate. “His [Verrinderjeet] proposal is selective: investment incentives remain important for attracting businesses, but their benefits need closer scrutiny. He links Malaysia’s shift towards outcome-based incentives to its response to Global Minimum Tax,” said CIMB IB. It added, “Their effectiveness will depend on monitoring whether investors deliver the intended economic benefits”. Malaysia’s headline corporate income tax rate is currently 24%, but the amount of tax companies ultimately pay is also affected by deductions, exemptions and investment incentives. On major tax changes, CIMB IB said Malaysia is unlikely to introduce new tax changes in Budget 2027, with stronger collection from existing taxes and a wider tax base offering the main scope for raising government revenue. The government is expected to focus on improving tax collection, particularly by bringing more businesses into the tax net and identifying income that is not fully reported. Smaller businesses are likely to offer more room for additional collections, as larger companies are already more visible to the tax authorities, said CIMB IB. “His central message was that stronger collection and targeted refinements to existing taxes offer the main near-term revenue opportunities. Against a continued focus on cost-of-living support and the social agenda, he expects few substantial tax changes in the coming budget,” said CIMB IB. E-invoicing could help identify unreported taxable activity, although smaller businesses face additional compliance and technology costs. CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet expects participation to broaden as economic conditions improve. CIMB IB also sees scope for greater use of data analytics by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) and Customs to identify businesses and income outside the existing tax net. On indirect taxes, CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet does not expect the goods and services tax (GST) to return in Budget 2027. Instead, the focus is likely to remain on improving the existing sales and service tax (SST). SST is estimated to cover about 78% to 80% of goods and services, approaching the breadth of the former GST regime. CIMB said broader exemptions for business inputs could reduce the cascading of tax costs through supply chains, although this would come at the cost of lower tax receipts. Veerinderjeet also does not expect an increase in the 2% dividend tax on annual dividend income above RM100,000, an extension of capital gains tax to listed shares or a further increase in the 30% top personal income tax rate in Budget 2027, according to the note. “Dr Veerinderjeet argues that the government should ‘sweat our assets’ through better collection, supported by greater investment in tax agency analytics. These efforts can deliver incremental gains, while broader personal, corporate and indirect tax bases offer scope to lift tax-to-GDP towards 15% over time,” said CIMB IB economists. Veerinderjeet estimates only 15% to 16% of the workforce currently pays personal income tax, with low wages limiting the number of taxpayers. Higher wages would therefore be important in expanding the personal income tax base. Budget 2027 is expected to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends lower, KLCI slides 1.26pc on cautious sentiment
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Bursa Malaysia ended lower on Thursday amid continued selling pressure, tracking a mixed and cautious Wall Street performance overnight. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 20.81 points, or 1.26 per cent, to 1,630.36 from Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. The benchmark index, which opened 1.30 points weaker at 1,649.87, moved between 1,630.10 and 1,649.87 throughout the trading session. Market breadth was also negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 750 to 342, while 495 counters were unchanged, 1,186 untraded and 12 suspended. Turnover fell to 3.1 billion units, worth RM2.7 billion, from 3.63 billion units valued at RM3.62 billion on Wednesday. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said sentiment was cautious, reinforced by weaker domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign selling. He said softer manufacturing momentum and portfolio rotation in global markets kept the benchmark index under pressure, with domestic institutional demand remaining an important counterbalance to persistent foreign outflows. Earlier, the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) edged slightly below the neutral 50.0 mark, falling to 49.9 in September from 50.2 in August, marking the first decline in four months after a sustained period of improvement. Regionally, the S&P Global ASEAN Manufacturing PMI fell to 52.1 in September from 52.3 in August. Among the heavyweight counters, Maybank fell four sen to RM9.95, while Public Bank lost three sen to RM4.67, and CIMB dropped 10 sen to RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional declined six sen to RM12.90, and IHH Healthcare erased 13 sen to RM7.70. In active trade, Zetrix AI firmed half a sen to 16.5 sen, VS Industry dipped one sen to 27 sen, and Jaks Resources slipped 2.5 sen to 18 sen. ACE Market debutant GB Bond slumped 4.5 sen to 20.5 sen, and HHRG gained half a sen to 16.5 sen. title: 'Penang’s draft plan could open more of its hills to building
body: 'Kam Suan Pheng and Evelyn Teh “Rising from the sea in that first light of dawn that touches reality with a gentle charm, the Penang hills provide an unforgettable landmark for the visitor sailing in by sea. From the palm-fringed bays as yet a black indistinguishable smudge, the eye follows the flowing silhouette of the hills.” – Margaret Khor, The Straits Times Annual, 1960. Ask anyone who has crossed on the ferry, or driven over the bridge at dusk, and they will say the same: that green line of hills is how you know you are home. That silhouette is part of what makes Penang, Penang. Beyond the scenery, the hills are part of the island’s natural public infrastructure – one that is rarely counted. They hold soil, absorb and direct water, support forests and wildlife, and shape the landscape where we and our ancestors have lived. That landscape could change significantly if the draft State Structure Plan 2040 is adopted without stronger safeguards for hill and slope development. First, some background. The current Penang State Structure Plan 2030 does not allow development on land 76 metres (250 feet) or more above sea level, or on slopes of 25 degrees or steeper. There are limited exceptions for infrastructure and utilities. The limit is stricter than the national guideline. The state set it because it recognised how fragile, and how important, the island’s hills are. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member The 2030 plan reads: Sebarang Pembangunan Perbandaran Yang Meliputi Pembangunan Skim Perumahan Perhotelan Resort Perdagangan Perindustrian Dan Sebarang Struktur Bangunan Footprint Tidak Dibenarkan Di Kawasan:- - Kawasan Tanah Tinggi Yang Diwartakan Di Bawah Akta Pemeliharaan Tanah 1960 Akta 385 Atau - Sebarang Tanah Yang Berada Pada Aras 76 meter 250 kaki) Ke Atas Atau - Kawasan Berkecerunan 25 Darjah Ke Atas KECUALI Bagi Pemajuan Infrastruktur Dan Utiliti Dibenarkan Dengan Syarat Syarat Dari Jabatan Teknikal Yang Berkaitan Dan Mendapat Kelulusan Dari Pihak Berkuasa Negeri. In English: Any urban development, including housing schemes, hotels, resorts, commercial or industrial developments, and any building structures, is prohibited in the following areas: - Highland areas gazetted under the Land Conservation Act 1960 (Act 385); or - Any land situated at an elevation of 76 metres (250 feet) or higher; or - Areas with a slope gradient of 25 degrees or steeper; EXCEPT for infrastructure and utility developments, which are permitted subject to conditions imposed by relevant technical departments and approval from the State Authority. The key concern The state government rolled out a new draft 2040 plan in August – years before 2030 arrives. It will overwrite the previous version. The draft 2040 plan says: Strategi Perancangan PS3-1: Pembangunan di Kawasan Khusus yang Melebihi Ketinggian 76 meter. Strategi ini merupakan pendekatan perancangan yang memberi kelonggaran kawalan ketinggian bangunan secara terpilih di kawasan khas yang telah dikenal pasti sebagai kawasan tumpuan pembangunan strategik. Pelaksanaan strategi ini bertujuan mengoptimumkan penggunaan tanah yang terhad melalui pembangunan berintensiti tinggi dan berorientasikan transit, khususnya di pusat bandar, koridor ekonomi dan kawasan pesisir yang mempunyai kapasiti infrastruktur mencukupi. Walau bagaimanapun, kebenaran ini tertakluk kepada penilaian teknikal terperinci seperti kesesuaian guna tanah, nisbah plot, kawalan kepadatan, impak trafik, keselamatan, impak visual serta pematuhan kepada garis panduan reka bentuk bandar dan kajian impak alam sekitar. In English: Planning Strategy PS3-1: Development in Special Areas Exceeding a Height of 76 Metres. This strategy is a planning approach that allows for selective flexibility regarding building height controls in specific areas identified as strategic development hubs. Its implementation aims to optimize limited land use through high-intensity, transit-oriented development, particularly in city centres, economic corridors and coastal areas with adequate infrastructure capacity. However, such approval is subject to detailed technical assessments covering aspects such as land-use suitability, plot ratio, density controls, traffic impact, safety, visual impact, and compliance with urban design guidelines and environmental impact studies. In plain terms, the 2040 draft swaps ‘don’t build there’ (in the 2030 plan) for ‘build there if the paperwork says it’s safe’. The 2030 plan took a precautionary approach: keep away from the risk altogether. The 2040 draft replaces it with case-by-case approval, where each project’s own technical studies decide whether a hill can take it. Are these adequate safeguards, or is this a problem waiting to happen? Why change the limit? The threshold of 76m above sea level was not arbitrary. It was a deliberate safeguard that Penang chose to keep. Penang had adopted stricter controls than the national KSAS (environmentally sensitive areas) elevation framework, which it is now reverting to. The Safety Guideline for Hillsite Development (second edition, 2020) says Penang Island covers roughly 285 sq km. About 40% of it is Class 3 and Class 4 land, with slopes steeper than 25 degrees. The first version of the guideline went further. It reduced the footprint of buildings on hill land to make slopes safer and keep more green areas. Now these precautions are set aside. The 2040 draft presents this as a development strategy, not as a finding that the 76m limit is irrelevant. Outside the draft, no new evidence, assessment or policy review shows that the precautionary approach is no longer needed. What evidence, then, supports such a significant change in risk management? Look closely at the numbers. The highest point in Penang is 833m above sea level, but the horizontal area of the hills is small. The slopes are therefore compressed into a limited range of height and width. Add the complex pattern of hills and ridges, and very few pockets of land are flat enough to build on without cutting into the surrounding slopes. Even if building is allowed on isolated pockets, the roads needed to reach them must cross steeper terrain. Their environmental impact will reach far beyond the site. We do not have to imagine what that looks like. In October 2017, a landslide at a construction site in Tanjung Bungah killed 11 workers. A year later, part of a ‘paired road’ at Bukit Kukus collapsed during construction, killing nine. Bukit Kukus was a road, exactly the kind of infrastructure the 2030 plan already allowed as an exception. If the exception alone could cost so many lives, what happens when the rule itself is lifted? This is probably why past planners chose the 76m (250ft) limit. That wisdom applies even more today, as climate change brings heavier and more frequent rain to fragile hills. And what happens on the hill does not stay on the hill. These slopes feed the Air Itam and Teluk Bahang dams that fill our taps. When forests can no longer hold the rain, it runs down into lowland streets as flash floods. One does not need to live on a hill to pay for what happens on one. Paperwork is not landscape planning Some may argue that a technical assessment before approval is a reasonable safeguard. It can tell us whether a project meets existing standards. These include the Penang Safety Guideline for Hill Site Development 2020, the EIA Guidelines for Development in Slope and Hill Areas issued by the Department of Environment, and the planning and management guide for environmentally sensitive areas by PLANMalaysia. But none of these answers the bigger question: how many projects can these hills absorb before the whole system gives way? The 2040 draft says hill development control is strengthened through risk assessment, including the environment’s carrying capacity and climate resilience. Any development on hill land between 300 and 1,200 metres, or between 150 and 300 metres, and on slopes above 25 degrees, must submit a geotechnical risk assessment and a climate risk assessment. However, we know of no publicly accessible study or official database that gathers the information needed as a baseline. This should be established before the first hill or slope proposal is submitted. It seems the draft simply adopted a guideline written for the highlands of the peninsula – not one drawn up for Penang island. Could we, or should we? With today’s engineering, there are many ways to stabilise a slope: retaining walls, modern drainage, soil nails, piles and engineered slopes. A project may well be shown to be safe on paper. But the natural slope will have been substantially altered. Its long-term safety then rests on things no approval can guarantee. These include construction quality, drainage maintenance, inspection, the capacity and funding of the agencies responsible, extreme weather and future changes in land use. The irony is that a retaining wall is only as safe as the last time someone cleared its drains. There is also no baseline of existing conditions or of the role the hills play. That role covers the watershed, ecological corridors, natural drainage and geological formations. Penang lacks a hill and slope master plan that understands how sensitive and connected the hills are. Only such a plan can properly define, map and measure the hills’ carrying capacity, including projected climate scenarios. So the question shifts. We could make hill and slope development safe. But should we, and at what cost, when we have no baseline data and no guarantee these projects will stay safe in the long term? A project being technically safe is not the same as the landscape being safe. Gazette first, assess later When a gazetted state structure plan marks an area as potentially developable, the effects ripple out quickly. Land values rise, investors form expectations, land changes hands, proposals are drawn up and contracts are signed. All of this happens long before any environmental impact or technical assessment is complete. That order of events tilts the outcome. Once money and contracts are committed, rejecting a project on environmental grounds carries legal and financial consequences. The seemingly rational way out is to reduce every risk to an ‘acceptable’ level and hope nothing goes wrong later. The assessment no longer decides whether to build, only how. Show us the evidence The 2040 draft marks a significant shift from precautionary restriction towards risk-based conditional development. That may be reasonable in some circumstances. But the draft must show why the previous limits are no longer needed. It must also explain how project-by-project checks will deal with risks that build up across the landscape, worsen with climate change and cannot be undone once a hill is cut. If Penang is deliberately moving beyond the precautionary framework to create more development opportunities, it should show us the evidence. That means the thresholds and landscape-level safeguards that justify the change, in the form of a hill and slope development master plan, published before the 2040 plan is gazetted, not after. In the end, for most of us, this is not really a debate about slope angles, geotechnical reports or even the state structure plan. It is about the hills we know, some of us since childhood. These are the hills we see from our windows, or on the drive home after a long day at work. On them lie the green trails we climb at weekends to take in the view of our beloved Penang from above. It is also about feeling safe when the torrential rain comes. Can we sleep soundly knowing the hills near us will keep doing what they have always done: holding the soil, soaking up the water and slowing the runoff before it reaches our neighbourhoods? Or will we rely more and more on concrete walls and drains to protect us from hills we ourselves have altered? Dr Kam Suan Pheng is a soil scientist and co-founder of Penang Hills Watch, with a doctorate in agronomy-soil from Cornell University. Evelyn Teh is a Penang-based public policy researcher and environmental scientist specialising in ecological management, climate change and urban studies. title: 'MOF Backs AirAsia Fundraising Drive Led by Alton, Sources Say
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Global aviation advisory firm Alton Aviation Consultancy has launched a campaign to help low-cost carrier AirAsia Group Bhd (KL:AAGB) raise as much as US$1 billion (RM4.1 billion), according to people familiar with the matter. The fundraising effort is backed by Malaysia’s Ministry of Finance (MOF), which is helping Alton attract lenders and investors as banks and other financiers become more selective in funding airlines amid tougher market conditions and surging jet fuel prices, the sources told The Edge. AirAsia has reportedly said it is seeking as much as US$1 billion primarily to support debt restructuring, refinancing, balance sheet consolidation, with the rest for operational needs. The move follows the MOF’s appointment of Alton to assess AirAsia’s funding requirements. The Edge, in its Aug 24 weekly, reported that the specialist advisory firm had been engaged to help the airline secure the proposed US$1 billion financing from international debt markets. The MOF has mandated Alton to seek potential sources of funding and has provided an undertaking or some form of guarantee that could help Alton secure borrowings of significant size, the sources said. Alton would also be entitled to a success fee if it secures the financing, with the fee calculated as a percentage of the amount raised, the sources said. The Edge has contacted Alton for comment and is still awaiting a response. "If true, the government’s involvement reflects AirAsia’s importance to Malaysia’s economy, particularly its role in domestic and regional air connectivity," Shukor Yusof, founder and analyst at aviation consultancy Endau Analytics. “They realise that they have a fiduciary duty to make sure that nothing bad happens to AirAsia because it would have a bigger impact on the domestic economy,” he added. A government-backed structure could also help AirAsia reach a wider pool of investors. Most bond issues require a credit rating to attract institutional investors and determine borrowing costs, Shukor noted. If AirAsia’s debt were able to benefit from Malaysia’s sovereign credit rating of A- from S&P Global Ratings, it could appeal to a wider pool of international institutional investors, he said. AirAsia’s funding needs have become more pressing as higher fuel costs and foreign exchange (forex) losses weigh on its finances. title: 'F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia
body: 'Intipati berita - 300,000 pengunjung disasarkan hadir ke SIC, termasuk 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa. - F1 dijangka menjana impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion kepada Malaysia. - MOTAC & Tourism Malaysia menyediakan pakej pelancongan untuk menggalakkan pelancong asing tinggal lebih lama di Malaysia. - F1 turut menjadi platform mempromosikan pelancongan, budaya dan seni Malaysia sempena Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027. Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 300,000 pengunjung sempena penganjuran Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) dari 2 hingga 4 Oktober. Menurut laporan Berita RTM, daripada jumlah itu, kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa dijangka hadir ke SIC bagi menyaksikan perlumbaan berprestij tersebut. Ketua Komunikasi Korporat MOTAC, Firna Azura Ekaputri Marzuki berkata, berdasarkan unjuran Hong Leong Bank Research, penganjuran F1 itu dijangka memberi impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion. Berdasarkan data penyelidikan Hong Leong Bank, penganjuran F1 ini sahaja dijangka mampu menjana pendapatan sebanyak RM1.3 bilion melalui sektor pelancongan sukan dan perbelanjaan pelancong asing. Setakat ini, kita menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa daripada keseluruhan 300,000 pengunjung yang dijangka membanjiri SIC bagi menyaksikan Grand Prix F1 tersebut. MOTAC ada sediakan pakej pelancongan? Menurut Firna Azura, penganjuran F1 ini turut bertepatan dengan Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027 dan menjadi platform untuk memperkenalkan budaya, seni serta produk pelancongan negara kepada pelancong antarabangsa. MOTAC menerusi Tourism Malaysia bersama SIC turut menyediakan beberapa pakej pelancongan bagi menggalakkan pengunjung luar negara melanjutkan tempoh penginapan mereka di Malaysia. Selain menyaksikan F1, kita turut menggalakkan mereka untuk berbelanja, membeli-belah dan melakukan aktiviti pelancongan seperti melawat destinasi menarik di negara ini. Ini kerana selepas penganjuran F1 di Malaysia, saingan seterusnya akan berlangsung di Singapura. Siapa terlibat dalam persiapan penganjuran? Dalam pada itu, persiapan di bawah Jawatankuasa Publisiti, Promosi dan Pelancongan kini dilaporkan mencapai kira-kira 90 peratus. Pelbagai kementerian dan agensi terlibat bagi memastikan penganjuran berjalan lancar, antaranya KUSKOP, KBS, Kementerian Komunikasi, Tourism Malaysia, Kraftangan Malaysia, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Majlis Perbandaran Sepang serta SIC. Apa maksudnya untuk anda? Bagi memeriahkan lagi penganjuran F1 hari kejadian, beberapa program berskala besar turut diatur dari 23 September hingga 4 Oktober. Antaranya ialah Litar Rasa MADANI, Sepang Food Festival di Mitsui Outlet Park, Citrawarna Speed Festival dan RIUH Pitstop di TRX. Selain itu, Malaysia International Craft Fair 2026 turut berlangsung di Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur. The post F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia appeared first on Oh! Media.

title: 'Hap Seng Consolidated to Sell Singapore Listed Unit Hafary for S$140 Mil
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 28): Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd (KL:HAPSENG) said it plans to sell its Singapore-listed building materials unit for about S$140 million (RM447 million) following a takeover offer. 23 Capital Pte Ltd is offering cash per share of S$0.64, or RM2.04, to take private Hafary Holdings Ltd and Hap Seng Consolidated has agreed to accept the offer for its 50.82% stake, according to an exchange filing. 23 Capital is a vehicle owned by the Hafary founding family. The proposed disposal will allow Hap Seng Consolidated to realise its investment in Hafary at a premium over its initial cost of just S$0.24 per share, as well as above market and historical trading prices, the company said. If the deal goes through, Hafary will cease to be a subsidiary of Hap Seng Consolidated, preventing any consolidation of any financial results. Hap Seng Consolidated will book an estimated gross gain on disposal of about RM187.3 million from the deal expected to be completed before the year ends. While it will miss out on future earnings from Hafary, “the proposed disposal enables the group to realise its investment in cash at an attractive valuation, thereby strengthening its financial position and enhancing financial flexibility”, Hap Seng Consolidated said. Proceeds from the sale have been earmarked by Hap Seng Consolidated for partial repayment of borrowings totalling RM6.9 billion at the end of 2025. Hafary, which manufactures and trades building materials such as tiles, stone, mosaic, wood-flooring, quartz tops and sanitary ware and fittings, contributed RM48.4 million to Hap Seng Consolidated’s profit and RM19.85 million in dividends. Low Kok Ann, a Singaporean and chief executive of Hafary, controls 23 Capital with his son Low See Ching and daughter Low Bee Lan. The elder Low, also known as Eric Low, started the business from a single ceramic tile shop in 1980. Hap Seng Consolidated bought into Hafary in 2015 as a stepping stone to expand in the region. At the time of the acquisition, Hap Seng Consolidated was mainly involved in upstream segment of the building materials market while Hafary was strong downstream. Maybank Investment Bank is as principal adviser to Hap Seng Consolidated while United Overseas Bank is advising the buyer 23 Capital. title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat.

Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat.

title: 'Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera maintains five sen per unit income distribution for year ended September
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) has maintained its income distribution at five sen per unit for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026 (FY2026), benefitting over 82,000 unitholders. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB), together with its fund manager, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), said the final income distribution for the six months ended Sept 30, 2026, comprises 2.1 sen per unit, with an additional bonus distribution of 0.4 sen per unit declared by PHB as the fund's sponsor. "The bonus distribution will be applied to the first 1,000,000 units held by each unitholder. Including the interim income distribution of 2.5 sen per unit declared in April 2026, AHB’s total income distribution for the financial year ended FY2026 amounts to five sen per unit," the statement said. PHB said RM120.13 million will be distributed in the final round, bringing the total annual payout to RM236.41 million. PHB group managing director Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad said the full-year income distribution reflects AHB’s continued resilience and the strength of its underlying property portfolio, supported by PHB’s disciplined approach to asset and investment management. “AHB’s performance this year reaffirms our commitment to delivering competitive returns to our unitholders. At the same time, we remain focused on strengthening AHB as an investment avenue for Bumiputera investors through prudent capital management, active portfolio optimisation and strategic growth," he said. Meanwhile, PHBAM chief executive officer Zulkifli Ishak said the fund manager remains focused on managing AHB responsibly while ensuring the fund continues to serve as an accessible investment option for Bumiputera investors. PHB said income distribution will be paid in the form of AHB units, credited directly into unitholders' AHB accounts by Oct 13, 2026 and automatically reinvested, allowing unitholders to increase their unit holdings and potentially benefit from the long-term compounding effect. "Bumiputera investors who wish to subscribe to AHB may do so at a fixed price of RM1 per unit, with a minimum investment of RM100 and a maximum of RM1 million. "Subscriptions are available through the respective branches of authorised distributors nationwide, namely Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, and Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd," it said. title: 'DNB completes RM5.2b financing, unlocking next phase of 5G growth in Malaysia - Newswav
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, a transaction that ranks among the largest syndicated loan facilities ever arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. DNB CEO Datuk Azman Ismail said, “The successful completion of this RM5.2 billion financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy. “This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets. “As Malaysia progresses under the dual network framework, DNB remains committed to providing world-class digital infrastructure that supports our shareholders, customers, enterprises and government agencies. “With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the government’s AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia’s next phase of digital growth.” Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers. AmInvestment Bank acted as financial adviser to DNB. This significant step marks DNB’s evolution as Malaysia transitions to the next phase of its dual 5G network framework. The financing strengthens DNB’s long-term financial position and facilitates the planned exit of Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOFInc) as an ordinary shareholder and the transition to equal ownership among its mobile network pperator shareholders, namely CelcomDigi Bhd through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd, expected in the early fourth quarter of 2026. MOF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests, ensuring continued stewardship of key strategic matters while enabling the company to advance its next phase of development. The syndicated financing exercise includes the refinancing of DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility, which expired on Sept 29, and establishes a sustainable long-term funding structure to support the company’s future growth. The completion of the financing coincides with the award of the full 100 MHz of the 3.3–3.4GHz spectrum and the conversion of DNB’s entire 240MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. Following the issuance of the spectrum assignment by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the assignment took effect yesterday, providing greater regulatory certainty and strengthening DNB’s ability to support Malaysia’s evolving 5G connectivity needs. The 240 MHz spectrum block will enhance network capacity, efficiency, and performance, enabling faster speeds, lower latency, and an improved customer experience. It also supports the deployment of advanced technologies, including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities, further strengthening DNB’s leadership in next-generation connectivity. Together, the financing and the spectrum assignment strengthen DNB’s ability to enhance network quality and resilience, support future demand, and advance Malaysia’s digital economy ambitions.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Experiences Downturn at Mid-Afternoon
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia saw a decline at mid-afternoon, with selling pressure noted in selected heavyweight stocks. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 19 points to 1,632.17 at 3 pm, down from Wednesday's close of 1,651.17. The index had initially opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth was negative, with 614 decliners compared to 322 gainers. Additionally, 488 counters remained unchanged, 1,349 were untraded, and 12 were suspended. The turnover was recorded at 1.98 billion units valued at RM1.50 billion. Among the prominent stocks, Maybank decreased by three sen to RM9.96, Public Bank fell five sen to RM4.65, CIMB was down seven sen to RM7.72, Tenaga Nasional declined four sen to RM12.92, and IHH Healthcare dropped 16 sen to RM7.67. In active trading, Zetrix AI rose half a sen to 16.5 sen, VS Industry fell half a sen to 27.5 sen, Jaks Resources lost one sen to 19.5 sen, GB Bond retreated 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, and Dagang Nexchange increased by 1.5 sen to 50 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which surged RM1.34 to RM41.74, Ayer Holdings, up 20 sen to RM7.70, MI Technovation, rising 16 sen to RM5.36, Riverview Rubber Estates, strengthening 13 sen to RM3.03, and Vitrox, improving 11 sen to RM10.02. Among the top losers, Kuala Lumpur Kepong fell 72 sen to RM21.48, Allianz Malaysia dropped 62 sen to RM21.00, and United Plantations decreased 46 sen to RM31.10. Hong Leong Bank and Batu Kawan both fell 42 sen to RM22.72 and RM20.10, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 103.44 points to 17,471.22, the FBM Emas Index decreased 117.43 points to 12,174.59, and the FBM Top 100 Index reduced by 121.55 points to 11,962.89. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened by 112.81 points to 12,063.54, while the FBM ACE Index decreased by 27.38 points to 5,506.90. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index fell 2.02 points to 178.39, the Energy Index eased 8.88 points to 836.82, the Financial Services Index dropped 168.21 points to 19,048.82, and the Plantation Index retreated 150.10 points to 9,046.57.

title: 'Accelerating earnings and returns under Acceler8
body: 'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 5, 2026 - October 11, 2026 Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) has made a clean sweep this year, bagging all three awards under the financial services (below RM10 billion market capitalisation) category. The awards are for the Highest return on equity (ROE) over three years, the Highest growth in profit after tax over three years and the highest returns to shareholders over three years. This also marks the banking group’s first wins in The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) Awards. Alliance Bank’s net profit growth over the past three years has been impressive. It registered a three-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.8% between FY2022 and FY2025. Net earnings hit successive record highs as the banking group made significant strides under its Acceler8 2027 transformation strategy. From RM572.8 million in FY2022, net profit grew 18.33% to RM677.8 million in FY2023 and 1.87% to RM690.5 million the following year. Net profit continued to grow in FY2025, rising 8.7% year on year (y-o-y) to a record RM750.7 million, supported by a record revenue of RM2.3 billion arising from a 13.2% growth in net interest income. Net interest margin in FY2025 stood at 2.45%, while other operating income increased 7.7% y-o-y, largely due to higher revenue from treasury and investment income as well as trade fees. Alliance Bank, whose financial year ends on March 31, again posted a record net profit and revenue of RM826.5 million and RM2.5 billion respectively for FY2026. Achieving a top-quartile ROE in the banking industry is one of Alliance Bank’s goals under the Acceler8 2027 programme. Between FY2023 and FY2025, its ROE averaged between 9.9% and 10.3%, resulting in an adjusted weighted ROE of 10.1% over the period. Meanwhile, Alliance Bank’s net profit growth momentum has caught investors’ attention. Its share price rose from RM2.82 on March 31, 2023, to RM3.26 on March 31, 2024. The upward trajectory continued over the following two years, with the stock reaching RM4.82 on March 31, 2026 — the final date of the review period for the BRC awards. This translated into a three-year shareholders’ return CAGR of 19.5%. Its share price slipped slightly to a low of RM4.42 on April 13, 2026, before rebounding to close at RM4.92 on Aug 28. Alliance Bank paid a lower dividend of 19.1 sen per share in FY2026, compared with 19.4 sen in FY2025, 22.3 sen in FY2024 and 22 sen in FY2023. The group has started FY2027 on a strong note. Its 1QFY2027 net profit rose 25% y-o-y to RM248.3 million, mainly due to a 98.7% decline in loan loss provisions following the recovery of a corporate loan in the construction sector. In a report, CGS International Securities anticipates that the normalisation of loan loss provisions will result in a drop in 2QFY2027 net profit, bringing it back in line with the levels recorded between 2QFY2026 and 4QFY2026. CIMB Research, which has a “hold” call on the stock, pointed out that the banking group has demonstrated a steadier asset quality trend on a y-o-y basis, with its gross impaired loan (GIL) ratio edging down to 1.83% from 1.96% a year earlier, driven by credit recovery in its books. However, GIL ratios for its consumer and small to medium enterprises portfolios continued to deteriorate, rising to 2.2% and 2.1% respectively. The 30 days-past-due ratio also continued to creep up, although the research house noted that the stress was isolated to certain higher-risk borrowers. CGS also said Alliance Bank could see an enhancement of 60 to 70 basis points in its common equity Tier-1 (CET1) capital ratio following the Basel III reforms. “The bank does not expect to pay out any excess capital from the above as special dividends. Instead, the enhancement in its CET1 capital ratio would enable the bank to increase its dividend payout ratio (from 40%-50% guided for FY2027) in the longer term,” according to the bank. CGS has an “add” call on the banking group with a target price of RM5.70, citing potential rerating catalysts including strong growth in non-interest income, above-industry loan growth, potential write-back in management overlays and its expectation of a higher dividend payout ratio from FY2027 to FY2029. title: 'Former Maybank tech head Ravinder Singh joins Bursa Malaysia
body: 'By Asia Samachar | Malaysia | After more than two decades navigating the technology side of banking and financial services — including 11 years with Maybank and another five with AmBank — Ravinder Singh Bachan Singh is moving to Bursa Malaysia to lead the stock exchange operator’s technology function. The 45-year-old has been appointed Director, Group Technology at Bursa Malaysia Bhd, effective Sept 28, 2026. He will also be designated a Principal Officer of the company. Ravinder was previously Regional Head of Technology at Maybank Investment Banking Group, where he was responsible for technology across its investment banking and asset management businesses. His 11-year stint with Maybank formed a significant part of a financial services career spanning more than 20 years. Before that, he spent about five years with AmBank Bhd, including as Head of Cash Management, Group IS. Over the years, Ravinder has built experience across investment banking, asset management, wealth management and transaction banking, both in Malaysia and internationally. His areas of expertise include technology strategy and transformation, digital platforms, cybersecurity, operational resilience and technology governance across multiple markets. At Bursa Malaysia, Ravinder will take charge of the group technology function, placing him in a key leadership role overseeing an increasingly critical component of the Malaysian capital market operator’s operations. Ravinder holds a Degree in Computing from Staffordshire University in the United Kingdom. He is also TOGAF 9 certified by The Open Group, a professional certification in enterprise architecture. Bursa Malaysia announced his appointment in an exchange filing on Sept 25. title: 'RHB online banking to drop support for older browsers from Oct 31
body: 'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank has announced that its online banking platform will stop supporting older, outdated browsers from Oct 31. These outdated browsers will not be able to access the platform after this date. In a notice on its website, the bank says the change is intended to provide a safer and more secure banking experience for customers. It adds that this is due to older browsers no longer receiving security updates from their respective providers. The bank has set the minimum versions for five browsers, consisting of Google Chrome (V149 and above), Microsoft Edge (V149 and above), Mozilla Firefox (V151 and above), Opera (V130 and above), and Apple Safari (V18 and above). No action is needed if the browser is already on a newer version. For customers unable to update their browser to a newer version, RHB Bank advises them to use the RHB Mobile Banking App, available on both the Google Play Store and Apple App Store.

title: 'Bursa once said no to crypto. LIDAC26 showed how far Malaysia has come since
body: 'Back in 2024, I wrote a column lamenting Bursa Malaysia’s decision to keep bitcoin and other crypto assets off its new multi-asset exchange, asking whether it might go down as Bursa’s biggest blunder.  Two Thursday’s ago, I spent the better part of a day at M Resort & Hotel in Kuala Lumpur listening to regulators, bankers and fund managers talk about digital assets not as a fringe curiosity, but as the plumbing for the next generation of our capital market. What a difference two years makes.  The event was LIDAC26, the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference, now in its second edition. Luno, one of the digital asset exchanges registered with the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC), pitched it squarely at institutions rather than retail punters, and the room reflected that.  The main hall kept the headline sessions flowing from 9.30am, four breakout sessions ran in smaller rooms alongside it through the day, and the session screens I saw all carried a QR code for live audience questions.  Attendees could even earn seven continuing professional development (CPD) points, the credits licensed finance professionals collect to keep their qualifications current, which tells you exactly who the organisers were courting.  So what were the big takeaways? Three stood out.  1. Stablecoins are the real story  Luno chief executive James Lanigan opened proceedings with a slide that cut through a lot of the noise. By Luno’s count, about RM1.43 trillion worth of assets had been tokenised, or recorded as digital tokens on a blockchain, by the first quarter of 2026, and roughly RM1.26 trillion of that was stablecoins, tokens pegged to a currency such as the US dollar.  That’s right. Around 90% of all tokenised assets are, in effect, digital cash, the overwhelming majority of which is tokenised USD, cementing it as not only the world’s reserve currency but the currency of choice in the budding crypto economy.  Lanigan’s framing was that the industry had moved from speculation, through building infrastructure, and was now firmly in its institutional era, with one of his final slides declaring that Malaysia was not a late market, but an early one.  2. The regulator wants substance, not buzzwords  The most anticipated session was that by Wong Huei Ching, the SC’s executive director of digital strategy and innovation, who laid out where Malaysia’s rules are heading.  Her message, stripped to its core, was that putting an asset on a blockchain is not innovation in itself, and that pilots need to prove their worth before the rules are rewritten.  The SC is practising what it preaches. In April, it teamed up with Khazanah Nasional, our sovereign wealth fund, to price Malaysia’s first tokenised sukuk (an Islamic bond recorded on a blockchain), a RM100 million pilot that SC chairman Mohammad Faiz Azmi said would test tokenisation’s potential “in a controlled and credible manner”.  The market she regulates is growing fast, too. Trading value on Malaysia’s licensed digital asset exchanges hit RM17.14 billion in 2025, a 23% jump from RM13.93 billion the year before, according to the SC.  3. The ringgit is going on-chain  John Ho, head of legal and financial markets at Standard Chartered, walked participants in the main hall through Bank Negara Malaysia’s growing list of experiments. These include Project Mawar, which explores a wholesale digital ringgit for banks, and the central bank’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, where Standard Chartered and Capital A are testing a ringgit stablecoin, while Maybank trials tokenised deposits.  The prize is not small. One industry estimate cited on stage, and widely reported, puts Malaysia’s tokenisation opportunity at around RM175 billion by 2030.  The tidbits  Many other speakers added flair and colour to the proceedings. Former deputy international trade and industry minister Ong Kian Ming spoke on navigating digital assets in a fragmenting global order, while Harjit Singh of HSS Advisory and Anil Puri of EY tackled a question plenty of Malaysian crypto investors have been asking for years: how exactly will all this be taxed?  My favourite, though, was a breakout billed as Malaysian builders shaping the global digital asset landscape. On one stage sat TM Lee, co-founder of CoinGecko, Matthew Tan, founder of Etherscan, and Siong Ong, co-founder of Jupiter, products used by crypto traders the world over.  CoinGecko and Etherscan were both born right here in Kuala Lumpur, and I can’t help but feel proud that some of the most widely used tools in the industry were built by Malaysians.  Siong Ong’s speaker photo on the big screen? A Pudgy Penguin, an uber popular non-fungible token (NFT) collection. In a day full of suits, it was a welcome reminder of where this industry came from.  The one glaring miss  I was, however, surprised that bitcoin, the 800-pound gorilla in the room, barely got a look-in. Bitcoin alone is worth around RM6.9 trillion today, according to CoinGecko, and together with ether, the Ethereum network’s native token, the pair make up about two-thirds of the entire crypto market.  Stablecoins, for all the stage time they got, account for a mere 10%. Despite more than a decade of relentless innovation in the industry, bitcoin still commands over half of all crypto value, and not telling that story was a missed opportunity.  So where does that leave us? The SC revised its guidelines on Mar 2 to permit digital currency exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and Bursa, the very exchange that shut crypto out of its multi-asset platform in 2024, said in March that it welcomed the listing of digital currency ETFs, and told reporters in July that it planned to add them to its line-up.  The regulator has built the framework, Khazanah has shown the plumbing can work and Bank Negara is already testing the ringgit on-chain. All that’s left is for the first digital currency ETF to actually start trading on Bursa. After all, it’s about time the exchange that once said no had something to show for its yes.

title: 'ViTrox Hits New Record High as AI-driven Growth Boosts Outlook
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Shares in ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL:VITROX) hit their highest level since the company’s listing on the ACE Market in 2005 on Tuesday, driven by its strong growth prospects amid the AI infrastructure boom. ViTrox designs & manufactures vision inspection system & handler for back-end semiconductor industry. In a The Edge Malaysia weekly’s Sept 21-Sept 27 issue, its co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng said the company’s numbers will double this year, with strong growth momentum expected to continue over the next few years. The Penang-based automated test equipment maker’s shares charted an all-time high of RM10.08 before closing up 21 sen or 2.2% at RM10 on Tuesday, giving the company a market capitalisation of a little under RM19 billion. The share price remains below the consensus 12-month target price of RM10.67, while the highest 12-month target price is RM13. The majority of analysts covering the company have a “buy” call on the stock, with 11 “buy” calls, two “hold” calls and one “sell” call. Analysts noted that ViTrox has positioned itself as a key beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending. Research houses have also upgraded their earnings forecasts, with Apex Securities raising its net profit forecasts for FY2026, FY2027 and FY2028 to RM275.6 million, RM362.4 million and RM408.2 million, respectively, citing sustained AI infrastructure demand. CIMB Securities noted that ViTrox’s 1HFY2026 results exceeded expectations, coming in at more than 60% of its full-year consensus estimate. The research house reiterated its “buy” rating with a target price of RM10.00 and raised its FY2026–FY2028 earnings per share estimates by 28% to 37%, citing expanding order books, a favourable product mix and recurring service income. ViTrox saw its revenue double year-on-year in the second quarter ended June 30 (2QFY2026) to RM375 million from RM183 million in the same period last year. Net profit for the quarter jumped to RM85.04 million, bringing the company’s cumulative net profit for the first half of 2026 to RM136.24 million, surpassing its full-year net profit of RM133.18 million in 2025. Chu said the optimism surrounding the company is understandable, given that, much like its peers in the semiconductor-related industry, ViTrox is operating at full capacity and expanding to cope with the surge in demand. title: 'CIMB, Zetrix AI, Top Glove, Samaiden, Mesiniaga, Scientex, Dialog, Elridge Energy, Insights Analytics, SLGC
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 7): Here is a brief recap of some business news and corporate announcements that made the headlines on Tuesday: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200 million (RM817 million). — CIMB considers selling Philippine business — Bloomberg Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314 million in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. — Zetrix says still finalising amount owed to JPJ after Loke reveals RM314m arrears Top Glove Corporation Bhd (KL:TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78 billion pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72 billion in FY2026. The group’s net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63 million in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25 billion. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15. For the full FY2026, Top Glove’s net profit nearly tripled to RM307.96 million. Revenue increased 21% to RM4.23 billion as volume grew close to 30%. — Top Glove eyes higher output but says manpower remains key hurdle; Top Glove says ready for storms ahead as 4Q net profit jumps nearly five times Samaiden Group Bhd (KL:SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (KL:YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. — Samaiden reveals RM238 mil contract value for LSS5+ solar project Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. — Mesiniaga wins two-year RM32.3m contract extension from Customs Dept Scientex Bhd (KL:SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. — Scientex to acquire 503 acres in Johor for RM580 mil Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. — Dialog JV bags onshore O&G concession in Thailand Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (KL:ELRIDGE) is investing RM45 million to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45 million in cash. — Elridge Energy invests RM45m to venture into activated carbon business Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44 million subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. — Insights Analytics secures contract for Suai water treatment plant in Miri Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm’s shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intra-day low of 24 sen as more than 83 million shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140 million. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. — Construction firm SLGC ends first trading day below IPO price

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Rises Amid Bargain Hunting
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia's key index rose on Wednesday, rebounding from recent losses as oversold conditions prompted bargain hunting. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) increased by 7.21 points, or 0.43 percent, ending at 1,651.17 compared to Tuesday's close of 1,643.96. The index opened 2.53 points higher at 1,646.49, fluctuating between 1,645.03 and 1,657.41 throughout the session. Market breadth was negative, with 703 decliners surpassing 413 gainers, while 572 counters remained unchanged, 1,167 were untraded, and 95 were suspended. Turnover improved, reaching 3.63 billion units valued at RM3.62 billion, up from 3.31 billion units worth RM2.95 billion on Tuesday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd's vice-president of equity research, Thong Pak Leng, noted that the local market's recovery was tentative as investors awaited the August US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index. This key inflation gauge could influence further movements in bond yields. Domestically, a cautious stance is maintained due to the elevated US 10-year Treasury yield and ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia. Thong remarked that the recent market correction has made selected blue-chip valuations more attractive, potentially providing downside support and encouraging more bargain hunting. He anticipates a gradual return of buying interest in fundamentally strong stocks, though a sustained recovery may require a more favorable external backdrop. The FBM KLCI is expected to trend within the 1,640-1,670 range for the remainder of the week. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 0.45 of a point to 180.41, while the Energy Index dropped 23.00 points to 845.70. The Financial Services Index fell 44.35 points to 19,216.49, and the Plantation Index decreased by 19.67 points to 9,196.67. The Main Market volume increased to 2.23 billion units worth RM3.28 billion from 1.88 billion units valued at RM2.58 billion on Tuesday. Warrants turnover decreased to 887.74 million units worth RM138.36 million from 978.19 million units valued at RM190.60 million previously. The ACE Market volume expanded to 510.54 million units valued at RM201.45 million from 447.33 million units worth RM181.49 million the previous day. title: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank at APAC Innovation Awards 2026
body: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank at APAC Innovation Awards 2026 Red Hat has named Hong Leong Bank as the Malaysian winner of the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026, recognising the bank’s use of open source technologies to modernise its infrastructure and improve digital services. This year’s awards, themed “Unlock what’s next,” recognise 32 organisations across 13 Asia Pacific markets for using Red Hat solutions to address complex business challenges and drive innovation. The awards cover five areas: Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud-Native Development, Automation, Virtualization and AI. Hong Leong Bank Modernises Its Infrastructure Hong Leong Bank was recognised in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category for its efforts to improve the scalability and performance of a critical online business application. The bank moved the application from a traditional monolithic architecture to a containerised environment using Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. It also adopted Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to modernise its existing database infrastructure and bring virtual machines and containers together on a common platform. The move has helped reduce software deployment cycles from months to weeks while eliminating manual virtual machine patching for containerised workloads. The new architecture also allows applications to scale dynamically during periods of high traffic. According to Hong Leong Bank, the modernised infrastructure provides a more flexible foundation for introducing new digital banking capabilities while maintaining the reliability expected by customers. Red Hat said the 2026 winners demonstrate how open source technologies can help organisations simplify complex IT environments, modernise operations and create greater flexibility as technologies such as AI, hybrid cloud and automation continue to evolve. William Streitberg, Chief Information & Technology Officer at Hong Leong Bank, said the collaboration with Red Hat has provided the bank with a common foundation for both existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing new capabilities to be introduced more quickly. The recognition highlights Hong Leong Bank’s ongoing efforts to modernise its technology infrastructure while supporting the continued development of its digital banking services.

title: 'Maybank Championship makes stellar return, returns with prize bonanza
body: 'THE Maybank Championship is set for another star-studded chapter when Asia’s premier ladies’ golf event returns to Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC) from Oct 29 to Nov 1. With a $3 million (RM12.3m) prize purse, the fourth edition brings together Major champions, LPGA Tour winners and Southeast Asia’s emerging talents for four days of world-class competition at KLGCC. The competition for the coveted Tiger Trophy has never been more intense. Defending champion and Major winner Miyu Yamashita of Japan is one of the most in-form players this season, highlighted by a dominant nine-stroke victory at the CPKC Women’s Open in Canada in August, and a playoff win at the Sony JLPGA Championship in Japan in September. Having claimed a dramatic three-way playoff victory at last year’s Maybank Championship, she will have every intention of becoming the tournament’s first repeat champion. Crowd favourite and World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand is also on a rich vein of form, having already claimed three LPGA Tour victories in 2026 to take her total title tally to ten. She returns for a fourth consecutive year in pursuit of the elusive Tiger Trophy, having narrowly missed out in each of her last appearances. Thitikul’s close friend Ruoning Yin of China, the 2024 Maybank Championship winner and a Major champion, will also return to Malaysia in winning mode having triumphed at the FM Championship in August. The spotlight will also firmly be turned on Korean ace Haeran Ryu, who is currently second on the LPGA Tour’s Race to CME Globe ranking on the back of successive Major victories in 2026 at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship and the Amundi Evian Championship. Adding her considerable star power to the field is the perennially popular New Zealander Lydia Ko, a three-time Major winner and reigning Olympic champion who was inducted into the LPGA Hall of Fame in 2024 at age 27. Australian stalwart Hannah Green and Hye-Jin Choi of South Korea, who were the two other protagonists in last year’s playoff, will return with unfinished business on their agendas. The 2023 Maybank Championship winner Céline Boutier of France, who edged Thitikul in a nail-biting nine-hole playoff at KLGCC three years ago, is also in the field. Other fan favourites who have signed up include emerging English sensation Lottie Woad and her experienced compatriot Charley Hull, and Japanese twins Aki and Chizzy Iwai. The Maybank Championship is more than Asia’s premier golf event. It provides a distinctive regional pathway for Southeast Asian talent to earn their place alongside the world’s best. This year, five players who earned their places through the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier bring that story to life. Held in August at KLGCC’s West Course, the 36-hole qualifier concluded with Thai professional Pimnipa Panthong and her amateur compatriots Sarisa Pojanalai and Achiraya Sriwong locked together at four-under-par 140. Standout Thai amateur Marisa Tojai, who had already claimed four amateur titles in 2026 before arriving at the qualifier, secured the fourth spot at two-under 142, while Malaysia’s Liyana Durisic rounded out the top five at one-under 143. Through this performance-based pathway, each of these five players earned the right to play alongside the world’s best in a full-fledged LPGA Tour event, which is the primary objective of the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier. For Malaysian fans, there will be plenty to roar about. Liyana Durisic is currently in great form, having already claimed four PGM Tour titles in 2026, and the Women’s World Sand Greens Championship held in Australia in March. She will be joined by a talented and recognizable group of Malaysian players entering as Sponsor’s Invitations, namely Mirabel Ting, Jeneath Wong, Natasha Oon and Kelly Tan, to make up a five-strong Malaysian challenge. 2025 Annika Award winner Mirabel Ting made headlines in 2024 by becoming the highest-finishing Malaysian in Maybank Championship history, with a T12 finish as an amateur. Her fine performances continued into her debut season on this year’s Epson Tour, helping her clinch two victories in 2026. The wins propelled Ting to the top of the Epson Tour’s Race for the Card standings and secured her place on the LPGA Tour for the 2027 season. Joining Ting is Malaysia’s highest-ranked amateur (currently ranked 59th), Jeneath Wong. After a stellar season in 2023 that saw her earn her a major championship start at the US Women’s Open, Wong made history as the first Malaysian to win the Women’s Amateur Asia-Pacific Championship in 2025. The victory earned her further major championship starts, bringing an increasingly impressive international resume to KLGCC. One-time Epson Tour winner and 2023 Epson Tour Rookie of the Year Natasha Oon makes her first appearance at the Maybank Championship since 2023, seeking to capitalize on her encouraging performance at the recent CPKC Women’s Open. The LPGA Tour rookie is rebuilding her momentum following a lengthy injury that saw her miss most of the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Completing the Malaysian line-up is two-time Olympian Kelly Tan, Malaysia’s most successful LPGA Tour player. Tan recorded her career-best results on the LPGA Tour with runner-up finishes at the Dow Great Lakes Bay Invitational in 2022 and 2023, and returns to KLGCC for the third time, bringing over a decade of elite professional experience and an intimate knowledge of the West Course. The Maybank Championship reflects Maybank’s belief in Harnessing Collective Power, bringing together world-class players, emerging ASEAN talent, partners and fans to elevate the game and create opportunity across the region.

title: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank for Unlocking New Possibilities with Open Source at the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 for Malaysia
body: 'Red Hat, Inc., the world’s leading provider of open source solutions, today announced the winners of the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 for Malaysia. This year, Red Hat recognises Hong Leong Bank for their leadership through open source, demonstrating how open source technologies help organisations navigate complexity, modernise operations, and deliver sustainable growth. As organisations across Asia Pacific embrace AI, hybrid cloud, automation, and cloud-native technologies, managing complexity has become just as important as driving innovation. With AI strategies increasingly spanning different models, accelerators, and cloud environments, enterprises are looking to open source because openness brings choice, and choice brings greater flexibility. That flexibility enables them to adopt the technologies best suited to their business needs while building the agility needed to respond to change. Reflecting this year’s theme, “Unlock what’s next,” the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 celebrate organisations that are leading the way with open source. This year’s awards recognise 32 winners across the region whose innovative use of Red Hat solutions is helping solve complex business challenges and deliver meaningful outcomes for customers, employees, and communities. The winners were recognised for demonstrating how open source can help organisations turn complexity into opportunity. By modernising technology foundations, streamlining operations, and accelerating innovation, each organisation has delivered measurable outcomes that strengthen business resilience and create lasting value. Their achievements reflect Red Hat’s continued collaboration with enterprises across 13 APAC countries to solve real-world challenges through open source. The awards comprise five categories: Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud-Native Development, Automation, Virtualization, and AI. Category: Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development Winner: Hong Leong Bank Hong Leong Bank, one of Malaysia’s leading digital-forward banks, has been recognised in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category for its infrastructure enhancement efforts. As part of the bank’s continuous innovation efforts, the bank sought to improve scalability of a critical online business application by addressing legacy architecture and manual processes. To overcome these performance bottlenecks, Hong Leong Bank transitioned the application from a monolithic framework to a containerised environment using Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. The bank also deployed Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to create a structured path for modernising its existing database infrastructure, effectively unifying virtual machines and containers onto a single, common platform. The architectural shift has transformed the bank’s operational efficiency, cutting software deployment cycles from months to weeks while eliminating manual virtual machine patching for containerised workloads. By enabling applications to scale dynamically during traffic spikes, Hong Leong Bank has built an agile foundation to accelerate the continuous delivery of innovative digital banking services. Supporting Quotes Daniel Aw, Vice President & General Manager, APAC, Red Hat APAC “Enterprise technology is becoming more complex than ever, but success is no longer about how many new technologies an organisation adopts. What matters more is how effectively these solutions work together to address real business challenges and deliver tangible value. This year’s winners demonstrate that the organisations best positioned for long-term success are those building open, flexible foundations that allow them to innovate on their own terms. Their achievements are a testament to what organisations can accomplish when technology decisions are guided by business needs rather than trends, and it is this approach that we are proud to celebrate through the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards.” William Streitberg, Chief Information & Technology Officer, Hong Leong Bank “Enhancing a bank’s technology environment does not happen overnight, and updating infrastructure requires us to understand what is the right-fit for our operations. Red Hat has equipped us with a common foundation for both our existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing us to introduce new capabilities faster while maintaining the reliability our customers expect.”

title: 'MARC Ratings affirms PNB Merdeka Ventures’ sukuk at AAA
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd’s (PNBMV) Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah Programme of up to RM6bil, with a stable outlook. The rating agency, in a statement, said the rating is equalised with the AAA/Stable corporate credit rating of Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), based on publicly available information. It said the equalisation reflects PNB’s unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee to cover any shortfall in principal and profit payments under the sukuk programme. PNBMV, a wholly owned subsidiary of PNB, is undertaking the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in Kuala Lumpur. The development includes the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank, a retail mall and sites earmarked for two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. MARC Ratings said PNBMV has leased all 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement, under which PNB bears property-related expenses in addition to rental and service charges. About 70% of the office tower's 1.6 million sq ft of net lettable area has been sub-leased, comprising 40% or 33 floors to Maybank, 20% to PNB and about 10% to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to rise to about 90% over the next five years, while the office tower is projected to generate annual net property income of about RM137mil. For the 750,324 sq ft retail mall, lease agreements covering 81% of its net lettable area have either been signed or are under negotiation, at an indicative average rental rate of RM11.92 per sq ft. The mall is expected to open in November. Meanwhile, two residential apartment buildings with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM2bil are targeted for launch in the first half of 2027. A serviced apartment component, with an estimated GDV of RM745mil, is planned for a later launch. MARC Ratings noted that the residential and serviced apartment components are exposed to demand risk due to competing developments in Kuala Lumpur. The Merdeka 118 development has incurred RM10.6bil in development costs to date, while the upcoming residential projects are expected to require another RM1.4bil, funded through a combination of borrowings and equity injections. MARC Ratings said recurring income from the completed development could reach RM500mil to RM600mil annually over the medium term.

title: 'Customary land: Between Orang Asli rights and the law
body: 'The sultan of Pahang has called for greater clarity over the use of the term tanah adat (customary land), saying Orang Asli land claims must be assessed according to the legal status of the land, including its gazetting, boundaries and history of occupation.
