title: 'Liyana shares lead after sizzling start at The Ladies
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Defending champion Liyana Durisic made a strong start to her title defence at The Ladies 2026 after firing a seven-under 64 to share the opening-round lead with Genevieve Ling at The Mines Resort & Golf Club on Thursday. Liyana produced one of the rounds of the day but found herself matched by Genevieve as the pair opened up a two-shot advantage at the top of the leaderboard. Charlayne Chong kept herself firmly in contention with 66, setting up an intriguing second-round battle among the leading trio. Geraldine Wong and Zulaikah Nasser are another two shots back after carding matching 68s, while Allycia Gan and Afifah Razif returned 69s. Amalia Shahzan, Jocelyn Chee, Tan Ying Ying and Durriyah Damian also remained within striking distance following opening rounds of 70. The Ladies, now in its second edition, features a field of 50 professionals and amateurs and was established to provide Malaysian women golfers with greater competitive opportunities on home soil. The tournament also offers the local professionals valuable tournament exposure ahead of the US$3 million Maybank Championship at Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club later this month. Malaysian two-time Olympian Kelly Tan is also among the leading names competing this week. The tournament began with Wednesday's Royal Pro-Am and official opening ceremony, which was officiated by Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah. The three-day championship concludes with the final round on Saturday.

title: 'MKH bakal dinyahsenarai selepas Batu Kawan kuasai 95.16% saham
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt – MKH Bhd bakal dinyahsenarai daripada Bursa Malaysia selepas Batu Kawan Bhd bersama anak syarikatnya, Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd serta pihak yang bertindak bersama mereka menguasai 95.16% saham syarikat pemaju hartanah itu. Jumlah pegangan tersebut bersamaan 548.85 juta saham MKH setakat penutupan dagangan pada 30 Sept 2026, menurut kenyataan yang dikeluarkan oleh Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bagi pihak Batu Kawan dan Whitmore. Dengan pegangan yang sudah melepasi 90%, Batu Kawan dan Whitmore kini boleh mengambil alih baki saham MKH yang masih dipegang pemegang saham yang tidak menerima tawaran pengambilalihan tersebut. Baki saham MKH akan diambil alih secara wajib Langkah itu akan dibuat di bawah Seksyen 222(1) Akta Pasaran Modal dan Perkhidmatan 2007 yang membolehkan baki saham diperoleh secara wajib. Tawaran pengambilalihan pada harga RM2 sesaham itu masih dibuka sehingga 8 Oktober 2026 selepas tarikh tutup asal pada 17 September lalu dilanjutkan. Selepas tempoh tawaran tamat, Bursa Malaysia Securities akan menggantung dagangan saham MKH selepas lima hari pasaran, sebelum Batu Kawan dan Whitmore meneruskan proses untuk menarik balik status penyenaraian MKH. Pengambilalihan MKH bernilai RM1.15 bilion Langkah Batu Kawan mengambil alih MKH bermula pada Mei lalu apabila Whitmore bersetuju membeli kepentingan 47.7% dalam MKH daripada anggota keluarga Chen pada harga RM2 sesaham, membabitkan nilai RM549.8 juta. Pembelian itu kemudiannya disusuli tawaran kepada pemegang saham MKH yang lain pada harga sama bagi membolehkan Batu Kawan meningkatkan pegangannya dalam syarikat tersebut. Secara keseluruhan, pengambilalihan MKH untuk menjadikannya syarikat persendirian bernilai sehingga RM1.15 bilion, termasuk kos pembelian kepentingan awal daripada keluarga Chen. Tawaran RM2 sesaham terima pandangan berbeza Bagaimanapun, tawaran tersebut sebelum ini mendapat pandangan berbeza daripada penasihat bebas MKH dan MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd, iaitu cabang perladangan MKH yang disenaraikan secara berasingan. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, yang bertindak sebagai penasihat bebas MKH, menilai tawaran RM2 sesaham itu sebagai “tidak adil tetapi munasabah”, dengan mengambil kira harga tawaran yang lebih rendah daripada nilai aset wajar MKH. Bagi MKH Oil Palm pula, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd menggesa pemegang saham menolak tawaran 66.26 sen sesaham daripada Batu Kawan, yang disifatkannya sebagai “tidak adil dan tidak munasabah”. Menurut Mainstreet, harga tawaran itu mewakili diskaun 47% kepada nilai aset bersih (NAV) MKH Oil Palm. Pada masa sama, Batu Kawan bercadang mengekalkan MKH Oil Palm sebagai syarikat yang disenaraikan di Bursa Malaysia.- DagangNews.com

title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on bid to stop RHB closing shipping firm’s accounts
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The High Court here today fixed October 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.  Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.  Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.  He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.  Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer is that of debtor and creditor.  In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.  According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.  On October 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated October 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.  The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines were allegedly breached.  The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.  The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.  The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.  Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.  This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.  It also claimed that the bank’s conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests. — Bernama

The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.  The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.  The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.  Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.  This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.  It also claimed that the bank’s conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests. — Bernama

title: 'Analysts Stay Neutral On Banks As Funding Costs, Asset Quality Risks Build
body: 'RHB Research has maintained its Neutral stance on Malaysia’s banking sector, citing pressure on net interest margins, rising bond yields, a gradual increase in gross impaired loans and thinner provisioning buffers despite resilient loan growth.  The research house said system loans expanded 5.7% year-on-year and 0.4% month-on-month in August 2026, bringing annualised year-to-date growth to 5.6%, slightly ahead of its full-year forecast of between 5% and 5.5%.  Non-household lending led the increase, rising 6.8% year-on-year, supported by transport and communications loans, which jumped 21%, utilities at 20%, and education and health at 14%.  Household loans grew 5.0% year-on-year, driven mainly by residential mortgages and auto financing, both of which expanded 5%.  RHB said lending indicators remained healthy, with loan applications up 13.8% year-on-year, approvals rising 19.3% and disbursements increasing 10.2% in August.  For the first eight months of the year, loan applications, approvals and disbursements rose 8.5%, 14.0% and 6.5% respectively, pointing to a healthy pipeline for near-term drawdowns.  System deposits increased 5.2% year-on-year in August, with current and savings account deposits rising 8%, ahead of 4% growth in fixed and other deposits.  The system CASA ratio improved to 32.5%, from 31.4% a year earlier.  However, the loan-to-deposit ratio rose to 89.8%, from 88.8% in July and 89.4% a year ago, while the liquidity coverage ratio eased to 145.9%.  RHB said margin pressure could intensify as lending growth continues to outpace deposit growth, while higher capital-market rates are expected to push up wholesale deposit costs and eventually spill over into retail funding rates.  The research house also flagged the potential impact of higher bond yields on trading income and mark-to-market valuations.  Total gross impaired loans rose 6.1% year-on-year and 1.2% month-on-month, lifting the system GIL ratio slightly to 1.44%, from 1.43% previously.  The increase was driven by wholesale and retail trade, households, transport and communications, and primary agriculture.  Within the household segment, the GIL ratio increased to 1.11%, with auto and personal financing showing notable deterioration.  At the same time, system loan-loss coverage remained broadly stable month-on-month at 81.4%, but was lower than 89.9% a year earlier.  RHB said capital positions remained comfortable, with the CET-1 ratio at 14.1% and the total capital ratio at 17.8%.  The research house maintained AMMB Holdings, Malayan Banking and Hong Leong Bank as its preferred banking names, while retaining a cautious sector view in the absence of strong near-term catalysts.

title: 'Court allows temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport
body: 'The Sessions Court has granted the temporary release of former PM’s political secretary Shamsul Iskandar’s passport for travel to Germany and London. KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, the former senior political secretary to the Prime Minister, has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month. The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption. According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties. He said he intended to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11. “Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities. “Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the MADANI principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit. Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14. He said the summit aimed to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices. Shamsul Iskandar also said he planned to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December. During today’s proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court Judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport. He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month. Deputy Public Prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online. However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release. Judge Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective today, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16. The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249, respectively, from Tei for the same purpose. The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024. In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei’s company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.

title: 'RHB Makeover Flexi Loan for Home Renovation
body: '21st September 2026 - 3 min read You can now include renovation costs in your home loan with the Makeover Flexi Loan, from RHB Bank and The Makeover Guys. It covers up to 90% of the property’s value, plus up to 30% more for renovation and related costs, for a total of up to 120%. With a standard home loan, you can usually borrow up to 90% of the property’s value, and the renovation is paid for separately with savings, a personal loan, or a renovation loan. The extra 30% can go towards your renovation, legal and documentation fees, and Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance (MRTA). MRTA is insurance that pays off the rest of your home loan if you pass away or become totally and permanently disabled. If you take an Islamic home loan, the same cover is called Mortgage Reducing Term Takaful (MRTT). It’s also a full flexi loan. You can put extra cash, like a bonus, into the loan, which lowers what you still owe and the interest you pay on it. If you need that money back later, you can take it out again, which is called a redraw. As an example, on a RM500,000 home, you could borrow up to RM450,000 to buy the property, and you’d pay the remaining RM50,000 yourself as your down payment. You could then borrow up to RM150,000 more for your renovation, MRTA, and legal fees. The final loan amount you get depends on RHB Bank’s check of your income and any loans you already have. Since the renovation is part of your home loan, you apply once and make one monthly repayment. Home loan interest rates are generally lower than personal loan rates. Your renovation cost is also spread over your home loan’s repayment period of up to 35 years or until you turn 70, whichever comes first, while most personal loans run for up to 10 years. The savings you’d have set aside for renovation can go towards furniture or your emergency fund instead. RHB Bank pays out the renovation money bit by bit, each time your contractor finishes a stage of the work. The renovation is done through The Makeover Guys, which handles the design, project management, and construction. Your renovation budget is set when you apply for the loan, so get a quote first to see how much of the extra 30% you’ll need. You can also compare home loan rates before sending an enquiry through The Makeover Guys’ website. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates. Her current interests are learning the best ways to optimise spending and credit card hacks to gain more airline miles.

title: 'Malaysia’s freedom of information test
body: 'Malaysia’s proposed Freedom of Information Bill is under renewed scrutiny after civil society groups raised concerns over broad exemptions, existing secrecy laws and the effectiveness of its appeals process. What needs to change for the bill to deliver genuine access to information, and can Malaysia balance greater government transparency with legitimate safeguards? title: 'Bursa Appoints Former Maybank Technology Head As Group Tech Director
body: 'Bursa Malaysia Bhd has appointed Ravinder Singh Bachan Singh as Director, Group Technology, effective Sept 28, 2026.  The stock exchange operator said Ravinder, 45, will also be designated as a Principal Officer of the company upon assuming his new role.  Ravinder brings more than 20 years of experience in the domestic and international financial services industry, spanning investment banking, asset management, wealth management and transaction banking.  Prior to joining Bursa Malaysia, he served as Head of Technology for Maybank Investment Banking Group, where he oversaw technology functions across its investment banking and asset management businesses.  His expertise includes technology strategy and transformation, digital platforms, cybersecurity, operational resilience and technology governance across multiple markets.  Ravinder holds a Degree in Computing from Staffordshire University in the United Kingdom and is TOGAF 9 certified by The Open Group, a professional qualification in enterprise architecture.

title: 'The greater isolation of lesser Israel
body: 'Vijay Prashad When Benjamin Netanyahu rose to address the UN General Assembly on 24 September, the rows of empty seats spoke before he did. Diplomats walked out, while others stayed away from the outset. News reports citing an Israeli tally put the number of delegations absent or departing at 77. This was not a recorded UN vote, nor did all 77 stage a coordinated walkout. Yet the image of an Israeli prime minister speaking to a depleted chamber captured a real political fact: the destruction of Gaza and the consolidation of occupation have made Israel increasingly isolated across much of the world. The diplomats who stayed away or who walked out were overwhelmingly drawn from Africa, Asia, the Arab world and Latin America, although European states including Spain and Ireland boycotted the address. Brazil and South Africa did not show up, while Indonesia, Pakistan, Senegal, Sudan and Turkey stayed away. The empty seats did not mean that each of these countries stayed away for the same reason. However, it is essential to point out that for many of them, Palestine is not a distant diplomatic file but a liberation project akin to their own struggles against colonial rule and for sovereignty. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member They refused to listen to Netanyahu as the occupation, apartheid, genocide and expropriation were happening in plain sight. The rebuke came at the correct time. In his address, Netanyahu rejected all genocide allegations. However, in June 2026, a UN independent commission said that Israeli authorities and forces continued to commit genocide and other atrocity crimes, specifically in their treatment of Palestinian children. This commission had previously concluded in 2025 that Israel was committing a genocide. These are findings of a UN investigative body, not a final judgment in the genocide case before the International Court of Justice. The difference between a commission’s findings and a court’s eventual ruling matters legally, but it does not make the evidence of Israeli violence and Palestinian suffering disappear. Permanent genocide The 10 October 2025 ceasefire did not bring an end to the genocide or the suffering. UN humanitarian reporting in September 2026 describes continuing deaths, restricted access to essential supplies, mass displacement and a landscape of shattered homes and public services. Just before the report was published, in Tal al-Hawa on 16 September, a building damaged by Israeli attacks collapsed and killed at least 21 people, including eight children. “Israeli air strikes, shelling, drone attacks and ground operations have continued,” the UN investigators write, “and Palestinian casualties continue to mount. “Around two-thirds of Gaza remains inaccessible or subject to severe access restrictions, leaving Palestinian civilians confined to overcrowded and insecure areas.” Jaco Cilliers, the United Nations Development Programme’s special representative in Gaza, told Seham Tantesh: “The estimate of the total rubble in Gaza is 61 million tonnes. It is approximately 20 times the amount of rubble generated in all wars across the world over the last 18 years.” The global outrage at the genocide is not only retrospective, directed at the devastation of the years before the ceasefire. It responds to a present in which Palestinians remain exposed to violence, deprivation and political subjugation. Gaza is only one of three parts of the occupied Palestinian territory, the other two parts being East Jerusalem and the West Bank. In July 2024, the International Court of Justice held in an advisory opinion that Israel’s continued presence in the occupied territory was unlawful and that the Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the seizures of buildings and land in East Jerusalem violated international law. Drawing on this opinion, the UN General Assembly demanded that Israel end its unlawful presence within a year. As if to snub the UN, in April 2025 Israel established a new enforcement unit within its land authority to identify ‘illegal’ Palestinian construction in the West Bank with the intent of demolishing them and building more illegal settlements. The UN secretary general published his report in September 2025, which showed that nothing had changed a year after the UN General Assembly’s deadline passed. The gap between international legal principle and the facts imposed on the ground has become impossible to disguise with appeals to an indefinitely postponed peace process. Profits from apartheid On 25 September, the UN human rights office updated its database of businesses engaged specific activities connected to Israel’s illegal settlements. Its latest report, A/HRC/63/20, lists 214 enterprises based in 11 countries, compared with 158 in the 2025 edition. The UN says the list is limited to activities identified under its Human Rights Council mandate, and so it is not a catalogue of every company with commercial links to Israel, nor a judicial finding that each listed firm has committed a crime. Its purpose is to make the economic machinery of the settlements visible, which had been done in 2025 in the report by Francesca Albanese ‘From economy of occupation to economy of genocide. Report of the special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967’. These reports show that the settler machinery reaches well beyond the settler movement itself to companies that provide construction, finance, telecoms, services and markets. Through the work of these companies the ‘temporary’ nature of the settlements is made permanent. The database supplies a practical and concrete list for tracing the relationships between settlers and these companies and asks governments and investors what they will do about these relationships. Most listed enterprises are Israeli, but foreign firms included businesses that are mostly headquartered in the US and several European countries. These governments that invoke a ‘rules-based order’ cannot treat their own companies’ participation in such a blatantly unlawful settlement economy as an incidental commercial matter. The facts established in the list should now put additional pressure on states (in particular, Canada, France and the UK) whose public opposition to settlements is contradicted by the continuation of their firms in the settlement economy. The UN database does not automatically prescribe sanctions against named companies, but it does make indifference harder to defend. Governments can investigate listed activities, exclude settlement products and services from preferential treatment, examine public contracts and require firms to end involvement that sustains occupation. These measures would connect the principles proclaimed at the UN to the economic system that keeps settlements viable. Incomplete isolation Israel’s diplomatic isolation is substantial but incomplete. full_text: 'The greater isolation of lesser Israel. 'Vijay Prashad When Benjamin Netanyahu rose to address the UN General Assembly on 24 September, the rows of empty seats spoke before he did. Diplomats walked out, while others stayed away from the outset. News reports citing an Israeli tally put the number of delegations absent or departing at 77. This was not a recorded UN vote, nor did all 77 stage a coordinated walkout. Yet the image of an Israeli prime minister speaking to a depleted chamber captured a real political fact: the destruction of Gaza and the consolidation of occupation have made Israel increasingly isolated across much of the world. The diplomats who stayed away or who walked out were overwhelmingly drawn from Africa, Asia, the Arab world and Latin America, although European states including Spain and Ireland boycotted the address. Brazil and South Africa did not show up, while Indonesia, Pakistan, Senegal, Sudan and Turkey stayed away. The empty seats did not mean that each of these countries stayed away for the same reason. However, it is essential to point out that for many of them, Palestine is not a distant diplomatic file but a liberation project akin to their own struggles against colonial rule and for sovereignty. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member They refused to listen to Netanyahu as the occupation, apartheid, genocide and expropriation were happening in plain sight. The rebuke came at the correct time. In his address, Netanyahu rejected all genocide allegations. However, in June 2026, a UN independent commission said that Israeli authorities and forces continued to commit genocide and other atrocity crimes, specifically in their treatment of Palestinian children. This commission had previously concluded in 2025 that Israel was committing a genocide. These are findings of a UN investigative body, not a final judgment in the genocide case before the International Court of Justice. The difference between a commission’s findings and a court’s eventual ruling matters legally, but it does not make the evidence of Israeli violence and Palestinian suffering disappear. Permanent genocide The 10 October 2025 ceasefire did not bring an end to the genocide or the suffering. UN humanitarian reporting in September 2026 describes continuing deaths, restricted access to essential supplies, mass displacement and a landscape of shattered homes and public services. title: 'Zetrix Says Still Finalising Amount Owed to JPJ After Loke Reveals RM314m Arrears
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314 million in unpaid remittances. It said this in a bourse filing on Tuesday following queries from Bursa Malaysia about several news reports by The Edge about the arrears, and the subsequent suspension of Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG Sdn Bhd as JPJ collection agents, which Zetrix confirmed. To Bursa's queries regarding the reasons for the suspension and the circumstances that led to it, Zetrix gave a similar answer: that it was due to delays in remittances to JPJ, and that the company is in the process of finalising the outstanding amount with JPJ. On steps taken to address the issue, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. As to how long the suspension would last, Zetrix said the suspension would remain in place until its discussions with JPJ, the Ministry of Transport and other relevant government authorities are completed. "The company anticipates that the temporary suspension will be lifted upon mutual agreement and acceptance of the proposed solution framework submitted by the company to the relevant authorities," it said. "The company is actively engaging with JPJ, the Ministry of Transport Malaysia and the relevant government authorities to finalise the outstanding matters and the proposed solution framework as expeditiously as possible, with a view to minimising operational downtime. The company will make further announcements once a formal timeline or resolution is confirmed," Zetrix added. On operational impact, the group flagged that the suspension will result in a temporary loss of revenue and profit contributions from JPJ services in the fourth quarter of its financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (4QFY2026), but did not give any estimates. The affected services include road tax and driving licence renewals, learner's driving licence applications, summons enquiries and payments, vehicle ownership transfers and the Malaysian Computerised Driving Theory Test. On Monday, Loke revealed that Zetrix owes JPJ RM314 million after failing to remit collections — which it was required to do daily, within one working day of each transaction — between May and September this year. This led to the ministry and JPJ holding four engagement sessions with the company and issuing 35 reminders for the arrears to be settled, to no avail, he said. The government subsequently suspended Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG Sdn Bhd as JPJ collection agents. Loke also said Zetrix had issued the government a RM231 million cheque in September to settle the arrears, but the bank did not process it after the company instructed the bank to stop payment when the cheque was credited on Sept 30. The government will continue pursuing the arrears and could consider civil action, while Zetrix's JPJ services will not be restored until the outstanding amount is settled, Loke said. Even after payment, additional conditions would be imposed, including requiring collections to be credited directly into the government's account, he said. Zetrix, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, has provided online processing of JPJ services such as road tax and driving licence renewals since 2000, while its latest three-year contract began in May 2023. As of end-June, the company held RM541.6 million in cash and RM532.9 million in digital assets (cryptocurrencies), against RM2.19 billion in borrowings and RM90 million in trade payables, other payables and accruals. On Tuesday, Zetrix shares rebounded 2.5 sen or 38.5% to close at nine sen, valuing the company at RM727.1 million. The counter skidded to a 13-year low of 6.5 sen on Monday after its share price plunged 90% in just over a month following a sell-off at the counter that began at the end of August. The rout came amid reports that its largest shareholder Wong Thean Soon — better known as TS Wong — was facing forced selling. TS Wong's stake has since shrunk from 29% to 10%. title: 'Sabah Energy Corp raises RM350 mil in maiden sukuk, Maybank IB appointed as adviser
body: 'Sabah Energy Corp raises RM350 mil in maiden sukuk, Maybank IB appointed as adviser KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 17): Sabah Energy Corporation Sdn Bhd (SEC) has raised RM350 million through its maiden sukuk issuance under a RM3 billion sukuk wakalah programme. The issuance was announced in a joint statement with Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK). The sukuk was rated AAA with a stable outlook by RAM Rating Services Bhd and was priced through book-building, with demand reaching 2.2 times the amount offered. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd was appointed as the sole principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager and sustainability structure adviser, as well as shariah adviser and facility agent. “This landmark issuance broadens and diversifies SEC's access to long-term ringgit funding while raising the profile of both SEC and Sabah among domestic and international institutional investors. The strong over-subscription reflects investors' confidence in SEC's credit strength and growth trajectory," said Maybank IB chief executive officer Michael Oh-Lau. Maybank said the issuance gives the Sabah state-owned energy company a longer-term funding source as it plans investments across its energy businesses, including natural gas infrastructure, power generation and renewable energy. SEC said the funding platform will support its strategic roadmap called PETA (Pelan Strategik dan Hala Tuju) 2030, which covers the expansion of its gas and infrastructure operations, power generation and renewable energy activities, as well as investments across Sabah's energy value chain. “In turn, this supports the broader outcomes envisaged under SERAMP 2040: stronger energy security, a faster energy transition and more reliable supply for Sabah," said SEC group chief executive officer Datuk Adzmir Abd Rahman. SEC has been Sabah's sole natural gas aggregator, transporter and distributor since its corporatisation in 1997. It has since expanded into power generation, renewable energy and offshore oil and gas support services. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. Refer to the original content for accurate info. title: 'MHC reschedules Deepavali Day matches after public backlash
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The public are annoyed and are questioning why Malaysian Hockey League (MHL) matches will be played on Nov 8, Deepavali Day. The second round of MHL started on Monday, and two matches, Terengganu Hockey Team against Armed Forces and TNB Thunderbolts against Maybank, will be held on Nov 8. Both matches are to be played at TNB Stadium in Bangi. Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) chief executive officer V. Jayanandhan, when contacted, said that they are aware of it. "The two MHL hockey matches scheduled on Nov 8 will be changed to another date. I have already informed the MHL tournament director Dalit Singh," said Jayanandhan. "The Terengganu Hockey Team's match against Armed Forces will be played on Nov 9 while the match between TNB Thunderbolts and Maybank will be played on Nov 14.: League leaders Tenaga Nasional (TNB) were unhappy with the fixtures, as they have to play Forces on Wednesday with only 11 players having arrived from Japan on Monday after playing in the Asian Games. Daljit said they would make changes to the fixtures so that TNB's match against Forces will be played on another date. Clubs have to release national players for the six-nation Asian Champions Trophy in Punjab, India from Oct 27 to Nov 5 while the national league will continue during the tournament. This will affect clubs that won't have the services of national players in the MHL during the period. Officials need to be more professional in organising the MHL, as the national league is in haywire.

title: 'Haze keeps air quality unhealthy across most of S'pore as smoke drifts from Indonesia; Will haze affect the S'pore F1 Grand Prix? No race-day forecast yet from weatherman: Singapore live news
body: 'Haze keeps air quality unhealthy across most of S'pore as smoke drifts from Indonesia; Will haze affect the S'pore F1 Grand Prix? No race-day forecast yet from weatherman: Singapore live news A curated selection of some of the biggest, most important, and fascinating news that's making waves online, featured by Yahoo Singapore Air quality in four of Singapore's five regions remained unhealthy early on Tuesday (6 Oct), with the 24-hour PSI at 6am reaching 130 in the central region, 117 in the west, 112 in the east and 107 in the north, while only the south stayed moderate at 95, according to reports. One-hour PM2.5 levels were elevated in the central, west and east regions but normal in the north and south, following a worsening on Monday evening when the east joined the west and central regions in the unhealthy band. The National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast a 24-hour PSI in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range as south-easterly winds carry moderate to dense smoke from Kalimantan and southern Sumatra towards Singapore. NEA advises healthy people to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion while the PSI is unhealthy, with the elderly, pregnant women and children told to minimise it and people with chronic heart or lung disease told to avoid it. The PSI first breached the unhealthy threshold on 4 Sept, the first haze-driven breach since October 2023, and peaked at a 2026 high of 164 in central Singapore on 29 Sept. The Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS) said a strong El Niño could delay the end of the dry season, with the monsoon transition expected only in late October or early November. Political, business and cryptocurrency leaders, including Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, are gathering in hazy Singapore for finance conferences ahead of this weekend's Formula One Grand Prix. Hotel rates have soared, with the Fullerton Bay Hotel beside the track charging S$5,030 a night for a room that usually costs US$1,460, as hundreds of thousands of fans and about 90,000 top executives arrive, according to reports. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects F1 to generate S$160 million in tourism receipts this year, up from the usual S$145 million, while the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) said the events showed strong momentum despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty, Reuters reported. Slumping bond prices and cooling sentiment on artificial intelligence are expected to dominate the Forbes CEO Conference and the Milken Asia Summit, while a crypto event is nearly sold out even after the market's value fell about a quarter in a year. Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast "high moderate to mid unhealthy" air for Tuesday (6 Oct) but gave no forecast for Sunday's race, and weather analyst Fergus Keatinge said there was no clear sign the haze would end quickly. Indonesia recorded 15,461 hotspots in September, second only to 2015, as a strong El Niño fuelled fires that left Singapore the world's third-most polluted city on 30 Sept. Read more in our live blog below, including the latest local and international news and updates. - Joel Balbin Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1 as haze shrouds city Political, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are gathering in Singapore for a series of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Formula One Grand Prix, as haze from Indonesian fires continues to cover the city-state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, co-founder of his family's cryptocurrency business, are expected to attend, along with hundreds of thousands of F1 fans, according to Reuters. The Fullerton Bay Hotel beside the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933) a night for a room that usually costs US$1,460, as the night race and about 40 sideline events draw visitors. F1 generates about S$145 million a year in incremental tourism receipts, according to official estimates, and Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects that to reach S$160 million this year, plus broader gains from deals struck at sideline events, Reuters reported. The Singapore Tourism Board (STB) said F1 and its related events had strong momentum, reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. About 90,000 top-ranking executives are expected in town. Slumping bond prices and a shift in sentiment on artificial intelligence, from euphoric to cautious, are expected to occupy investors at the Forbes CEO Conference and the Milken Asia Summit, which begins on Wednesday (7 Oct). The total value of the cryptocurrency market has fallen about a quarter over 12 months to US$3 trillion, yet organisers of a crypto event said it was nearly sold out, with 25,000 attendees expected, matching last year, according to Reuters. Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast air quality in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range for Tuesday but gave no longer-range forecast for Sunday's race. Fergus Keatinge, director of WeatherMapping.com, said air quality would vary daily with wind and showers, but there was "no clear sign of a sustained pattern change" to end the haze quickly, according to Bloomberg. Kuala Lumpur topped IQAir's global pollution rankings on 30 Sept, with Singapore third, and poor air quality had forced organisers to shorten a Singapore half marathon at the last minute the previous weekend. Indonesia's forestry ministry recorded 15,461 hotspots in September, above 2019 levels and second only to 2015, as a strong El Niño brought abnormally hot and dry conditions. - Joel Balbin Air quality unhealthy as smoke drifts from Indonesia into Singapore amid haze Air quality in four of Singapore's five regions stayed in the unhealthy range early on Tuesday (6 Oct), with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) at 6am reading 130 in the central region, 117 in the west, 112 in the east and 107 in the north. Only the south, at 95, remained in the moderate band, where a reading of 101 to 200 is classed as unhealthy, Straits Times reported. One-hour PM2.5 readings, which guide immediate activities, were elevated in the central (60), west (59) and east (56) regions, while the north (48) and south (35) stayed at normal levels, according to Straits Times. The morning readings followed a deterioration on Monday evening, when the east reached a PSI of 101 at 6pm to join the west at 120 and the central region at 122 in the unhealthy band, with PM2.5 elevated in all five regions. The National Environment Agency (NEA) said in its 5 Oct advisory that with winds expected from the south-east or east-south-east, the 24-hour PSI was forecast to be in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range. Dry conditions are expected to persist over Kalimantan and southern Sumatra, where moderate to dense smoke plumes were seen drifting towards Singapore. Under NEA guidance, healthy people should reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion when the 24-hour PSI is unhealthy, while the elderly, pregnant women and children should minimise it and people with chronic heart or lung disease should avoid it. When PM2.5 is elevated, healthy people are advised to cut strenuous outdoor activity for the next hour, and vulnerable groups should avoid it. The PSI first crossed into the unhealthy range on 4 Sept, the first haze-driven breach since October 2023, and the year's highest reading of 164 was recorded in central Singapore on 29 Sept. The Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS) told the media that strong El Niño events tend to delay the end of the dry season, and that it expects Singapore's monsoon transition only in late October or early November, later than in the previous two years. title: 'El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities
body: 'El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 7): Hotter and drier conditions from El Niño could put greater pressure on Malaysia’s electricity and water systems into 2027, according to CIMB Securities. The research house said El Niño is expected to persist into early 2027 and peak between March and May, potentially lifting electricity demand for cooling while worsening water shortages. It said Malaysia is particularly exposed as electricity demand is already rising, while about 37% of treated water is lost through non-revenue water (NRW). “Hotter and drier conditions could further strain both systems, strengthening the need for cooling efficiency, water conservation, and better infrastructure management,” CIMB said. Malaysia’s peak electricity demand is projected to increase to 33.5 gigawatts (GW) by 2035 from 21.3GW in 2026, while data centres could account for 31% of Peninsular Malaysia’s electricity demand by then. CIMB said hotter weather could further increase cooling demand across commercial buildings, industrial facilities and data centres, adding to the country’s underlying electricity load growth. On the water side, Malaysia’s NRW rate remained high at 37.1% in 2024, meaning more than one-third of treated water was lost before reaching consumers. The losses are estimated to cost more than RM2 billion annually. Water stress is already visible in some areas, with two of the 49 dams monitored nationwide at critical levels as at Aug 31, namely the Muda Dam in Kedah and Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan. CIMB said the government’s RM2.5 billion National NRW Programme and RM1.7 billion allocation under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800km of critical water pipes should support efforts to improve water efficiency. The research house named KJTS Group Bhd (KL:KJTS) and Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB) as its preferred beneficiaries of the theme. KJTS offers direct exposure to rising cooling demand through its cooling energy and energy-efficiency businesses, while Insights Analytics provides digital water solutions including leak detection, pressure management and smart metering. CIMB maintained “buy” calls on both companies, with target prices of RM1.35 for KJTS and RM1.95 for Insights Analytics. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body: 'SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460. This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee

title: 'Asia Among Most Vulnerable to AI Correction, Asean Unit Warns
body: '(Oct 5): Southeast Asia plus China, Japan and South Korea are more at risk than most economies to any potential collapse in the artificial-intelligence boom, which could trigger shocks across financial markets and the real economy. The region is “particularly exposed” because it’s at the centre of global AI supply chains and “increasingly integrated into AI-related financial markets,” the Asean+3 Macroeconomic Research Office said in its 2026 Financial Stability Report published on Monday. “A disorderly correction could therefore propagate through multiple channels — including lower technology exports, portfolio losses, capital outflows, refinancing pressure on leveraged technology and infrastructure firms, and weaker investor confidence,” it said. The report comes amid growing investor concern about the AI boom, including the high valuation of tech companies, the surge in spending on chips and data centres, and circular financing deals in which companies appear to be funding each other. Tech-related exports have been helping Asia withstand the impact of high energy prices and US tariffs. Much of the physical production in the technology cycle takes place in Asia, from memory chips in South Korea to semiconductor assembly in Malaysia. The region accounted for two-thirds of the growth in global AI-related trade, Amro said. Should AI demand suddenly fall short, a pullback in capital spending would undermine export revenues, investments and broader economic growth. Some regional equity markets are also heavily concentrated on AI, such as South Korea, exposing them to a sharp correction in prices. Other markets like Japan and Hong Kong have come to move closely in line with US AI and technology firms, meaning shocks could also be transmitted even absent a domestic trigger, according to Amro. As hyperscalers increasingly turn to borrowings to fund costly data centre buildouts, higher leverage could amplify shocks if AI returns disappoint, the report said. Opaque private credit markets and circular financing deals could worsen the instability. “A sharp correction in AI-related financial assets could spill over to the broader financial system through forced deleveraging and tighter credit conditions,” Amro said. Central bankers around the world, from the Bank of England to the Monetary Authority of Singapore, have increasingly raised concerns about whether massive AI investments can be sustainable. The technology has developed at breakneck speed, but stiff competition among developers, higher borrowing costs and growing pushback against data centres and AI’s security threats have raised concerns. title: 'CIMB Says Lindung 24 Can Narrow Malaysia’s Protection Gap
body: 'Evidently, the SOCSO’s Lindung 24 social insurance scheme is expected to significantly broaden accident protection for workers without materially disrupting the private insurance and takaful industry.  In a sector report, CIMB Securities said Lindung 24, which was implemented by the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) on June 1, extends protection beyond work-related accidents to provide eligible workers with 24-hour coverage for non-employment accidents, alongside income replacement, rehabilitation and dependants’ benefits.  The research house maintained its Neutral stance on Malaysia’s insurance sector, saying the scheme is primarily aimed at underinsured workers and complements rather than replaces private medical, life and disability coverage.  CIMB said the protection gap remains substantial. Citing Perkeso, it noted that only about 48% of Malaysians have insurance protection beyond motor insurance, while coverage among the bottom 40% income group is estimated at just 4%.  About 38,000 claims were rejected between 2015 and 2025 because employees did not meet traditional eligibility requirements for employment-related accidents. With Lindung 24, Perkeso estimates that roughly 250,000 employees a year could benefit from protection for accidents previously outside the conventional workplace definition.  Take-up has also remained high. As at Sept 9, 8.5 million workers, or 87.6% of the estimated workforce, remained enrolled after the opt-out period for local workers ended on Aug 31. Around 1.2 million workers opted out, with 52% of them earning below RM3,500 per month.  Lindung 24 covers non-work accidents occurring at home, during personal travel, recreational activities, religious activities and other off-duty situations, complementing Perkeso’s existing Employment Injury Scheme, which applies to work-related accidents.  The contribution rate is currently 0.75% of monthly salary until May 2028. It will increase to 1.0% from June 2028 and 1.25% from June 2031, with both contributions and benefits capped at a monthly wage of RM6,000.  Benefits include temporary and permanent disablement payments, medical treatment, rehabilitation, dependants’ benefits, funeral assistance and education support. CIMB noted that fully disabled contributors could receive up to 90% of covered income for life, subject to Perkeso’s assessment and applicable rules.  For insurers, CIMB sees the greatest potential overlap in standalone and employer-sponsored personal accident policies. Employers could eventually rationalise duplicated accident benefits and redirect spending towards medical coverage and other employee benefits.  However, private insurance remains relevant for higher-income workers because Lindung 24 benefits are capped at the RM6,000 salary ceiling, while private products provide broader medical, life, critical illness and income protection.  CIMB said the longer-term effect could be positive by raising awareness of underinsurance and encouraging insurers to focus on higher-value protection and health products. It maintained its Neutral sector view, while remaining more constructive on LPI Capital than Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia meningkat semula untuk dibuka tinggi pada Jumaat didorong oleh hasil Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang rendah dan sentimen Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) yang berhati-hati memberikan kelegaan kepada pelabur. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.49 mata atau 0.09 peratus kepada 1,631.85 daripada 1,630.36 semasa ditutup pada Khamis. Indeks dibuka tinggi 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 239 berbanding 137 manakala 270 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,127 tidak diniagakan dan 24 yang lain digantung. Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 173.94 juta saham bernilai RM95.98 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata penurunan terkini telah mendorong indeks kembali kepada keadaan terlebih jual, yang boleh menggalakkan aktiviti belian saham pada harga rendah. “Bagaimanapun, dengan situasi jualan asing yang dilaporkan, kami percaya sebarang peningkatan awal mungkin kekal sederhana. “Namun demikian, aliran penurunan membuka peluang untuk membeli secara terpilih saham yang mempunyai asas kukuh terutamanya dalam kalangan bank yang mapan, syarikat utiliti dan syarikat semikonduktor,” katanya kepada Bernama. Thong berkata pemulihan yang lebih mampan memerlukan penyertaan yang lebih baik daripada kaunter saham wajaran tinggi dan peningkatan jumlah saham daripada pelbagai sektor. Oleh itu, beliau menjangka dagangan berhati-hati hari ini dalam julat 1,625 hingga 1,640. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank mendatar pada RM9.95, Public Bank dan CIMB, masing-masing menurun satu sen kepada RM4.66 dan RM7.68, Tenaga Nasional naik empat sen kepada RM12.94 dan IHH Healthcare meningkat satu sen kepada RM7.71. Dalam dagangan aktif, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources dan Genetec, masing-masing kekal tidak berubah pada 16.5 sen, 18 sen dan 32.5 sen, V.S Industry naik satu sen kepada 28 sen, bagaimanapun Kinergy Advancement menurun setengah sen kepada 39.5 sen. Kaunter paling untung ialah Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat 58 sen kepada RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining naik 19 sen kepada RM3.83, Petronas Chemicals menokok 15 sen kepada RM4.28 serta UWC dan MI Technovation, masing-masing menambah 10 sen kepada RM7.20 dan RM5.36. Kaunter paling rugi termasuklah MISC menurun 14 sen kepada RM7.54, LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB dan RHB Bank, masing-masing merosot empat sen kepada RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78 dan RM7.43. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 75.93 mata kepada 17,434.91, Indeks FBM Emas naik 17.18 mata kepada 12,160.71 dan Indeks FBM Top 100 menokok 21.58 mata kepada 11,954.73. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menambah 34.76 mata kepada 12,047.77 dan Indeks FBM ACE naik 18.61 mata kepada 5,501.58. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk Perindustrian dan Perkhidmatan meningkat 1.10 mata kepada 178.83, Indeks Tenaga naik 9.45 mata kepada 844.46, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menurun 26.33 mata kepada 19,034.58 manakala Indeks Perladangan menokok 2.75 mata kepada 9,029.32.- Bernama

title: 'Mustapha Proposes Committee to Work Out Mechanism for Sabah, Sarawak Parliamentary Seat Increase
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud has proposed the establishment of a special committee under the Technical Committee of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) to work out the mechanism for increasing parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak. He also proposed that the special committee be co-chaired by him and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. “The increase in the number of members of Parliament from Sabah and Sarawak has been included in the agenda of MTPMA63 and its Technical Committee meetings, and has also been discussed extensively at Cabinet meetings. “Following the decision, I held preliminary discussions with the Election Commission (EC) to seek its views and determine the next course of action,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat on Monday. He said this in response to a supplementary question from Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo), who sought clarification on the mechanisms and legislative steps required to increase parliamentary seats for the two states. Mustapha said discussions on the matter would continue at upcoming meetings of the MTPMA63 Technical Committee. Meanwhile, he said 13 of the 26 matters under the MTPMA63 negotiation platform had been categorised as resolved, following decisions made at the first MTPMA63 meeting held on Sept 11. “Of the 26 matters, three have been categorised as partially resolved, five remain unresolved, while another five have been brought before the prime minister, the Sarawak premier and the Sabah chief minister for discussion,” he said. Mustapha said the MA63-related matters brought before the highest level for discussion and decision-making included oil royalties and petroleum cash payments, stamp duties, the Territorial Sea Act 2012, and state rights over the continental shelf. He said the Madani government was committed to expediting the resolution of all claims under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), although the timeframe for resolving each claim was subject to the relevant legal processes. “The Madani government remains firmly committed to ensuring the prudent and inclusive implementation of MA63, grounded in the spirit of strong federalism,” he said. title: 'M’sians Camp Outside Maybank From 4am For BTS Card, Turning It Into Mini ‘Concert’ | WeirdKaya
body: 'What time would you wake up for a debit card? For some Malaysian BTS fans, apparently before the sun even comes up. Fans were seen gathering outside Maybank’s Shah Alam Main Branch in Seksyen 14 from the early hours of the morning after the Maybank Visa | BTS WORLD TOUR ‘ARIRANG’ Debit Card became available on Sept. 23. And judging from the crowd, you might have mistaken the bank for a BTS concert venue. Fans arrived as early as 4am A staff member shared photos of the situation on Threads, showing BTS fans waiting both inside and outside the Shah Alam branch. In one post, he jokingly asked: Is this a bank or a BTS concert?” Speaking to WeirdKaya, Irfan confirmed that the scenes were taken at the Shah Alam Main Branch in Seksyen 14. According to him, customers had already begun showing up at around 3am to 4am. And the excitement did not stop after the first day. Day 2 also saw fans ‘camping’ outside In another update the following morning, Irfan shared a photo showing a group of customers sitting outside the bank while waiting for it to open. “Pagi ni pun ramai betul dah camping depan bank eh 😂,” he wrote. The photo showed fans sitting along the walkway with their bags and belongings, looking more like they were waiting for concert doors to open than preparing for a banking transaction. Once inside, the BTS energy continued. Photos shared by Irfan showed a packed banking hall, with customers holding BTS themed items while staff attended to the crowd. The atmosphere even prompted Irfan, who handles the branch’s speaker, to ask followers what songs they wanted him to play for the day. Staff came early to hype up the crowd too “I came early as I usually do just to hype up the crowd,” he said. The hype surrounds the limited edition Maybank Visa | BTS WORLD TOUR ‘ARIRANG’ Debit Card, which became available from Sept. 23, 2026.

title: 'Bomba’s Fire Safety Manager Mandate for 9,451 Buildings Puts Compliance Demand in Focus for Unique Fire
body: 'Malaysia’s move to make building owners directly accountable for fire safety is set to widen the compliance market for fire protection suppliers, placing Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) among the companies positioned to benefit. From 1 April 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint a Fire Safety Manager (FSM) and a Fire Safety Officer (FSO), and to establish a Fire Safety Organisation at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement is in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025. Nor Hisham said any building inspected over the next one to two years that is required to hold a Fire Certificate will have to put the new structure in place. He was speaking after launching the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur on 6 October 2026, where the first cohort of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs received their certificates. A key change lies in how Fire Certificates will be renewed. Going forward, JBPM will assess annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs for certificate renewal, instead of physically inspecting every building each year. JBPM currently has 13 registered training providers and has issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. Compliance shifts to building owners The framework transfers day-to-day fire safety responsibility from the authorities to building owners and their certified in-house personnel. Under the programme, FSMs undergo a five-day course covering building inspections, evacuation planning, reporting and maintenance, while FSOs complete a three-day technical course. With a certified FSM accountable for an annual report that underpins Fire Certificate renewal, building owners are expected to place greater emphasis on keeping fire extinguishers, hose reels, hydrants, sprinkler systems, detection and alarm devices and suppression systems in working order. This points to steadier demand for equipment replacement, servicing and refilling across the 9,451 designated premises, which include high-occupancy and high-risk buildings. Unique Fire, established in 1997 and headquartered in Shah Alam, Selangor, assembles, manufactures and distributes active fire protection systems, equipment and accessories for the built environment. Its range spans hand portable fire extinguishers, fire hose reels, hydrant and sprinkler systems, wet and dry riser systems, fire detection and alarm devices, and fire suppression systems including wet chemical and carbon dioxide systems. The Group markets products under its own Unique, Unique227, Yama and Commander brands alongside third-party brands such as Kidde, and also provides fire protection equipment servicing and dry chemical fire extinguisher refilling machines. The Group has already identified the amended Act as a demand driver. For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, Unique Fire’s revenue rose 6.2% to RM114.7 million, supported by stronger assembly and distribution sales, particularly of fire suppression systems. Executive Director Marcus Liew said the core fire protection business continued to grow amid a supportive regulatory environment, backed by enforcement of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025 and project rollouts under the 13th Malaysia Plan, and that the Group expects sustained demand driven by regulatory compliance requirements and ongoing contract awards. The Group is also extending its reach beyond Malaysia through Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, a 60:40 joint venture with Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd to manufacture and supply fire sprinklers, with Shanghai Mosafe providing technical support towards Underwriters Laboratories (UL) certification. With the FSM and FSO requirement taking effect in less than six months, the new compliance regime is set to move fire safety from a once-a-year inspection exercise to a continuous obligation for building owners, a shift that plays directly into Unique Fire’s product and service offering.

title: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah jemput orang ramai ke ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ sempena perkahwinan
body: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah jemput orang ramai ke ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ sempena perkahwinan KUALA LUMPUR – Bakal raja sehari, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan tunangnya, Bella Astillah menjemput orang ramai menghadiri majlis ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ sempena perkahwinan mereka yang bakal berlangsung pada 10 Oktober ini. Majlis berkenaan akan diadakan di Muar, Johor pada 25 Oktober, sebelum diteruskan di Kota Kinabalu, Sabah pada 31 Oktober. Syed Saddiq yang juga Ahli Parlimen Muar berkata, kedua-dua majlis resepsi itu dirancang dalam tempoh kurang dua bulan, sekali gus menyebabkan mereka berdepan kekangan masa dan kesukaran mendapatkan lokasi yang sesuai. Katanya, konsep ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ dipilih dengan mengetengahkan semangat rewang dan meraikan perkahwinan bersama masyarakat. “Majlis kahwin kami nanti bertemakan rewang. Kalau sebelum ini, sambutan Hari Raya yang saya anjurkan di Muar sudah mencecah 10,000 orang, jadi kita jangka untuk kenduri kami lebih ramai yang akan datang. “Jadi, majlis itu nanti berkonsepkan ‘siapa cepat dia dapat’ (nikmati juadah). Jika makanan habis sekalipun, kami akan berada di sana untuk bersama dengan tetamu,” katanya pada majlis Walimatulurus Bella Astillah dan Syed Saddiq, di sini hari ini. Sebanyak 10,000 cenderahati istimewa turut disediakan untuk tetamu yang hadir ke majlis berkenaan. Ditanya mengenai perasaannya menghitung hari bahagia bersama Bella pada 10 Oktober nanti, Syed Saddiq pantas menjawab: “Saya tak sabar nak menghalalkan hubungan kami.” Menurut Syed Saddiq, dia mengakui tidak rasa berdebar, tetapi tidak sabar untuk bergelar suami kepada Bella. “Perasaan saya lebih kepada tidak sabar berbanding berdebar. Tak sabar nak kongsikan hari bahagia kami bersama semua termasuklah keluarga dan sahabat andai. “Saya selalu kongsikan kepada bakal isteri saya, kebahagiaan perlu dikongsikan kepada semua kerana tanpa doa, sokongan dan dorongan orang ramai, mungkin hari ini (perkahwinan) tidak akan terjadi. Setiap orang ada saham dalam menjayakan perkahwinan kami,” katanya. Sebelum ini, Syed Saddiq dan Bella mengesahkan mereka bakal disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada 10 Oktober ini. Majlis pernikahan pasangan itu dijadual berlangsung di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, di sini, dengan konsep serba putih yang disulami elemen Arab dan Islamik atas permintaan keluarga. Menariknya perjalanan kisah cinta mereka dari mula perkenalan sehingga menjelang hari perkahwinan bakal disiarkan dalam program khas Walimatulurus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq yang akan ditayangkan di Astro Ria bermula 6 Oktober 2026. Syed Saddiq dan Bella dilaporkan mula berkenalan dengan lebih rapat pada 2025 sebelum mengikat tali pertunangan pada 28 Mac lalu.

title: 'Maybank, Gallant Venture to develop Bintan halal hub
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has teamed up with Gallant Venture to develop the Bintan Inti Halal Hub (BIHH), a halal industrial ecosystem in Bintan, Indonesia amid growing global demand for halal products and services. The collaboration brings together Maybank's regional banking and halal ecosystem expertise with Gallant's industrial infrastructure to create opportunities for businesses looking to expand across Asean's growing halal economy. Maybank will provide a comprehensive suite of Islamic banking and financial solutions to businesses operating within BIHH and across the broader halal value chain. "This includes account services, deposits, cash management solutions, foreign exchange services, trade and working capital financing, payroll and settlement solutions, as well as access to Maybank's regional network and Islamic banking expertise," the bank said in a statement. The hub will support businesses expanding across Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia, while attracting international investment into regional manufacturing and trading operations. Businesses will also gain access to halal certification support, business matching, strategic partners and Salaam Marketplace, Malaysia's first B2B halal marketplace, which expanded to Singapore in November 2025. Maybank Islamic Bhd group chief executive officer of Islamic banking and Maybank Islamic Bhd chief executive officer Yasin Abdullah said the initiative strengthens the ecosystem needed to help businesses connect, grow and tap into regional halal trade opportunities. He said the halal economy was among the fastest-growing segments globally, presenting significant opportunities for businesses across Southeast Asia. "This initiative also supports our ROAR30 aspirations - powering the real economy, opening up RM100 billion in opportunities for small and medium enterprise, and building the foundations for Maybank's global Islamic leadership. "By bringing together financing, market access, industry partnerships and halal ecosystem capabilities, we aim to support businesses throughout their expansion journey and contribute meaningfully to Asean's halal economy," he added.

title: 'Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.   Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).   “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today.

title: 'Refugees are not ‘foreign fugitives’
body: 'Charles Santiago The Ministry of Home Affairs should be careful about the language it uses to describe Myanmar nationals in Malaysia. People who have fled genocide, conflict or religious persecution are not “foreign fugitives” simply because they lack regular immigration status. Immigration status and criminality are not interchangeable. The government says the repatriation programme is voluntary, orderly and based on individual consent. But a genuinely voluntary return requires more than a signature. People must be able to make an informed decision, free from coercion, with a proper assessment of the risks they face on return. It is particularly troubling that the UNHCR, the UN’s refugee agency, says it had no role in Malaysia’s repatriation process. It has also warned that Myanmar remains unsafe for refugee returns. Consultation needs to be transparent too. Where is the meaningful engagement with the UNHCR, Suhakam, refugee-led organisations and civil society groups that have worked directly with these communities for years? - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member These groups hold information about individual vulnerabilities, family circumstances, protection concerns and conditions in Myanmar. Government agencies cannot simply assume they know these things. If the government has carried out comprehensive screening and concluded that every person returned can safely go home, it should publish the methodology, safeguards and independent verification mechanisms behind that conclusion. And if the government’s justification is that Myanmar nationals are a ‘financial burden’ or a ‘security threat’, the people of Malaysia deserve evidence. What is the actual public expenditure? Which specific security threats are being referred to? Are they a bigger threat than the two million undocumented migrant workers who have been in the country for the past 20 years or so? This is not about asking Malaysia to abandon immigration enforcement or national sovereignty. It is about insisting that sovereignty and the rule of law operate alongside due process, evidence and protection from return to danger. The return of 1,476 people has now begun. That makes transparency and independent scrutiny even more urgent. It also makes it harder for Malaysia to claim the moral authority to speak forcefully about the forced displacement of Palestinians, or to champion refugee rights elsewhere. Vulnerable people are being returned to a country where they could face detention, torture, forced conscription or death. Charles Santiago is a prominent Malaysian politician, economist and human rights advocate who served three terms as the MP for Klang and has twice chaired the National Water Services Commission. title: 'PNB unit eyes up to RM600mil recurring annual income from Merdeka 118
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd expects recurring income from the completed Merdeka 118 development to reach RM500 million-RM600 million a year over the medium term. About 70 per cent of the project's office space is already sub-leased, according to MARC Ratings. The firm said the office component is fully leased to parent Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) under a triple-net master lease. This shields PNB Merdeka from occupancy and most property-related cost risks. MARC said about 70 per cent of the tower's 1.6 million sq ft net lettable area (NLA) has been sub-leased. This comprises 40 per cent, or 33 floors, sub-leased to Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), 20 per cent to PNB and about 10 per cent to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to rise to about 90 per cent over the next five years, with the office tower projected to generate annual net property income of about RM137 million. MARC has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka's RM6 billion Merdeka sukuk Wakalah with a stable outlook. The rating aligns with PNB's AAA/Stable corporate credit rating, supported by PNB's unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee covering any shortfall in principal and profit payments under the sukuk. MARC said for the seven-storey retail mall, which is expected to open next month, lease agreements covering 81 per cent of its 750,324 sq ft NLA have either been signed or are under negotiation, at an indicative average rental of RM11.92 per sq ft. The Merdeka 118 development, near Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, has incurred RM10.6 billion in development costs to date. The cost was largely funded by two earlier sukuk programmes that have since been restructured into the current rated issuance. The planned residential components are expected to add another RM1.4 billion in development costs, to be funded through a mix of borrowings and equity injections. Two residential towers, with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM2 billion, are targeted for launch in the first half of 2027, while a serviced apartment project has an estimated GDV of RM745 million. MARC said these residential and serviced apartment components remain exposed to demand risk amid competing developments in Kuala Lumpur. PNB Merdeka is wholly owned by PNB and was established to undertake the Merdeka 118 project. This includes the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank, a 17-floor luxury hotel, a three-floor observation deck and the upcoming retail mall. PNB Merdeka is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both designated National Heritage sites.
