title: 'F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia | Oh! Media
body: 'Intipati berita - 300,000 pengunjung disasarkan hadir ke SIC, termasuk 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa. - F1 dijangka menjana impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion kepada Malaysia. - MOTAC & Tourism Malaysia menyediakan pakej pelancongan untuk menggalakkan pelancong asing tinggal lebih lama di Malaysia. - F1 turut menjadi platform mempromosikan pelancongan, budaya dan seni Malaysia sempena Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027. Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 300,000 pengunjung sempena penganjuran Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) dari 2 hingga 4 Oktober. Menurut laporan Berita RTM, daripada jumlah itu, kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa dijangka hadir ke SIC bagi menyaksikan perlumbaan berprestij tersebut. Ketua Komunikasi Korporat MOTAC, Firna Azura Ekaputri Marzuki berkata, berdasarkan unjuran Hong Leong Bank Research, penganjuran F1 itu dijangka memberi impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion. Berdasarkan data penyelidikan Hong Leong Bank, penganjuran F1 ini sahaja dijangka mampu menjana pendapatan sebanyak RM1.3 bilion melalui sektor pelancongan sukan dan perbelanjaan pelancong asing. Setakat ini, kita menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa daripada keseluruhan 300,000 pengunjung yang dijangka membanjiri SIC bagi menyaksikan Grand Prix F1 tersebut. MOTAC ada sediakan pakej pelancongan? Menurut Firna Azura, penganjuran F1 ini turut bertepatan dengan Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027 dan menjadi platform untuk memperkenalkan budaya, seni serta produk pelancongan negara kepada pelancong antarabangsa. MOTAC menerusi Tourism Malaysia bersama SIC turut menyediakan beberapa pakej pelancongan bagi menggalakkan pengunjung luar negara melanjutkan tempoh penginapan mereka di Malaysia. Selain menyaksikan F1, kita turut menggalakkan mereka untuk berbelanja, membeli-belah dan melakukan aktiviti pelancongan seperti melawat destinasi menarik di negara ini. Ini kerana selepas penganjuran F1 di Malaysia, saingan seterusnya akan berlangsung di Singapura. Siapa terlibat dalam persiapan penganjuran? Dalam pada itu, persiapan di bawah Jawatankuasa Publisiti, Promosi dan Pelancongan kini dilaporkan mencapai kira-kira 90 peratus. Pelbagai kementerian dan agensi terlibat bagi memastikan penganjuran berjalan lancar, antaranya KUSKOP, KBS, Kementerian Komunikasi, Tourism Malaysia, Kraftangan Malaysia, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Majlis Perbandaran Sepang serta SIC. Apa maksudnya untuk anda? Bagi memeriahkan lagi penganjuran F1 hari kejadian, beberapa program berskala besar turut diatur dari 23 September hingga 4 Oktober. Antaranya ialah Litar Rasa MADANI, Sepang Food Festival di Mitsui Outlet Park, Citrawarna Speed Festival dan RIUH Pitstop di TRX. Selain itu, Malaysia International Craft Fair 2026 turut berlangsung di Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur.

title: 'Mosti’s Cradle Fund Sees Overcrowding in Applicants as 70% Are AI-related Startups
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Artificial intelligence (AI)-related startups now account for about 60% to 70% of the estimated 1,000 applications received by Cradle Fund each year, but investors are becoming more selective as the space grows increasingly crowded. Cradle Fund group chief executive officer Norman Matthieu Vanhaecke said the government agency has seen a sharp increase in startups positioning themselves as AI-driven, AI-enabled or AI-native. “The market is getting really, really crowded. So it's kind of tough for venture capitalists later on, and even for us as well, to really decide where to park, for us, especially taxpayers money into,” he said during a panel session at the Alliance Bank BizSmart Business Conference. "At the end of the day, for us, the return has to come back to the country and the people. So it's tough for us. So you have to really differentiate," he added. This has made it more difficult for investors and Cradle Fund, which manages taxpayer funds, to determine which AI businesses have sufficient potential to warrant funding, he said. Cradle Fund was created by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mosti) in 2023. It provides grants, equity investment, commercialisation support, and mentorship to tech entrepreneurs. Startups need to differentiate themselves by developing niche solutions that can serve not only the Malaysian market but also regional and international markets, Vanhaecke said. At the same conference, Sunway iLabs — the innovation arm of Sunway Bhd (KL:SUNWAY) — chief operations officer Karen Lau said investors also need to distinguish between companies that genuinely have AI capabilities and those that are simply using AI as part of their positioning. Investors are looking at the defensibility of the technology, including whether a startup is merely building a layer on top of existing frontier models or has technology that can be integrated deeply into customers’ business processes, she said. Meanwhile, fellow panellist 1337 Ventures CEO and founding partner Bikesh Lakhmichand said the firm looks for founders with expertise in a specific industry, such as healthcare, fashion or marketing, rather than startups built around generic AI applications. “What we are funding is your expertise in the sector, not so much AI,” he said, adding that startups need to demonstrate how their technology addresses specific workflows. Lakhmichand said generic AI applications could face greater competition as foundation models continue to develop. The panel also highlighted a broader shift in how investors assess startups, with traction, market potential and the ability to scale becoming more important than simply positioning a company as an AI business. The session was focused on What It Really Takes for Scaling, Funding, and Strategic Exits?, and was moderated by Redwood Global Capital managing partner Lennise Ng. title: 'Stock Today: Maybank Gains 0.5% After ASB Disposal
body: 'Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) rose 0.5% in late morning trade on Friday, despite Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) having disposed of 13 million shares in the bank earlier this week.  As of 10.56am, Maybank gained five sen to RM10.00, after opening at RM9.95. The stock traded between RM9.93 and RM10.02 during the session.  Some 1.33 million shares had changed hands, with the last done price above the previous adjusted close of RM9.95.  At the time, 598,000 shares were queued to buy at RM9.99 while 1.52 million shares were queued to sell at RM10.00.  Maybank disclosed on Oct 1 that AmanahRaya Trustees Bhd, as trustee for ASB, had disposed of 13 million shares on Sept 29 through a sale of shares.  Following the disposal, ASB’s direct stake in Maybank stood at 3.418 billion shares, representing 28.261% of the bank’s issued shares.  The notice of change in substantial shareholding was dated Sept 29 and received by Maybank on Oct 1.

title: 'Religious council to bear sisters’ funeral costs after Tambun accident
body: 'IPOH: The Perak Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIPk) will bear the funeral costs for two sisters who died in a road accident near Taman Perpaduan Ria, Tambun here on Friday (Oct 2). title: 'Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). "From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises," he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce the department's workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. "In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by the department for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year," he said. To meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, the department expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide, he said. He said the fire department currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony.

body: 'Bursa Malaysia meneruskan penurunan pada tengah hari Khamis apabila tekanan jualan kembali mendominasi pasaran, selari dengan prestasi bercampur pasaran global ketika kenaikan hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat terus mengehadkan sentimen risiko. Saham Bank Dan Tenaga Terus Tertekan Dalam kalangan saham berwajaran tinggi, Maybank dan Tenaga Nasional masing-masing susut 6 sen kepada RM9.93 dan RM12.90. Public Bank pula turun 4 sen kepada RM4.66, manakala CIMB berkurang 5 sen kepada RM7.74. IHH Healthcare turut susut 19 sen kepada RM7.64. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Index Falls Amid Heavyweight Declines
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia continued to experience a downturn at mid-morning, largely driven by selling pressures in leading sectors such as healthcare, industrial products, and utilities. According to BERNAMA News Agency, at 11 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped by 11.73 points to 1,639.44, compared to the previous day's close of 1,651.17, after opening slightly lower at 1,649.87. In the healthcare sector, IHH Healthcare saw a decrease of 13 sen to RM7.70. Within industrial products, Petronas Chemicals fell 11 sen to RM4.07, Press Metal Aluminium went down nine sen to RM7.36, and Sunway dipped two sen to RM4.40. Utilities counters also took a hit, with YTL Power dropping six sen to RM5.81, YTL Corporation declining by one sen to RM2.27, and Tenaga Nasional decreasing by two sen to RM12.94. The overall market saw 484 decliners surpassing 273 gainers, with 460 counters unchanged. Additionally, 1,556 counters remained untraded, and 12 were suspended. The market turnover was recorded at 1.18 billion shares valued at RM769.76 million. Hong Leong Investment Bank noted that the ongoing US-Iran tensions and the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance could prolong the benchmark index's risk-off consolidation, influenced by high oil prices, bond yields, and continued foreign outflows. Among major stocks, Maybank and CIMB each dropped by two sen to RM9.97 and RM7.77, respectively, while Public Bank declined three sen to RM4.67. In active trades, Zetrix AI increased by half a sen to 16.5 sen, V.S Industry rose one sen to 29 sen, Jaks Resources fell half a sen to 20 sen, ACE Market newcomer GB Bond decreased by 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, and Dagang Nexchange rose two sen to 50.5 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which increased by 62 sen to RM41.02, Malayan Cement rising by 12 sen to RM5.57, and both MI Technovation and Hengyuan Refining gaining 10 sen to RM5.30 and RM3.66, respectively. Vitrox saw an increase of eight sen to RM9.99. Conversely, Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 74 sen to RM21.46, followed by Allianz Malaysia, which shed 68 sen to RM20.94. Nestle fell 40 sen to RM89.60, United Plantations dropped 30 sen to RM31.26, and Hong Leong Bank lost 28 sen to RM22.86. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased by 71.17 points to 17,503.50, the FBM Emas Index fell 72.18 points to 12,219.83, and the FBM Top 100 Index declined by 76.32 points to 12,008.12. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened by 71.61 points to 12,104.73, and the FBM ACE Index decreased by 22.64 points to 5,511.64. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index dropped by 1.24 points to 179.17, the Energy Index eased by 5.43 points to 840.27, the Financial Services Index fell 87.09 points to 19,129.40, and the Plantation Index retreated by 104.26 points to 9,092.41.

title: 'Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai kelmarin menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja yang dirasmikan oleh Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah Almarhum Sultan Iskandar Al-Haj di The Mines Resort and Golf Club. Kejohanan yang berlangsung selama tiga hari itu menyaksikan penyertaan seramai 50 pemain merangkumi kelompok profesional dan amatur termasuklah kemunculan semula juara bertahan, Liyana Durisic serta atlet Olimpik negara, Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan itu adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan selain bertindak sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Katanya, penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. “Ia adalah satu jemputan kepada generasi baharu untuk melihat golf profesional bukan sekadar sesuatu yang dimainkan di tempat lain di dunia tetapi sebagai laluan kerjaya yang boleh diceburi oleh wanita Malaysia,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Dalam pada itu, saingan Pro-Am Diraja hari ini menyaksikan pasukan yang dibarisi Dianna Lee, Ang Bee Ee, Jojo Goh dan digandingkan bersama pemain profesional Kelly Tan dinobatkan sebagai juara keseluruhan. Tempat kedua diraih oleh pasukan Miran Shin, Raina Azene Ramli, Nur Azreen dan pemain profesional Tan Ying Ying manakala kedudukan ketiga disandang oleh Yang Amat Mulia Che Puan Besar Kedah, Che Puan Hajah Hamimah Haji Hamidun, Datuk Norfaizah Zainal, June Yap bersama pemain profesional, Zulaikah Nasser. Menurutnya lagi, selain memperkukuh pembangunan bakat tempatan, penganjuran edisi kali ini turut mendapat sokongan padu pelbagai syarikat korporat terkemuka seperti Prudential, 100PLUS, Power Root dan Delon. Jelasnya, pihak penganjur turut mempunyai perancangan jangka panjang untuk meningkatkan kualiti kejohanan itu dengan sasaran hadiah terkumpul mencecah kira-kira RM12.5 juta pada masa hadapan. “Objektifnya bukan sekadar meningkatkan wang kemenangan tetapi untuk mewujudkan acara yang mempunyai status kukuh bagi menarik perhatian antarabangsa, di samping memberikan pemain Malaysia platform yang lebih berkesan ke pentas global,” katanya. – UTUSAN The post Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026 appeared first on Utusan Malaysia.

Tempat kedua diraih oleh pasukan Miran Shin, Raina Azene Ramli, Nur Azreen dan pemain profesional Tan Ying Ying manakala kedudukan ketiga disandang oleh Yang Amat Mulia Che Puan Besar Kedah, Che Puan Hajah Hamimah Haji Hamidun, Datuk Norfaizah Zainal, June Yap bersama pemain profesional, Zulaikah Nasser. Jelasnya, pihak penganjur turut mempunyai perancangan jangka panjang untuk meningkatkan kualiti kejohanan itu dengan sasaran hadiah terkumpul mencecah kira-kira RM12.5 juta pada masa hadapan. “Objektifnya bukan sekadar meningkatkan wang kemenangan tetapi untuk mewujudkan acara yang mempunyai status kukuh bagi menarik perhatian antarabangsa, di samping memberikan pemain Malaysia platform yang lebih berkesan ke pentas global,” katanya. – UTUSAN The post Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026 appeared first on Utusan Malaysia.

KUALA LUMPUR, 5 Oktober – Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi sedikit hari ini sejajar dengan prestasi positif di pasaran serantau susulan penerimaan risiko yang bertambah baik.

Peningkatan penerimaan risiko ini disokong oleh data lemah pasaran buruh Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang meredakan jangkaan Rizab Persekutuan AS mengetatkan dasarnya serta tekanan ke atas hasil bon.

Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 0.88 mata kepada 1,631.75 daripada paras penutup 1,630.87 pada Jumaat minggu lepas.

Indeks petunjuk pasaran yang dibuka tinggi naik 2.55 mata kepada 1,633.42, bergerak antara paras 1,630.95 dan 1,640.46 sepanjang sesi dagangan.

Bagaimanapun, di keseluruhan pasaran, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 599 berbanding 564, manakala 523 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,087 tidak diniagakan dan 24 digantung.

Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion daripada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion pada Jumaat minggu lepas.

Naib presiden penyelidikan ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata kaunter teknologi merupakan antara saham yang meraih keuntungan tinggi.

Di Wall Street semalaman, indeks S&P 500 meningkat 0.73 peratus kepada 7,722.72 dan Nasdaq Composite naik 1.19 peratus kepada 27,190.86.

Beliau berkata pasaran saham tempatan dijangka kekal positif dalam tempoh terdekat ini memandangkan FBM KLCI masih berada dalam kedudukan terlebih jual susulan penurunan ketara minggu lepas yang mana keadaan ini dijangka terus menarik minat pembelian pada harga rendah khususnya bagi saham mewah terpilih.

“Kecairan domestik juga terus menyokong, dengan institusi tempatan merekodkan pembelian bersih sebanyak RM352.4 juta pada minggu lepas, walaupun aktiviti penjualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing kekal menjadi faktor hambatan,” katanya kepada Bernama.

Justeru, Thong menjangkakan indeks petunjuk pasaran akan mencatatkan pemulihan secara beransur-ansur namun kekal tidak menentu, dengan FBM KLCI berkemungkinan diniagakan dalam jajaran 1,620-1,650 pada minggu ini.

Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Public Bank meningkat lima sen kepada RM4.71, CIMB naik lapan sen kepada RM7.73, Tenaga Nasional menokok empat sen kepada RM13.00, Maybank susut dua sen kepada RM10.00, dan IHH Healthcare turun empat sen kepada RM7.76.

Dalam kalangan saham aktif, V.S Industry meningkat tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 6.5 sen, Jaks Resources turun sedikit sebanyak satu sen kepada 17 sen, Excel Force MSC merosot empat sen kepada 17 sen, manakala NationGate tidak berubah pada RM1.83.

Dalam kalangan kaunter paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.00 kepada RM43.40, UMS Integration melonjak 37 sen kepada RM9.40, Kelington naik 49 sen kepada RM9.12, Nestle menokok 48 sen kepada RM90.00, dan Samaiden menambah 35 sen kepada RM3.19.

Dalam kalangan saham paling rugi, Batu Kawan susut RM1.48 kepada RM18.98, United Plantations turun 32 sen kepada RM31.06, Hengyuan Refining Company berkurangan 18 sen kepada RM3.46 manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong dan YTL Power International menyusut 14 sen masing-masing kepada RM20.86 dan RM5.54.

Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 61.56 mata kepada 17,543.49, Indeks FBM Emas menambah 19.78 mata kepada 12,190.35, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 15.70 mata kepada 11,973.38, Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menokok 8.69 mata kepada 12,069.01 dan Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 77.15 mata kepada 5,606.61.

Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik sedikit sebanyak 0.45 mata kepada 178.97 dan Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menambah 99.63 mata kepada 19,140.14, manakala Indeks Tenaga susut 3.09 mata kepada 829.94 dan Indeks Perladangan turun 125.52 mata kepada 8,931.03.

Jumlah dagangan Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 3.13 bilion unit bernilai RM2.41 bilion daripada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion pada Jumaat minggu lepas.

Jumlah dagangan waran naik kepada 1.04 bilion unit bernilai RM208.20 juta daripada 973.40 juta unit bernilai RM160.21 juta sebelumnya.

Jumlah dagangan Pasaran ACE menokok kepada 611.02 juta unit bernilai RM267.66 juta daripada 593.05 juta unit bernilai RM205.21 juta.

Sementara itu, kaunter produk dan perkhidmatan pengguna menyumbang sebanyak 248.10 juta saham di Pasaran Utama, diikuti produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (439.37 juta), pembinaan (183.56 juta), teknologi (1.76 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (49.02 juta), hartanah (106.95 juta), perladangan (22.08 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (10.76 juta), dana tertutup (152,900), tenaga (106.66 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (103.20 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (22.11 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (40.92 juta), utiliti (38.48 juta), serta amanah perniagaan (162,200). -BERNAMA

title: 'AEON Credit Closes in on One-year Low as 2Q Results Underwhelm Investors, Analysts
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 30): AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd (KL:AEONCR) fell to its lowest in nearly a year while analysts turned cautious following a weaker-than-expected quarter at the consumer finance firm. At least two research houses downgraded the stock post-results. Earnings in the first-half only accounted for about one-third of the consensus’ full-year forecast, and there are now concerns over rising provisions and write-offs of bad loans going forward. “In our view, this negative trend is likely to persist” into the rest of the financial year ending February 2027, CIMB Securities said and lowered its recommendation to 'reduce' from 'buy'. AEON Credit fell as much as 19 sen or a little under 4% to RM5.00, their lowest since October 2025. The stock closed at RM5.02, down 17 sen or 3.3%, valuing the group at RM2.56 billion. Shares of AEON Credit have been volatile this year as non-performing loans crept up while the company grappled with general slowdown consumer spending on big-ticket items amid macroeconomic uncertainties. Year to date, the stock has lost 12% of its value. RHB Research, meanwhile, cut its recommendation to 'neutral' from 'buy' and flagged rising non-performing loans weighing on profitability. AEON Credit’s pivot towards customers with better credit quality has also led to lower asset yields and some compression in net interest margins, further limiting earnings growth, the house noted. “While financing growth remains healthy, we believe the combination of higher credit costs and weaker yields warrants a more cautious stance,” RHB Research added. The stock still has three 'buy' calls from the five analysts tracked by Bloomberg. The average 12-month target price stood at RM6.25. On Tuesday (Sept 29), AEON Credit reported an 18% year-on-year decline in net profit to RM59.30 million for the second quarter ended Aug 31, 2026, as higher impairment losses on financing receivables offset 7.7% growth in revenue. For the first half, net profit rose 3.1% to RM154.47 million. title: 'New Hilux catches fire after 40 days, son and mother awarded RM427,000
body: 'KUALA KUBU BARU: The Sessions Court has awarded more than RM427,000 in damages to a man and his mother after their new Toyota Hilux caught fire 40 days after it was registered, with the blaze spreading to their house. Judge Norhayati Johar found that the fire was caused by electrical arcing at the vehicle's battery terminal connection and ruled that the Hilux did not meet the safety, durability and quality reasonably expected of a new vehicle. She ruled in favour of plaintiffs V. Thiagarajan and V.C. Kamalam in their suit against Maybank Islamic Bhd and Toyota dealer Telagamas Motors Sdn Bhd. The plaintiffs were awarded RM397,220 in special damages and RM30,000 in general damages, as well as RM25,000 in costs and interest. Telagamas was also ordered to indemnify Maybank for the judgment sum and damages for which the bank was liable. According to the grounds of judgment, Thiagarajan bought a new Toyota Hilux D/C 2.8 Rogue from Telagamas under a hire-purchase facility provided by Maybank. The vehicle was registered on Aug 19, 2023. On Sept 28, the Hilux caught fire while parked at the porch of the plaintiffs' house in Rumah Murah Kilat near Kerling here. The fire started at the front of the vehicle before spreading to the house, causing substantial damage to the Hilux and the property. On the cause of the fire, Norhayati said the evidence pointed to electrical arcing at the battery terminal connection. The court found that the Hilux was new, stationary and had its engine switched off when the electrical failure occurred. Norhayati said the short period between the vehicle's registration and the fire was significant when considering its durability. "I do not regard the 40-day period, by itself, as determinative. However, this was a new vehicle which suffered a serious failure within that period, resulting in its destruction. "In those circumstances, I find that the vehicle did not possess the durability reasonably expected of a new motor vehicle," she said. She said no misuse, modification, improper maintenance or other intervening conduct by the plaintiffs had been established. The court found that the vehicle was not of merchantable quality, was not reasonably fit for its purpose and did not meet the standard of acceptable quality under the Hire-Purchase Act 1967 and Consumer Protection Act 1999. Maybank had relied on several clauses in the hire-purchase agreement concerning inspection, suitability, warranty and maintenance to dispute the claim. However, Norhayati said the contractual provisions could not defeat the statutory protections afforded to the buyer. She said there was no evidence that the electrical condition which caused the fire was externally apparent or could reasonably have been discovered during an ordinary examination before delivery. On Telagamas' liability, the court accepted evidence that its salesman had described the Hilux as strong, durable, safe and reliable during the purchase. Norhayati said those qualities concerned the condition and expected performance of the vehicle itself. "An electrical failure at the battery terminal connection which caused a new vehicle to catch fire approximately 40 days after registration is difficult to reconcile with those descriptions," she said. Thiagarajan was alerted by the vehicle's alarm and horn before discovering the Hilux on fire at the car porch. He tried unsuccessfully to extinguish the blaze before he and his family were forced to escape through the rear of the house. Norhayati said the family home became uninhabitable and they had to relocate to Behrang. "The deprivation was substantial. This was not a case involving minor defects or temporary inconvenience while the occupants remained in the premises," she added. The plaintiffs were represented by K.M. Kabilan, while Kirpal Singh Sarban Singh and Jasmeetpal Singh acted for Maybank and Telagamas respectively.

"In those circumstances, I find that the vehicle did not possess the durability reasonably expected of a new motor vehicle," she said. She said no misuse, modification, improper maintenance or other intervening conduct by the plaintiffs had been established. The court found that the vehicle was not of merchantable quality, was not reasonably fit for its purpose and did not meet the standard of acceptable quality under the Hire-Purchase Act 1967 and Consumer Protection Act 1999. Maybank had relied on several clauses in the hire-purchase agreement concerning inspection, suitability, warranty and maintenance to dispute the claim. However, Norhayati said the contractual provisions could not defeat the statutory protections afforded to the buyer. She said there was no evidence that the electrical condition which caused the fire was externally apparent or could reasonably have been discovered during an ordinary examination before delivery. On Telagamas' liability, the court accepted evidence that its salesman had described the Hilux as strong, durable, safe and reliable during the purchase. Norhayati said those qualities concerned the condition and expected performance of the vehicle itself. "An electrical failure at the battery terminal connection which caused a new vehicle to catch fire approximately 40 days after registration is difficult to reconcile with those descriptions," she said. Thiagarajan was alerted by the vehicle's alarm and horn before discovering the Hilux on fire at the car porch. He tried unsuccessfully to extinguish the blaze before he and his family were forced to escape through the rear of the house. Norhayati said the family home became uninhabitable and they had to relocate to Behrang. "The deprivation was substantial. This was not a case involving minor defects or temporary inconvenience while the occupants remained in the premises," she added. The plaintiffs were represented by K.M. Kabilan, while Kirpal Singh Sarban Singh and Jasmeetpal Singh acted for Maybank and Telagamas respectively.

title: 'DNB completes RM5.2 bil syndicated Islamic financing ahead of ownership transition
body: 'DNB completes RM5.2 bil syndicated Islamic financing ahead of ownership transition KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth. In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding. The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL:CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL:YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026. Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment. The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission. DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets. DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider. In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing. AmInvestment Bank was the financial adviser to DNB. title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends slightly higher as technology counters dominate trading
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Bursa Malaysia staged a slight recovery on Friday as bargain-hunting emerged following a recent sharp sell-off, said an analyst. However, the rebound lacked momentum as broader Asian markets remained under pressure ahead of key United States labour market data. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.51 points, or 0.03 per cent, to 1,630.87 from Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The benchmark index, which opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, moved between 1,630.63 and 1,640.78 throughout the trading session. Market breadth turned positive with gainers leading losers 585 to 541, while 558 counters were unchanged, 1,089 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover climbed to 4.23 billion units, worth RM2.70 billion, from 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion on Thursday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the recent sell-off had brought valuations of selected blue-chip stocks to more attractive levels, which could encourage gradual accumulation and provide some downside support. However, he said investors continued to adopt a defensive stance as bond yields and crude oil prices remained elevated. “As for the local bourse, we remain cautious despite today’s rebound, as external headwinds are likely to keep market volatility elevated,” Thong told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose seven sen to RM10.02, Public Bank fell one sen to RM4.66, CIMB eased four sen to RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional firmed up six sen to RM12.96, and IHH Healthcare added 10 sen to RM7.80. In active trade, Zetrix AI erased five sen to 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources remained unchanged at 18 sen, JCY International jumped 10.5 sen to 66 sen, V.S Industry ticked up two sen to 29 sen, and PUC went up one sen to 4.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries rose RM1.28 to RM42.40, UWC rallied 47 sen to RM7.57, Vitrox bounced 46 sen to RM10.46, United Plantations gained 42 sen to RM31.38, and UMS Integration improved 38 sen to RM9.03. Top losers were led by Nestle, which reduced 48 sen to RM89.52; Kuala Lumpur Kepong fell 42 sen to RM21; Enra trimmed 25.5 sen to 72.5 sen, while Allianz Malaysia and Hong Leong Bank both shaved off 20 sen to RM20.80 and RM22.64, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 122.94 points to 17,481.93, the FBM Emas Index added 27.04 points to 12,170.57, and the FBM Top 100 Index advanced 24.52 points to 11,957.68. The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 47.31 points to 12,060.32, and the FBM ACE Index improved 46.49 points to 5,529.46. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.79 points to 178.52, while the Energy Index shaved off 1.98 points to 833.03. The Financial Services Index eased 20.40 points to 19,040.51, and the Plantation Index grew 29.97 points to 9,056.55. The Main Market volume increased to 2.67 billion units worth RM2.34 billion from 1.82 billion units valued at RM2.42 billion on Thursday. Warrant turnover soared to 973.40 million units worth RM160.21 million from 618.78 million units valued at RM72.71 million previously. The ACE Market volume eased to 593.05 million units valued at RM205.21 million from 650.13 million units worth RM226.92 million yesterday. Meanwhile, consumer products and services counters accounted for 241.01 million shares traded on the Main Market, industrial products and services (266.57 million), construction (183.37 million), technology (1.41 billion), financial services (50.26 million), property (152.37 million), plantation (19.73 million), real estate investment trusts (15.78 million), closed-end fund (214,200), energy (99.69 million), healthcare (103.06 million), telecommunications and media (28.89 million), transportation and logistics (47.35 million), utilities (46.61 million), and business trusts (119,600). — Bernama

title: 'CIMB, Zetrix AI, Top Glove, Samaiden, Mesiniaga, Scientex, Dialog, Elridge Energy, Insights Analytics, SLGC
body: 'CIMB, Zetrix AI, Top Glove, Samaiden, Mesiniaga, Scientex, Dialog, Elridge Energy, Insights Analytics, SLGC KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 7): Here is a brief recap of some business news and corporate announcements that made the headlines on Tuesday: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200 million (RM817 million). — CIMB considers selling Philippine business — Bloomberg Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314 million in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. — Zetrix says still finalising amount owed to JPJ after Loke reveals RM314m arrears Top Glove Corporation Bhd (KL:TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78 billion pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72 billion in FY2026. The group’s net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63 million in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25 billion. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15. For the full FY2026, Top Glove’s net profit nearly tripled to RM307.96 million. Revenue increased 21% to RM4.23 billion as volume grew close to 30%. — Top Glove eyes higher output but says manpower remains key hurdle;Top Glove says ready for storms ahead as 4Q net profit jumps nearly five times Samaiden Group Bhd (KL:SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (KL:YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. — Samaiden reveals RM238 mil contract value for LSS5+ solar project Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. — Mesiniaga wins two-year RM32.3m contract extension from Customs Dept Scientex Bhd (KL:SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. — Scientex to acquire 503 acres in Johor for RM580 mil Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. — Dialog JV bags onshore O&G concession in Thailand Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (KL:ELRIDGE) is investing RM45 million to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45 million in cash. — Elridge Energy invests RM45m to venture into activated carbon business Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44 million subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. — Insights Analytics secures contract for Suai water treatment plant in Miri Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm’s shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intra-day low of 24 sen as more than 83 million shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140 million. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. — Construction firm SLGC ends first trading day below IPO price The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Daily Market Commentary - 29 Sep 2026
body: 'The local stock market traded sideways with slight downward bias on Monday, as subdued domestic catalysts and heightened global uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The FBM KLCI inched down by 1.60 points to close at 1,670.02, off an low of 1,668.61 and high of 1,674.11, as losers led gainers 748 to 388, on total turnover of 3.11bn shares worth RM2.40bn. Uncertainty surrounding Middle East tensions and persistent inflationary pressures is likely to continue clouding the outlook for the local market. Immediate support for the index stays at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat. - DagangNews.com

title: 'EdgeProp Daily Digest — 6 October 2026 | EdgeProp
body: 'Daily Digest · Tuesday, 6 October 2026· Updated: about 4 hours ago Scientex proposes RM580.16m Pulai land purchase; Sunway Ipoh Mall reaches 80% leasing Scientex proposed a RM580.16 million Pulai land purchase, while Sunway reported 80% leasing at its upcoming Ipoh mall. Privasia received conditional approval for a Perak data centre. Residential launch reports, warehouse contracts, Merdeka 118 leasing figures and new fire-safety requirements broadened the property news flow ahead of Budget 2027. Quick takes - Privasia’s Silver Streams Technofarm received MITI approval for its Bagan Datuk data centre, on Tuesday (Oct 6). The approval letter was dated Sept 7 and required an off-grid energy supply with maximum demand of 50MW, compliant with applicable energy and renewable-energy rules. Approval did not establish that the power supply had been secured - Housing and data centre efficiency conditions feature in pre-Budget priorities, OCBC said. Its report specified neither housing allocations nor efficiency requirements. It identified development spending, estimated at RM86 billion annually under the 13th Malaysia Plan, as the main adjustment lever. Budget 2027 is scheduled for tabling on Oct 9. - Developer SevenCo broke ground on its first Klang Valley residential project, Maison Sungai Besi in Taman Castlefield, Kuala Lumpur. EdgeProp reported a 48-storey tower with 537 homes measuring 721 to 1,206 sq ft. The developer planned solar panels and EV charging bays. The ceremony marked construction commencement rather than completed homes. - Axis REIT had RM250 million in acquisitions under negotiation, with one or two announcements possible before year-end, Maybank Investment Bank said. The Edge reported that earlier seven-year and ten-year financing provided some protection against rising rates. Gearing was forecast at about 39% after signed acquisitions; the negotiating pipeline remained prospective Scientex signs conditional agreement for 14 Pulai parcels Packaging manufacturer and property developer Scientex Bhd proposed buying 14 freehold parcels in Mukim Pulai, Johor Bahru, for RM580.16 million. Its wholly owned subsidiary Scientex Quatari Sdn Bhd signed the conditional agreement with Pangkal Budiman Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Leong Hup Holdings Sdn Bhd, on Oct 6. The filing put the aggregate area at 502.5906 acres, or 21,892,847 sq ft, and the price at RM26.50 per sq ft. The land adjoins Taman Pulai Mutiara, Taman Pulai Mutiara 2, Taman Pulai Duta and Taman Pulai Duta 2. Scientex proposed a mixed-property development, but had not determined its gross development value, costs, profits or timetable. It said more than 90% of units launched in its existing Pulai developments had been sold. Completion was targeted for 2H2027, subject to block-title renewal and applicable land-transfer approvals. Funding would combine internal funds and borrowings. No independent valuation was undertaken, and shareholder approval was not required. The acquisition supported Scientex’s stated target of completing 50,000 affordable homes nationwide by 2028. Why it matters The purchase would expand Scientex’s landbank beside existing projects. Development value and delivery dates remained undetermined, and completion depended on the agreement’s conditions. Sunway Ipoh Mall reports leasing commitments ahead of 2027 opening Shopping mall owner and operator Sunway Malls said Sunway Ipoh Mall was 80% leased ahead of its scheduled 4Q2027 opening. Its Oct 6 statement described a RM1 billion development with 1.2 million sq ft of net lettable area across four retail floors and 400 shops. It unveiled 25 brands and concepts, including seven anchors and nine brands making their Perak debut. The mall forms part of the 1,350-acre Sunway City Ipoh township. Planned facilities include an ice rink, a 36-lane bowling centre, an exhibition centre and a ten-hall cinema. Sunway said portfolio occupancy was 98%, against a national average of 79%, and first-half sales grew 5%, compared with industry growth of 3.1%. Both comparisons were supplied by the group. At the same tenant-unveiling event, group managing director HC Chan sought Budget 2027 relief on mall electricity costs and SST. He proposed extending protection from fuel-adjustment charges to malls and considering an SST reduction to 3%. These remained industry requests, with no government approval announced. Why it matters Leasing commitments established part of the tenant base before opening. The mall's operating-cost proposals remained separate from any measures the government might adopt in Budget 2027. Bomba says designated premises must appoint fire-safety personnel from April 2027 Owners of 9,451 designated buildings will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers and Fire Safety Officers from April 1, 2027, Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said, according to Bernama on Oct 6. He said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, concerning the establishment of a Fire Safety Organisation at designated premises. He said owners would receive preparation periods of six to 18 months before full enforcement, depending on existing Fire Certificate expiry dates and inspection schedules. Nor Hisham said annual inspection reports prepared by managers would be assessed for certificate renewal, reducing the need for the department to inspect every building physically each year. The department expected appointments of 6,000 managers and 18,000 officers nationwide for industry needs from 2026 to 2030. It had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase providers and instructors. The requirement concerned designated premises subject to Fire Certificate obligations, rather than every property. Why it matters Affected building owners would need qualified personnel and an internal fire-safety organisation. Preparation and enforcement would depend on certificate renewal and inspection schedules. Also on the radar today Kimori report puts Phase 1 bookings at 73% Developer Premierex reported 73% bookings for Phase 1 of Kimori Residences in EdgeProp’s Oct 6 article, following the Oct 3 launch in Bukit Serdang. The freehold development comprises 418 units, with prices from RM481,600 and expected completion in 4Q2029. Layouts measure approximately 857 sq ft and 1,095 sq ft. The current report describes bookings, rather than completed sales. Setia and Gentari explore EV charging at selected developments S P Setia and Gentari Green Mobility signed an MoU to explore EV charging at selected Setia developments on Tuesday (Oct 6). The Oct 5 media release covered site identification, feasibility, installation, operation and maintenance. No sites, charging-point count or value were stated. body: 'The FBM KLCI rose 0.1% to 1,631.8 points on Monday due to improved risk appetite in line with firmer regional markets, after softer US labour data eased expectations of further Fed tightening and took some pressure off bond yields. Technology (+1.7%), Health Care (+1.4%) and Financial Services (+0.5%) led sectoral gains, driven by Nestle (+0.5%), Hong Leong Bank (+0.2%) and Misc (+0.2%). Market breadth, however, was negative, with 598 losers ahead of 564 gainers, while 524 counters closed unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Monday as a weaker-than-expected US jobs report reduced bets on another Fed rate hike, lowering bond yields and setting off a rebound in rate-sensitive technology stocks, following Wall Street's rally on Friday. Taiwan's TAIEX led regional gains (+2.6%), followed by Japan's Nikkei 225 (+2.4%) and Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+0.3%), while markets in mainland China and South Korea were closed for public holidays. In their last trading sessions, Chinese gains were led by Health Care (+2.9%), Consumer Staples (+1.7%) and Financials (+1.0%), with CanSino Biologics (+20%), Shanghai Model Organisms (+19.9%) and Suzhou Novoprotein Scientific (+13.5%) the top performers. In South Korea, Health Technology, Commercial Services and Health Services each rose 1.6%, driven by Enplus, Pusan Cast Iron and CK Solution. European equities mostly advanced on Monday, with STOXX 50 gaining 0.2% and STOXX 600 adding 0.3%. Spanish stocks led, surging over 1% after PM Pedro Sánchez called a snap November 29 election following a parliamentary setback. France's CAC 40 fell around 1% on fiscal and political concerns ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with the euro weakening to a 17- month low. Schneider Electric plunged over 9% after announcing its largestever deal, a $22.6 billion acquisition of US software firm PTC, worrying investors. Banco Santander supported the market, climbing over 4%. US stocks closed higher Monday as heavyweight tech gains outweighed elevated oil prices and bond yields. The S&P 500 rose 0.7%, Nasdaq 100 gained 0.9% to a record 31,076 and Dow added 91 points. Strong earnings, consumer spending and AI investment supported equities despite rising borrowing and energy costs and inflation concerns. Hyperscalers Alphabet (+0.9%), Meta (+1.9%) and Microsoft (+1.5%) gained. Among chipmakers, Nvidia and Broadcom (both +2.1%) mostly offset Micron (-1%), AMD (-0.3%) and Intel (-2.6%). Tesla rose 2.2%; SpaceX jumped 7.6% on reported potential TSMC cooperation with Musk's Terafab. US: 10-Year Yield Rises to 5.33% on Monday The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.33% on Monday, near its highest level since March 2022 as investors assessed fresh economic data and prepared for the release of the Federal Reserve’s September meeting minutes. The latest ISM report showed that services-sector activity continued to expand, with the PMI at 54.9 in September, slightly below August but broadly in line with expectations. At the same time, cost pressures intensified, highlighting renewed inflation risks despite the moderation in business activity. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Losses as Mideast Exports Recover 5.33% on Monday Crude oil traded near $89 per barrel on Tuesday after declining for two consecutive sessions, pressured by signs that Middle East crude exports are recovering toward pre-war levels. JPMorgan said crude shipments have rebounded to 17.5 million barrels a day, or 98% of prewar levels, while product flows such as diesel and gasoline reached 3 million barrels a day, or 58%. (Trading Economics) US: Services Growth Eases as Price Pressures Intensify The ISM Services PMI fell to 54.9 in September 2026 from 55.4 in August, compared with expectations of 55. The index nevertheless remained in expansion territory for a 27th consecutive month, indicating continued growth in the US services sector. Business activity eased more noticeably, with the Business Activity Index dropping to 56.5 from 61.7, while new orders also moderated to 59.8. Employment improved, moving back above the 50 threshold to 50.1 after two months of contraction. (Trading Economics) US: Gold ticks higher on softer Fed outlook as strong dollar limits gains Gold prices advanced on Monday, supported by continued worries about rising US government debt and fading expectations of an immediate US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike, although a firmer dollar limited gains. Spot gold rose 0.4% to US$4,159.89 (RM17,001.89) per ounce by 1138 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery added 0.64% to US$4,188.70. (Reuters) UK: Expected to follow EU with China EV tariffs, report says The UK is preparing to impose import levies on Chinese electric vehicles to meet a key demand from the European Union, the Times of London reported, in a blow to a group that now accounts for nearly one in four cars sold in the country. Brussels has made clear that the UK faces being cut from the Made in Europe local-content rules if it does not act on the tariffs, the newspaper said, adding that EU officials are concerned the UK could become a backdoor for Chinese exports into Europe. (Bloomberg) UK: Job slump longer than during financial crisis, PMI says Britain’s jobs market is stuck in its longest downturn since the early 2000s, according to a closely-watched survey, surpassing the decline during the financial crisis. S&P Global’s UK purchasing managers’ index (PMI) said employers cut back on staff for a 24th consecutive month. (Bloomberg) UK: Hits 17-month low, dollar near pre-Liberation Day highs The euro slid to a 17-month low against the dollar on Monday as concerns about France's ability to rein in its budget deficit and a sharp bond market sell-off last week stirred fears of a return of sovereign debt crisis dynamics in the eurozone. French government bonds have come under pressure as expectations of higher policy rates and rising political uncertainty ahead of the 2027 election cast doubt on the ability of the euro area's second-largest economy to put its public finances on a more sustainable footing. (Reuters) CN: To pump $54bn into state banks and insurers to boost economy China is pumping tens of billions of dollars into eight state-owned banks and insurance companies to help shore up the country's financial system and boost its slowing economy. The cash injection, which is being led by China's finance ministry, will total 360 billion yuan ($53.6bn; £39.7bn), state news agency Xinhua said on Sunday. (BBC) JP: Service sector activity slows from five-month high, PMI shows Japan's service sector expanded at a weaker pace in September as business activity and new orders grew more slowly and earthquake disruption dampened demand, a business survey showed on Monday. The S&P Global final Japan Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) eased to 51.3 in September from a five-month high of 52.5 in August, a survey by S&P Global showed, worse than a flash reading of 51.6. (Reuters) JP: Takaichi pledges fiscal discipline as Japan's debt bill rises Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields. She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies. (Reuters) MY: Govt to boost high-value commodity exports, reduce reliance on food imports - minister The government remains committed to strengthening the nation’s agrifood sector by driving higher production and exports of high-value commodities such as pineapples and durians, while narrowing the country’s food trade gap. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the move would not only boost the agrifood sector’s contribution to export earnings but also reduce the country’s reliance on food imports. (The Edge) MY: Govt dividend receipts up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on higher BNM, Khazanah payouts - AG's report The federal government received RM39.55 billion in dividends from its investments in 2025, up by 1.4% from RM39.01 billion a year earlier, as higher payouts from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Khazanah Nasional Bhd outweighed lower receipts from other entities. The dividends came from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in 2024. (The Edge) MY: BNM: Household financial position remains resilient amid West Asia risks The financial position of households has remained generally resilient, supported by Malaysia's stable labour market conditions, according to Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). It said domestic policy measures, including expanded government cash assistance and continued fuel subsidies, have also helped contain the pass-through of higher global costs to domestic consumer prices. (The Edge) MY: Palm oil stockpiles balloon to record on output surge Palm oil inventories in Malaysia likely swelled to a record last month, buffering supplies of the world’s most-used vegetable oil as an intensifying El Niño threatens to disrupt production in the coming year. The burgeoning supplies could deepen a recent slump in prices, as traders also await a ramp-up in exports to major markets like India that would help draw down the massive stockpiles. (Bloomberg) IJM: Appoints Johan Idris as new chairman Construction and property conglomerate IJM Corporation Bhd has appointed non-executive chairman of KPMG Malaysia Datuk Johan Idris as its independent non-executive director and chairman, effective Monday. Johan, who previously served as KPMG Malaysia's managing partner and country senior partner, succeeds long-serving chairman Tan Sri Krishnan Tan following his retirement. (The Edge) ZETRIX: Owes JPJ RM314m from May to September this year; firm stopped RM231m cheque meant to settle arrears - Loke Zetrix AI Bhd owes the Road Transport Department some RM314 million as it failed to remit collections from May to September this year. The outstanding amount is the reason behind the ministry’s decision to suspend Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG under their three-year contract, which took effect on Monday, according to Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. (The Edge) ZETRIX: Extends decline to lowest in more than a decade Zetrix AI Bhd fell to its lowest in 13 years after the Ministry of Transport revealed that the digital services company owed the government some RM314 million. The stock fell five sen or more than 40% to close Monday at 6.5 sen, the lowest since May 2013. More than one billion shares exchanged hands, the highest daily volume since Zetrix’ managing director Wong Thean Soon suffered forced selling on his accounts in September. (The Edge) JTGROUP: Bags two TNB contracts worth RM15.7m Jati Tinggi Group Bhd has secured two contracts from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) worth a combined RM15.7 million for underground cable works in Selangor and a submarine power cable monitoring system in Perlis. The larger contract, worth RM13.44 million, was awarded to Jati Tinggi’s wholly-owned subsidiary Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd for the installation, testing and commissioning of 11kV underground cables and related accessories for TNB’s distribution network in Selangor. (The Edge) CITAGLB: Unit secures RM29m portion of Thai waste-to-energy contract Citaglobal Bhd said on Monday its indirect unit LAWI Engineering GmbH (LAWI Germany) has secured a RM29 million share of a RM52.1 million contract for a waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Thailand. LAWI Germany, together with an unnamed consortium partner, was awarded the contract by Siam Power Co Ltd for the engineering, procurement and construction of a steam boiler plant for the Siam Power Naklang WTE project in Nakhon Ratchasima Province. (The Edge) WESTRVR: Secures RM17.5m electrical, solar works for Selangor logistics park West River Bhd has secured a RM17.5 million subcontract for electrical, security and solar panel system works at the E-Metro Logistic Park in Bandar Bukit Raja 2, Selangor. The subcontract was awarded by Al-Ambia Sdn Bhd to West River's wholly owned subsidiary West River Engineering Sdn Bhd, according to the group's bourse filing on Monday. (The Edge) GOHUB: Bags RM65m contract from KTMB unit Information technology solutions provider Go Hub Capital Bhd has secured a five-year service contract worth RM65 million from Keretapi Tanah Melayu (KTMB) unit Tenang Capital Bhd. In a bourse filing, Go Hub said the job was secured via its wholly owned NSS IT Solution Sdn Bhd, which was awarded the letter of acceptance on Sept 30 to provide maintenance and support services for KTMB's Integrated Ticketing System. (The Edge) YINSON: Secures additional RM2.5bn in Ghana FPSO contract Yinson Holdings Bhd said it has secured about US$600 million (RM2.5 billion) in additional firm contract backlog following an amendment to its contract for the FPSO John Agyekum Kufuor offshore of Ghana. The amendment, signed with Eni Ghana Exploration and Production Ltd on Oct 2, covers a major upgrade to the floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel’s gas handling and processing capacity and extends its firm contract by four years to 2036, said Yinson. (The Edge) ASTEEL: Stake to 53.08% after mandatory takeover offer Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong has increased his stake in Asteel Group Bhd to 53.08% stake following the close of his unconditional mandatory takeover offer on Monday. According to a press statement on Monday issued by principal adviser UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd, Hii's investment vehicle, Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd, received acceptances for 724,585 shares as at 5pm on Monday. (The Edge) PERTAMA: Ran eJamin for five years without formal contract, invested bail funds without approval - PAC eJamin, an online bail payment system operated by an indirect unit of Practice Note 17 (PN17) company Pertama Digital Bhd, ran for five years without a formal contract, the Public Accounts Committee found. Bail funds were also deposited into a commercial bank account held by Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd, instead of the federal government’s consolidated trust account, in contravention of the Federal Constitution and the Financial Procedure Act 1957, according to the committee’s report released on Monday. (The Edge) SPSETIA: Gentari sign MOU to explore green mobility solutions across Setia developments S P Setia Bhd and clean energy solutions provider Gentari Green Mobility Sdn Bhd have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to explore a collaboration in clean energy and green mobility solutions, according to a press statement issued on Monday. Gentari Green Mobility is a subsidiary of Gentari Sdn Bhd, which is wholly owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS). (The Edge) MKLAND: Talks of major corporate exercise at MK Land resurface TALKS of a potential corporate exercise at property developer MK Land Holdings Bhd have resurfaced, with a source familiar with the matter saying an adviser has been appointed to explore possible options. The source spoke on condition of anonymity because the discussions are private. (The Edge) EVOCOM: IPO Watch: ACE Market-bound Evocom charts broader logistics footprint E-COMMERCE logistics and workforce solutions provider Evocom Bhd is set to make its debut on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market on Monday (Sept 28), with the group looking to broaden its logistics footprint through an expansion of its air freight transhipment business, technology investments and a new headquarters near Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s (KLIA) air cargo terminal. The company’s initial public offering (IPO) comprises 113.91 million new shares and an offer for sale of 22 million existing shares, both priced at 18 sen apiece. (The Edge) KGB: Unit wins further RM133m contract for Kuching data storage plant Kelington Group Bhd said its wholly owned unit has been awarded a second contract by a manufacturer operating in the Sama Jaya Free Industrial Zone in Kuching, Sarawak, worth about RM133 million. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the group said the award was given to Kelington Technologies Sdn Bhd (KTSB) on Oct 2 and covers the main structural steel works for the customer's data storage manufacturing facility, which is being expanded. (The Edge) ALPHA: Targets Main Market transfer in 4Q Alpha IVF Group is planning to transfer from the ACE Market to the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia, with completion expected sometime in the fourth quarter this year. The fertility care group said the transfer will be through the accelerated transfer process under the Securities Commission Malaysia’s Equity Guidelines, with shareholder approval required at a general meeting.
