full_text: 'Daily Newswatch - 6 Oct 2026. 'The FBM KLCI rose 0.1% to 1,631.8 points on Monday due to improved risk appetite in line with firmer regional markets, after softer US labour data eased expectations of further Fed tightening and took some pressure off bond yields. Technology (+1.7%), Health Care (+1.4%) and Financial Services (+0.5%) led sectoral gains, driven by Nestle (+0.5%), Hong Leong Bank (+0.2%) and Misc (+0.2%). Market breadth, however, was negative, with 598 losers ahead of 564 gainers, while 524 counters closed unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Monday as a weaker-than-expected US jobs report reduced bets on another Fed rate hike, lowering bond yields and setting off a rebound in rate-sensitive technology stocks, following Wall Street's rally on Friday. Taiwan's TAIEX led regional gains (+2.6%), followed by Japan's Nikkei 225 (+2.4%) and Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+0.3%), while markets in mainland China and South Korea were closed for public holidays. In their last trading sessions, Chinese gains were led by Health Care (+2.9%), Consumer Staples (+1.7%) and Financials (+1.0%), with CanSino Biologics (+20%), Shanghai Model Organisms (+19.9%) and Suzhou Novoprotein Scientific (+13.5%) the top performers. In South Korea, Health Technology, Commercial Services and Health Services each rose 1.6%, driven by Enplus, Pusan Cast Iron and CK Solution. European equities mostly advanced on Monday, with STOXX 50 gaining 0.2% and STOXX 600 adding 0.3%. Spanish stocks led, surging over 1% after PM Pedro Sánchez called a snap November 29 election following a parliamentary setback. France's CAC 40 fell around 1% on fiscal and political concerns ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with the euro weakening to a 17- month low. Schneider Electric plunged over 9% after announcing its largestever deal, a $22.6 billion acquisition of US software firm PTC, worrying investors. Banco Santander supported the market, climbing over 4%. US stocks closed higher Monday as heavyweight tech gains outweighed elevated oil prices and bond yields. The S&P 500 rose 0.7%, Nasdaq 100 gained 0.9% to a record 31,076 and Dow added 91 points. Strong earnings, consumer spending and AI investment supported equities despite rising borrowing and energy costs and inflation concerns. Hyperscalers Alphabet (+0.9%), Meta (+1.9%) and Microsoft (+1.5%) gained. Among chipmakers, Nvidia and Broadcom (both +2.1%) mostly offset Micron (-1%), AMD (-0.3%) and Intel (-2.6%). Tesla rose 2.2%; SpaceX jumped 7.6% on reported potential TSMC cooperation with Musk's Terafab. US: 10-Year Yield Rises to 5.33% on Monday The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.33% on Monday, near its highest level since March 2022 as investors assessed fresh economic data and prepared for the release of the Federal Reserve’s September meeting minutes. The latest ISM report showed that services-sector activity continued to expand, with the PMI at 54.9 in September, slightly below August but broadly in line with expectations. At the same time, cost pressures intensified, highlighting renewed inflation risks despite the moderation in business activity. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Losses as Mideast Exports Recover 5.33% on Monday Crude oil traded near $89 per barrel on Tuesday after declining for two consecutive sessions, pressured by signs that Middle East crude exports are recovering toward pre-war levels. JPMorgan said crude shipments have rebounded to 17.5 million barrels a day, or 98% of prewar levels, while product flows such as diesel and gasoline reached 3 million barrels a day, or 58%. (Trading Economics) US: Services Growth Eases as Price Pressures Intensify The ISM Services PMI fell to 54.9 in September 2026 from 55.4 in August, compared with expectations of 55. The index nevertheless remained in expansion territory for a 27th consecutive month, indicating continued growth in the US services sector. Business activity eased more noticeably, with the Business Activity Index dropping to 56.5 from 61.7, while new orders also moderated to 59.8. Employment improved, moving back above the 50 threshold to 50.1 after two months of contraction. (Trading Economics) US: Gold ticks higher on softer Fed outlook as strong dollar limits gains Gold prices advanced on Monday, supported by continued worries about rising US government debt and fading expectations of an immediate US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike, although a firmer dollar limited gains. Spot gold rose 0.4% to US$4,159.89 (RM17,001.89) per ounce by 1138 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery added 0.64% to US$4,188.70. (Reuters) UK: Expected to follow EU with China EV tariffs, report says The UK is preparing to impose import levies on Chinese electric vehicles to meet a key demand from the European Union, the Times of London reported, in a blow to a group that now accounts for nearly one in four cars sold in the country. Brussels has made clear that the UK faces being cut from the Made in Europe local-content rules if it does not act on the tariffs, the newspaper said, adding that EU officials are concerned the UK could become a backdoor for Chinese exports into Europe. (Bloomberg) UK: Job slump longer than during financial crisis, PMI says Britain’s jobs market is stuck in its longest downturn since the early 2000s, according to a closely-watched survey, surpassing the decline during the financial crisis. S&P Global’s UK purchasing managers’ index (PMI) said employers cut back on staff for a 24th consecutive month. (Bloomberg) UK: Hits 17-month low, dollar near pre-Liberation Day highs The euro slid to a 17-month low against the dollar on Monday as concerns about France's ability to rein in its budget deficit and a sharp bond market sell-off last week stirred fears of a return of sovereign debt crisis dynamics in the eurozone. French government bonds have come under pressure as expectations of higher policy rates and rising political uncertainty ahead of the 2027 election cast doubt on the ability of the euro area's second-largest economy to put its public finances on a more sustainable footing. (Reuters) CN: To pump $54bn into state banks and insurers to boost economy China is pumping tens of billions of dollars into eight state-owned banks and insurance companies to help shore up the country's financial system and boost its slowing economy. The cash injection, which is being led by China's finance ministry, will total 360 billion yuan ($53.6bn; £39.7bn), state news agency Xinhua said on Sunday. (BBC) JP: Service sector activity slows from five-month high, PMI shows Japan's service sector expanded at a weaker pace in September as business activity and new orders grew more slowly and earthquake disruption dampened demand, a business survey showed on Monday. The S&P Global final Japan Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) eased to 51.3 in September from a five-month high of 52.5 in August, a survey by S&P Global showed, worse than a flash reading of 51.6. (Reuters) JP: Takaichi pledges fiscal discipline as Japan's debt bill rises Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields. She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies. (Reuters) MY: Govt to boost high-value commodity exports, reduce reliance on food imports - minister The government remains committed to strengthening the nation’s agrifood sector by driving higher production and exports of high-value commodities such as pineapples and durians, while narrowing the country’s food trade gap. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the move would not only boost the agrifood sector’s contribution to export earnings but also reduce the country’s reliance on food imports. (The Edge) MY: Govt dividend receipts up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on higher BNM, Khazanah payouts - AG's report The federal government received RM39.55 billion in dividends from its investments in 2025, up by 1.4% from RM39.01 billion a year earlier, as higher payouts from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Khazanah Nasional Bhd outweighed lower receipts from other entities. The dividends came from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in 2024. (The Edge) MY: BNM: Household financial position remains resilient amid West Asia risks The financial position of households has remained generally resilient, supported by Malaysia's stable labour market conditions, according to Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). It said domestic policy measures, including expanded government cash assistance and continued fuel subsidies, have also helped contain the pass-through of higher global costs to domestic consumer prices. (The Edge) MY: Palm oil stockpiles balloon to record on output surge Palm oil inventories in Malaysia likely swelled to a record last month, buffering supplies of the world’s most-used vegetable oil as an intensifying El Niño threatens to disrupt production in the coming year. The burgeoning supplies could deepen a recent slump in prices, as traders also await a ramp-up in exports to major markets like India that would help draw down the massive stockpiles. (Bloomberg) IJM: Appoints Johan Idris as new chairman Construction and property conglomerate IJM Corporation Bhd has appointed non-executive chairman of KPMG Malaysia Datuk Johan Idris as its independent non-executive director and chairman, effective Monday. Johan, who previously served as KPMG Malaysia's managing partner and country senior partner, succeeds long-serving chairman Tan Sri Krishnan Tan following his retirement. (The Edge) ZETRIX: Owes JPJ RM314m from May to September this year; firm stopped RM231m cheque meant to settle arrears - Loke Zetrix AI Bhd owes the Road Transport Department some RM314 million as it failed to remit collections from May to September this year. The outstanding amount is the reason behind the ministry’s decision to suspend Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG under their three-year contract, which took effect on Monday, according to Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. (The Edge) ZETRIX: Extends decline to lowest in more than a decade Zetrix AI Bhd fell to its lowest in 13 years after the Ministry of Transport revealed that the digital services company owed the government some RM314 million. The stock fell five sen or more than 40% to close Monday at 6.5 sen, the lowest since May 2013. More than one billion shares exchanged hands, the highest daily volume since Zetrix’ managing director Wong Thean Soon suffered forced selling on his accounts in September. (The Edge) JTGROUP: Bags two TNB contracts worth RM15.7m Jati Tinggi Group Bhd has secured two contracts from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) worth a combined RM15.7 million for underground cable works in Selangor and a submarine power cable monitoring system in Perlis. The larger contract, worth RM13.44 million, was awarded to Jati Tinggi’s wholly-owned subsidiary Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd for the installation, testing and commissioning of 11kV underground cables and related accessories for TNB’s distribution network in Selangor. (The Edge) CITAGLB: Unit secures RM29m portion of Thai waste-to-energy contract Citaglobal Bhd said on Monday its indirect unit LAWI Engineering GmbH (LAWI Germany) has secured a RM29 million share of a RM52.1 million contract for a waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Thailand. LAWI Germany, together with an unnamed consortium partner, was awarded the contract by Siam Power Co Ltd for the engineering, procurement and construction of a steam boiler plant for the Siam Power Naklang WTE project in Nakhon Ratchasima Province. (The Edge) WESTRVR: Secures RM17.5m electrical, solar works for Selangor logistics park West River Bhd has secured a RM17.5 million subcontract for electrical, security and solar panel system works at the E-Metro Logistic Park in Bandar Bukit Raja 2, Selangor. The subcontract was awarded by Al-Ambia Sdn Bhd to West River's wholly owned subsidiary West River Engineering Sdn Bhd, according to the group's bourse filing on Monday. (The Edge) GOHUB: Bags RM65m contract from KTMB unit Information technology solutions provider Go Hub Capital Bhd has secured a five-year service contract worth RM65 million from Keretapi Tanah Melayu (KTMB) unit Tenang Capital Bhd. In a bourse filing, Go Hub said the job was secured via its wholly owned NSS IT Solution Sdn Bhd, which was awarded the letter of acceptance on Sept 30 to provide maintenance and support services for KTMB's Integrated Ticketing System. (The Edge) YINSON: Secures additional RM2.5bn in Ghana FPSO contract Yinson Holdings Bhd said it has secured about US$600 million (RM2.5 billion) in additional firm contract backlog following an amendment to its contract for the FPSO John Agyekum Kufuor offshore of Ghana. The amendment, signed with Eni Ghana Exploration and Production Ltd on Oct 2, covers a major upgrade to the floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel’s gas handling and processing capacity and extends its firm contract by four years to 2036, said Yinson. (The Edge) ASTEEL: Stake to 53.08% after mandatory takeover offer Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong has increased his stake in Asteel Group Bhd to 53.08% stake following the close of his unconditional mandatory takeover offer on Monday. According to a press statement on Monday issued by principal adviser UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd, Hii's investment vehicle, Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd, received acceptances for 724,585 shares as at 5pm on Monday. (The Edge) PERTAMA: Ran eJamin for five years without formal contract, invested bail funds without approval - PAC eJamin, an online bail payment system operated by an indirect unit of Practice Note 17 (PN17) company Pertama Digital Bhd, ran for five years without a formal contract, the Public Accounts Committee found. Bail funds were also deposited into a commercial bank account held by Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd, instead of the federal government’s consolidated trust account, in contravention of the Federal Constitution and the Financial Procedure Act 1957, according to the committee’s report released on Monday. (The Edge) SPSETIA: Gentari sign MOU to explore green mobility solutions across Setia developments S P Setia Bhd and clean energy solutions provider Gentari Green Mobility Sdn Bhd have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to explore a collaboration in clean energy and green mobility solutions, according to a press statement issued on Monday. Gentari Green Mobility is a subsidiary of Gentari Sdn Bhd, which is wholly owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS). (The Edge) MKLAND: Talks of major corporate exercise at MK Land resurface TALKS of a potential corporate exercise at property developer MK Land Holdings Bhd have resurfaced, with a source familiar with the matter saying an adviser has been appointed to explore possible options. The source spoke on condition of anonymity because the discussions are private. (The Edge) EVOCOM: IPO Watch: ACE Market-bound Evocom charts broader logistics footprint E-COMMERCE logistics and workforce solutions provider Evocom Bhd is set to make its debut on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market on Monday (Sept 28), with the group looking to broaden its logistics footprint through an expansion of its air freight transhipment business, technology investments and a new headquarters near Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s (KLIA) air cargo terminal. The company’s initial public offering (IPO) comprises 113.91 million new shares and an offer for sale of 22 million existing shares, both priced at 18 sen apiece. (The Edge) KGB: Unit wins further RM133m contract for Kuching data storage plant Kelington Group Bhd said its wholly owned unit has been awarded a second contract by a manufacturer operating in the Sama Jaya Free Industrial Zone in Kuching, Sarawak, worth about RM133 million. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the group said the award was given to Kelington Technologies Sdn Bhd (KTSB) on Oct 2 and covers the main structural steel works for the customer's data storage manufacturing facility, which is being expanded. (The Edge) ALPHA: Targets Main Market transfer in 4Q Alpha IVF Group is planning to transfer from the ACE Market to the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia, with completion expected sometime in the fourth quarter this year. The fertility care group said the transfer will be through the accelerated transfer process under the Securities Commission Malaysia’s Equity Guidelines, with shareholder approval required at a general meeting. title: '13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty honours real estate excellence |  Penang Property Talk
body: '13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty honours real estate excellence Top developers celebrated the 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia in partnership with iProperty, presented by Lim Soh & Goonting Advocates & Solicitors, at The St. Regis Kuala Lumpur. Guided by the theme “Defined by Excellence,” the 2026 PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty recognised the country’s best in real estate across 62 categories. From township developers to breakthrough companies, this year’s awards were comprehensive, honouring the best in different real estate segments and regions. Timber Land Group won the evening’s top honour, Best Developer, marking its first-ever win in the category, in addition to Best Developer (East Malaysia). CPI Land was named Best Developer (Central Malaysia) alongside award-winning project Tuan Straits. Tanah Sutera took both Best Developer (Southern Malaysia) and Best Landed Homes Developer, buoyed by winning project The Seed. JLand Group, named Best Township Developer, collected the most awards of any company, covering Developer, Development, and Design categories for projects including Arena Larkin; Bandar Tiram; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – Aspiration Park; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – STeP West; and Medora One. JRK Holdings Berhad won both Best Breakthrough Developer and Best Boutique Developer. Keck Seng (Malaysia) Berhad was named Best Mixed Use Developer, also winning for the project Daya 1 Residences, Taman Daya. Penang developers also made their mark at this year’s awards, with PTL Properties, Aspen and Pinnacle Group among the winners. PTL Properties was named Best Lifestyle Developer, with The Rimbun also winning Best Mass Market Landed Development (Northern) and Best Townhouse Development. Aspen’s Aspen Vision City received the Best Township Development (Northern) award, while Pinnacle Group won Best Premium High-Rise Development (Northern) for Pinnacle Bukit Gambier. Other companies with winning projects include Amalan Setar (M) Sdn Bhd, which won for Ixora Garden – Sari Alamanda 4 Phase 2; Armani Group (Armani Hallson Bukit Bintang); Astaka Kimlun Sdn Bhd (Amora Serviced Residence); BCB Land Sdn. Bhd. (Straya Heights); Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd (Coronation Square; Coronade Twins – Serviced Residences); CTC Development Malaysia Sdn Bhd (CTC Skyone @ Bukit Chagar); Faire Development (bée); Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd (Taman Impian Emas); Infra Park Sdn Bhd (MLIMA Kiara); KEB Berhad (Residensi Cove @ Kota Syahbandar); Matrix Concepts (Levia Residence Puchong); OCR Templer Sdn Bhd (D’Templer Hilltop Residences); Peter’s Group (Cherita Residences); Puncak Concept Sdn Bhd (Puncak LakePark City @ Cyberjaya); R&F Development Sdn Bhd (R&F Princess Cove); Steadfast Properties (Laguna Residences); Tiram Industrial Park Sdn Bhd (Akasia Business Park); Tropicana Corporation Berhad (Clarissa Serviced Suites, Tropicana Cenang); UEM Sunrise Berhad (Intrika, Serene Heightshase s); and Worldwide Holdings Berhad (Pavonia Worldwide, Bukit Bandaraya Shah Alam). Outstanding real estate figures The 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty celebrated some of the impactful figures in Malaysian real estate. Tan Sri Dato’ Seri Dr. Jeffrey Cheah KBE AO, founder and chairman of Sunway Group, received the Life Achievement Award. Dato’ Seri Azmir Merican, group managing director and chief executive officer of Sime Darby Property, was named Real Estate Personality of the Year. Dato’ Sri Edwin Tan Pei Seng, executive chairman of Paragon Globe Berhad, was honoured as Rising Star, while Ms. Maggie Ng Mui Kit, chief executive officer of Kuok Group Property Division (Southern), received the Woman Changemaker Award. Consumers, catalysts, and consistency The Consumer Demand Award continued this year, recognising the property that captured the strongest genuine interest from Malaysian property seekers. Determined by consumer views and leads across PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com.my, Leisure Farm Resort by Mulpha International was named Most In-Demand Bungalow/Villa, in addition to winning Best Resort-Style Township Development. The People’s Choice Awards also continued the tradition of tapping consumer opinion to identify the nation’s 10 favourite developers. This year, 15,383 votes were cast for developers that consumers in Malaysia admire and trust. body: 'The local stock market traded sideways with slight downward bias on Monday, as subdued domestic catalysts and heightened global uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The FBM KLCI inched down by 1.60 points to close at 1,670.02, off an low of 1,668.61 and high of 1,674.11, as losers led gainers 748 to 388, on total turnover of 3.11bn shares worth RM2.40bn. Uncertainty surrounding Middle East tensions and persistent inflationary pressures is likely to continue clouding the outlook for the local market. Immediate support for the index stays at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). Meanwhile, immediate resistance is maintained at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Any weakness on Maybank shares towards the 38.2%FR (RM9.74) or the 23.6%FR (RM9.27) should encourage buying on weakness ahead of recovery upside towards the 76.4%FR (RM10.96) with next resistance coming from the 25/02/26 high (RM11.71). Sime Darby shares remain in base building mode pending recovery to the 123.6%FP (RM2.67), with a confirmed breakout to aim for the 138.2%FP (RM2.82) and 150%FP (RM2.94), while immediate chart supports are from the 30-day ma (RM2.45) and 76.4%FR (RM2.19). Asian markets traded mixed on Monday as uncertainty over the Middle East weighed on sentiment, following U.S. President Donald Trump’s rejection of Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Over the weekend, US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming Tehran was desperate to make a deal. Trump said talks would continue this week, though Iran shows no sign of watering down its proposals. Rates will be in focus again this week, with a slew of key economic data on deck. The August personal consumption expenditure price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, is due on Wednesday. New U.S. manufacturing numbers are due Thursday, while the closely watched September jobs report is set for release Friday. Central banks have responded with a round of rate hikes, with the Reserve Bank of Australia likely to be the next to tighten when it meets on Tuesday. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.17% to 8,679.70, while South Korea’s Kospi slumped 2.70% to 6,889.74. In Japan, the Nikkei 225 fell 0.73% to 65,877.62 and the Topix lost 0.40% to 4,112.00. In the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index dropped 1.67% to 3,823.62, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index gained 0.54% to 24,642.51. Wall Street closed lower overnight as renewed US-Iran tensions pushed oil prices higher, while rising Treasury yields added pressure ahead of a week packed with key economic data. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.67% to 51,481.51. The S&P 500 slipped 0.77% to 7,683.69, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.92% to 26,820.38. Crude oil prices initially surged after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran but gains later eased as hopes grew that Qatari mediators could help bring the two sides back to the negotiating table. Iran presented the proposal during last week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York and said it had been conveyed to the United States through Qatar. With officials back at the negotiating table, Trump told Axios that US negotiators were expected to continue discussions with Iran this week. Meanwhile, a packed week of inflation and labour market data awaits investors. From the Personal Consumption Expenditures report on Wednesday to the monthly employment report on Friday, investors will find new insights on the health of the economy. Expectations for a rate hike from the Fed at its October meeting have climbed in recent d ays, in part due to economic data indicating the economy was growing at a solid pace. Gamuda Bhd said on Monday it secured an A$790mn (RM2.3bn) engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract in Australia to develop the first stage of the Mortlake Energy Hub. (The Edge) KKB Engineering Bhd (Not Rated) secured RM462mn in new contracts from Sarawak Shell and other customers, including a major offshore EPC project for the SK408 TeJa & Populus and Temu & Inai field developments. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) Willowglen MSC Bhd (Not Rated) secured a RM108mn, 8-year-11-month systems contract through its Singapore subsidiary, which is currently being divested as part of its proposed RM215.2mn disposal to Elixir II. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) AWC Bhd (Not Rated) has secured two contracts from Gujarat International Finance TecCity Co Ltd (GIF) in relation to upcoming developments in the Domestic Tariff Area and Special Economic Zone areas in Gujarat International Finance Tec-City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India, for a combined sum of RM13.1mn. (The Star) HSS Engineers Bhd’s (Not Rated) associate HSSI secured a RM11.0mn, 42-month engineering consultancy and site supervision contract for sewage treatment plant upgrades in Negeri Sembilan and Melaka. (The Star) Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd (Not Rated) agreed to dispose of its 50.82% stake in Hafary for RM447mn, realising an estimated RM187.3mn gross gain, with proceeds earmarked for partial repayment of its borrowings. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) AYER Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) proposed to acquire 9.11 acres of freehold land in Jalan Kuchai Lama for RM138mn, at a 4.8% discount to valuation, for future development, funded 20% internally and 80% through bank borrowings. (The Edge/ Bursa Malaysia) Sunsuria Bhd (Not Rated) proposed to dispose of 183,973 sq m of freehold commercial land in Sepang to Amazon Data Services Malaysia for RM316.8mn. (The Star) GUH Holdings Bhd (Not Rated)received the final RM23.7mn compensation payment from the Suzhou government, completing the RM114.9mn disposal of its industrial land and paving the way for the recognition of a RM95.3mn gain. (The Edge) Kinergy Advancement Bhd (Not Rated) founder Datuk Dr Lai Keng Onn acquired a 20.02% stake in Avangaad Bhd (Not Rated) for RM69.6mn, raising his direct holding to 23.08% and making him the marine vessels operator’s largest shareholder, alongside his existing 51% indirect interest. (The Edge) Willowglen MSC Bhd (Not Rated) shareholders have been advised to approve the proposed RM215.2mn disposal of its core remote building automation businesses to Elixir II, which is deemed fair and reasonable and would allow Willowglen to retain a 37.8% stake in Elixir II while unlocking value and funding a 5 sen/share dividend. (The Edge) IHH Healthcare Bhd (Not Rated) reiterated that its 2018 Fortis Healthcare investment was conducted through a transparent and fully regulated bidding process, while it will cooperate with the ongoing forensic audit following the Indian Supreme Court ruling. (Bernama/ The Star) Zetrix AI Bhd’s (Not Rated) external auditor TGS TW PLT resigned, citing portfolio rationalisation and resource management, with the company to appoint a new auditor within the required 21-day notice period. (The Edge) Aumas Resources Bhd (Not Rated) CEO Chong Tzu Khen has been placed on administrative leave after being charged with three counts of alleged bribery involving RM18,000, while the company said its mining operations will continue under senior management. (The Edge) Poh Kong Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) posted a record FY2026, with net profit surging 59.7% YoY to RM193.4mn on 14.5% higher revenue, driven by stronger gold prices and margins, while proposing a higher 5 sen final dividend. (The Edge) RedPlanet Bhd (Not Rated) launched its ACE Market IPO at 19 sen/share, aiming to raise RM15.2mn, with RM13.3mn earmarked mainly for expansion, project procurement, working capital and business development ahead of its scheduled listing on Oct 22. (The Edge) PESB Bhd (Not Rated), an electrical engineering specialist with RM35.2mn FY25 net profit, has filed for an ACE Market IPO to fund capacity expansion, project performance bonds and working capital amid rising demand for power infrastructure driven by data centre growth. (The Edge) Thong World Bhd (Not Rated), operator of the Thong Bowl restaurant chain, plans an ACE Market IPO of 176.8mn shares to fund outlet expansion and its packaged food segment. (The Star) Malaysia’s Producer Price Index (PPI) local production rose by 10.7% in August 2026, compared to a 9.7% increase in July 2026, said the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). In its PPI Local Production report for August 2026, DOSM said the mining sector jumped by 41.2% in August 2026, up from 30.5% in July 2026, driven by the extraction of crude petroleum and natural gas, which rose by 49.8% and 14.7%, respectively. “The manufacturing sector increased by 8.8%, compared to 8.2% in the preceding month, mainly driven by the manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products (33.5%) and the manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products (12.4%),” it said in a statement. The agriculture, forestry and fishing sector also increased by 4.6%, although this moderated from the 7.2% growth recorded in July 2026, with animal production registering an increase of 13.9%. The utility-related sectors also continue their upward trend, with water supply and electricity and gas supply increasing by 7.8% and 6.4%, respectively. (The Edge, Bernama) Any decision on a possible increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 should be left to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement when tabling Budget 2027, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said. He said the impact of any adjustment, particularly on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), would also need to be taken into consideration to ensure employers could sustain higher operating costs. “We are taking into account several segments and how implementation can be balanced so that we can continue to look after our workers while ensuring the sustainability of employers, particularly small businesses and MSMEs,” he told reporters after visiting the Kluang District Police Headquarters (IPD) quarters here on Monday. (The Edge, Bernama) The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing (FMM) has called for any review of the minimum wage to be negotiated through the National Wages Consultative Council’s tripartite process, with factors including productivity, cost of living and employers’ capacity to pay taken into account. The statement follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s comments that the government will announce more decisive measures on wages in Budget 2027, to be tabled on Oct 9. FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said employers recognise the need for better wages, but the ability to absorb higher payroll costs varies between companies. “Many larger firms already pay above the statutory minimum wage, while smaller manufacturers and labourintensive businesses generally have less room to absorb a sudden increase in payroll costs,” said Lee in the statement. Profits of a small number of highly successful corporations should not be taken as representative of the wider business community, with Lee noting that micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) accounted for 96.1% of business establishments in 2024, based on figures from SME Corporation Malaysia. (The Edge) The Malaysian Automotive Association (MAA) is proposing that the government provide a personal income tax rebate for the purchase of electrified vehicles (xEVs) and voluntarily scrapping of old vehicles in Budget 2027. MAA president Mohd Shamsor Mohd Zain said the association is suggesting a personal income tax rebate of between RM7,000 and RM10,000 to accelerate the mainstream adoption of xEVs, particularly among middle-income taxpayers keen on xEVs but sensitive to the price. The MAA proposal was submitted to the Ministry of Finance recently, he told Bernama. Mohd Shamsor said there is no direct purchase subsidy or tax rebate currently available for xEV buyers, citing that the existing relief is mainly limited to charging equipment. Mohd Shamsor said the MAA proposed that the government extend the existing RM2,500 individual income tax relief for home charging expenses beyond 2027. (The Edge, Bernama) Malaysia's financial markets adjusted in an orderly manner despite external pressures, and conditions remain conducive for corporates to raise funds, Bank Negara Malaysia's Financial Markets Committee (FMC) said. In a statement on Monday following the FMC's meeting on Sept 21, the committee cited sound economic fundamentals and strong foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows for the resilience of the domestic market. It said United States Federal Reserve rate hikes that led to a stronger US dollar and higher US Treasury yields were main drivers of recent market movements. “Nevertheless, the domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants,” said the FMC. The committee noted strong interest in corporate bond issuance and increased hedging as the ringgit moderated in September after being relatively stable in July and August, and increased Malaysian Government Security yields after remaining flat for a prolonged period. (The Edge, BNM) China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on US$60bn worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended US$30bn of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30% of US exports to China, he said. The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week. One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans. Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. (Reuters) China's industrial profit growth slowed further in August as strength in technology manufacturing amid the AI boom was outweighed by persistently weak domestic demand. Firms are increasingly struggling to maintain pricing power due to soft consumption and excess capacity in some sectors. Profits at China's industrial firms in August rose 4.2% from a year earlier, down from 11.2% in July, while profit increased 15.7% in the first eight months, easing from 17.6% in the January-July period, National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data showed on Monday. Profits in computer, communication and other electronic equipment manufacturing led the gains, jumping 110% in the first eight months, according to a breakdown of NBS data. By contrast, the wine, beverages and refined tea manufacturing industry was among the worst performers, with profits falling 34.7%. (Reuters) White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett suggested that, while the US economy is now on track for strong growth, “outside” factors could get in the way of the administration’s hopes for at least a 3% expansion rate. Given gains in US productivity and wages, economic growth “should be cruising around 4% instead of 3%,” Hassett said to the Economic Club of New York in an event Monday. He said that was his “sort of base case — no disruptions from the outside world.” While administration officials including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have targeted a 3% sustained pace for gross domestic product gains during President Donald Trump’s current term in office, private economists expect growth closer to 2%. The artificial intelligence investment boom has supported GDP gains in recent quarters, but economists point to a slowdown in labour-force growth as a key headwind. Turning to the fiscal outlook, Hassett also indicated that complications — which he didn’t spell out — could thwart achieving the target of a 3% budget gap as a ratio of GDP that Bessent has laid out. (Bloomberg) US President Donald Trump said he is still looking “very seriously” at implementing a US ban on diesel exports to combat high prices, even as others in his administration continue to focus on other possible steps. “That can oftentimes lead to a little bit of an increase on gasoline for cars, so we’re looking at it very seriously — we may do it,” Trump told a Fox News reporter on Sunday while attending the Presidents Cup golf tournament final near Chicago. Several farm-state lawmakers have urged Trump to limit US diesel exports during the peak of the fall harvest season, as global fuel markets reel from the disruption to flows in the critical Strait of Hormuz and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The US has emerged as the supplier of last resort to the world, with diesel exports surging to a weekly record near two million barrels a day last month. National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been analysing the ramifications of a potential short-term ban on US diesel exports over the last week, underscoring the seriousness of the administration’s consideration of the idea. (Bloomberg) Rising bond yields will curb economic expansion and limit the transfer of elevated energy costs to inflation, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said. “While growth has been resilient, since our last meeting long-term interest rates have risen notably, which will slow growth and reduce pass-through by more than projected in our September exercise,” Lagarde said Monday. With second-round effects so far absent, that means the ECB should adopt a “measured response as appropriate to keep inflation in check,” she told European lawmakers in Brussels. Traders pared monetary-tightening bets and now see a less than 40% chance of a hike by the ECB next month. ECB officials are weighing the need for further interest-rate increases to bring inflation under control and avoid higher energy costs spilling into broader prices and wage demands. description: 'Local stock market trades sideways amid geopolitical risks and US-Iran tensions, while Asian and Wall Street markets face mixed results. Explore latest economic and corporate updates.
full_text: 'Daily Brief - 29 Sep 2026. 'The local stock market traded sideways with slight downward bias on Monday, as subdued domestic catalysts and heightened global uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The FBM KLCI inched down by 1.60 points to close at 1,670.02, off an low of 1,668.61 and high of 1,674.11, as losers led gainers 748 to 388, on total turnover of 3.11bn shares worth RM2.40bn. Uncertainty surrounding Middle East tensions and persistent inflationary pressures is likely to continue clouding the outlook for the local market. Immediate support for the index stays at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). Meanwhile, immediate resistance is maintained at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Any weakness on Maybank shares towards the 38.2%FR (RM9.74) or the 23.6%FR (RM9.27) should encourage buying on weakness ahead of recovery upside towards the 76.4%FR (RM10.96) with next resistance coming from the 25/02/26 high (RM11.71). Sime Darby shares remain in base building mode pending recovery to the 123.6%FP (RM2.67), with a confirmed breakout to aim for the 138.2%FP (RM2.82) and 150%FP (RM2.94), while immediate chart supports are from the 30-day ma (RM2.45) and 76.4%FR (RM2.19). Asian markets traded mixed on Monday as uncertainty over the Middle East weighed on sentiment, following U.S. President Donald Trump’s rejection of Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Over the weekend, US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming Tehran was desperate to make a deal. Trump said talks would continue this week, though Iran shows no sign of watering down its proposals. Rates will be in focus again this week, with a slew of key economic data on deck. The August personal consumption expenditure price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, is due on Wednesday. New U.S. manufacturing numbers are due Thursday, while the closely watched September jobs report is set for release Friday. Central banks have responded with a round of rate hikes, with the Reserve Bank of Australia likely to be the next to tighten when it meets on Tuesday. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.17% to 8,679.70, while South Korea’s Kospi slumped 2.70% to 6,889.74. In Japan, the Nikkei 225 fell 0.73% to 65,877.62 and the Topix lost 0.40% to 4,112.00. In the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index dropped 1.67% to 3,823.62, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index gained 0.54% to 24,642.51. Wall Street closed lower overnight as renewed US-Iran tensions pushed oil prices higher, while rising Treasury yields added pressure ahead of a week packed with key economic data. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.67% to 51,481.51. The S&P 500 slipped 0.77% to 7,683.69, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.92% to 26,820.38. Crude oil prices initially surged after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran but gains later eased as hopes grew that Qatari mediators could help bring the two sides back to the negotiating table. Iran presented the proposal during last week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York and said it had been conveyed to the United States through Qatar. With officials back at the negotiating table, Trump told Axios that US negotiators were expected to continue discussions with Iran this week. Meanwhile, a packed week of inflation and labour market data awaits investors. From the Personal Consumption Expenditures report on Wednesday to the monthly employment report on Friday, investors will find new insights on the health of the economy. Expectations for a rate hike from the Fed at its October meeting have climbed in recent d ays, in part due to economic data indicating the economy was growing at a solid pace. Gamuda Bhd said on Monday it secured an A$790mn (RM2.3bn) engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract in Australia to develop the first stage of the Mortlake Energy Hub. (The Edge) KKB Engineering Bhd (Not Rated) secured RM462mn in new contracts from Sarawak Shell and other customers, including a major offshore EPC project for the SK408 TeJa & Populus and Temu & Inai field developments. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) Willowglen MSC Bhd (Not Rated) secured a RM108mn, 8-year-11-month systems contract through its Singapore subsidiary, which is currently being divested as part of its proposed RM215.2mn disposal to Elixir II. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) AWC Bhd (Not Rated) has secured two contracts from Gujarat International Finance TecCity Co Ltd (GIF) in relation to upcoming developments in the Domestic Tariff Area and Special Economic Zone areas in Gujarat International Finance Tec-City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India, for a combined sum of RM13.1mn. (The Star) HSS Engineers Bhd’s (Not Rated) associate HSSI secured a RM11.0mn, 42-month engineering consultancy and site supervision contract for sewage treatment plant upgrades in Negeri Sembilan and Melaka. (The Star) Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd (Not Rated) agreed to dispose of its 50.82% stake in Hafary for RM447mn, realising an estimated RM187.3mn gross gain, with proceeds earmarked for partial repayment of its borrowings. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) AYER Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) proposed to acquire 9.11 acres of freehold land in Jalan Kuchai Lama for RM138mn, at a 4.8% discount to valuation, for future development, funded 20% internally and 80% through bank borrowings. (The Edge/ Bursa Malaysia) Sunsuria Bhd (Not Rated) proposed to dispose of 183,973 sq m of freehold commercial land in Sepang to Amazon Data Services Malaysia for RM316.8mn. (The Star) GUH Holdings Bhd (Not Rated)received the final RM23.7mn compensation payment from the Suzhou government, completing the RM114.9mn disposal of its industrial land and paving the way for the recognition of a RM95.3mn gain. (The Edge) Kinergy Advancement Bhd (Not Rated) founder Datuk Dr Lai Keng Onn acquired a 20.02% stake in Avangaad Bhd (Not Rated) for RM69.6mn, raising his direct holding to 23.08% and making him the marine vessels operator’s largest shareholder, alongside his existing 51% indirect interest. (The Edge) Willowglen MSC Bhd (Not Rated) shareholders have been advised to approve the proposed RM215.2mn disposal of its core remote building automation businesses to Elixir II, which is deemed fair and reasonable and would allow Willowglen to retain a 37.8% stake in Elixir II while unlocking value and funding a 5 sen/share dividend. (The Edge) IHH Healthcare Bhd (Not Rated) reiterated that its 2018 Fortis Healthcare investment was conducted through a transparent and fully regulated bidding process, while it will cooperate with the ongoing forensic audit following the Indian Supreme Court ruling. (Bernama/ The Star) Zetrix AI Bhd’s (Not Rated) external auditor TGS TW PLT resigned, citing portfolio rationalisation and resource management, with the company to appoint a new auditor within the required 21-day notice period. (The Edge) Aumas Resources Bhd (Not Rated) CEO Chong Tzu Khen has been placed on administrative leave after being charged with three counts of alleged bribery involving RM18,000, while the company said its mining operations will continue under senior management. (The Edge) Poh Kong Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) posted a record FY2026, with net profit surging 59.7% YoY to RM193.4mn on 14.5% higher revenue, driven by stronger gold prices and margins, while proposing a higher 5 sen final dividend. (The Edge) RedPlanet Bhd (Not Rated) launched its ACE Market IPO at 19 sen/share, aiming to raise RM15.2mn, with RM13.3mn earmarked mainly for expansion, project procurement, working capital and business development ahead of its scheduled listing on Oct 22. (The Edge) PESB Bhd (Not Rated), an electrical engineering specialist with RM35.2mn FY25 net profit, has filed for an ACE Market IPO to fund capacity expansion, project performance bonds and working capital amid rising demand for power infrastructure driven by data centre growth. (The Edge) Thong World Bhd (Not Rated), operator of the Thong Bowl restaurant chain, plans an ACE Market IPO of 176.8mn shares to fund outlet expansion and its packaged food segment. (The Star) Malaysia’s Producer Price Index (PPI) local production rose by 10.7% in August 2026, compared to a 9.7% increase in July 2026, said the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). In its PPI Local Production report for August 2026, DOSM said the mining sector jumped by 41.2% in August 2026, up from 30.5% in July 2026, driven by the extraction of crude petroleum and natural gas, which rose by 49.8% and 14.7%, respectively. “The manufacturing sector increased by 8.8%, compared to 8.2% in the preceding month, mainly driven by the manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products (33.5%) and the manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products (12.4%),” it said in a statement. The agriculture, forestry and fishing sector also increased by 4.6%, although this moderated from the 7.2% growth recorded in July 2026, with animal production registering an increase of 13.9%. The utility-related sectors also continue their upward trend, with water supply and electricity and gas supply increasing by 7.8% and 6.4%, respectively. (The Edge, Bernama) Any decision on a possible increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 should be left to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement when tabling Budget 2027, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said. He said the impact of any adjustment, particularly on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), would also need to be taken into consideration to ensure employers could sustain higher operating costs. “We are taking into account several segments and how implementation can be balanced so that we can continue to look after our workers while ensuring the sustainability of employers, particularly small businesses and MSMEs,” he told reporters after visiting the Kluang District Police Headquarters (IPD) quarters here on Monday. (The Edge, Bernama) The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing (FMM) has called for any review of the minimum wage to be negotiated through the National Wages Consultative Council’s tripartite process, with factors including productivity, cost of living and employers’ capacity to pay taken into account. The statement follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s comments that the government will announce more decisive measures on wages in Budget 2027, to be tabled on Oct 9. FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said employers recognise the need for better wages, but the ability to absorb higher payroll costs varies between companies. “Many larger firms already pay above the statutory minimum wage, while smaller manufacturers and labourintensive businesses generally have less room to absorb a sudden increase in payroll costs,” said Lee in the statement. Profits of a small number of highly successful corporations should not be taken as representative of the wider business community, with Lee noting that micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) accounted for 96.1% of business establishments in 2024, based on figures from SME Corporation Malaysia. (The Edge) The Malaysian Automotive Association (MAA) is proposing that the government provide a personal income tax rebate for the purchase of electrified vehicles (xEVs) and voluntarily scrapping of old vehicles in Budget 2027. MAA president Mohd Shamsor Mohd Zain said the association is suggesting a personal income tax rebate of between RM7,000 and RM10,000 to accelerate the mainstream adoption of xEVs, particularly among middle-income taxpayers keen on xEVs but sensitive to the price. The MAA proposal was submitted to the Ministry of Finance recently, he told Bernama. Mohd Shamsor said there is no direct purchase subsidy or tax rebate currently available for xEV buyers, citing that the existing relief is mainly limited to charging equipment. Mohd Shamsor said the MAA proposed that the government extend the existing RM2,500 individual income tax relief for home charging expenses beyond 2027. (The Edge, Bernama) Malaysia's financial markets adjusted in an orderly manner despite external pressures, and conditions remain conducive for corporates to raise funds, Bank Negara Malaysia's Financial Markets Committee (FMC) said. In a statement on Monday following the FMC's meeting on Sept 21, the committee cited sound economic fundamentals and strong foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows for the resilience of the domestic market. It said United States Federal Reserve rate hikes that led to a stronger US dollar and higher US Treasury yields were main drivers of recent market movements. “Nevertheless, the domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants,” said the FMC. The committee noted strong interest in corporate bond issuance and increased hedging as the ringgit moderated in September after being relatively stable in July and August, and increased Malaysian Government Security yields after remaining flat for a prolonged period. (The Edge, BNM) China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on US$60bn worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended US$30bn of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30% of US exports to China, he said. The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week. One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans. Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. (Reuters) China's industrial profit growth slowed further in August as strength in technology manufacturing amid the AI boom was outweighed by persistently weak domestic demand. Firms are increasingly struggling to maintain pricing power due to soft consumption and excess capacity in some sectors. Profits at China's industrial firms in August rose 4.2% from a year earlier, down from 11.2% in July, while profit increased 15.7% in the first eight months, easing from 17.6% in the January-July period, National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data showed on Monday. Profits in computer, communication and other electronic equipment manufacturing led the gains, jumping 110% in the first eight months, according to a breakdown of NBS data. By contrast, the wine, beverages and refined tea manufacturing industry was among the worst performers, with profits falling 34.7%. (Reuters) White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett suggested that, while the US economy is now on track for strong growth, “outside” factors could get in the way of the administration’s hopes for at least a 3% expansion rate. Given gains in US productivity and wages, economic growth “should be cruising around 4% instead of 3%,” Hassett said to the Economic Club of New York in an event Monday. He said that was his “sort of base case — no disruptions from the outside world.” While administration officials including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have targeted a 3% sustained pace for gross domestic product gains during President Donald Trump’s current term in office, private economists expect growth closer to 2%. The artificial intelligence investment boom has supported GDP gains in recent quarters, but economists point to a slowdown in labour-force growth as a key headwind. Turning to the fiscal outlook, Hassett also indicated that complications — which he didn’t spell out — could thwart achieving the target of a 3% budget gap as a ratio of GDP that Bessent has laid out. (Bloomberg) US President Donald Trump said he is still looking “very seriously” at implementing a US ban on diesel exports to combat high prices, even as others in his administration continue to focus on other possible steps. “That can oftentimes lead to a little bit of an increase on gasoline for cars, so we’re looking at it very seriously — we may do it,” Trump told a Fox News reporter on Sunday while attending the Presidents Cup golf tournament final near Chicago. Several farm-state lawmakers have urged Trump to limit US diesel exports during the peak of the fall harvest season, as global fuel markets reel from the disruption to flows in the critical Strait of Hormuz and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The US has emerged as the supplier of last resort to the world, with diesel exports surging to a weekly record near two million barrels a day last month. National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been analysing the ramifications of a potential short-term ban on US diesel exports over the last week, underscoring the seriousness of the administration’s consideration of the idea. (Bloomberg) Rising bond yields will curb economic expansion and limit the transfer of elevated energy costs to inflation, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said. “While growth has been resilient, since our last meeting long-term interest rates have risen notably, which will slow growth and reduce pass-through by more than projected in our September exercise,” Lagarde said Monday. With second-round effects so far absent, that means the ECB should adopt a “measured response as appropriate to keep inflation in check,” she told European lawmakers in Brussels. Traders pared monetary-tightening bets and now see a less than 40% chance of a hike by the ECB next month. ECB officials are weighing the need for further interest-rate increases to bring inflation under control and avoid higher energy costs spilling into broader prices and wage demands. As well as the conflict in the Middle East, they’re grappling with a global bond-market selloff that’s a particular worry for some fiscally strained members of the euro zone. title: 'Siapa Hijjas Kasturi? Tokoh Sebalik Mercu Tanda Di Malaysia
body: 'Siapa Hijjas Kasturi? Tokoh Sebalik Mercu Tanda Di Malaysia Beliau turut membina mercu tanda seperti Menara Maybank, Menara Telekom, Shahzan Tower dan lain-lain. - Hijjas Kasturi, bapa seni bina moden Malaysia, mencipta bangunan ikonik yang mencerminkan identiti budaya dan Islam negara. - Karya terkenalnya termasuk Menara Tabung Haji, Menara MBPJ, dan PICC, setiap satunya menggabungkan elemen tradisional Melayu. Jangan lupa follow channel Telegram TRPbm untuk ketahui updates semasa & relevan! Pemandangan ibu kota Kuala Lumpur dipenuhi dengan pelbagai bangunan dan pencakar langit yang mempunyai identiti, cita rasa serta seni bina tersendiri menghasilkan rupa unik. Namun, ramai tidak sedar bahawa di sebalik beberapa bangunan menghiasi ibu kota, terdapat satu nama yang sama. Nama tersebut ialah Hijjas Kasturi, seorang tokoh yang digelar sebagai bapa seni bina moden Malaysia. Sehingga kini, karyanya bukan sahaja menghiasi landskap negara, malah menjadi inspirasi kepada ramai generasi muda. Bermula Di Singapura Pada Tahun 1936 Hijjas Kasturi dilahirkan di Singapura pada 26 September 1936. Ibunya berketurunan Cina telah berkahwin dengan seorang lelaki berketurunan Jawa-Singapura. Beliau mendapat pendidikan di Raffles Institution, sebelum menerima biasiswa dari Kerajaan Australia untuk menyambung pelajaran. Menariknya, Hijjas telah mula belajar di University of Adelaide, sebelum menjadi graduan daripada University of Melbourne. Pada tahun 1967, Hijjas berpindah ke Malaysia dan mengasaskan program ijazah profesional pertama di negara ini, iaitu School of Art and Architecture di Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM). Bermula Sebagai Seorang Pelukis Pelan Perjalanan kerjaya Hijjas bermula seawal tahun 1956 sebagai seorang Draughtsman bersama Singapore Housing Trust. Dia bertanggungjawab untuk menyediakan master plan bagi kawasan Queenstown dan rumah apartment kos rendah. Kemudian, kerjayanya berkembang merentasi dua buah negara menerusi beberapa jawatan penting seperti: - 1959: Menyertai South Australian Housing Trust, menyediakan master plan Elizabeth Town dan skim perumahan. - 1961: Menjadi Pembantu Seni Bina dengan Brown & Davis yang terlibat dalam perancangan hospital, bangunan komersial dan perumahan. - 1965: Menjadi arkitek dengan Hume Proprietary Ltd, Melbourne bertanggungjawab merancang pembinaan kilang, gudang dan pejabat. - 1966: Kembali semula ke Singapura sebagai Arkitek / Perancang dengan Housing and Development Board (HDB). Hijjas turut mengetuai pasukan kajian penubuhan ITM dan menjadi Ketua Pengasas School of Art and Architecture. Pada tahun 1969, Hijjas menjadi rakan kongsi pengasas Arkitek Bersekutu, sebelum akhirnya menubuhkan firma sendiri, iaitu Hijjas Kasturi Associates Sdn (HKAS). Proses Mencari Identiti Seni Bina Melambangkan Malaysia Bagi Hijjas, seni bina bukan sekadar membina bangunan, tetapi membentuk identiti sebuah bangsa. “Saya mahu menyumbang kepada kebaikan budaya dan rakyat dengan mencipta landskap visual yang mencerminkan identiti Malaysia.” Pencarian identiti itu merupakan satu tindak balas selepas tamatnya zaman penjajahan di Tanah Melayu. Ketika negara kita mencapai kemerdekaan pada tahun 1957, kita masih belum mempunyai gaya seni bina nasional yang jelas. Apa yang ada pada waktu itu ialah seni bina rumah kampung tradisional dan telah menjadi inspirasi pertama Hijjas. Contohnya, rumah kampung Melayu terkenal dengan bumbung tinggi, dibina atas tiang dan mempunyai ruang seperti anjung untuk menyambut kehadiran tetamu. Elemen-elemen tradisional dan agama Islam tidak diterapkan secara bulat-bulat. Sebaliknya diolah menjadi sentuhan halus dan mempunyai maksud tersirat dalam setiap reka bentuknya. Menara Tabung Haji Menjadi Antara Karya Paling Ikonik Antara karya Hijjas yang paling dikenali ialah Menara Tabung Haji, siap sepenuhnya pada tahun 1984. Menara pejabat setinggi 37 tingkat mempunyai siluet dramatik, dengan bahagian sisi melengkung dan tirus menyerupai bentuk jam pasir. Pelan lantainya mempunyai bentuk bulat direka dengan lima tiang di bahagian sisi melambangkan Rukun Islam. Di samping itu, bangunan ini turut direka bagi menampung kemasukan jemaah haji setiap tahun, lengkap dengan ruang masuk kenderaan yang luas. Ia juga dibina sebelum kemunculan aplikasi perisian komputer (CAD) yang canggih menggabungkan lukisan tangan bagi setiap tingkat dengan teknik pembinaan pada zaman tersebut. Menara MBPJ Berdiri Megah Dalam Persekitarannya Satu lagi karya Hijjas yang menarik ialah Menara Majlis Bandaraya Petaling Jaya (MBPJ). Berbeza dengan bangunan lain, menara 27 tingkat ini mengutamakan sebuah dataran bandar yang luas dan kawasan membeli-belah di bahagian bawahnya. Dataran tersebut telah berhubung dengan kawasan pejalan kaki memudahkan orang untuk masuk ke dalam. Selain itu, bahagian menara turut berhubung dengan kawasan jalan sekeliling menerusi jambatan berbumbung. Reka bentuk bangunan ini cuba menyesuaikan diri dengan kawasan kedai-kedai di persekitarannya. Disebabkan itu, bangunan ini dihias bagi mengurangkan ketinggiannya dan melembutkan penampilannya secara semula jadi. Pusat Konvensyen Yang Menjadikan Kerongsang Sebagai Inspirasi Sering disebut sebagai antara karya Hijjas paling hebat ialah Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) yang dibina atas sebuah bukit di Putrajaya. Siap pada tahun 2003, bentuk bumbung yang menyerupai pending perak, iaitu kepala tali pinggang tradisional digunakan oleh golongan diraja Melayu. Malah, reka bentuk bangunan ini juga mesra alam dengan menggabungkan penggunaan cahaya siang secara semula jadi. Selain itu, ia turut menampilkan laluan lapan, bumbung tergantung untuk menyejukkan ruang di bawahnya. Hasilnya ialah sebuah permata seni bina yang sangat cantik di atas sebuah bukit hijau. Dedikasi terhadap seni bina dan peka kepada budaya tempatan bukan sahaja telah mengubah pemandangan ibu kota negara, malah mengajar kita untuk menghargai setiap satu bangunan yang telah wujud. title: 'Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. “In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said. Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide. He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony. — Bernama

title: 'UK Job Slump Longer Than During Financial Crisis, PMI Says
body: '(Oct 5): Britain’s jobs market is stuck in its longest downturn since the early 2000s, according to a closely-watched survey, surpassing the decline during the financial crisis. S&P Global’s UK purchasing managers’ index (PMI) said employers cut back on staff for a 24th consecutive month. The figures will be a concern for Andy Burnham’s government ahead of the budget later this month with the intensifying energy shock and artificial intelligence (AI) threatening to dampen demand for workers. Employers have been shedding staff since the Labour government raised payroll taxes and the minimum wage shortly after returning to power in 2024. There were some signs of the slump bottoming out, however, as job cuts in the services sector were the smallest in almost a year. Furthermore, Britain’s official unemployment rate remains much lower than during the period after the global financial crisis. Britain’s labour market has been soft despite the wider economy smashing expectations during a resilient first half of the year. S&P’s survey suggested that the private sector is largely holding up against the energy shock for now, with demand boosted by stronger consumer spending and technology services amid a rush to harness AI. The composite PMI eased to 52 in September from 52.5 the previous month, remaining above the 50 threshold separating growth from contraction. It was slightly better than the 51.7 reading in the flash estimate. Still, the outlook has darkened since a resurgence in energy prices last month that has prompted traders to ramp up bets on the Bank of England raising interest rates several times to stop inflationary pressures spreading across the economy. “Subdued demand conditions and rising inflationary pressures contributed to weaker business activity expectations for the year ahead,” said Tim Moore, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence. “Greater-than-expected business requirements seem to have helped to stem the jobs downturn in recent months.” The survey pointed to price pressures growing. Firms’ cost burdens and the prices they charge customers both rose at the quickest pace since June. title: 'Sunway Construction could bag RM1b mixed-use development contracts near Bukit Chagar — Maybank IB
body: 'Sunway Construction could bag RM1b mixed-use development contracts near Bukit Chagar — Maybank IB KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 10): Sunway Construction Group Bhd (KL:SUNCON) could win an estimated RM1 billion in podium and tower contracts for an integrated mixed-use development at the Bukit Chagar RTS Link, Johor Bahru, according to Maybank Investment Bank. The research house noted that the potential win came from a joint venture development between its parent company, Sunway Bhd (KL:SUNWAY), and Mass Rapid Transit Corporation (MRT Corp), which could increase Sunway Construction’s overall net profit by about RM60 million. Consequently, Maybank IB mantained its “buy” call and RM9.62 target price, pegged to 17.7 times the financial year ending Dec 31, 2027 (FY2027) estimated price earnings. Previously, Sunway Construction had secured a RM1.5 billion contract to undertake construction works for the rapid transit system (RTS) transit-oriented development at Bukit Chagar, Johor, in a related-party transaction last year. At the time of writing, Sunway Construction shares were down three sen or 0.38% at RM7.95, valuing the company at RM10.6 billion. RM11 billion worth of development value surrounding Bukit Chagar station Analysts estimate that the total development value surrounding the Bukit Chagar station will reach a combined RM11 billion across the three largest surrounding projects. The commercial opening of the RTS Link in late 2026 or early 2027 is widely anticipated to catalyse property demand and accelerate construction timelines in the zone. The three anchor projects driving the node represent a combined gross development value of RM11.1 billion, consisting of the RM5 billion Coronation Square, the RM3.5 billion Causewayz Square, and the RM2.6 billion Sunway-MRT Corp integrated development. Of the trio, Coronation Square — an eight-tower integrated hub comprising offices, residential units, medical facilities, and an Ascott hotel — is slated for completion by 2029. Meanwhile, the wider Sunway-MRT Corp integrated development will be phased over eight years, with its primary components targeted for completion between 2033 and 2036. Binastra emerges as major Causewayz Square’s beneficiary Causewayz Square, a high-density mixed residential and retail project developed by EXSIM Group, is targeted for full completion by December 2030. Maybank IB highlighted the project's significance for Binastra Corporation Bhd (KL:BNASTRA), noting that the RM1.3 billion worth of contracts secured from this development accounts for approximately 20% of the builder's outstanding order book. Within this package, the main RM1.2 billion construction job is projected to contribute roughly RM90 million to the group's net profit. At the time of writing, Binastra Corporation shares were down one sen or 0.4% at RM2.47, valuing the company at RM2.7 billion. The proposed 50km elevated transit network will comprise 32 stations across the Skudai, Tebrau and Iskandar Puteri corridors, converging at the Bukit Chagar station. It will serve as the RTS Link’s feeder and last-mile connection, dispersing up to 10,000 cross-border passengers per hour into the Johor Bahru area. The content is a snapshot from Publisher.
