title: 'PublicInvest Research Headlines - 24 Sep 2026
body: 'Global: Inflation will linger and Fed will hike rates again, OECD says. Inflation around the world will be faster than forecast in 2027, an outlook that necessitates more tightening from the US to Australia. The Paris-based club of rich countries raised projections compared with June for consumer-price growth in every Group-of-20 economy apart from China and Saudi Arabia. Monetary policy across the globe may have to respond. The analysis underscores how the economic impact of the Middle East war unleashed by US President Donald Trump is now set to endure into the second half of his term in office. The OECD's assessment follows a round of tightening this month, with the US Fed, the ECB and BOJ all raising interest rates within little more than a week of each other. The organisation's officials reckon more such action is in the offing, while suggesting it won't match the aggressive policy moves seen in the wake of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Bloomberg) US: Business activity at more than five-year high; inflation pressures building. US business activity raced to a more than five-year high in Sep, fueled by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher. S&P Global's flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month. That was the highest level since July 2021 and followed a reading of 56.0 in August. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. The rise in the PMI reflected strong gains in both the services and manufacturing sectors. The PMI was consistent with the economy growing at around a 5% annualised rate. It also noted a sharp rise in work backlogs and supply chain delays, pointing to a lack of operating capacity which fed through to higher prices. (Reuters) EU: Eurozone business activity hits three-year high on services. Private-sector activity in the euro area grew at the fastest pace in more than three years as the service sector unexpectedly improved. The Composite PMI compiled by S&P Global increased to 53.1 from 52 in August, well above the 50 threshold separating growth from contraction. Analysts in a Bloomberg survey had anticipated a small decline to 51.7. The region's two largest economies both exceeded expectations, with activity in Germany growing at the fastest pace since Oct 2025 and France unexpectedly expanding at the quickest in more than two years. The euro-area economy is showing greater resilience than expected to the Middle East conflict and the resulting jump in energy costs. How long it can resist such headwinds remains uncertain, however, with inflation at its highest level in almost three years and borrowing costs rising. (Bloomberg) UK: Business activity cools as inflation pressure ramps up ahead of budget. Growth in British business activity cooled this month and inflation pressure built, an awkward backdrop for Finance Minister John Healey ahead of his first budget next month. The S&P Global UK services PMI fell in Sep to 51.7 from 52.5 in August, a three-month low. A Reuters poll of economists had pointed to a reading of 52.0. Prices charged by services companies, the backbone of Britain's economy, rose at the fastest pace in four months. They also reported accelerating cost pressures following a rise in energy prices stemming from the escalating war in Iran. S&P Global's survey pointed to quarterly economic growth of around 0.1%, compared with 0.4% in 2Q.. (Reuters) Indonesia: Holds rate, boosting hedging incentives for rupiah. Indonesia's central bank kept its interest rate unchanged for a third straight meeting, choosing to rely on continued intervention and increased hedging incentives to support the rupiah in the face of higher oil prices and US yields. The new governor Destry Damayanti and her board held the BI-Rate at 5.75% on Wednesday as expected by 33 of 36 economists surveyed by Bloomberg. The rest had pencilled in a quarter-point hike. Bank Indonesia also further cut the premiums for conventional hedging swaps on portfolio investments by up to 25% and for domestic non-deliverable forwards by up to 30%. These perks are applicable for portfolio investments, foreign loans and foreign direct investments. The Indonesian rupiah and bonds held earlier gains after the decision, with the currency strengthening 0.4% to 17,800 per dollar to outperform regional peers on Wednesday. Stocks rallied further to 1.5%, the biggest rise in almost a month. (Bloomebrg) Singapore: Core inflation climbs to 2.2% in August. Singapore's core inflation rose in August, driven by higher inflation for services, retail and other goods, and food. Core inflation, which excludes private transport and accommodation to better reflect household expenses, came in at 2.2%, up from 2% in July. The figure was in line with a median estimate in a Bloomberg poll. Overall inflation increased to 2.3% in August, from 2.2% in July, as higher core inflation more than offset lower private transport inflation. Private transport inflation slowed to 7.5% in August, from 8% in July, due to a smaller increase in car prices. Meanwhile, accommodation inflation was unchanged at 0.8%, with housing rents increasing in August at the same pace as in July. Services inflation edged up to 2% in August, from 1.7% in July, as airfares and prices of point-to-point transport services climbed at a faster pace. (The Straits Times) CTOS: Detects cyber breach, limited consumer data accessed. CTOS Digital said that its cybersecurity system recently detected unauthorised access to an environment supporting its consumer business. Certain data files containing a limited subset of processed consumer information were accessed from the affected environment, the credit reporting agency said. However, CTOS did not disclose what specific personal information was accessed. (The Edge) Aneka Jaringan: Secures RM26m foundation works contract for 53-storey KL serviced apartment. Aneka Jaringan Holdings has won a RM26.2m contract for the foundation works for a 53-storey serviced apartment project at Jalan Yap Kwan Seng here. Aneka Jaringan said its wholly-owned subsidiary accepted the LoA for the project from WDA Architecture SB, acting on behalf of Exsim YKS 54 SB, a member company of Exsim Group. The contract for earthworks, piling, pile caps, retaining wall and sub-structure works commenced on Sept 15, is scheduled to conclude on Aug 14, 2028. (The Edge) Carimin Petroleum: Unit to acquire property in Sarawak worth RM21.1m. Carimin Petroleum's 90%-owned subsidiary, Sri Borneo Energy SB, proposes to acquire leasehold land and buildings in Sarawak from Sarwaja Timur SB for RM21.1m. Carimin Petroleum said its unit entered into a SPA with Sarwaja on Sept 14. The company said the acquisition would include the reactivation of the galvanising and metal fabrication business, leveraging the former plant's track record and customer recognition. (The Edge) Paragon Globe: Eyes RM1.69bn industrial park in Sedenak. Paragon Globe is pursuing a land acquisition in Sedenak, Johor, for a proposed industrial park with a preliminary GDV of RM1.69bn. The proposed development, located within the Kulai-Sedenak flagship zone of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), is expected to comprise industrial factories, commercial components and worker accommodation. (The Star) AYS Ventures: To sell 74% stake in Steelaris for SGD5.2m. AYS Ventures's indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Ann Yak Siong (Singapore) Pte Ltd (AYSS) has agreed to dispose of its 74% stake in Singapore-based Steelaris Pte Ltd to CosmoSteel Holdings Pte Ltd for SGD5.2m. AYS Ventures said AYSS will receive SGD1.8m in cash and 13.5m new CosmoSteel shares at an issue price of SGD0.25 each. (The Star) YTL Power: YTL AI Labs partners with NVIDIA to create dataset for training Malaysia-context AI. YTL AI Labs SB, a subsidiary of YTL Power International, announced the creation of a dataset of 1.35m synthetic personas that will help in the development of AI models that suit Malaysia's diversity. The dataset, called Nemotron-Personas-Malaysia, was developed in collaboration with tech giant Nvidia. (The Edge) Destini: Signs two-year pact with Siemens Mobility for digital railway MRO. Destini will collaborate with transit and rail technology company Siemens Mobility SB to realise its ambition of becoming a digitally enabled railway maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) service provider. The group's 70%-owned unit M Rail Technics SB (Railtec) has signed a two-year agreement with Siemens Mobility to establish a reliability control centre for data-driven MRO. (The Edge) The KLCI might open lower higher today as pressure from the US bond market hit a new level on Wall Street Wednesday after a surprisingly strong report on the economy raised worries about inflation, while oil prices halted their slide. The squeeze caused US stocks to sink. The S&P 500 fell 0.8% after finishing the prior day just 0.4% below its record set last month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 352 points, or 0.7%, while the Nasdaq composite sank 1.1% from its own all-time high. Stocks wilted after the yield on the 10-year Treasury jumped to 5.10% from 4.96% late Tuesday, which is a considerable move for the bond market. High yields undercut prices for stocks and other investments, while also slowing the economy by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money. Wednesday's jump briefly sent the 10-year yield near 5.14%, back to where it was in 2007 before the global financial crisis caused yields to crater. Yields have been climbing since bottoming out in the COVID pandemic, and they've accelerated recently because of worries about high inflation, the US government's heavy debt and other concerns. Worries about inflation got a jolt Wednesday morning after a preliminary report suggested growth in US business activity surged to its strongest level in more than five years. That's an encouraging signal, to be sure, but it indicates the economy may have plenty of fuel for more inflation. In stock markets elsewhere, indices slipped across much of Europe and Asia. Stock indices fell 1% in Hong Kong and 0.4% in Shanghai ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington, which is kicking off Wednesday. Back home, the KLCI lost 7.07 points or -0.4% to end at 1,676.43. title: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, construction stocks seen as key beneficiaries of Budget 2027
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday.

In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion.

It believes the higher allocation “could provide a modest boost to mass-market consumption, particularly benefitting companies exposed to lower- and middle-income households”.

Among the counters poised to benefit are 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (KL:99SMART), Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd (KL:ECOSHOP) and MR DIY Group (M) Bhd (KL:MRDIY), as well as food and beverage manufacturers Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:NESTLE), Life Water Bhd (KL:LWSABAH) and QL Resources Bhd (KL:QL).

CIMB Securities also expects gross development expenditure to rise to RM83 billion in 2027, with higher spending on water infrastructure among the potential areas of focus.

Among the counters it sees as well positioned to benefit are Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM), Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT) and Insight Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB).

Healthcare sector seen supported

Separately, Maybank Investment Bank expects Budget 2027 to remain supportive of the healthcare sector.

Potential measures include tax relief for healthcare and medical insurance, support for the nationwide MediAsas rollout, continued medical-tourism incentives and greater public-private collaboration to ease congestion at public hospitals, it said.

Local pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturers may also benefit from continued government support for manufacturing, procurement, research and development, Maybank IB said.

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday.

In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion.

title: 'Govt dividend receipts up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on higher BNM, Khazanah payouts — AG’s report
body: 'Govt dividend receipts up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on higher BNM, Khazanah payouts — AG’s report KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The federal government received RM39.55 billion in dividends from its investments in 2025, up by 1.4% from RM39.01 billion a year earlier, as higher payouts from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Khazanah Nasional Bhd outweighed lower receipts from other entities. The dividends came from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in 2024. The increase was RM535.06 million compared to last year, according to the latest auditor general’s report released on Monday. Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS) paid RM32 billion, unchanged from 2024. BNM paid RM5.25 billion, up from RM2.85 billion, an increase of RM2.4 billion or 84.2%. Khazanah's dividend doubled to RM2 billion from RM1 billion. Bank Simpanan Nasional paid RM25 million, down from RM52 million. Dividends from statutory bodies rose 81.8% to RM5.28 billion, while those from companies fell 5.1% to RM34.27 billion. In all, nine companies and one statutory body paid RM7.43 billion, against RM3.98 billion in 2024, an increase of RM3.45 billion or 86.7%. Twelve companies and one statutory body paid less compared to 2024, as three companies paid the same amount in both years. Piramid Pertama Sdn Bhd, which paid RM2.73 billion in 2024, made no payment in 2025. Dividends from Prokhas Sdn Bhd fell to RM5.6 million from RM56.24 million. Three companies, Perbadanan Nasional Bhd, Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd and Malaysia Digital Economy Corp Sdn Bhd paid dividends in 2025 after paying none in 2024. title: 'Warga Palestin diculik: Waran tangkap terhadap tertuduh ketujuh
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR – Mahkamah Tinggi di sini pada Jumaat mengeluarkan waran tangkap terhadap seorang daripada lapan tertuduh dalam kes penculikan seorang lelaki warga Palestin pada 2022. Hakim, Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin mengeluarkan perintah itu terhadap Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, selepas tertuduh tidak hadir pada prosiding kes berkenaan. Ketika pengurusan kes, penjamin tertuduh memaklumkan bahawa, usaha menjejaki Muhammad Iqmal termasuk pergi ke rumahnya di kawasan ladang kelapa sawit telah dilakukan sebelum ini. “Saya pergi ke kampungnya di Tanjung Sepat, tetapi adik-beradik dia kata tidak jumpa,” katanya. Sementara itu, Timbalan Pendakwa Raya, Zaileen Nadia Zubir berkata, pihak pendakwaan juga sudah berusaha mengesan tertuduh ketujuh itu sejak 11 September lalu. Menurutnya, pihak berkuasa turut pergi ke Tanjung Sepat, Banting, Kuala Langan dan bertanyakan mengenai keberadaan tertuduh kepada bapanya. “Bapa tertuduh memberitahu lelaki berkenaan tidak balik kampung sejak Januari lalu dan pihak berkuasa masih berusaha mengesan tertuduh,” katanya. Susulan itu, Hakim, Mohd Arief Emran mengeluarkan waran tangkap terhadap Muhammad Iqmal. Mahkamah turut memerintahkan wang jaminan sebanyak RM50,000 dikembalikan kepada penjamin selepas mengambil kira usaha yang dilakukan bagi mengesan tertuduh. Dalam prosiding itu, Muhammad Iqmal diwakili peguam, Goh Cia Yee. Sebelum ini, mahkamah menetapkan perbicaraan kes berkenaan ditetapkan pada 12 hingga 15, 19 hingga 23 dan 26 hingga 29 October. Pada Oktober 2022, seramai 13 lelaki dan seorang wanita didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret di sini atas pertuduhan menculik warga Palestin, Omar Z M Albelbaisy Raeda, 35, bagi mendapatkan ganjaran berupa rahsia maklumat berkaitan perisian menggodam telefon bimbit. Mereka ialah Edy Ko’im Said, 46, Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 47, Dody Junaidi, 48, Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45, Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45, Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46, Muhammad Iqmal, Mohamad Sufian Saly, 29, Muhammad Al Hatim Mohd Fauzi, 29, Nidarahayu Zainal, 40, Raibafie Amdan, 45, Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60, Mohd Azwan Jamaludin 55, dan Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 55. Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan di Jalan Mayang, di sini, pada jam 10.40 malam 28 September 2022. Pertuduhan dibuat mengikut Seksyen 3 Akta Penculikan 1961 dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 Kanun Keseksaan yang memperuntukkan hukuman penjara antara 30 hingga 40 tahun serta sebatan, jika sabit kesalahan. Pada 20 Oktober 2023, Tengku Arif Bongsu bersama pasangan suami isteri, Nidarahayu dan Raibafie turut didakwa atas 19 pertuduhan pengubahan wang haram berjumlah lebih RM250,000. Bagi pertuduhan pertama hingga keempat, Nidarahayu didakwa melupuskan wang RM20,650.86 hasil aktiviti haram daripada akaun simpanannya di CIMB Bank ke dua akaun bank lain di CIMB Bank dan Maybank Islamic Berhad di Cawangan Taman Maluri, antara 15 September hingga 3 Oktober 2022. Dia turut berdepan 13 pertuduhan memindahkan wang RM184,985.46 ke dalam akaun empat syarikat dan lapan individu, juga hasil aktiviti haram, antara 15 September hingga 2 Oktober tahun sama. Raibafie dan Tengku Arif Bongsu masing-masing didakwa menerima RM30,350 dan RM25,000 daripada dua akaun bank milik Nidarahayu serta sebuah syarikat, di CIMB Bank Cawangan Jalan Bukit Bintang dan Taman Mutiara, Cheras antara 29 September hingga 2 Oktober 2022. Pertuduhan dibuat mengikut Seksyen 4(1)(b) Akta Pencegahan Pengubahan Wang Haram, Pencegahan Pembiayaan Keganasan dan Hasil daripada Aktiviti Haram 2001 yang membawa hukuman penjara maksimum 15 tahun dan denda lima kali ganda nilai aktiviti haram atau RM5 juta, yang mana lebih tinggi, jika sabit kesalahan. Pada 10 Julai 2025, enam lelaki dihukum penjara lima tahun oleh Mahkamah Tinggi di sini selepas mengaku bersalah atas pertuduhan pilihan melarikan dan mengurung seorang lelaki Palestin itu. Hakim, K Muniandy yang kini hakim Mahkamah Rayuan di Putrajaya, menjatuhkan hukuman itu terhadap Mohamad Norakmal, Mohd Azwan, Dody, Mohamad Sufian, Tengku Hazarul Ismail dan Muhammad Al Hatim. Mengikut pertuduhan, mereka didakwa melarikan mangsa secara paksa terhadap lelaki Palestine sama dengan dikurung secara salah dan rahsia di Jalan Mayang, Dang Wangi di sini pada jam 10.40 malam, 28 September 2022. Kesemua tertuduh didakwa mengikut Seksyen 365 Kanun Keseksaan dan dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 akta sama yang membawa hukuman penjara sehingga tujuh tahun dan boleh dikenakan denda. Mengikut fakta kes, mangsa dilarikan dan dikurung di sebuah chalet di Hulu Langat. Serbuan polis yang dilakukan berdasarkan maklumat berjaya menyelamatkan mangsa yang ketika itu berada dalam keadaan tangan dan kaki diikat dengan pengikat kabel.

title: 'Maybank, Asian Banking School Explore Certification Programme For Wealth Advisory
body: 'Maybank and the Asian Banking School (ABS) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to explore the development of a professional certification framework for wealth advisory in Malaysia, aimed at introducing an industry-recognised benchmark for advisory capability.  The proposed certification framework, to be known as the ABS Wealth Advisory & Management Certification Programme, is intended to establish competency standards specifically for wealth advisory professionals in banking. Upon its launch, it will be Malaysia’s first industry-wide professional certification framework dedicated to wealth advisory.  The parties noted that as wealth management needs grow more complex, clients increasingly require advice that connects different aspects of their financial lives. This initiative they added aims to establish a consistent benchmark for the advisory capabilities required to serve clients holistically.  Maybank will serve as the Founding Industry Partner, contributing insights and its experience in developing wealth talent, while ABS will bring its expertise in professional banking development and certification. ABS will retain independence over the standards and how they are assessed and certified.  “This collaboration with the Asian Banking School allows us to contribute that experience beyond our organisation, to raise professional standards for wealth advisory in Malaysia, with the opportunity to extend elements of the programme across the region over time,” said Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, Group CEO, Community Financial Services, Maybank.  The programme’s first intake is expected in the second half of 2027, and Maybank intends to incorporate the programme into Maybank Wealth Academy, connecting it with structured learning and career development through practical workplace application. The parties will also explore opportunities to extend relevant certification pathways to wealth professionals across the region.

title: 'MGS sell-off set to hit RHB's Q3 earnings: HLIB
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd's near-term earnings are likely to come under pressure from higher Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields, said Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research.   Analyst Raymond Ng said the recent spike in MGS yields would likely hurt trading income in the third quarter of financial year 2026 (Q3 FY26), with limited time left in the quarter for a recovery.   He said stronger contributions from wealth management, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, broking and loan-related fees should provide some cushion but are unlikely to fully offset the trading income weakness.

title: 'Bursa retreats after opening higher on selling pressure
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday but retreated shortly after, weighed down by selling activity in selected heavyweight counters, led by financial services and industrial products and services. At 9.11am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 3.68 points to 1,629.67 from Tuesday’s close of 1,633.35. The index opened 0.19 points higher at 1,633.54. However, on the broader market, gainers outpaced decliners 221 to 180, with 306 counters unchanged, 2,083 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 327.37 million units worth RM150.56 million. Hong Leong Bank eased 10 sen to RM21.98, CIMB slid 15 sen to RM7.55, and Press Metal Aluminium fell six sen to RM7.13. These three counters collectively pulled down the composite index by a combined 7.23 points. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng noted that Wall Street maintained its positive momentum overnight, with the S&P 500 testing an intra-day record high underpinned by a tech-inspired rally. “This is despite the US 10-year yield remaining elevated at 5.286% while Brent stayed above the US$100 per barrel mark. Over in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index maintained its uptrend, underpinned by renewed interest in tech-related stocks as sentiment recovered amid the steadying crude oil prices,” he told Bernama. Back home, Thong said he is anticipating bargain-hunting activities to emerge, although any upside may be hampered by selling from foreign funds following the FBM KLCI’s mildly positive close yesterday. “In view of this, we expect the index to continue consolidating within the 1,630-1,640 range today,” he added. Among other heavyweights, AMMB slipped five sen to RM6.42, Petronas Gas erased eight sen to RM17.20, and Mr D.I.Y. edged down one sen to RM1.24. IHH Healthcare added three sen to RM7.94, and Maybank gained two sen to RM9.99. In active trade, Top Glove gained 5.5 sen to 93 sen, and Supermax added 2.5 sen to 48.5 sen, while Zetrix AI and Ni Hsin inched down half a sen each to 8.5 sen and 37 sen, respectively. Metronic Global was flat at half a sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries jumped 62 sen to RM45.58, Nestle gained 32 sen to RM91.58, and Mi Technovation rallied 19 sen to RM6.19. Critical Holdings bounced 12 sen to RM2.81, and Hengyuan Refining Company gained nine sen to RM3.55. Among the top losers, TMK Chemical cut eight sen to RM2.61, and Pekat fell five sen to RM2.91, while Stratus Global and Solarvest slipped four sen each to RM3.09 and RM4.33, respectively. Malaysia Smelting shrank three sen to RM1.65. title: 'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan 5.00 sen seunit, pemegang unit terima RM236.41 juta bagi FY2026 | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan jumlah agihan pendapatan termasuk bonus sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 September 2026 (FY2026), dengan keseluruhan pembayaran RM236.41 juta yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Berhad (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Berhad (PHBAM), mengumumkan agihan pendapatan akhir sebanyak 2.10 sen seunit bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 September 2026, menurut kenyataan PHB bersama hari ini. PHB selaku penaja dana turut mengisytiharkan edaran bonus sebanyak 0.40 sen seunit, menjadikan jumlah agihan bagi tempoh tersebut sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit. Bonus itu diberikan kepada pegangan sehingga satu juta unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Selepas mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit yang diumumkan pada April 2026, jumlah agihan bagi FY2026 mencapai 5.00 sen seunit. Agihan akhir itu membabitkan pembayaran RM120.13 juta. Agihan pendapatan tersebut adalah bersih selepas cukai dan zakat, membolehkan pemegang unit menerima jumlah penuh tanpa sebarang potongan atau tanggungan tambahan. Pembayaran akan dibuat dalam bentuk unit AHB dan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Oktober 2026. Pengarah Urusan Kumpulan PHB, Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan bagi FY2026 mencerminkan ketahanan berterusan AHB dan kekuatan portfolio hartanahnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset serta pelaburan yang berdisiplin. “Prestasi AHB pada tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit,” katanya. Beliau berkata PHB terus memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera melalui pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan dinamik dan pengoptimuman portfolio bagi memastikan pertumbuhan mampan serta penciptaan nilai jangka panjang. Menurut Mazuki, penawaran tambahan sebanyak 400 juta unit AHB yang diumumkan baru-baru ini memperluas peluang kepada lebih ramai pelabur Bumiputera untuk mengambil bahagian dalam pelaburan hartanah komersial utama. Beliau berkata AHB akan terus menyokong pembentukan kekayaan jangka panjang Bumiputera dan menjana nilai mampan kepada pemegang unit. Komitmen itu selaras dengan aspirasi Pelan Transformasi Ekonomi Bumiputera 2035 (PUTERA35) untuk memperkukuh penyertaan ekonomi, pemilikan dan pembentukan kekayaan Bumiputera. Agihan dilaburkan semula secara automatik Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM, Zulkifli Ishak berkata pihaknya kekal komited menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab supaya dana itu terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. Agihan pendapatan akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, menambah pegangan unit pelabur dan membolehkan mereka berpotensi menikmati manfaat pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. Unit tambahan akan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun tanpa memerlukan permohonan berasingan. Pelabur Bumiputera boleh melanggan AHB pada harga tetap RM1.00 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. Langganan boleh dibuat di cawangan pengedar sah AHB seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), AmBank Berhad, AmBank Islamic Berhad, Bank Islam Malaysia Berhad dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Berhad. Sejak ditubuhkan pada 2010, AHB telah mengagihkan sejumlah RM2.7 bilion pendapatan kepada pemegang unit Bumiputera.

title: '[VIDEO] ‘Tidak Sabar Hadiri Pernikahan Kami’ – Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah Kenang Pertemuan Terakhir Dengan Allahyarham Tun Hasmah
body: 'Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq dan bakal isteri, Bella Astillah menyifatkan pertemuan bersama Allahyarham Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali selama dua jam pada tiga hari lalu sebagai momen yang sangat bermakna buat mereka. Artikel Berkaitan: [VIDEO] ‘Baru Hendak Tulis Muka Surat Pertama’ – Syed Saddiq & Bella Astillah Akui Tak Layak Disamakan Dengan Tun M & Allahyarhamah Tun Hasmah Artikel Berkaitan: Bella Astillah Kongsi Keadaan Syed Saddiq – ‘Dia Tak Mampu Teruskan Apa Yang Telah Dirancang Hari Ini’ Pertemuan akhir Ketika ditemui , Saddiq atau nama penuhnya, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman berkata pada pertemuan itu Allahyarham berkongsi rasa tidak sabar untuk menghadiri pernikahan mereka selain kelihatan ceria dan gembira. Menurutnya, momen tersebut menjadi salah satu kenangan manis yang tidak akan dilupakan bersama tokoh yang disayangi ramai itu. Kalau tidak silap, kami bertemu tiga hari sebelum Allahyarhamah meninggalkan kita semua. Ketika pertemuan itu, Allahyarhamah berada dalam keadaan sangat ceria. Beliau juga berkongsi rasa tidak sabar untuk menghadiri majlis pernikahan kami. Saddiq berkata demikian pada sidang media Walimatulurus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq di Kuala Lumpur pada Jumaat. Berkongsi lanjut, Saddiq berkata, Allahyarham banyak menitipkan nasihat kepadanya terutama mengenai kehidupan selepas berkahwin. Banyak nasihat yang disampaikan, khususnya mengenai pentingnya kompromi dalam rumah tangga. Perkahwinan bukan sekadar soal cinta semata-mata, tetapi mengenai toleransi dan bagaimana kita bijak berkompromi, melalui ujian serta menangani isu seperti perasaan cemburu dalam hubungan. Ketika ditanya sama ada dia melihat sebarang perubahan pada Allahyarham ketika pertemuan terakhir mereka, Saddiq berkata, Allahyarham masih sempat bergurau dan berkongsi kisah-kisah lama, termasuk kisah cintanya bersama Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. Allahyarham masih boleh bergurau dan mengingati perkara yang berlaku 50 atau 60 tahun lalu, termasuk kisah cintanya bersama Tun Dr. Mahathir. Manakala, Bella turut berkongsi antara pesanan Allahyarham supaya menjadi seorang wanita yang kuat, selain mengingatkan bahawa kehidupan sebagai isteri kepada seorang ahli politik bukanlah mudah. Allahyarham berpesan supaya saya menjadi seorang wanita yang kuat, sentiasa berada di sisi suami serta menjadi wanita yang lembut tetapi pada masa sama mempunyai kekuatan. Ada juga nasihat yang boleh saya kongsikan dan ada yang saya memilih untuk simpan kerana menghormati Allahyarham. Beliau memberitahu bahawa perjalanan sebagai isteri kepada seorang ahli politik bukan sesuatu yang mudah. Namun, selagi ada kepercayaan dalam hubungan, insya-Allah rumah tangga akan berkekalan. Toleransi dan rasa hormat terhadap pasangan juga sangat penting. Dalam perkembangan lain, Saddiq dan Bella akan disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada sebuah majlis di Kuala Lumpur pada 10 Oktober depan. Majlis pernikahan mereka akan berlangsung di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank dengan konsep serba putih disulami elemen Arab atau Islamik atas permintaan keluarga. title: 'From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s approach of leveraging sports as a platform for diplomacy, economic activity and nation branding is helping position Malaysia back on the global sporting stage, according to an analyst. Global Peace Institute, London senior fellow Prof Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said Malaysia had, in recent months, demonstrated how global sporting events could be used not only to entertain the public but also to strengthen international relationships, generate economic activity and create a sense of shared national excitement. “Sport is often treated as entertainment, but for governments it can also be diplomacy, economic policy and nation branding rolled into one,” he said in a statement today. Formula 1’s return to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years and Malaysia’s efforts to ensure access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup broadcasts demonstrated how sports could be used to strengthen the country’s international engagement. Mohd Mizan said Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2–4 demonstrated the international dimension of sports diplomacy, after the Bahrain Grand Prix could not proceed at its original venue due to geopolitical conditions in West Asia. He said the arrangement went beyond a commercial transaction involving a racetrack, as it was facilitated within the wider relationship between Malaysia and Bahrain, with the support of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa also travelled to Malaysia and met Anwar during the race weekend. Mohd Mizan said Anwar’s attendance at the qualifying session at Sepang, visit to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas pit and participation in a reception hosted by Prince Salman further demonstrated how the sporting event created a platform for diplomatic engagement. “Sport had therefore created a diplomatic platform. Leaders met, bilateral relations were reinforced and Malaysia was placed before a global audience not through a formal summit but through one of the world’s most recognisable sporting spectacles,” he said. Mohd Mizan said the public response to F1’s return was equally significant, with around 95,000 three-day tickets sold by late September and SIC expecting sales to reach about 100,000, which would be the highest ticket sales recorded for races held at the circuit. He said the event also generated significant economic spillovers, with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture estimating that it could draw around 300,000 tourists, including about 50,000 international visitors, while Hong Leong Bank Research projected an economic impact of approximately RM1.3 billion through sports tourism and foreign visitor spending. “Formula 1 does not benefit only the circuit. Visitors spend on hotels, restaurants, transport, retail and tourism. Television coverage carries images of Malaysia around the world. International teams, sponsors, journalists and corporate leaders arrive in the country,” he said. Turning to football, Mohd Mizan said the government’s decision to ensure Malaysians had access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup represented the domestic dimension of sports diplomacy, with football remaining one of the country’s most widely followed sports. RTM and Unifi TV were appointed official broadcasters, with all 104 matches made available through the participating platforms, while the government allocated RM26.2 million to secure the broadcasting rights and strategic cooperation with the private sector helped widen access and distribution, he said. Mohd Mizan also said that access to the World Cup through legitimate and accessible channels represented a form of social inclusion, as major sporting events could create shared experiences cutting across race, age, geography and income. “Few things temporarily dissolve Malaysia’s normal social divisions as effectively as sport. During major football tournaments, mamak restaurants, living rooms, community halls and public viewing areas become shared national spaces,” he said. He said Anwar’s approach showed that diplomacy today operated far beyond formal conference rooms, with Malaysia using F1 and Fifa to bring the world closer to its people while strengthening its position on the global sporting stage. “Sometimes diplomacy happens through bilateral negotiations. Sometimes it happens through football and sometimes, at 300 kilometres per hour around Sepang,” he said. — Bernama

Visitors spend on hotels, restaurants, transport, retail and tourism. Television coverage carries images of Malaysia around the world. International teams, sponsors, journalists and corporate leaders arrive in the country,” he said. Turning to football, Mohd Mizan said the government’s decision to ensure Malaysians had access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup represented the domestic dimension of sports diplomacy, with football remaining one of the country’s most widely followed sports. RTM and Unifi TV were appointed official broadcasters, with all 104 matches made available through the participating platforms, while the government allocated RM26.2 million to secure the broadcasting rights and strategic cooperation with the private sector helped widen access and distribution, he said. Mohd Mizan also said that access to the World Cup through legitimate and accessible channels represented a form of social inclusion, as major sporting events could create shared experiences cutting across race, age, geography and income. “Few things temporarily dissolve Malaysia’s normal social divisions as effectively as sport. During major football tournaments, mamak restaurants, living rooms, community halls and public viewing areas become shared national spaces,” he said. He said Anwar’s approach showed that diplomacy today operated far beyond formal conference rooms, with Malaysia using F1 and Fifa to bring the world closer to its people while strengthening its position on the global sporting stage. “Sometimes diplomacy happens through bilateral negotiations. Sometimes it happens through football and sometimes, at 300 kilometres per hour around Sepang,” he said. — Bernama

title: 'Maybank Turned Its Cash Back Card Perks Into A Playground At Mid Valley
body: 'Last week, we dropped by Mid Valley Megamall to check out the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum showcase. title: 'Foreign selling on Bursa extends to second week, TNB, Maybank and RHB lead outflows
body: 'FOREIGN institutions remained net sellers of Malaysian equities for a second consecutive week, recording RM799.9 million in net outflows for the week ended Oct 2, with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) and RHB Bank Bhd bearing the brunt of the selling.   According to MBSB Research’s weekly fund flow report released today, foreign institutions were net sellers on all five trading days, with the largest outflow recorded on Wednesday at RM228.4 million.   Stock-level data showed TNB recorded the largest net foreign outflow at RM278.1 million, followed by Maybank at RM159.3 million and RHB Bank at RM135.9 million.

title: 'Hong Leong Bank, PetChem Lead Bursa Losers As ViTrox Tops Gainers
body: 'Hong Leong Bank Bhd and Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PetChem) led Bursa Malaysia’s biggest decliners, while ViTrox Corp Bhd emerged as the top gainer as market breadth remained subdued.  Hong Leong Bank shed 36 sen, or 1.5%, to close at RM23.10, making it the day’s biggest loser by absolute price movement. PetChem followed closely, sliding 34 sen, or 6.5%, to RM4.86 on 14.15 million shares.  Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd declined 26 sen to RM22.86, while Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd dropped 22 sen to RM18.56.  Bursa Malaysia Bhd rounded out the five biggest losers, falling 18 sen to RM8.07.  Selling pressure outweighed buying interest across the broader market, with 673 decliners against 465 gainers. Another 548 counters were unchanged, 1,170 untraded and 13 suspended.  On the upside, automated test equipment maker ViTrox led gainers with a 48-sen, or 5.3%, jump to RM9.58 on 4.65 million shares.  Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd advanced 40 sen to RM40.10, while Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd climbed 36 sen to RM12.74.  Nestlé (M) Bhd gained 34 sen to RM90.52, while Petronas Dagangan Bhd added 30 sen to RM21.08.  Trading activity strengthened, with market turnover rising to 3.6 billion units worth RM3.25 billion compared to 3.34 billion units valued at RM3.25 billion on Sept 15.

title: 'IOI Properties Gets Bursa Securities Approval for RM7.58b REIT Listing
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) said Bursa Malaysia Securities has approved the listing of its proposed RM7.58 billion IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG REIT) on the Main Market. In a filing on Thursday, the property developer said Bursa Malaysia Securities had, via a letter dated Sept 30, approved the admission of IOIPG REIT to the Official List of Bursa Securities, and the listing and quotation of its 5.5 billion units under the REITs sector. Bursa Malaysia Securities also approved the listing and quotation of up to 300 million new units to be issued as payment of management fees to IOI REIT Management Sdn Bhd — the REIT’s manager. The approval marks another step forward for the listing of IOIPG REIT. IOI Properties received approval from the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) last month for listing of the trust that will house RM7.58 billion worth of retail, office and hotel assets. The target was to complete the listing before the year ends. Other assets include the IOI City Towers and PFCC Towers, as well as six hotels — Putrajaya Marriott Hotel, Le’ Meridien Putrajaya, Moxy Putrajaya, Four Points by Sheraton Puchong, W Kuala Lumpur and Courtyard by Marriott Penang. It also plans to pay out at least 90% of its distributable income on a quarterly basis. The RM7.58 billion acquisition will be satisfied through the issuance of 5.5 billion units at 90 sen each, alongside RM2.65 billion in cash to be funded through sukuk issuance. As part of the proposed offering, 715.61 million units will be offered under the retail portion, including 550.61 million units through a restricted offer for sale to existing IOI Properties shareholders. Eligible shareholders will be entitled to one REIT unit for every ten IOI Properties shares held on an entitlement date to be announced later. Another 55 million units will be allocated to eligible persons, while 110 million units will be made available to the Malaysian public. The institutional offering, meanwhile, will comprise up to 1.48 billion units, including 687.5 million units for Bumiputera investors approved by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti), with up to 796.89 million units allocated to other Malaysian and foreign institutional and selected investors. On Sept 14, the company revised the planned use of proceeds. It cut the allocation for debt repayment to RM1.53 billion, or 32.9%, from RM3.04 billion, or 65.6%. It raised the allocation for project development, property investment and related activities to RM3.07 billion, or 66%, from RM1.55 billion, or 33.6%. Total proceeds were put at RM4.66 billion, assuming the over-allotment option is not exercised, compared with RM4.62 billion previously. Shares of IOI Properties were down by five sen or 1.5% to RM3.41 at Thursday’s trading day break, giving it a market value of RM18.8 billion. Year to date, its shares have increased by 28.68%. title: 'High Court issues arrest warrant for accused in Palestinian abduction case
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today issued an arrest warrant for an accused in the 2022 abduction of a Palestinian man after he failed to appear for pre-trial case management. Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin issued the warrant against Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, the seventh of eight accused, after allowing an application by deputy public prosecutor Zaileen Nadia Zubir. During the proceedings, Zaileen told the court that Iqmal had been uncontactable since Sept 11 and that his bailor had lodged a police report. The judge then asked the bailor to explain the situation. She told the court that she had gone to Iqmal's house to look for him but was unable to locate him. "I also went to his village in Tanjung Sepat, Kuala Langat, in Selangor and even searched a nearby oil palm plantation. "However, even his siblings did not know his whereabouts. "That prompted me to lodge a police report on his disappearance," she said. Zaileen also said police had gone to Tanjung Sepat to interview Iqmal's parents about his whereabouts. "Police investigations showed that his father said his son had not returned to the village since January. Efforts to trace him are still ongoing," she said. In addition to issuing the arrest warrant, Arief Emran ordered the RM50,000 bail to be returned to the bailor after hearing that she had made efforts to locate Iqmal. Iqmal was represented by lawyer Goh Cia Yee. The other seven accused, who are out on bail, were present in court today. They are Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45; Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45; Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46; Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60; Nidarahayu Zainal, 40; Raibafie Amdan, 45; and Edy Ko'im Said, 46. The court had previously fixed the trial for Oct 12 to 15, Oct 19 to 23, and Oct 26 to 29. In October 2022, 13 men and a woman were charged at the magistrate's court here with abducting Palestinian Omar ZM Albelbaisy Raeda, 35, allegedly to obtain a reward in the form of information relating to software used to hack mobile phones. They were Edy Ko'im, 45; Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 46; Dody Junaidi, 47; Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 44; Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 44; Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 45; Muhammad Iqmal, 30; Mohamad Sufian Saly, 28; Muhammad Al Hatim; Nidarahayu Zainal, 39; Raibafie Amdan, 44; Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 59; Mohd Azwan Jamaludin, 42; and Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 54. They were charged with committing the offence at Jalan Mayang here about 10.40pm on Sept 28, 2022. The charge was framed under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between 30 and 40 years and whipping upon conviction. On Oct 20, 2023, Tengku Arif Bongsu, together with married couple Nidarahayu and Raibafie, were also charged with 19 counts of money laundering involving more than RM250,000. For the first to fourth charges, Nidarahayu was accused of disposing of RM20,650.86 in proceeds from unlawful activity from her savings account at CIMB Bank into two other bank accounts at CIMB Bank and Maybank Islamic Bhd's Taman Maluri branch between Sept 15 and Oct 3, 2022. She also faced 13 charges of transferring RM184,985.46 into the accounts of four companies and eight individuals, also allegedly proceeds from unlawful activity, between Sept 15 and Oct 2 that year. Raibafie and Tengku Arif Bongsu were respectively charged with receiving RM30,350 and RM25,000 from two bank accounts belonging to Nidarahayu and a company at CIMB Bank's Jalan Bukit Bintang and Taman Mutiara, Cheras branches between Sept 29 and Oct 2, 2022. The charges were framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, which carries a maximum 15-year jail term and a fine of five times the value of the unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher, upon conviction. On July 10, 2025, six men were sentenced to five years in jail by the High Court here after pleading guilty to an alternative charge of forcibly taking and confining the victim. Judge K. Muniandy, who is now a Court of Appeal judge, imposed the sentence on Mohamad Norakmal, Mohd Azwan, Dody, Mohamad Sufian, Tengku Hazarul Ismail and Muhammad Al Hatim. According to the charge, they were accused of forcibly taking the victim and wrongfully and secretly confining him at Jalan Mayang, Dang Wangi, here, at 10.40pm on Sept 28, 2022. All six were charged under Section 365 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which carries a jail term of up to seven years and a fine. According to the facts of the case, the victim was abducted and confined at a chalet in Hulu Langat. A police raid, carried out based on information received, led to the victim's rescue. He was found with his hands and legs tied with cable ties.

title: 'Insider Moves: Cuscapi Bhd, Zetrix AI Bhd, Excel Force MSC Bhd, Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd, MyMBN Bhd, RHB Bank Bhd, Gamuda Bhd
body: 'Insider Moves: Cuscapi Bhd, Zetrix AI Bhd, Excel Force MSC Bhd, Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd, MyMBN Bhd, RHB Bank Bhd, Gamuda Bhd This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 Notable filings During the week of Sept 7 to 11, notable changes in shareholding at Bursa Malaysia-listed companies included those at IT company Cuscapi Bhd (KL:CUSCAPI), where Datin Seri Lee Lan Moi and Jessie Lim Me Xian ceased to be substantial shareholders. According to Bursa filings, Lee hived off 67.5 million shares or a 7.14% stake in an off-market deal, while Lim sold 58.5 million shares via a separate off-market transaction. Both transactions took place on Sept 3. Separately, Cuscapi’s largest shareholder, Wong Thean Soon, saw his stake cut from 28.07% to 13.43%, as the share price tumbled from nine sen at end-August to close at six sen last Thursday, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM56.7 million. Filings showed that the bulk of the shares Wong disposed of had been pledged, and were likely forced sold as the share price fell. There have also been a slew of boardroom changes at Cuscapi. Following the transactions, Tan Boon Seng emerged as a substantial shareholder of Cuscapi after acquiring 100.33 million shares or a 10.62% stake on Sept 11. Wong had emerged as a substantial shareholder of Cuscapi in March 2022, with a 7.73% stake. Apart from his shares in Cuscapi, Wong’s shares in his flagship Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) and Excel Force MSC Bhd (KL:EFORCE) were also likely forced sold after their market prices plummeted. During the week in review, Wong’s direct stake in Zetrix AI was slashed by 571.36 million shares to 525.27 million shares, or a 6.67% stake, while his indirect interest held via Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd was substantially reduced after 632.05 million shares were sold, bringing the firm’s stake in Zetrix AI down to 5.56% or 438.17 million shares. Wong now has 12.23% equity interest in Zetrix AI, in stark contrast to the 29.25% he held in early April this year. Meanwhile, his stake in Excel Force was reduced to 14.01% or 85.42 million shares after 104.21 million shares were disposed of. At Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd (KL:FPI), privately held OS Capital Sdn Bhd emerged as a substantial shareholder of the audio products manufacturer after acquiring 53.45 million shares or 20.01% equity interest on Sept 10. OS Capital is the vehicle of Gan Chun Hui, who also has a direct stake of 0.36% or 955,500 shares in Formosa Prosonic. The shares acquired by Gan could have come from Taiwanese managing director Shih Chao Yuan, who sold 66.78 million shares or a 24.88% stake on Sept 10 and ceased to be a substantial shareholder. Another substantial shareholder of Formosa Prosonic, Singaporean Wu Swee Ngor, sold 44.18 million shares or a 16.46% stake in the company. Formosa Prosonic’s share price closed at RM1.08 last Thursday, giving the company a market value of RM288.5 million. Meanwhile, privately held Gentle Rainbow Sdn Bhd — the private vehicle of Fong Hew Chung and Hew Hong Thee — ceased to be a substantial shareholder of edible bird’s nest processor MyMBN Bhd (KL:MBN) after disposing of 28.8 million shares or a 7.46% stake in the company during the week in review. While Fong ceased to be a substantial shareholder, Hew still has 129.6 million shares, or 33.58% equity interest, in MyMBN. Hew is the mother of Lavernt Chen Vun Wo, executive director and CEO of MyMBN. In early September, MyMBN chairman Liw Chong Liong sold 43.2 million shares or an 11.19% stake in the company, halving his shareholding. It is not clear who acquired those shares. From eight sen at end-June, MyMBN’s share price had doubled to 17 sen in the first week of September, before tapering off and finishing at 14.5 sen last Thursday, valuing the company at RM56 million. Notable movements Bursa filings during the week in review showed the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) accumulating shares in RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK). The provident fund acquired another 31.46 million shares to bring its equity interest to 35.47% or 1.55 billion shares. At end-June, it held 1.51 billion shares or a 34.54% stake in RHB. RHB’s share price closed at a multi-year high of RM8.88 on Aug 10, having gained 11% since early April. However, it had since eased 12.05% from its high to close at RM7.81 last Thursday, giving the banking group a market capitalisation of RM34.09 billion. Bourse filings also showed that EPF continued to accumulate Gamuda Bhd’s (KL:GAMUDA) shares and emerged as a net buyer during the week in review, having mopped up 20.92 million shares to bring its equity interest to 21.93% or 1.32 billion shares. In early July, the provident fund held a 20.83% stake or 1.24 billion shares in the construction giant. Gamuda’s share price closed at RM4.74 last Thursday, having gained about 17% since early July. This gave the group a market capitalisation of RM28.64 billion. Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'Ex-secretary to PM's graft case: Temporary passport release for Shamsul Iskandar
body: 'Ex-secretary to PM's graft case: Temporary passport release for Shamsul Iskandar KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, a former senior political secretary to the prime minister, has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month. The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption. According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties. He said he intends to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11. “Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities. “Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the Madani principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit. Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14. He said the summit aims to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices. Shamsul Iskandar also said he plans to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December. During Monday's proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport. He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month. Deputy public prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online. However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release. Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective from Monday, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16. The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249 respectively, from Tei for the same purpose. The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024. In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei's company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction. title: 'BNM: Banks Working Towards Fraud Alert Before Transaction Is Completed
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Malaysian banks are working towards introducing fraud alert capabilities that can flag potential risks before a transaction is completed. A pilot test involving selected banks is targeted for the first half of 2027 ahead of wider implementation, Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said in his speech text for a conference on financial crime and counter terrorism financing on Tuesday. “These alerts will prompt customers to pause, think and verify before proceeding,” he said. Fraudulent transactions and scams are a major problem globally. In Malaysia, the financial sector has prevented some RM1.9 billion in attempted fraudulent transactions, surpassing the RM1.2 billion prevented during the whole of 2025, according to the central bank’s data. More than 1,600 suspicious accounts, many of which were subsequently assessed as presenting mule-related risks, were flagged to-date by Malaysia’s digital payment backbone PayNet. The planned fraud alerts may introduce “additional friction for customers,” Abdul Rasheed acknowledged. “However, these measures are necessary to strike an appropriate balance between offering convenience and protecting customers from fraud, particularly authorised scams,” he stressed. title: 'Maybank completes RM2.5bil AT1 sukuk mudharabah issuance
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively. The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033. Meanwhile, the RM650 million tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036. "The relevant reset distribution rates for the three tranches are based on the prevailing five-year, seven-year and 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rates, respectively, plus their respective initial spreads for fixed rates of 0.98 per cent, 0.97 per cent and 0.98 per cent per annum," said Maybank. The proceeds would be used for shariah-compliant purposes, including investments in ringgit- and foreign currency-denominated Islamic financial instruments approved by Bank Negara Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council or the Securities Commission Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council. It would also be used to fund the Islamic business activities of Maybank's subsidiaries and overseas branches, as well as other shariah-compliant business activities, said Maybank. The returns from the investments would be used for the periodic distributions of the AT1 sukuk mudharabah, which are payable semi-annually. The sukuk has been assigned an AA3 rating by RAM Rating Services Bhd.

title: 'Hong Leong Bank declares 80 sen final dividend
body: 'by ANN ZAINUDDIN   HONG Leong Bank Bhd has declared a final single-tier dividend of 80 sen per share for the financial year ended June 30, 2026.   In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the group said the dividend will be payable on Oct 21, 2026.    The ex-date for the dividend is set for Oct 7, while the entitlement date falls on Oct 8 at 5pm.   Shareholders whose securities are transferred into their central depository system (CDS) accounts before 4:30pm on the entitlement date will qualify for the payout.   At market close, Hong Leong Bank’s share price declined 0.77% or 18 sen to RM23.20, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM50.29 billion.

body: 'SHAH ALAM (Sept 30): Genneva Gold Sdn Bhd, the company behind a massive gold investment scam, has been wound up by the High Court here, which could see victims recouping their losses.  In her brief judgment on Wednesday, Justice Wan Fadhilah Nor Wan Idris found that the company, which had been convicted for unlawful deposit-taking, had lost its foundation as it had ceased operations for many years and lacked the licences and permits to resume its original business.  The court also noted the deficiencies in its records and that the company did not have a functioning board of directors.  The court granted the winding-up order and confirmed interim liquidator Wong Weng Foo to his role in dissolving the firm.  Ng Wan Yee, who holds a major stake of 750,000 shares in the company, had moved to wind up the company in August 2024, to prevent other company directors from removing more than RM21 million in released company assets.  The move follows a Sessions Court order on June 28, 2024, that revoked seizure orders under anti-money laundering laws on millions of ringgit and approximately 28.3kg of gold bars.  In her petition, Wan Yee said there was a "high likelihood" that functional directors or other relevant parties might dissipate these assets for personal benefit rather than settling claims of thousands of investors.  She claimed that some directors had already attempted to "siphon monies" under the guise of paying professional fees.  An opposing creditor, Liew Chio Chuan, a 25% shareholder of Genneva, had challenged the appointment of Wong, arguing there was "material non-disclosure" by Wan Yee and that there was "no real danger" of assets being lost before a formal hearing before the court.  Central to the dispute was the movement of funds just days before the petition was filed. title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM1.6 bilion saham di Bursa Malaysia pada September 2026 - CGS International | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 6 Okt - Pelabur asing kekal sebagai penjual bersih ekuiti Malaysia pada September 2026 dengan aliran keluar bersih RM1.6 bilion, susut 17.1% berbanding RM2 bilion pada Ogos, menurut CGS International. Aktiviti dagangan kasar meningkat bagi kedua-dua belian dan jualan sepanjang bulan itu, namun pembelian asing meningkat lebih pantas sebanyak 12.1% bulan ke bulan kepada RM22.1 bilion berbanding kenaikan 9.5% dalam jualan kepada RM23.7 bilion. Bagaimanapun, tekanan jualan semakin meningkat menjelang akhir September apabila aliran keluar bersih terkumpul pelabur asing melebihi RM1 bilion antara 23 hingga 30 September. Peningkatan jualan pada penghujung bulan itu berlaku ketika Dewan Undangan Negeri Melaka dibubarkan. Perkembangan itu menjadikan jualan bersih terkumpul pelabur asing sebanyak RM6.5 bilion bagi sembilan bulan pertama 2026. Jumlah aliran keluar sejak 2024 pula mencecah RM33.1 bilion, manakala pegangan asing dalam ekuiti Malaysia susut ke satu lagi paras terendah baharu sebanyak 17.8% pada September. Pegangan asing susut kepada 17.8% Pelabur institusi tempatan turut mengambil pendekatan lebih berhati-hati pada September apabila pembelian bersih mereka merosot mendadak kepada RM206 juta daripada RM1.6 bilion pada bulan sebelumnya. Pelabur runcit tempatan pula meningkatkan pembelian bersih kepada RM1.4 bilion daripada RM375 juta pada Ogos, paras bulanan tertinggi sejak Januari 2025. FBM KLCI merosot 4.3% pada September untuk ditutup pada 1,651 mata, sekali gus menyebabkan prestasinya sejak awal tahun bertukar negatif. Prestasi itu lebih lemah berbanding Indeks MSCI All Country Asia ex-Japan yang susut 0.7% bulan ke bulan dan Indeks MSCI Emerging Markets yang turun 1%. Pasaran global secara keseluruhannya berdepan bulan yang mencabar, dengan hanya KOSPI Korea Selatan yang meningkat 0.7% dan Nikkei Jepun naik 0.5%. Dalam kalangan pasaran MIST iaitu Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapura dan Thailand, Straits Times Index Singapura mencatat prestasi terbaik dengan penurunan 0.4%, sekali gus menamatkan kenaikan selama lima bulan berturut-turut. Tenaga dan pembinaan mengatasi kelemahan pasaran SET Index Thailand pula susut 1.8% walaupun Fitch Ratings pada 18 September menyemak semula prospek negara itu kepada “stabil” daripada negatif, dengan menyatakan peningkatan keyakinan terhadap penstabilan hutang. FBM KLCI yang merosot 4.3% dan Jakarta Composite Index Indonesia yang jatuh 6.9% merupakan dua pasaran berprestasi paling lemah dalam kalangan negara MIST. Sentimen terhadap pasaran Indonesia merosot pada pertengahan bulan susulan kebimbangan fiskal selepas kemas kini belanjawan menunjukkan defisit sebanyak Rp240.1 trilion sehingga Ogos. Kelemahan turut berlaku secara meluas di Bursa Malaysia apabila hanya empat daripada 13 indeks sektor mencatat kenaikan pada September. 3 sektor berprestasi terbaik Tiga sektor berprestasi terbaik ialah tenaga yang meningkat 8.6%, pembinaan 7.1% dan utiliti 2.9%. Tiga sektor berprestasi paling lemah pula ialah hartanah yang susut 7.5%, pengguna 6.5% dan kewangan 5.1%. Kelemahan itu turut ketara dalam kalangan konstituen FBM KLCI apabila hanya lima daripada 30 saham mencatat kenaikan. Gamuda menjadi saham berprestasi terbaik dengan kenaikan 14.9%, diikuti Telekom Malaysia sebanyak 3.8% dan YTL Power sebanyak 2.8%. IOI Properties pula mencatat kejatuhan terbesar sebanyak 14.6%, diikuti Sunway yang susut 13.8% dan RHB Bank 13.6%. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Banking, Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Gamuda Bhd, QL Resources Bhd
body: 'This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Banking POSITIVE BIMB SECURITIES RESEARCH (Sept 22): Global bond markets experienced higher yields amid tighter US monetary policy and higher-for-longer interest rates. On Sept 16, the Federal Open Market Committee raised the federal funds rate target by 25 basis points (bps) to 3.75%-4.00%. The 10-year Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yield stands at 4.15% as at Sept 21, and remains elevated by historical standards but is still below the peak of 4.57% recorded in October 2022. According to our economist’s assessment, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to hover around the 4.0% level in the near term before gradually moderating towards the 3.75%-3.90% range by year end. Current yield levels appear to reflect market expectations of close to two policy rate hikes in Malaysia. However, given our view that the Overnight Policy Rate will remain unchanged at 2.75% throughout 2026 and 2027, coupled with a contained domestic inflation outlook, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to ease from its current elevated level over time. Banks typically maintain an average securities portfolio duration of around five to six years, which is considered moderate rather than long term. As a result, their investment portfolios are generally less sensitive to interest rate movements and face lower interest rate risk compared with portfolios concentrated on longer-dated securities. The impact on fair value through other comprehensive income securities is expected to result in lower FVOCI reserves due to revaluation losses in 3Q26, as the 10-year MGS yield is likely to remain elevated in the near term. Nevertheless, the effect on ROE could be favourable, as the decline in shareholders’ funds reduces the equity base used in the ROE calculation. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) (fair value: RM11.40), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) (FV: RM8.75) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) (FV:RM8.50), which have exposure to the Singapore market, are likely to see improved net interest margins as the rise in three-month Singapore overnight rate change (SORA), in tandem with Fed rate hikes, lifts asset yields and helps mitigate fair value through profit and loss (FVTPL) mark-to-market losses in 3Q26. Banks’ funding profiles remain largely anchored by longer-tenor liabilities, including Medium Term Notes with maturities of at least two to three years, which help maintain robust Net Stable Funding Ratio positions and reduce near-term refinancing pressures. As such, banks are unlikely to rush into refinancing and are more likely to adopt a wait-and-see approach when considering the rollover of maturing papers. We do not expect deposit competition to become more aggressive from here, given that 1Q26 and 2Q26 had already witnessed intense competition, with banks offering promotional fixed deposit rates of up to 3.7%-3.8% for 10- to 12-month placements. Solarvest Holdings Bhd Target price: RM4.50 BUY AMINVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 21): We believe that Solarvest Holdings Bhd (KL:SLVEST) would benefit from the government’s CRESS Acceleration Package. Under the package, a System Access Charge (SAC) of 14 sen/kWh will be introduced. We think that the lower SAC would spur the rollout of CRESS projects, as under the previous CRESS scheme, the SAC were perceived as too high. The SAC under the previous CRESS were 20 sen/kWh for projects with battery systems and 40 sen/kWh for projects without battery systems. We reckon that battery and solar systems contracts are worth about RM3.5million/mw to RM4million/mw based on recently announced projects. There is incentive for data centres to do solar under the new CRESS. This is because the tariffs under the new CRESS package would come up to about 45 to 50 sen/kWh compared with their present electricity tariffs of 50 to 60 sen/kWh. Solarvest is bidding for 11,800mw worth of projects. Out of these, about 1,200mw are expected to come from battery projects. We have raised Solarvest’s FY2028F net profit by 13.5% and FY29F net earnings by 40.4% to account for a higher EPCC (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) order book due to the new CRESS projects. Gamuda Bhd Target price: RM5.42 BUY TA SECURITIES (Sept 22): Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), via the Gamuda-BMD joint venture, has clinched the A$624 million (RM1.8 billion) Elizabeth Drive Upgrade — Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 Package from government agency Transport for New South Wales. Based on its 50% effective interest in the JV, Gamuda is entitled to roughly RM908 million in contract value. Given that the award also comes with cost-pass-through clauses, we believe this should limit Gamuda’s execution risk and exposure to volatile material prices. Based on the management-guided PBT margin of 5%, we estimate the project could generate approximately RM45.4 million in PBT over the contract period. Looking ahead, we expect Western Sydney’s rapid development to support sustained infrastructure spending, particularly across the road network. This should provide a healthy pipeline of replenishment opportunities for Gamuda. Gamuda’s FY2027 year-to-date new job wins have reached RM10.2 billion, lifting its unbilled construction order book to RM62.5 billion. We believe Gamuda’s near-term order book replenishment prospects remain healthy, with potential wins likely to come from data centre projects from new and repeat clients in Malaysia, renewable energy projects in Australia, particularly solar EPCCs (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) works, and railway infrastructure projects in Taiwan. QL Resources Bhd Target price: RM5.10 BUY HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 23): QL Resources Bhd’s (KL:QL)’s 1QFY2027 marine products manufacturing (MPM) revenue rose 18.2% year on year while PBT jumped 51.5%, with management attributing the bulk of the circa RM30 million y-o-y earnings uplift to fishmeal driven by Peru’s lower catch quota and a temporary El Niño fishing ban. Peru, which supplies roughly a fifth of the world’s fishmeal, in August called off its main anchovy season having landed only 25% of an already reduced quota. That keeps global supply tight, and fishmeal prices in July were still running about 11% above where they averaged through QL’s 1QFY27. Grade C egg prices recovered from the low RM0.20s in April to May to RM0.33 by end-June and >RM0.40 at the farm gate by August We remain constructive on QL, given that MPM is delivering into a supply shock with further runway into FY27, and did so in a seasonally soft quarter with the stronger quarters still ahead. Clean energy under BM Greentech Bhd (KL:BMGREEN] now has a working commercial proof point inside QL’s own plant while Innofood will begin contributing from 2HFY28. Integrated livestock farming and convenience store chain segments have, in our view, both passed their respective troughs, with egg prices recovering off the April low and FamilyMart's top line turning after three quarters of decline. title: 'HLB Offers RM300 Voucher With iPhone 18 Pro Purchases
body: '15th September 2026 - 2 min read Buying an iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max with a Hong Leong Bank (HLB) Credit Card can get you RM300 in accessories vouchers at selected retailers. HLB also offers 0% Extended Payment Plan (EPP) options, depending on where you buy. The campaign runs from 12 September to 31 October 2026, or until the vouchers run out. Spend at least RM5,499 in a single receipt on an iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max at Switch, Urban Republic or Machines. The purchase must be made through HLB’s EPP. Switch and Urban Republic accept 24-, 36- and 48-month plans, while Machines accepts 24- and 36-month plans. The voucher can only be redeemed in-store and is limited to one per cardholder. There are 115 vouchers available at Switch and Urban Republic, and 80 at Machines, all on a first-come, first-served basis. The campaign also covers other Apple products. Spend at least RM5,000 in a single receipt on products such as an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch and you’ll get a RM200 accessories voucher at Switch, Urban Republic, Machines or Senheng. The EPP periods vary by retailer. Senheng accepts 24-, 36-, 48- and 60-month EPP purchases, while Machines accepts 24- and 36-month plans. There’s also a separate RM300 accessories voucher for an iPhone Duo purchase, with 50 vouchers available at Switch and Urban Republic and 20 at Machines. If you buy from Apple The Exchange TRX or the Apple Store Online, HLB offers 0% EPP for 6, 12 or 24 months. You can also trade in an existing device through Apple’s trade-in partners. Trade-in quotes are estimates, with the final value depending on the device’s condition, year and model. Any balance left after the trade-in credit can be paid with an eligible HLB Credit Card in full or through 0% EPP. The accessories vouchers aren’t stated as being available for purchases made directly from Apple. If you’re buying from one of the participating retailers specifically for the voucher, check availability before paying.
