full_text: 'EU-Malaysia trade deal: Jangan jejaskan produk perubatan mampu milik dan hak petani / Don’t put affordable medicines, farmers’ rights at risk. '[ENGLISH VERSION BELOW] Persatuan Pengguna Pulau Pinang (CAP) dan 40 pertubuhan masyarakat sivil Malaysia yang lain menggesa kerajaan Malaysia supaya menolak tuntutan hak harta intelek oleh Kesatuan Eropah (EU) yang melangkaui kewajipan Malaysia di bawah Perjanjian WTO mengenai Aspek Hak Harta Intelek Berkaitan Perdagangan (TRIPS). Bersama-sama pertubuhan-pertubuhan ini, CAP telah mengemukakan surat kepada Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim, memberi amaran bahawa tuntutan TRIPS-plus oleh EU ini boleh menjejaskan akses kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, melemahkan industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan Malaysia, menyekat hak petani serta mengancam keselamatan makanan. Memandangkan pusingan terkini rundingan Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Malaysia-EU sedang berlangsung dari 21 hingga 25 September 2026, kerajaan mestilah memastikan komitmen perdagangan tidak menyekat keupayaan Malaysia untuk melindungi kesihatan awam serta memelihara kepentingan petani dan pengguna. CAP amat bimbang mengenai cadangan EU berkaitan eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, pelanjutan tempoh paten, rahsia perdagangan, penguatkuasaan hak harta intelek, reka bentuk perindustrian dan perlindungan varieti tumbuhan. Langkah-langkah TRIPS-plus ini boleh melanjutkan perlindungan monopoli, melambatkan persaingan ubat generik serta meningkatkan kos bagi pengguna dan sistem penjagaan kesihatan awam. Harga ubat yang lebih tinggi Cadangan EU bagi melanjutkan tempoh paten sehingga lima tahun akan memanjangkan tempoh monopoli farmaseutikal melebihi tempoh paten 20 tahun yang ditetapkan di bawah TRIPS. Apabila digabungkan dengan peluasan eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, peruntukan sebegini boleh melambatkan kemasukan ubat generik yang mampu milik. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Satu kajian semula pada 2022 terhadap 91 kajian mendapati bahawa monopoli farmaseutikal yang lebih kukuh, yang terhasil daripada peruntukan TRIPS-plus, secara umumnya dikaitkan dengan harga ubat yang lebih tinggi, kelewatan ketersediaan ubat serta peningkatan kos bagi pengguna dan kerajaan. Kajian yang sama menganggarkan bahawa kesan gabungan pelanjutan tempoh paten dan eksklusiviti data di bawah Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Colombia–EU boleh meningkatkan perbelanjaan farmaseutikal Colombia sebanyak $756j pada 2025. Cadangan TRIPS-plus EU juga boleh menjejaskan industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan, yang telah dikenal pasti sebagai sektor penting secara strategik di bawah Pelan Induk Perindustrian Baharu 2030 bagi meningkatkan kemampuan, aksesibiliti dan pengeluaran dalam negara. Malaysia juga merupakan pengimport bersih harta intelek, dengan aliran keluar bersih royalti harta intelek berjumlah kira-kira $2.7bn pada 2024, berbanding penerimaan sebanyak kira-kira $348j. Perlindungan harta intelek yang lebih kukuh dan lebih lama akan meningkatkan aliran keluar royalti serta membebankan pengguna Malaysia, program kesihatan awam dan pengeluar tempatan dengan kos tambahan. “Pada masa belanjawan kesihatan Malaysia telah pun dikurangkan, adalah satu tindakan yang sangat tidak bertanggungjawab bagi kerajaan Malaysia untuk bersetuju dengan cadangan EU yang boleh melonjakkan lagi harga produk perubatan serta menambah beban kewangan kepada rakyat Malaysia dan sistem kesihatan awam yang sedia terbeban,” kata Mohideen Abdul Kader, presiden Persatuan Pengguna-Pengguna Pulau Pinang (CAP). Lindungi hak petani CAP dan 40 pertubuhan masyarakat sivil yang lain turut berasa amat bimbang mengenai cadangan EU yang menuntut Malaysia melindungi varieti tumbuhan selaras dengan Akta 1991 Konvensyen Antarabangsa bagi Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu (Upov). Malaysia sudah pun mempunyai sistem perlindungan varieti tumbuhan sendiri di bawah Akta Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu 2004. Rangka kerja ini melindungi pembiak baka tumbuhan komersial di samping memelihara hak petani untuk menyimpan, menggunakan, menukar dan menjual benih varieti yang dilindungi yang disimpan sendiri. Ia juga mengandungi langkah-langkah perlindungan seperti langkah untuk mencegah biopirasi sumber genetik tumbuhan tempatan, serta memastikan ketersediaan benih pada harga yang berpatutan bagi petani Malaysia. Menyelaraskan sistem Malaysia dengan Upov hanya akan menyumbang kepada penguasaan korporat yang lebih besar dalam sektor benih, dan seterusnya meningkatkan kos benih yang membawa implikasi lebih luas kepada pengguna akibat kenaikan harga makanan, serta menjejaskan keselamatan makanan, kepelbagaian biologi pertanian dan daya tahan sektor pertanian Malaysia. Kepentingan EU adalah untuk meningkatkan akses pasaran bagi syarikat benih Eropah di Malaysia. “Malaysia tidak perlu menerima komitmen TRIPS-plus untuk memuktamadkan perjanjian perdagangan yang bercita-cita tinggi dengan EU,” kata Chee Yoke Ling, pengarah eksekutif Third World Network, salah satu pihak yang turut menandatangani surat kepada perdana menteri itu. “Perjanjian EU dengan India baru-baru ini menunjukkan bahawa adalah mungkin untuk merundingkan perjanjian perdagangan tanpa perlu menyelaraskan dengan Upov 1991 dan bersetuju dengan peruntukan TRIPS-plus seperti pelanjutan tempoh paten, eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, serta kewajipan TRIPS-plus yang lain.” Surat itu menggesa kerajaan untuk: - Menolak semua peruntukan harta intelek (TRIPS-plus yang melangkaui kewajipan WTO Malaysia, termasuk eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, pelanjutan tempoh paten, perlindungan rahsia perdagangan dan reka bentuk perindustrian yang berlebihan, langkah-langkah sempadan harta intelek yang diperluas serta komitmen Upov - Melindungi ruang dasar Malaysia untuk menggunakan pelesenan wajib, penggunaan oleh kerajaan dan langkah-langkah perlindungan kesihatan awam yang lain - Mengekalkan Akta Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu 2004 dan menolak sebarang komitmen untuk menyelaraskan dengan atau menyertai Upov - Memastikan bahawa perjanjian perdagangan bebas itu tidak menjejaskan akses kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, persaingan ubat generik dan biosimilar, industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan Malaysia, hak petani atau daya tahan sistem pertanian - Memastikan ketelusan serta perundingan yang bermakna dengan masyarakat sivil, pertubuhan pengguna, kumpulan pesakit dan petani pekebun kecil sepanjang proses rundingan berlangsung CAP selanjutnya menyatakan bahawa kebimbangan terperinci telah pun dibangkitkan dengan kementerian berkaitan, termasuk melalui surat yang dihantar oleh Third World Network pada 4 Jun dan oleh Forum Kedaulatan Makanan Malaysia pada 19 Jun. Pertubuhan-pertubuhan masyarakat sivil itu menyatakan bahawa sehingga kini mereka masih belum menerima sebarang maklum balas daripada mana-mana kementerian mengenai status rundingan itu. CAP menggesa kerajaan supaya memastikan Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Malaysia-EU tidak mengorbankan akses rakyat Malaysia kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, hak petani, keselamatan makanan, mahupun keupayaan Malaysia untuk melaksanakan dasar-dasar demi kepentingan awam. Perjanjian perdagangan mestilah berteraskan kepentingan awam serta memelihara ruang dasar yang diperlukan bagi pembangunan kesihatan, pertanian dan ekonomi Malaysia dalam jangka masa panjang. Antara pihak yang menandatangani surat itu ialah Malaysian Agroecology Society – SRI-Mas, Majlis Aids Malaysia (MAC), Yayasan Aids Malaysia (MAF), Forum Kedaulatan Makanan Malaysia (FKMM) dan Malaysian Rare Disorders Society; Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) – cawangan Malaysia; Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia (PPIM); Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM); serta Together Against Cancer Association. – CAP, 25 September English version EU-Malaysia trade deal must not put affordable medical products, farmers’ rights and food security at risk The Consumers’ Association of Penang (CAP) and 40 other Malaysian civil society organisations call on the Malaysian government to reject intellectual property demands by the EU that go beyond Malaysia’s obligations under the World Trade Organization’s on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS). Together with these organizations, CAP has sent a letter to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, warning that these TRIPS-plus demands of the EU could undermine access to affordable medicines, weaken Malaysia’s domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, restrict farmers’ rights and threaten food security. With the latest round of the Malaysia–EU free trade agreement negotiations taking place from 21 to 25 September, the government must ensure that trade commitments do not restrict Malaysia’s ability to protect public health, and safeguard the interests of farmers and consumers. CAP is particularly concerned about the EU’s proposals on data and marketing exclusivity, patent-term extension, trade secrets, intellectual property enforcement, industrial designs and plant variety protection. These TRIPS-plus measures could extend monopoly protection, delay generic competition and increase costs for consumers and the public healthcare system. Higher medicine prices competition The EU’s proposals for patent-term extensions of up to five years would extend pharmaceutical monopolies beyond the 20-year patent term required under TRIPS. Combined with expanded data and marketing exclusivity, such provisions could delay the entry of affordable generic medicines. A 2022 review of 91 studies found that stronger pharmaceutical monopolies created through TRIPS-plus provisions are generally associated with higher drug prices, delayed availability and increased costs for consumers and governments. The same review estimated that the combined impact of patent-term extensions and data exclusivity under the Colombia–EU Free Trade Agreement could increase Colombia’s pharmaceutical spending by $756m in 2025. The EU’s TRIPS-plus proposals can also undermine the domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, which has been identified as strategically important under the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 for improving affordability, accessibility and domestic production. Malaysia is also a net importer of intellectual property, with about $2.7bn in net intellectual property royalty outflows in 2024, compared with around $348m in receipts. Stronger and longer intellectual property protection would increase royalty outflows and impose additional costs on local consumers, public health programmes and domestic manufacturers. “At a time when Malaysia’s health budget has already been cut, it would be deeply irresponsible for the Malaysian government to agree to EU proposals that could further drive up the prices of medical products and place additional financial burdens on the Malaysian people and on an already stretched public health system,” said Mohideen Abdul Kader, president of the Consumers’ Association of Penang. Protect farmers’ rights CAP and the other 40 civil society organisations are also deeply concerned about the EU’s proposal requiring Malaysia to protect plant varieties in accordance with the 1991 Act of the International Convention for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (Upov). Malaysia already has its own plant variety protection system under the Protection of New Plant Varieties Act 2004. This framework protects commercial plant breeders while preserving farmers’ rights to save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seeds of protected varieties. It also contains safeguards such as measures to prevent biopiracy of local plant genetic resources, and ensure the availability of seeds at reasonable prices for Malaysian farmers. Aligning Malaysia’s system with Upov will only contribute to greater corporate concentration in the seed sector, and consequently increase the costs of seeds with wider implications for consumers as food prices increase, food security, agrobiodiversity and the resilience of Malaysian agriculture. The EU’s interest is to increase market access for European seed companies in Malaysia. “Malaysia does not need to accept TRIPS-plus commitments to conclude an ambitious EU trade agreement,” said Chee Yoke Ling, the executive director of Third World Network, another signatory to the letter to the prime minister. “Recent EU agreement with India demonstrates that it is possible to negotiate a trade agreement without having to align with Upov 1991 and agree to TRIPS-plus provisions such as patent-term extension, data and marketing exclusivity, and other TRIPS-plus obligations.” The letter calls on the government to: - Reject all TRIPS-plus intellectual property provisions that go beyond Malaysia’s WTO obligations, including data and marketing exclusivity, patent-term extensions, excessive trade-secret and industrial-design protection, expanded intellectual property border measures and Upov commitments - Protect Malaysia’s policy space to use compulsory licensing, government use and other public health safeguards - Maintain the Protection of New Plant Varieties Act 2004 and reject any commitment to align with or accede to Upov - Ensure that the free trade agreement does not undermine access to affordable medicines, generic and biosimilar competition, Malaysia’s domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, farmers’ rights or the resilience of the agricultural system - Ensure transparency and meaningful consultation with civil society, consumer organisations, patient groups and smallholder farmers throughout the negotiations CAP further notes that detailed concerns have already been raised with the relevant ministries, including through letters sent by Third World Network on 4 June and by the Malaysian Food Sovereignty Forum on 19 June. The civil society organisations state that, to date, they have not received a response from any ministry concerning the status of the negotiations. CAP urges the government to ensure that the Malaysia–EU free trade agreement does not trade away Malaysians’ access to affordable medicines, farmers’ rights, food security or Malaysia’s ability to pursue public interest policies. Trade agreements must serve the public interest and preserve the policy space needed for Malaysia’s long-term health, agricultural and economic development. Signatories to the letter include the Malaysian Agroecology Society – SRI-Mas, Malaysian Aids Council, Malaysian Aids Foundation, Malaysian Food Sovereignty Forum, Malaysian Rare Disorders Society; Médecins Sans Frontières Malaysian chapter; Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia; Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth) – SAM; and Together Against Cancer Association. – CAP, 25 September Mohideen Abdul Kader is the president of the Consumers’ Association of Penang (CAP). title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher Tracking Wall Street Gains
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday morning, tracking overnight gains on Wall Street as softer US payroll growth eased investor concerns regarding an immediate interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. At 9:10 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) climbed 5.01 points, or 0.31 per cent, to 1,635.88 compared to last Friday’s closing figure of 1,630.87. The benchmark index initially opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42. Across the broader market, advancing counters outpaced decliners 224 to 158, while 337 counters remained unchanged, 2,054 untraded, and 24 suspended. Total market turnover stood at 206.30 million shares valued at RM98.78 million. Key market indices and sector performances during early trade included: - Heavyweight Movement: Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB, and Tenaga Nasional each gained four sen to reach RM10.06, RM4.70, RM7.69, and RM13.00, respectively. Conversely, IHH Healthcare shed six sen to RM7.74. - Top Active Stocks: VS Industry advanced three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTec gained four sen to 74.5 sen, GB Bond edged up half-a-sen to 23.5 sen, SFP Tech added one sen to 28.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange traded flat at 51.5 sen. - Top Gainers: Samaiden surged 19 sen to RM3.03, UWC gained 16 sen to RM7.73, Critical Holdings rose 15 sen to RM2.61, Mi Technovation moved up nine sen to RM5.30, and Solarvest advanced eight sen to RM4.25. - Top Decliners: Nestle led losses, dropping 32 sen to RM89.20, followed by Vitrox (down 14 sen to RM10.32), Kobay Technology (down 12 sen to RM2.18), Kelington (down five sen to RM8.58), and YTL Power International (down four sen to RM5.64). - Index & Sector Breakdown: The Financial Services Index gained 97.59 points to 19,138.10, the Energy Index added 2.57 points to 835.60, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.59 of a point to 179.11, and the Plantation Index moved up 2.23 points to 9,058.78. The FBM Mid 70 Index climbed 28.14 points to 17,510.07, the FBM Emas Index rose 33.81 points to 12,204.38, and the FBM ACE Index improved 31.41 points to 5,560.87. –NMT

title: 'Maybank Completes Acquisition Of Remaining Stake In MAHB From Ageas
body: 'Malayan Banking announced that it has completed the proposed acquisition of the remaining 30.95% interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad (MAHB) after signing a share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV on 8 September 2026.  This follows regulatory approvals from Bank Negara Malaysia that were received on 1 September 2026 for the Proposed Acquisition. MAHB is the holding company for the Etiqa business in Malaysia and Singapore, providing a full range of life and general conventional insurance products as well as family and general takaful products through multi-channel distribution.  President and Group CEO of Maybank, Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, said “With MAHB being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa’s position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank’s customer base. Our focus will be unlocking further value for our customers across Southeast Asia via our regional wealth propositions through cross-selling and delivering more integrated and personalised financial solutions. It will also enhance sustainable and resilient long-term value creation for Maybank with improved capital management within the MAHB group, hence facilitating more effective capital management at the Maybank group level.”  Moving forward, the full ownership provides Maybank and MAHB with greater agility to accelerate product innovation, deepen bancassurance penetration and expand takaful propositions while enhancing capital and operational efficiency across the Group,” added Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli.

title: 'The Makeover Guys and RHB Bank Introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan with Up to 120% Financing for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – Media OutReach Newswire – 15 September 2026 – The Makeover Guys has partnered with RHB Bank Berhad as RHB Bank’s Home Makeover Partner to introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan– an integrated financing solution that enables eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility, with financing support of up to 120% of the property’s value. Demand for home renovations continues to rise in Malaysia. The home improvement and renovation market was valued at RM47.7 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow to RM59.2 billion by 2029, as more homeowners invest in upgrading their living spaces to suit changing lifestyles and personal preferences. While home financing is widely available, renovation financing is often treated as a separate borrowing decision. This means many homeowners need to secure additional financing or rely on personal savings after purchasing a property before they can begin renovations. The Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank offers a different approach by enabling eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility. Instead of managing separate financing arrangements, homeowners can plan both from the outset, providing greater financial certainty and a more seamless homeownership journey. title: 'BT Buys Over TalkTalk to Save UK's Broadband Provider From Collapse
body: '(Oct 5): BT Group plc bought TalkTalk and PlatformX Communications Ltd out of administration, preventing the collapse of a UK broadband provider that is also a major customer. The deal, which is expected to have a total cash impact of £400 million (RM2.16 billion) for the 2027 fiscal year, was made “in the public interest” after talks to sell TalkTalk’s consumer and wholesale businesses fell through, BT said in a statement on Monday. “This is a genuinely unprecedented situation, where millions of citizens and businesses were at risk if TalkTalk had collapsed,” BT chief executive officer Allison Kirkby said in the statement. “Our immediate priority is to stabilise the business and provide a safety net for the households and businesses who rely on TalkTalk.” TalkTalk has struggled under its debt load since it was bought out in 2021 by Toscafund Asset Management LLP and private equity firm Penta Capital. The company was founded as a low-cost broadband provider, reselling wholesale access on BT’s Openreach network to consumers. However, high levels of competition and persistent inflation undermined its business. The deal will pay off after TalkTalk’s business stabilises and the companies combine operations, according to BT, which maintained its financial targets. BT shares rose 1.5% to 199.2 pence at 8.56am in London. TalkTalk ended talks with Octopus Investments to sell its wholesale network division, Sky News reported last month. That came after discussions with the private equity firm Epiris didn’t result in a deal. The two companies will continue to work separately while regulators review the deal. TalkTalk, which has lost customers in recent years, was the UK’s fourth-biggest broadband provider with an 8% market share, according to a 2025 Ofcom report. BT, formerly the UK’s phone monopoly, was the largest with a 30% share. UK State Secretary for digital Lisa Nandy will weigh wider public interest when reviewing the Competition and Markets Authority’s report on antitrust concerns. Critical infrastructure, including emergency services and hospital communications rely on TalkTalk’s services, Nandy’s department said in a statement. Kirkby sought government assurances beforehand that a takeover of TalkTalk would not trigger an in-depth antitrust review, the Financial Times reported previously. Over the last year, TalkTalk reported revenues of about £1.2 billion and was loss-making. The company has about 1.5 million retail customers and one million wholesale customers in the UK. title: 'Sabah Energy Issues Inaugural RM350 Million Sukuk With Maybank Investment
body: 'Sabah Energy Corporation Sdn Bhd (SEC) has completed its maiden RM350 million sukuk issuance under a RM3 billion Sukuk Wakalah Programme, marking its first entry into Malaysia’s sukuk capital market.  The Sabah state-owned integrated energy company said the sukuk was assigned a long-term AAA rating with a stable outlook by RAM Rating Services Bhd. The issuance was priced through a book-building exercise, the first for a Sabah state government-linked company, and was oversubscribed by 2.2 times despite volatile market conditions.  Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as sole principal advisor, sole lead arranger, sole lead manager, sole sustainability structuring adviser, Shariah advisor and facility agent for the transaction.  SEC Group Chief Executive Officer Datuk Ir Adzmir Abd Rahman said the programme gives the company a scalable and flexible funding platform to support its PETA 2030 agenda.  He said the funding would support efforts to strengthen SEC’s gas and infrastructure businesses, expand power generation and renewable energy, and pursue investments across Sabah’s energy value chain.  The programme also supports the broader SERAMP 2040 objectives of strengthening energy security, accelerating the energy transition and improving supply reliability in Sabah.  SEC has evolved from a gas utility operator into a diversified energy group with interests in natural gas infrastructure, power generation, renewable energy and offshore oil and gas support services. It is also Sabah’s sole natural gas aggregator, transporter and distributor.

title: 'Carbon Tax Deferment Gives Ministry More Time to Finalise Regulatory, Policy Framework, Says Arthur
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. title: 'CIMB Bank wins big at Euromoney Awards
body: 'PETALING JAYA: CIMB Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank have won top accolades at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026, taking home top honours as Malaysia’s Best Retail Bank, Malaysia’s Best Digital Bank for SMEs, and Malaysia’s Best Investment Bank. The bank said in a statement that the awards reflected the ongoing focus on providing customer-centric solutions through innovation, digital capabilities and deep market expertise across its retail, small and medium enterprise (SME), and investment banking businesses. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd group chief executive officer Novan Amirudin commented that the recognitions are a testament to the trust of the group’s customers and the dedication of its teams. “They reaffirm CIMB’s purpose of advancing customers and society by making financial solutions more accessible, relevant and impactful for the people and businesses we serve,” he added. “As their needs continue to evolve, we remain committed to being a trusted partner supporting individuals in realising their aspirations and helping businesses achieve their growth ambitions through meaningful and lasting value creation.” CIMB’s latest wins come amid the bank’s continued efforts to empower customers through accessible, inclusive and purpose-driven financial solutions. In retail banking, it has been working to deepen its franchise through personalisation offerings, digitally enabled journeys, and stronger engagement across segments. The bank said revenue and profitability had advanced during the year, underpinned by market share gains in auto finance, credit cards and retail deposits, on top of progress in digital sales and customer cross-sell. It also continued to strengthen wealth proposition through differentiated investment solutions, broader product diversity, chief investment office-led advisory capabilities and enhanced digital wealth platform, with particular momentum seen in the “Preferred” affluent segment as it expands its advisory-led and relationship-based wealth capabilities. Meanwhile, the bank has continued to advance its SME services, having launched the CIMB OCTO Biz digital banking platform, which has amassed more than 280,000 customers to date. Additionally, it has expanded financing access through embedded merchant financing with TNG eWallet and its flexible financing through its SME FlexiCash. Beyond this, CIMB Investment Bank in 2025 secured the top ranking in Malaysian equity and debt capital markets by deal value and share of wallet, as well as the highest position in Asean equity and debt capital markets by deal value, cementing its position both locally and regionally.

title: 'Allianz, Hong Leong Bank Lead Bursa Losers As Selling Pressure Dominates
body: 'Allianz Malaysia Bhd and Hong Leong Bank Bhd led Bursa Malaysia’s decliners at the close of trading session on Sept 11, as selling pressure remained broad with 809 losers outnumbering 427 gainers.  Allianz was the top loser, sliding 56 sen to RM21.12, followed by Hong Leong Bank, which fell 52 sen to RM23.08. Sunway Construction Group Bhd dropped 47 sen to RM7.44, while Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd lost 44 sen to RM23.56 and ViTrox Corp Bhd declined 32 sen to RM9.15.  The weaker breadth underscored cautious sentiment across the market, with 474 counters unchanged, 1,121 untraded and 32 suspended at 5pm.  On the upside, Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd topped the list, rising 27 sen to RM5.09. Eurospan Holdings Bhd advanced 18 sen to RM3.15, while Batu Kawan Bhd and Concrete Engineering Products Bhd each added 12 sen, closing at RM20.16 and RM4 respectively.  Mega Fortris Bhd rounded out the top five gainers, climbing nine sen to RM2.40.  Total market turnover stood at 3.57 billion units worth RM3.28 billion compared to 3.98 billion units valued at RM3.14 billion on Sept 10.

title: 'RHB Bank And The Makeover Guys’ New Home Loan Includes Up To 30% For Renovation
body: 'You can now include renovation costs in your home loan with the Makeover Flexi Loan, from RHB Bank and The Makeover Guys. It covers up to 90% of the property’s value, plus up to 30% more for renovation and related costs, for a total of up to 120%.  Up To 120% Financing With Flexi Features  With a standard home loan, you can usually borrow up to 90% of the property’s value, and the renovation is paid for separately with savings, a personal loan, or a renovation loan.  The extra 30% can go towards your renovation, legal and documentation fees, and Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance (MRTA). MRTA is insurance that pays off the rest of your home loan if you pass away or become totally and permanently disabled. If you take an Islamic home loan, the same cover is called Mortgage Reducing Term Takaful (MRTT).  It’s also a full flexi loan. You can put extra cash, like a bonus, into the loan, which lowers what you still owe and the interest you pay on it. If you need that money back later, you can take it out again, which is called a redraw.  Example Of 120% Financing On A RM500,000 Home  As an example, on a RM500,000 home, you could borrow up to RM450,000 to buy the property, and you’d pay the remaining RM50,000 yourself as your down payment. You could then borrow up to RM150,000 more for your renovation, MRTA, and legal fees.  The final loan amount you get depends on RHB Bank’s check of your income and any loans you already have.  One Application And One Repayment For Your Home And Renovation  Since the renovation is part of your home loan, you apply once and make one monthly repayment. Home loan interest rates are generally lower than personal loan rates. Your renovation cost is also spread over your home loan’s repayment period of up to 35 years or until you turn 70, whichever comes first, while most personal loans run for up to 10 years. The savings you’d have set aside for renovation can go towards furniture or your emergency fund instead.  RHB Bank pays out the renovation money bit by bit, each time your contractor finishes a stage of the work. The renovation is done through The Makeover Guys, which handles the design, project management, and construction.  Get A Renovation Quote Before You Apply  Your renovation budget is set when you apply for the loan, so get a quote first to see how much of the extra 30% you’ll need. You can also compare home loan rates before sending an enquiry through The Makeover Guys’ website.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Key Index Continues Uptrend at Midday
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia's key index maintained its upward trend, increasing by 0.33 percent at midday due to bargain hunting in selected heavyweights. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose by 5.44 points to 1,635.80 from the previous day's close of 1,630.36. The index opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, fluctuating between 1,630.63 and 1,640.78 during the morning trading session. Across the broader market, there were more decliners than gainers, with 507 losers compared to 499 gainers. Additionally, 494 counters remained unchanged, 1,273 were untraded, and 24 were suspended. The market saw a turnover of 2.24 billion shares worth RM1.26 billion. Hong Leong Investment Bank noted that the barometer index might continue its risk-off consolidation amid high oil prices and bond yields. It also highlighted persistent foreign outflows, US-Iran tensions, and a hawkish Federal Reserve stance as factors affecting market sentiment. The bank identified immediate resistance levels at 1,667-1,682, followed by 1,705-1,720. Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose by nine sen to RM10.04, Public Bank added four sen to RM4.71, Tenaga Nasional increased 16 sen to RM13.06, and IHH Healthcare expanded by 11 sen to RM7.81. However, CIMB eased by one sen to RM7.68. In active trading, Jaks Resources firmed by half a sen to 18.5 sen, JCY International advanced 10 sen to 65.5 sen, V.S Industry ticked up two sen to 29 sen, and Top Glove inched up 3.5 sen to 77 sen, while Zetrix AI decreased 2.5 sen to 14 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries surged 84 sen to RM41.96, UWC gained 36 sen to RM7.46, United Plantations advanced 36 sen to RM31.32, and both Vitrox and UMS Integration climbed 34 sen to RM10.34 and RM8.99, respectively. Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 46 sen to RM20.96. Other notable decliners included Enra, which lost 29 sen to 69 sen, Allianz Malaysia, which fell 28 sen to RM20.72, BLD Plantations, which shed 26 sen to RM14.74, and Dutch Lady Milk Industries, which erased 20 sen to RM29.80. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 115.75 points to 17,474.73, the FBM Emas Index added 51.08 points to 12,194.61, and the FBM Top 100 Index advanced 50.09 points to 11,983.24. The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 66.45 points to 12,079.46, while the FBM ACE Index improved 6.33 points to 5,489.30. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.99 of a point to 178.72, the Energy Index gained 1.06 points to 836.07, the Financial Services Index rose 55.60 points to 19,116.51, and the Plantation Index increased by 4.58 points to 9,031.15.

title: 'PN Challenging Suspension in Court, Seeks Expedited Hearing as Melaka Polls Loom
body: 'PUTRAJAYA (Oct 5): Perikatan Nasional on Monday filed a legal challenge against its suspension and potential deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), and is seeking an expedited hearing to resolve the matter before the Melaka election. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition wants to quash notices issued by RoS under Sections 13(2) and 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966. Section 13(2) requires PN to explain its actions within 30 days or be deregistered. The Section 13(2A) notice informs PN that it must suspend its activities until it has responded to the matter. The suspension means PN cannot use its logo during the state polls. “The only reason given [for the notice and suspension] was that we did not invite Bersatu leaders for a meeting on July 16. But the official complaint by Bersatu was never given to us,” Takiyuddin, who is also secretary-general of PAS, said at a press conference on Monday. PN's application names RoS director-general Datuk Muhammad Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Datuk Sri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail as respondents. The Election Commission (EC) is expected to announce the date of the Melaka election after a meeting on Wednesday. The state polls must be held within 60 days of the Sept 23 dissolution of the Melaka assembly. Given the urgency, Takiyuddin said the coalition has also made a filing requesting that the case be expedited. “We want to ask the court to hear this case urgently because we need the court’s determination before the Melaka election is held,” he said. Takiyuddin said the coalition had engaged with the EC on this matter but the final word lay with the RoS. Asked whether PN component parties would use their own logos in the Melaka polls, Takiyuddin said: “These five parties, PAS, Wawasan, Gerakan, MIPP and Pejuang, have been negotiating that matter in view of all possibilities.” The suspension of PN comes after PAS said on June 8 it had ended political cooperation with Bersatu, the previously the dominant party in PN. However, the now beleaguered Bersatu was never expelled from the coalition. On Aug 11, Bersatu filed a complaint with RoS concerning its status in PN, as well as its exclusion from a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16. RoS sent the show-cause notice to PN on Sept 22, and the suspension order the next day as the Melaka assembly was dissolved. Takiyuddin said PN sent a letter to RoS on Sept 24 to obtain an explanation on the notice and suspension, but has yet to receive a response. He said Bersatu was excluded from the July 16 meeting due to the party's breaches of its own constitution earlier that week. Takiyuddin claimed that a Bersatu Supreme Council meeting had decided to use the party logo instead of the PN logo for the Negeri Sembilan polls, but that meeting had insufficient quorum as per the party’s constitution. He said PN feared that its deliberations would be invalid if Bersatu took part in the coalition’s supreme council meeting while in breach of its own party constitution. In the coalition's court filing, it argues that suspension order violated procedural fairness and the rules of natural justice, as PN was neither provided with details of Bersatu’s complaint nor granted an opportunity to be heard. PN said the suspension order impedes its ability to endorse candidates and its use of its registered name and symbol during the state election, thereby infringing upon rights under Articles 4(1), 8(1), 10(1)(a), 10(1)(c), and 119 of the Federal Constitution. Apart from quashing the RoS notices, PN wants the regulator to furnish all complaint documents and communications related to Bersatu within three days, as well as a stay on the suspension pending the disposal of the judicial review. Case management was fixed for Oct 13 before High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Arshad. title: 'Malaysia steps up healthcare push in Cambodia
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is stepping up efforts to attract Cambodian healthcare travellers, with Maybank (Cambodia) Plc and the Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC) showcasing 14 Malaysian hospitals in Phnom Penh. In a statement, Maybank Cambodia chief executive officer and country head Rath Sophoan said the event aimed to make it easier for Cambodian families to make informed healthcare decisions while incorporating financial planning into the process. "MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 was designed around a simple question: how can we make it easier for Cambodian families to take a confident next step when health matters? "The event connected families with the people, expertise and options behind Malaysia's healthcare institutions, while bringing financial readiness into the same conversation," he said. MH WellFest Cambodia 2026, held at Borey Peng Huoth Eco Park, drew about 2,000 visitors and almost 800 runners, providing Cambodian families with direct access to Malaysian healthcare providers and specialists. The two-day event, endorsed by the Malaysian Embassy in Phnom Penh, highlighted Malaysia's healthcare capabilities, including health screening, preventive care, specialist services and treatment options. MHTC chief executive officer Datuk Suriaghandi Suppiah said healthcare travel depended on trust and confidence in the quality of care available. "Malaysia Healthcare brings together quality care, specialist expertise, accessible healthcare options and a patient experience shaped by genuine hospitality. "MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 created a direct bridge between Cambodian visitors and this ecosystem, allowing them to meet Malaysian healthcare teams, learn from specialists and gain greater clarity and confidence as they consider care across borders," he said. Malaysian ambassador to Cambodia Shaharuddin Onn said stronger connectivity between Malaysia and Cambodia was creating more opportunities for families to access expertise and services across borders. "MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 reflects this progress by linking Cambodian communities directly with Malaysia's healthcare institutions and specialists," he said. The event featured a Wellness Discovery Hub with five health talks, giving visitors information on healthcare options and navigating treatment in Malaysia. Maybank and MHTC said the event marked a step towards strengthening cross-border healthcare connectivity and raising awareness of Malaysia as a healthcare destination among Cambodian families.

title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM799.9 juta ekuiti Bursa Malaysia untuk minggu kedua - MBSB Research | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt – Pelabur asing terus mengurangkan pegangan dalam pasaran saham Malaysia apabila mencatatkan jualan bersih RM799.9 juta bagi minggu berakhir 2 Oktober 2026, menurut MBSB Research. Jualan bersih itu menjadikan aliran keluar dana asing di Bursa Malaysia berterusan untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan pelabur asing menjadi penjual bersih pada kesemua lima hari dagangan sepanjang minggu berkenaan. “Jualan paling tinggi direkodkan pada Rabu sebanyak RM228.4 juta, diikuti Khamis RM187.9 juta, Selasa RM172.4 juta, Isnin RM142.1 juta dan Jumaat RM69.1 juta,” kata MBSB Research dalam nota kajiannya. Pelabur tempatan ambil peluang Berbeza dengan pelabur asing, institusi tempatan meneruskan trend pembelian bersih untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan aliran masuk RM352.4 juta. Pelabur runcit pula meneruskan pembelian bersih bagi minggu keenam berturut-turut dengan jumlah aliran masuk sebanyak RM447.5 juta. Ini menunjukkan tekanan jualan daripada pelabur asing sebahagiannya diimbangi oleh penyertaan pelabur tempatan. Dari segi aktiviti dagangan, purata dagangan harian pelabur runcit meningkat 3.7%, manakala institusi tempatan susut 7.9%. Penyertaan pelabur asing pula meningkat 8.6%. Sektor teknologi, tenaga jadi pilihan pelabur asing Walaupun pelabur asing secara keseluruhan mencatatkan jualan bersih, terdapat beberapa sektor yang masih menerima aliran masuk dana. Sektor teknologi menerima aliran masuk asing tertinggi sebanyak RM131 juta, diikuti sektor tenaga sebanyak RM93.2 juta dan pembinaan sebanyak RM78.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM460.6 juta, diikuti utiliti RM339.8 juta dan penjagaan kesihatan RM163.1 juta. Dari sudut saham pula, antara kaunter yang menerima aliran masuk bersih asing tertinggi ialah Gamuda sebanyak RM86.2 juta, Solarvest Holdings RM65.4 juta, Westports Holdings RM55.1 juta dan Southern Cable Group RM53.4 juta. Dalam tempoh sama, Tenaga Nasional Berhad mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM278.1 juta, diikuti Malayan Banking RM159.3 juta dan RHB Bank RM135.9 juta. September turut menyaksikan jualan pelabur asing Trend tersebut turut dapat dilihat sepanjang September apabila pelabur asing menjual bersih saham Malaysia sebanyak RM1.69 bilion. Dalam tempoh sama, institusi tempatan mencatatkan pembelian bersih RM205.7 juta, manakala pelabur runcit membeli bersih RM1.48 bilion. Bagi September, sektor perladangan menjadi penerima aliran masuk asing terbesar sebanyak RM290.6 juta, diikuti tenaga RM230.2 juta serta pengangkutan dan logistik RM204.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak RM1.48 bilion, diikuti utiliti RM642.2 juta dan produk serta perkhidmatan perindustrian RM310.8 juta. Aliran dana Asia kembali negatif Trend jualan asing di Malaysia berlaku ketika pelabur asing secara keseluruhan kembali mengeluarkan dana dari pasaran saham Asia. MBSB Research berkata, kesemua lapan pasaran Asia yang dipantau mencatatkan aliran keluar asing pada minggu berkenaan dengan jumlah keseluruhan AS$10.89 bilion, selepas mencatatkan pembelian bersih pada minggu sebelumnya. Korea Selatan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak AS$6.20 bilion, diikuti India AS$2.91 bilion dan Thailand AS$796.4 juta. Ekonomi Malaysia turut beri isyarat bercampur Dalam perkembangan ekonomi domestik, Indeks Pengurus Pembelian sektor pembuatan Malaysia susut kepada 49.9 pada September daripada 50.2 pada Ogos, menunjukkan kemerosotan keadaan operasi buat kali pertama sejak Mei 2026. MBSB Research berkata tempahan baharu merosot buat kali pertama dalam tempoh empat bulan, manakala pertumbuhan pengeluaran perlahan ke paras terendah dalam tempoh tujuh bulan. Keyakinan perniagaan turut jatuh ke paras terendah dalam tempoh lima bulan. Pada masa sama, inflasi harga pengeluar Malaysia meningkat 10.7% tahun ke tahun pada Ogos, iaitu peningkatan bagi bulan keenam berturut-turut dan kadar tertinggi sejak Jun 2022. Pasaran global kekal berhati-hati Di Amerika Syarikat, pertumbuhan pekerjaan yang lebih perlahan serta kadar inflasi yang masih melebihi sasaran menimbulkan ketidakpastian terhadap hala tuju dasar monetari negara itu. Dalam tempoh sama, dolar Amerika Syarikat meningkat 0.3% berbanding ringgit kepada RM4.0842, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent turun 2% kepada AS$102.25 setong dan minyak sawit mentah susut 2.9% kepada RM4,535 setan. title: 'Bursa once said no to crypto. LIDAC26 showed how far Malaysia has come since
body: 'Back in 2024, I wrote a column lamenting Bursa Malaysia’s decision to keep bitcoin and other crypto assets off its new multi-asset exchange, asking whether it might go down as Bursa’s biggest blunder. Two Thursday’s ago, I spent the better part of a day at M Resort & Hotel in Kuala Lumpur listening to regulators, bankers and fund managers talk about digital assets not as a fringe curiosity, but as the plumbing for the next generation of our capital market. What a difference two years makes. The event was LIDAC26, the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference, now in its second edition. Luno, one of the digital asset exchanges registered with the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC), pitched it squarely at institutions rather than retail punters, and the room reflected that. The main hall kept the headline sessions flowing from 9.30am, four breakout sessions ran in smaller rooms alongside it through the day, and the session screens I saw all carried a QR code for live audience questions. Attendees could even earn seven continuing professional development (CPD) points, the credits licensed finance professionals collect to keep their qualifications current, which tells you exactly who the organisers were courting. So what were the big takeaways? Three stood out. 1. Stablecoins are the real story Luno chief executive James Lanigan opened proceedings with a slide that cut through a lot of the noise. By Luno’s count, about RM1.43 trillion worth of assets had been tokenised, or recorded as digital tokens on a blockchain, by the first quarter of 2026, and roughly RM1.26 trillion of that was stablecoins, tokens pegged to a currency such as the US dollar. That’s right. Around 90% of all tokenised assets are, in effect, digital cash, the overwhelming majority of which is tokenised USD, cementing it as not only the world’s reserve currency but the currency of choice in the budding crypto economy. Lanigan’s framing was that the industry had moved from speculation, through building infrastructure, and was now firmly in its institutional era, with one of his final slides declaring that Malaysia was not a late market, but an early one. 2. The regulator wants substance, not buzzwords The most anticipated session was that by Wong Huei Ching, the SC’s executive director of digital strategy and innovation, who laid out where Malaysia’s rules are heading. Her message, stripped to its core, was that putting an asset on a blockchain is not innovation in itself, and that pilots need to prove their worth before the rules are rewritten. The SC is practising what it preaches. In April, it teamed up with Khazanah Nasional, our sovereign wealth fund, to price Malaysia’s first tokenised sukuk (an Islamic bond recorded on a blockchain), a RM100 million pilot that SC chairman Mohammad Faiz Azmi said would test tokenisation’s potential “in a controlled and credible manner”. The market she regulates is growing fast, too. Trading value on Malaysia’s licensed digital asset exchanges hit RM17.14 billion in 2025, a 23% jump from RM13.93 billion the year before, according to the SC. 3. The ringgit is going on-chain John Ho, head of legal and financial markets at Standard Chartered, walked participants in the main hall through Bank Negara Malaysia’s growing list of experiments. These include Project Mawar, which explores a wholesale digital ringgit for banks, and the central bank’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, where Standard Chartered and Capital A are testing a ringgit stablecoin, while Maybank trials tokenised deposits. The prize is not small. One industry estimate cited on stage, and widely reported, puts Malaysia’s tokenisation opportunity at around RM175 billion by 2030. The tidbits Many other speakers added flair and colour to the proceedings. Former deputy international trade and industry minister Ong Kian Ming spoke on navigating digital assets in a fragmenting global order, while Harjit Singh of HSS Advisory and Anil Puri of EY tackled a question plenty of Malaysian crypto investors have been asking for years: how exactly will all this be taxed? My favourite, though, was a breakout billed as Malaysian builders shaping the global digital asset landscape. On one stage sat TM Lee, co-founder of CoinGecko, Matthew Tan, founder of Etherscan, and Siong Ong, co-founder of Jupiter, products used by crypto traders the world over. CoinGecko and Etherscan were both born right here in Kuala Lumpur, and I can’t help but feel proud that some of the most widely used tools in the industry were built by Malaysians. Siong Ong’s speaker photo on the big screen? A Pudgy Penguin, an uber popular non-fungible token (NFT) collection. In a day full of suits, it was a welcome reminder of where this industry came from. The one glaring miss I was, however, surprised that bitcoin, the 800-pound gorilla in the room, barely got a look-in. Bitcoin alone is worth around RM6.9 trillion today, according to CoinGecko, and together with ether, the Ethereum network’s native token, the pair make up about two-thirds of the entire crypto market. Stablecoins, for all the stage time they got, account for a mere 10%. Despite more than a decade of relentless innovation in the industry, bitcoin still commands over half of all crypto value, and not telling that story was a missed opportunity. So where does that leave us? The SC revised its guidelines on Mar 2 to permit digital currency exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and Bursa, the very exchange that shut crypto out of its multi-asset platform in 2024, said in March that it welcomed the listing of digital currency ETFs, and told reporters in July that it planned to add them to its line-up. The regulator has built the framework, Khazanah has shown the plumbing can work and Bank Negara is already testing the ringgit on-chain. All that’s left is for the first digital currency ETF to actually start trading on Bursa. After all, it’s about time the exchange that once said no had something to show for its yes. title: 'Share price soars as earnings continue to shine
body: 'Share price soars as earnings continue to shine This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 5, 2026 - October 11, 2026 AMMB Holdings Bhd Once again, AMMB Holdings Bhd (KL:AMBANK) is taking home The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) award for Highest returns to shareholders over three years under the financial services category. Notably, its share price has climbed steadily over the last five years, with the most significant jump recorded between 2024 and 2025. The stock gained 41.9% from RM3.70 on March 31, 2024 to RM5.25 on March 28, 2025. Between March 28, 2025 and March 31, 2026, the banking group’s share price continued its upward trajectory, reaching RM6.59, before hitting another record high of RM7.37 on Aug 12. Much of the enthusiasm about the stock can be linked to the potential return of excess capital to shareholders, which could either come in the form of higher dividends or through other capital return initiatives. AMMB, under its five-year strategic plan called “Winning Together 2029” (WT29), aims to double its dividend per share by the financial year ending March 31, 2029 (FY2029) from 22.6 sen in FY2024. This would be supported by earnings growth and capital optimisation, with Basel 3.1 reforms providing a meaningful upside catalyst. AMMB has already been increasing its dividend payout ratio, from 40% to 50% in FY2025, exceeding its earlier dividend payout ratio guidance of 35% to 40%. Total dividends increased from 22.6 sen in FY2024 to 30.2 sen in FY2025 and 35 sen in FY2026. Its three-year compound annual growth rate for shareholder returns totalled 27.9% for the period between March 31, 2023 and March 31, 2026. The increase in dividends can also be attributed to the yearly improvements in earnings. In FY2026, the group achieved its highest-ever net profit of RM2.1 billion, 5% higher than the previous year’s RM2 billion, driven by both net interest income and non-interest income. Net profit was RM1.87 billion in FY2024. Net interest income rose 4.5% in FY2026, backed by higher margins, while non-interest income grew 5.1% mainly from trading gains. For FY2026, the bank recorded a return on equity (ROE) of 10%, in line with its guidance to analysts. The group’s ROE has stayed at 10% over the last three financial years. In the recent 1QFY2027 financial performance, AMMB’s net profit came in at RM520.23 million, up slightly from RM516.18 million in the previous year on account of improvement in net interest income growth. The earnings were within analyst expectations. Non-interest income grew 5.1% year on year, supported by stronger wealth management fee income but net interest income was softer, compressing to 1.93% in 1QFY2027 from 1.97% in 4QFY2026, as competitive asset pricing and funding mix pressures weighed on margins. CIMB Securities has downgraded its call on AMMB to “hold” with an unchanged target price of RM7.35, based on 1.09 times price-to-book value (PBV). “While we remain constructive on AMMB’s medium-term capital return and efficiency story, we believe the key rerating catalysts from its recent WT29 capital management update are largely priced in. The next catalyst, the Basel 3.1-driven capital release, remains some distance away given its implementation date of Jan 1, 2028,” said the research house in a report dated Aug 19. It added that while further rerating under the FY2028 valuation framework is possible, the rerating will need to be supported by earnings delivery rather than valuation roll-forward alone. Meanwhile, HLIB Research — which has kept its “buy” call on the stock for a target price of RM7.80 based on an implied 2027 PBV of 1.1 times — said its loan growth should remain firm going forward, led by mid-corporate and wholesale banking, adding that it should start contributing more meaningfully to non-interest income from 2QFY2027. Nonetheless, it also warned that the prolonged Middle East disruptions could create further stress among selected Business Banking accounts, although the management is expecting around half of the current stage 2 exposures to revert to stage 1 by September if logistics disruption normalises. HLIB Research added that the capital appreciation still has legs, “propelled by the plausible rerating catalyst of a potential RM2 billion capital return from FY2028”. It has estimated that the capital return could translate into a dividend yield of over 8.5% for 2028. Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower On Higher US Yields, West Asia Tensions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 – Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Thursday morning, tracking a mixed overnight performance on Wall Street as rising US Treasury yields and persistent geopolitical tensions in West Asia dampened investor appetite. At 9:10 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 3.74 points, or 0.22 per cent, to 1,647.43 compared to Wednesday’s closing level of 1,651.17. The key index opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth across the broader market was negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 200 to 142, while 307 counters traded unchanged, 2,124 untraded, and 12 suspended. Early turnover reached 246.59 million shares valued at RM118.14 million. Heavyweights and Active Counters Financial and utility heavyweights dragged on the benchmark index during early trade: - Public Bank fell 3 sen to RM4.67. - Tenaga Nasional lost 2 sen to RM12.94. - CIMB shed 1 sen to RM7.78. - Maybank and IHH Healthcare traded flat at RM9.90 and RM7.83, respectively. In active trading, ACE Market debutant GB Bond fell half a sen to 24.5 sen, while VS Industry traded unchanged at 28 sen. Divfex gained 2 sen to 11 sen, Jaks Resources rose 1 sen to 21.5 sen, and Astro Malaysia added half a sen to 6 sen. Energy and consumer-linked stocks featured among the top gainers: - Keck Seng advanced 11 sen to RM5.14. - Petron Malaysia picked up 7 sen to RM3.47. - Hengyuan Refining and Spritzer each rose 6 sen to RM3.62 and RM3.67, respectively. - Jati Tinggi gained 5 sen to RM1.44. Plantation and technology counters led early losses: - Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 18 sen to RM22.02. - UWC shed 15 sen to RM6.92. - Insights Analytics and MISC each declined 9 sen to RM1.20 and RM7.55, respectively. - Petronas Dagangan lost 8 sen to RM19.20. Index and Sectoral Trends Sectoral performance was mostly lower, with financial and plantation stocks leading the decline while energy counters bucked the trend: - The Plantation Index retreated 33.34 points to 9,163.33. - The Financial Services Index dropped 27.47 points to 19,189.02. - The Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 0.10 of a point to 180.31. - The Energy Index rose 1.41 points to 847.11. Across broader index boards: - The FBM Mid 70 Index dropped 42.26 points to 17,532.41. - The FBM Emas Index fell 26.32 points to 12,265.69. - The FBM Top 100 Index lost 27.82 points to 12,056.62. - The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 22.09 points to 12,154.26. - The FBM ACE Index trimmed 6.31 points to 5,527.97. –NMT

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends higher on positive regional sentiment
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended higher today, in line with gains across major Asian markets following Wall Street's overnight technology-led rally, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to temper risk appetite. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.60 points to 1,633.35 from Monday's close of 1,631.75. The benchmark index, which opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38, moved between 1,632.77 and 1,641.20 throughout the trading session. On the broader market, gainers surpassed decliners 667 to 456, while 551 counters were unchanged, 1,108 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover decreased to 4.18 billion units worth RM2.95 billion, compared with 4.78 billion units worth RM2.89 billion yesterday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.349 per cent, its highest since 2002, while the 30-year yield briefly reached 5.703 per cent. At the close on Monday, the S&P 500 gained 0.66 per cent to 7,773.95 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.05 per cent to 27,477.31. "On a positive note, Brent crude oil eased below US$100 per barrel as resilient West Asia exports and the Group of Seven's (G7) emergency stockpile release helped alleviate supply concerns," he told Bernama. Domestically, he said buying interest was seen in telecommunications and commodity-related stocks, while trading activity also broadened to selected small-cap technology, energy and plantation counters. "We believe selected blue chips could continue to attract bargain hunting following last week's sharp correction. "However, the lack of follow-through buying over the past three sessions suggests investors remain cautious, with persistent foreign selling and elevated bond yields likely to limit the pace of recovery," he said. Meanwhile, Thong said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 should provide some support to sentiment. "The 2027 Budget will be tabled on Friday, with strategic sectors including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, energy transition, pharmaceuticals, logistics, and aerospace among the areas highlighted by the government," he said. For the rest of the week, he expects the benchmark index to remain in consolidation mode, with a mild recovery bias as oversold conditions provide some downside support. "Nevertheless, a stronger recovery may require fresh catalysts, with Budget 2027, foreign fund flows, bond yields and geopolitical developments remaining key factors to watch. "We maintain our FBM KLCI trading range of 1,620-1,650 for the week," he added. Among the heavyweights, IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 15 sen to RM7.91, while Malayan Banking Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhdeased three sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.70, Public Bank Bhd shed four sen to RM4.67, and Tenaga Nasional Bhd slipped 10 sen to RM12.90. In active trade, Zetrix AI Bhd and Supermax Corp Bhd improved 2.5 sen to nine sen and 46 sen, respectively, Top Glove Corp Bhd put on nine sen to 87.5 sen, V.S Industry Bhd inched up one sen to 33 sen, while ACE Market debutant SLGC Bhd slid three sen to 25 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd increased RM1.56 to RM44.96, Nestle (M) Bhd rose RM1.26 to RM91.26, Pentamaster Corp Bhd leapt 64 sen to RM6.08, Mi Technovation Bhd jumped 59 sen to RM6.00, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd improved 46 sen to RM21.32. Top losers were led by Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd, which declined 30 sen to RM29.70, Allianz Malaysia Bhd fell 18 sen to RM20.62, TIME dotCom Bhd trimmed 16 sen to RM5.45, while Mega First Corp Bhd and Ayer Holdings Bhd shaved off 15 sen each to RM2.85 and RM7.55, respectively.

title: 'Hong Leong Bank Wins Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards In M'sia
body: 'Hong Leong Bank has been named Malaysia’s winner at the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026, taking the prize in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category. The bank was recognized for modernizing a critical online business application by moving away from a monolithic architecture to a containerized environment powered by Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. Hong Leong Bank’s Modernization Efforts Hong Leong Bank identified scalability limitations and manual processes within a legacy application architecture as key obstacles to its digital banking ambitions. To address this, the bank transitioned the application from a monolithic framework into a containerized environment using Red Hat OpenShift, while also deploying Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to modernize its existing database infrastructure. The deployment unified virtual machines and containers onto a single common platform, reducing the complexity of managing separate infrastructure stacks. Manual virtual machine patching for containerized workloads was also eliminated as part of the transition. The most measurable outcome from the shift is a dramatic reduction in software deployment cycles, which dropped from months to weeks – applications can now scale dynamically during traffic spikes, giving the bank the agility to deliver new digital banking features at a faster pace without compromising reliability. William Streitberg, Chief Information and Technology Officer at Hong Leong Bank, noted that updating infrastructure requires understanding the right fit for each operation, and that Red Hat has provided a common foundation for both existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing new capabilities to be introduced faster while maintaining the reliability customers expect. Daniel Aw, Vice President and General Manager for APAC at Red Hat, said that enterprise technology success is increasingly about how effectively solutions work together rather than how many new technologies an organisation adopts. He highlighted that this year’s award winners are building open, flexible foundations that allow them to innovate on their own terms. Red Hat positions open source as a response to growing complexity in AI, hybrid cloud, and automation strategies, where organisations need the flexibility to choose technologies best suited to their specific business requirements. Pokdepinion: Cutting deployment cycles from months to weeks is going to net them plenty of benefits down the line.

title: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Banking, Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Gamuda Bhd, QL Resources Bhd
body: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Banking, Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Gamuda Bhd, QL Resources Bhd This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Banking POSITIVE BIMB SECURITIES RESEARCH (Sept 22): Global bond markets experienced higher yields amid tighter US monetary policy and higher-for-longer interest rates. On Sept 16, the Federal Open Market Committee raised the federal funds rate target by 25 basis points (bps) to 3.75%-4.00%. The 10-year Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yield stands at 4.15% as at Sept 21, and remains elevated by historical standards but is still below the peak of 4.57% recorded in October 2022. According to our economist’s assessment, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to hover around the 4.0% level in the near term before gradually moderating towards the 3.75%-3.90% range by year end. Current yield levels appear to reflect market expectations of close to two policy rate hikes in Malaysia. However, given our view that the Overnight Policy Rate will remain unchanged at 2.75% throughout 2026 and 2027, coupled with a contained domestic inflation outlook, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to ease from its current elevated level over time. Banks typically maintain an average securities portfolio duration of around five to six years, which is considered moderate rather than long term. As a result, their investment portfolios are generally less sensitive to interest rate movements and face lower interest rate risk compared with portfolios concentrated on longer-dated securities. The impact on fair value through other comprehensive income securities is expected to result in lower FVOCI reserves due to revaluation losses in 3Q26, as the 10-year MGS yield is likely to remain elevated in the near term. Nevertheless, the effect on ROE could be favourable, as the decline in shareholders’ funds reduces the equity base used in the ROE calculation. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) (fair value: RM11.40), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) (FV: RM8.75) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) (FV:RM8.50), which have exposure to the Singapore market, are likely to see improved net interest margins as the rise in three-month Singapore overnight rate change (SORA), in tandem with Fed rate hikes, lifts asset yields and helps mitigate fair value through profit and loss (FVTPL) mark-to-market losses in 3Q26. Banks’ funding profiles remain largely anchored by longer-tenor liabilities, including Medium Term Notes with maturities of at least two to three years, which help maintain robust Net Stable Funding Ratio positions and reduce near-term refinancing pressures. As such, banks are unlikely to rush into refinancing and are more likely to adopt a wait-and-see approach when considering the rollover of maturing papers. We do not expect deposit competition to become more aggressive from here, given that 1Q26 and 2Q26 had already witnessed intense competition, with banks offering promotional fixed deposit rates of up to 3.7%-3.8% for 10- to 12-month placements. Solarvest Holdings Bhd Target price: RM4.50 BUY AMINVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 21): We believe that Solarvest Holdings Bhd (KL:SLVEST) would benefit from the government’s CRESS Acceleration Package. Under the package, a System Access Charge (SAC) of 14 sen/kWh will be introduced. We think that the lower SAC would spur the rollout of CRESS projects, as under the previous CRESS scheme, the SAC were perceived as too high. The SAC under the previous CRESS were 20 sen/kWh for projects with battery systems and 40 sen/kWh for projects without battery systems. We reckon that battery and solar systems contracts are worth about RM3.5million/mw to RM4million/mw based on recently announced projects. There is incentive for data centres to do solar under the new CRESS. This is because the tariffs under the new CRESS package would come up to about 45 to 50 sen/kWh compared with their present electricity tariffs of 50 to 60 sen/kWh. Solarvest is bidding for 11,800mw worth of projects. Out of these, about 1,200mw are expected to come from battery projects. We have raised Solarvest’s FY2028F net profit by 13.5% and FY29F net earnings by 40.4% to account for a higher EPCC (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) order book due to the new CRESS projects. Gamuda Bhd Target price: RM5.42 BUY TA SECURITIES (Sept 22): Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), via the Gamuda-BMD joint venture, has clinched the A$624 million (RM1.8 billion) Elizabeth Drive Upgrade — Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 Package from government agency Transport for New South Wales. Based on its 50% effective interest in the JV, Gamuda is entitled to roughly RM908 million in contract value. Given that the award also comes with cost-pass-through clauses, we believe this should limit Gamuda’s execution risk and exposure to volatile material prices. Based on the management-guided PBT margin of 5%, we estimate the project could generate approximately RM45.4 million in PBT over the contract period. Looking ahead, we expect Western Sydney’s rapid development to support sustained infrastructure spending, particularly across the road network. This should provide a healthy pipeline of replenishment opportunities for Gamuda. Gamuda’s FY2027 year-to-date new job wins have reached RM10.2 billion, lifting its unbilled construction order book to RM62.5 billion. We believe Gamuda’s near-term order book replenishment prospects remain healthy, with potential wins likely to come from data centre projects from new and repeat clients in Malaysia, renewable energy projects in Australia, particularly solar EPCCs (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) works, and railway infrastructure projects in Taiwan. QL Resources Bhd Target price: RM5.10 BUY HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 23): QL Resources Bhd’s (KL:QL)’s 1QFY2027 marine products manufacturing (MPM) revenue rose 18.2% year on year while PBT jumped 51.5%, with management attributing the bulk of the circa RM30 million y-o-y earnings uplift to fishmeal driven by Peru’s lower catch quota and a temporary El Niño fishing ban. Peru, which supplies roughly a fifth of the world’s fishmeal, in August called off its main anchovy season having landed only 25% of an already reduced quota. That keeps global supply tight, and fishmeal prices in July were still running about 11% above where they averaged through QL’s 1QFY27. Grade C egg prices recovered from the low RM0.20s in April to May to RM0.33 by end-June and >RM0.40 at the farm gate by August We remain constructive on QL, given that MPM is delivering into a supply shock with further runway into FY27, and did so in a seasonally soft quarter with the stronger quarters still ahead. Clean energy under BM Greentech Bhd (KL:BMGREEN] now has a working commercial proof point inside QL’s own plant while Innofood will begin contributing from 2HFY28. Integrated livestock farming and convenience store chain segments have, in our view, both passed their respective troughs, with egg prices recovering off the April low and FamilyMart's top line turning after three quarters of decline. title: 'Maybank completes Proposed Acquisition of remaining interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad | Maybank
body: 'Kuala Lumpur – Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) has today completed the proposed acquisition of the remaining 30.95% interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad (MAHB) (Proposed Acquisition) after signing a share purchase agreement (SPA) with Ageas Insurance International NV (Ageas) on 8 September 2026. This follows regulatory approvals from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) that were received on 1 September 2026 for the Proposed Acquisition. MAHB is the holding company for the Etiqa business in Malaysia and Singapore, providing a full range of life and general conventional insurance products as well as family and general takaful products through multi-channel distribution. President and Group CEO of Maybank, Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, said that this is a major milestone for Maybank as it continues to advance Etiqa’s ambition to be a national champion, expand across Southeast Asia and build a global takaful powerhouse under ROAR30. “With MAHB being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa’s position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank’s customer base. Our focus will be unlocking further value for our customers across Southeast Asia via our regional wealth propositions through cross-selling and delivering more integrated and personalised financial solutions. It will also enhance sustainable and resilient long-term value creation for Maybank with improved capital management within the MAHB group, hence facilitating more effective capital management at the Maybank group level.” “The Etiqa brand remains a strong and well-established insurance and takaful franchise, and it will continue to be positioned as one of Maybank’s flagship brands.” Meanwhile, MAHB is expected to remain well-positioned to capture growth opportunities in the insurance and takaful sector. This will be supported by Maybank’s extensive customer base and distribution network, and the increasing market demand for more integrated and personalised protection solutions. “We would also like to thank Ageas for their 25 years partnership with Maybank and contribution in developing the Etiqa franchise. Moving forward, the full ownership provides Maybank and MAHB with greater agility to accelerate product innovation, deepen bancassurance penetration and expand takaful propositions while enhancing capital and operational efficiency across the Group,” added Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli.
