title: 'Pintu itu terbuka pada tahun 2018. Ia boleh terbuka semula
body: 'Pada malam 9 Mei 2018, saya berada di rumah, terpaku di hadapan televisyen. Saya menonton dengan penuh keterujaan yang memuncak tatkala keputusan pilihan raya umum diumumkan sedikit demi sedikit. Menjelang akhir malam itu, pemerintahan selama lebih enam dekad oleh Barisan Nasional dan gabungan pendahulunya, Alliance atau Parti Perikatan, telah berakhir. Buat pertama kalinya, Malaysia menukar kerajaan persekutuannya menerusi peti undi. Rakyat telah memilih kerajaan Pakatan Harapan yang menjanjikan reformasi yang sekian lama dinanti-nantikan. Bagi ramai antara kita yang telah bertahun-tahun memperjuangkan reformasi, ia terasa seolah-olah sebuah keajaiban politik. Kita telah menyaksikan tatanan politik yang sama bertahan mengharungi pilihan raya demi pilihan raya serta protes demi protes. Kini, apa yang dahulunya dianggap mustahil, benar-benar telah berlaku. Sebuah pintu terbuka Perubahan itu membawa harapan. Timbul satu perasaan bahawa akhirnya sebuah pintu telah pun terbuka. Isu-isu yang sekian lama dibangkitkan oleh masyarakat sivil – kebebasan bersuara, akauntabiliti, kedaulatan undang-undang dan kebebasan institusi – tiba-tiba terasa seolah-olah boleh digapai. Namun, jangkaan sering kali dipengaruhi oleh keterujaan pada saat segalanya berlaku. Apabila euforia kian pudar, jelaslah bahawa pertukaran kerajaan dengan sendirinya tidak akan membawa reformasi. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Undang-undang, institusi dan amalan politik yang telah terbina selama berdekad-dekad tidak akan berubah dalam sekelip mata. Reformasi memerlukan masa, kehendak politik dan tekanan berterusan daripada orang ramai. Bulan-bulan awal kerajaan baharu itu kelihatan menjanjikan. Namun, kemajuan terbantut, dan peristiwa ‘Langkah Sheraton’ pada tahun 2020 menyebabkan kerajaan PH tumbang. Apa yang menyusul kemudian ialah satu tempoh ketidakstabilan politik yang melelahkan. Sebahagian besar harapan pada tahun 2018 akhirnya bertukar menjadi kekecewaan. Pilihan raya umum berikutnya pada bulan November 2022 membuka satu lagi peluang. Namun, tiada gabungan parti yang berjaya memperoleh majoriti. Anwar Ibrahim, yang sekian lama dianggap sebagai wajah gerakan reformasi, dilantik sebagai perdana menteri. ‘Kerajaan perpaduan’ pimpinannya turut merangkumi BN – gabungan yang telah ditentang oleh golongan reformis selama berdekad-dekad. Kembalinya PH ke tampuk kuasa disambut dengan rasa lega selepas bertahun-tahun dilanda ketidaktentuan. Walau bagaimanapun, orang ramai kekal berhati-hati, dan perasaan itu berasas. Boleh difahami jika reformasi mengambil masa. Namun, banyak reformasi yang sekian lama dituntut oleh masyarakat sivil telah ditangguhkan, dilemahkan atau diketepikan. Undang-undang yang bersifat menindas, seperti Akta Hasutan dan Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia, masih terus digunakan. Kadangkala ia digunakan oleh pihak-pihak yang suatu ketika dahulu pernah berkempen menentang undang-undang tersebut. Penahanan pemimpin Mandiri Layanan yang diterima baru-baru ini oleh kumpulan yang diterajui golongan muda, Mandiri, menunjukkan betapa jauh lagi perjalanan yang perlu ditempuhi. Menurut Mandiri, awal bulan ini [September], akaun bank mereka dibekukan dan larangan perjalanan dikenakan tanpa sebarang penjelasan kepada umum. Kemudian, pada 18 September, pihak polis menyerbu pejabat yang dikongsi oleh Mandiri dengan Hayat, sebuah kumpulan yang menentang hukuman mati. Seterusnya, pada 22 September, polis menahan pengarah eksekutif Mandiri, Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi, dan pengarah kewangannya, Dobby Chew, di bawah undang-undang pencegahan pengubahan wang haram. Mereka telah hadir secara sukarela di hadapan pegawai penyiasat untuk memberikan keterangan. Kedua-duanya kemudian dibebaskan, namun siasatan masih diteruskan. Walau apa pun kesudahannya, cara tindakan keras ini dilakukan menghantar mesej yang menggerunkan kepada sesiapa sahaja yang bersuara. Undang-undang yang bertujuan memerangi pengubahan wang haram tidak seharusnya digunakan untuk menakut-nakutkan masyarakat sivil. Perkara ini tidak boleh diterima di bawah kerajaan yang pernah berjanji untuk membuka ruang demokrasi. Pihak berkuasa mesti mendedahkan asas siasatan tersebut serta menarik balik pembekuan akaun dan larangan perjalanan yang dikenakan tanpa penjelasan. Mereka juga mesti menghentikan penggunaan kuasa pencegahan pengubahan wang haram terhadap kumpulan masyarakat sivil. Nampaknya, pertukaran pihak yang memerintah tidak menjamin perubahan dalam cara kuasa digunakan. Itulah sebabnya detik sekarang ini penting. Tekanan terhadap masyarakat sivil bukanlah satu isu terpencil. Ia merupakan sebahagian daripada kerja reformasi demokrasi yang belum selesai. Malah, kemajuan yang perlahan menjadikan peranan masyarakat sivil semakin penting, bukan sebaliknya. Apabila kerajaan bertukar tetapi struktur asas kekal, perlu ada pihak yang bersedia untuk mempersoalkan, meneliti dan menuntut akauntabiliti. Hal ini telah difahami oleh Aliran sejak ditubuhkan pada tahun 1977. Ia terus membangkitkan persoalan mengenai demokrasi, hak asasi manusia dan keadilan sosial di bawah setiap kerajaan yang pernah memerintah Malaysia. Setelah terlibat dengan Aliran selama hampir dua dekad, saya sendiri telah menyaksikan beberapa perubahan tersebut. Saya juga melihat betapa mudahnya untuk berasa tawar hati apabila, selepas bertahun-tahun berjuang, kemajuan tidak sentiasa dicapai sepantas yang kita harapkan. Harapan dalam perjuangan yang panjang Namun, kita juga harus mengingati tahun 2018. Selama bertahun-tahun, perubahan kelihatan mustahil. Kemudian, secara tidak disangka-sangka, ia berlaku. Perkara ini seharusnya membuatkan kita berhati-hati untuk tidak menganggap keadaan hari ini sebagai sesuatu yang kekal. Kita tidak tahu bila perubahan akan berlaku lagi, atau dalam bentuk apa ia akan muncul. Namun, masa depan tidak terikat kepada masa kini. Itulah erti harapan dalam sebuah perjuangan yang panjang. Ia bukanlah satu kepastian bahawa segala-galanya akan menjadi seperti yang kita inginkan. Ia adalah kesedaran bahawa keadaan boleh berubah, dan bahawa apa yang kita lakukan sementara itu penting. Václav Havel menghabiskan masa bertahun-tahun sebagai seorang disiden sebelum menjadi presiden Cekoslovakia yang bebas. Beliau mengungkapkannya begini: harapan “bukanlah keyakinan bahawa sesuatu perkara akan berakhir dengan baik, tetapi kepastian bahawa sesuatu perkara itu bermakna, tidak kira bagaimana kesudahannya nanti.” Perjuangan demi Malaysia yang lebih demokratik sejak awal lagi tidak mungkin dimenangi hanya melalui satu pilihan raya atau satu kerajaan. Pengajaran tahun 2018 bukanlah bahawa perubahan itu mudah. Pengajarannya ialah bahawa perubahan itu boleh berlaku. Dan apabila kemajuan kelihatan perlahan, itu sudah cukup menjadi alasan untuk kita terus melangkah. title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Laws alone will not shield our children online
body: 'AI and the relentless subscription to social media pose many new challenges to ordinary people, not just in Malaysia but around the world. The government deserves credit for introducing laws to safeguard the young from AI manipulation and social media abuse. New laws, new duties The Online Safety Act 2025 came into force on 1 January. This landmark law gives the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) sweeping powers to enforce safety standards on digital services. The laws aim to protect children from AI-generated child sexual abuse material, deepfakes, online grooming and voice cloning. They also shift responsibility from parents as watchdogs to digital platforms, which must have strict built-in accountability features. The Child Protection Code and the Risk Mitigation Code came into force on 1 June. They require platforms to build in ‘child-by-design’ safeguards. Platforms must also label AI-generated synthetic media, such as deepfakes, so young users and parents can spot manipulative or misleading content. Those that do not comply face fines of up to RM10m. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member There are also mandatory age-verification checks to stop children under 16 from registering for social media or high-risk content accounts. The Cybercrimes Bill 2026, passed in July, targets synthetic and AI-generated threats to children. Section 23 criminalises the use of deepfake technology to produce and spread harmful, malicious material. Section 24 outlaws the sharing of non-consensual intimate images. This extends protection to minors from AI that digitally alters school photos and similar images. The government has also set out seven key principles for responsible AI, focusing on reliability, safety, control, privacy and data security. These help protect children from AI tools that track data and use biased algorithms. The aim is a transparent, ethical system that acts as a shield for our most vulnerable – our children. Awareness must follow Other initiatives due in the months ahead include national digital literacy programmes. These aim to build resilience in children rather than rely on bans. The laws will need strong public awareness campaigns. They must reach not only consumers but also the AI back-end developers and social media programmers. Other ministries, including education and trade and economics, will need to work with the MCMC. Each should run campaigns covering the parts of the laws that apply to them. Only then can we hope for the vigilance needed to make these laws work. The video above, in which a mother describes how she lost her teenage son to the dangers of AI and social media, should send shivers down the spine. It is also a timely reminder to governments, leaders, parents, teachers and anyone else who helps protect the digital lives of children. However, given Malaysia’s track record of enthusiastic, knee-jerk reactions to new ideas that are quickly forgotten, there is much to worry about. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'Singapore’s strong economic growth masks cooling job market
body: 'AI adoption could reduce manpower needs, particularly in services sector, Maybank said.  Singapore’s strong economic growth is not translating into a comparable increase in employment, with job gains running well below the levels seen during previous economic booms, according to Maybank.  Employment excluding migrant domestic workers grew by 20,800 in the first half of 2026, while resident employment increased by 7,600. Real GDP, meanwhile, expanded 6.1% year on year over the same period.  During 2004-07, 2011-13 and 2021-22, average annual employment growth reached 133,000, whilst resident employment grew by an average 60,100.  “The Singapore economy is running hot on the AI boom, but the job market, paradoxically, appears to be cooling,” the bank said.  The current AI-driven and capital-intensive growth cycle is generating far fewer jobs, particularly in modern services, it noted.  Employment in financial, professional, and infocomm services increased by only 1,300 jobs in the second quarter of 2026, following contractions in the previous two quarters.  The labour market is also showing signs of weaker hiring and job mobility. Retrenchments rose to 4,600 in the second quarter, the highest level since the fourth quarter of 2020, with services accounting for most of the job cuts.  At the same time, the monthly recruitment rate fell to 1.4%, a historical low outside the pandemic years, whilst the monthly resignation rate declined to a record low of 1% in the second quarter.  The report describes Singapore’s labour market as “low-hire, low-quit,” reflecting subdued recruitment and job mobility alongside increased retrenchments.  The outlook is also expected to remain subdued despite continued GDP growth. Annual employment growth excluding migrant domestic workers is forecast to slow to 40,000 in 2026 and 35,000 in 2027, from 55,500 in 2025.  Resident employment growth is projected to be weaker at 12,000 in 2026 and 10,000 in 2027, compared with 11,600 in 2025. These would represent the most subdued employment growth figures since 2021.  Forward-looking surveys also point to cautious hiring. ManpowerGroup’s fourth-quarter Net Employment Outlook was stable from the previous quarter but moderated from a year earlier.  Separately, a Singapore National Employers Federation survey found that 54% of companies have no plans to increase headcount in 2027, whilst another 6% plan to cut jobs.  The report said existing government support measures could be expanded as workers face longer re-entry periods following retrenchment. These include SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support, which provides unemployed individuals with up to $6,000 over six months, as well as private and public sector traineeships, career transition measures, job placements, and Career Conversion Programmes that provide salary support to employers reskilling mid-career workers.  It also suggested raising the current $5,000 monthly income ceiling and extending the duration of financial support under the Jobseeker Scheme. Administrative minimum wage adjustments under the Progressive Wage Models may also need to be reviewed amid structural shifts in the resident labour market.  “Besides job security and unemployment, these structural shifts may have implications for retail spending; residential and commercial property demand; demographics; and widening income disparities,” the bank said.

title: 'HLB Islamic fund lifts Langkawi entrepreneurs’ income
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Aligned with its commitment to deepening its value-based intermediation (VBI) ecosystem, HLB Islamic has channeled RM138,600 in social financing towards social enterprise SURI Inspirasi under Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) iTEKAD framework, which has led to a 94% average surge in monthly income and over RM14,000 in total new earnings for participating entrepreneurs of SURI’s Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) programme. The SRI programme empowers underserved communities to upcycle discarded fabrics into unique fashion items, creating sustainable jobs and encouraging entrepreneurship while promoting zero-waste fashion and community empowerment. As part of the programme, the participating entrepreneurs, predominantly underserved single mothers, produced 1,000 school uniforms for students across five schools in Langkawi, generating RM30,000 in savings for local families. HLB Islamic commemorated the milestone through the handover of high-grade sewing machines to the participating entrepreneurs, marking the transition from classroom learning to active enterprise ownership. According to HLBIslamic CEO Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, “Our vision of financial stewardship is grounded in our Hayat @ HLB Islamic framework, which views wealth building as a purposeful journey across life stages, starting with wealth creation. Through our partnership with SURI, we are providing the community with the essential tools and training to unlock their entrepreneurial potential, and we hope this will catalyse a lifelong trajectory of building wealth towards financial independence that will enrich the community for generations to come.” This success marks a significant milestone in HLB Islamic’s ongoing collaboration with SURI, who first entered the bank’s ecosystem as a participant of the HLB Jumpstart initiative. Launched to incubate high-impact Malaysian social enterprises through commercial mentorship, branding, and digital capacity building, HLB Jumpstart provided SURI with the early framework to scale its operations, illustrating the bank’s long-term strategy of nurturing social ventures into self-sustaining implementation partners capable of delivering widespread impact.

title: 'Phoenix Distributing Expands Custom Home Builder Outreach with Addition of Dawn Lohr
body: 'Oct 6, 2026 Charleston-based residential fire protection company welcomes Dawn Lohr as Builder Partnerships Manager to strengthen relationships with custom home builders throughout the Lowcountry. Charleston, United States, October 6, 2026 -- Phoenix Distributing, LLC, a residential fire protection company specializing in residential fire sprinkler solutions, today announced that Dawn Lohr has joined the company as Builder Partnerships Manager. In her new role, Lohr will focus on developing and supporting relationships with custom home builders, developers and other residential construction professionals throughout the Charleston area and surrounding Lowcountry. As Phoenix Distributing continues expanding its residential fire sprinkler capabilities and builder-focused services, Lohr will serve as an important connection between the company and the residential construction community. Her responsibilities will include builder outreach, relationship development, educational initiatives and helping construction professionals better understand the planning and coordination involved in incorporating residential fire sprinkler systems into new homes. Dawn Lohr, Builder Partnerships Manager at Phoenix Distributing, works with a custom home builder on residential fire protection planning in the South Carolina Lowcountry. "Residential fire protection works best when it is considered early in the construction process and coordinated closely with the builder," said Phoenix Distributing CEO Charlie Stewart. "Dawn's ability to build relationships and communicate effectively makes her an excellent fit for what we're building at Phoenix. We want builders to view us as a long-term residential fire protection partner rather than simply another subcontractor." Lohr is based in Charleston and holds a degree in Marketing from Loyola University Maryland. She brings an entrepreneurial background and extensive experience building relationships, communicating with diverse audiences and developing community connections. In addition to her business career, Lohr is a published author and speaker. "I am excited to join Phoenix Distributing and have the opportunity to work directly with builders throughout the Lowcountry," said Lohr. "Residential fire sprinklers are an important part of protecting families and homes, and I look forward to helping builders better understand the solutions, resources and support Phoenix can provide." Phoenix Distributing works with custom home builders, developers, contractors, plumbing professionals and other industry partners to provide residential fire sprinkler expertise from project planning and design through supply, installation and inspection support. The company's approach is designed to make residential fire protection easier to coordinate within the home-building process while supporting applicable project and code requirements. The addition of Lohr comes as Phoenix increases its outreach to custom home builders throughout coastal South Carolina, including the greater Charleston area and communities extending along the Lowcountry coast. About Phoenix Distributing, LLC Phoenix Distributing, LLC specializes in residential fire protection solutions with decades of industry experience in residential fire sprinkler design, supply, installation and support. Through its specialized brands and operating companies, Phoenix provides builders and industry professionals with an integrated resource for residential fire sprinkler systems, technical expertise, education and field support. Phoenix is committed to advancing residential fire protection through professional expertise, education, innovation and strong partnerships with the building community. For more information, visit PhoenixHomeFireSprinklers.com. title: 'High-flying Miyu of Japan and Thai darling Jeeno Thitikul lead a world-class field of champions at the 2026 Maybank Championship
body: 'The Maybank Championship is set for another star-studded chapter when Asia’s premier ladies’ golf event returns to Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC) this October 29-November 1. With a US$3 million prize purse, the fourth edition brings together Major champions, LPGA Tour winners and Southeast Asia’s emerging talents for four days of world-class competition at KLGCC. The competition for the coveted Tiger Trophy has never been more intense. Defending champion and Major winner Miyu Yamashita of Japan is one of the season's most in-form players, highlighted by a dominant nine-stroke victory at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada in August and a playoff win at the Sony JLPGA Championship in Japan in September. Having claimed a dramatic three-way playoff victory at last year’s Maybank Championship, she will have every intention of becoming the tournament’s first repeat champion. Crowd favourite, Thai darling and World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand is also on a rich vein of form, having already claimed three LPGA Tour victories in 2026 to take her total title tally to ten. She returns for a fourth consecutive year in pursuit of the elusive Tiger Trophy, having narrowly missed out in each of her last appearances. Thitikul’s close friend Ruoning Yin of China, the 2024 Maybank Championship winner and a Major champion, will also return to Malaysia in winning mode having triumphed at the FM Championship in August. The spotlight will also firmly be turned on Korean ace Haeran Ryu, who is currently second on the LPGA Tour’s Race to CME Globe ranking on the back of successive Major victories in 2026 at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship and the Amundi Evian Championship. Adding her considerable star power to the field is the perennially popular New Zealander Lydia Ko, a three-time Major winner and reigning Olympic champion who was inducted into the LPGA Hall of Fame in 2024 at age 27. Australian stalwart Hannah Green and Hye-Jin Choi of South Korea, who were the two other protagonists in last year's playoff, will return with unfinished business on their agendas. 2023 Maybank Championship winner Céline Boutier of France, who edged Thitikul in a nail-biting nine-hole playoff at KLGCC three years ago, is also in the field. Other fan favourites who have signed up include emerging English sensation Lottie Woad and her experienced compatriot Charley Hull, and Japanese twins Aki and Chizzy Iwai. The identical twins have been in roaring form this season and will be among the frontrunners for the title. The Maybank Championship is more than Asia’s premier golf event. It provides a distinctive regional pathway for Southeast Asian talent to earn their place alongside the world’s best. This year, five players who earned their places through the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier bring that story to life. Held in August at KLGCC’s West Course, the 36-hole qualifier concluded with Thai professional Pimnipa Panthong and her amateur compatriots Sarisa Pojanalai and Achiraya Sriwong locked together at four-under-par 140 (Sriwong turned professional recently). Standout Thai amateur Marisa Tojai, who had already claimed four amateur titles in 2026 before arriving at the qualifier, secured the fourth spot at two-under 142, while Malaysia’s Liyana Durisic rounded out the top five at one-under 143. For Malaysian fans, there will be plenty to roar about. Liyana Durisic is currently in great form, having already claimed four PGM Tour titles in 2026, and the Women’s World Sand Greens Championship held in Australia in March. She will be joined by a talented and recognisable group of Malaysian players entering as Sponsor’s Invitations, namely Mirabel Ting, Jeneath Wong, Natasha Oon and Kelly Tan, to make up a five-strong Malaysian challenge. 2025 Annika Award winner Mirabel Ting made headlines in 2024 by becoming the highest-finishing Malaysian in Maybank Championship history, with a T12 finish as an amateur. Her fine performances continued into her debut season on this year’s Epson Tour, helping her clinch two victories in 2026. The wins propelled Ting to the top of the Epson Tour’s Race for the Card standings and secured her place on the LPGA Tour for the 2027 season. Joining Ting is Malaysia’s highest-ranked amateur (currently ranked 59th), Jeneath Wong. After a stellar season in 2023 that saw her earn her a major championship start at the US Women's Open, Wong made history as the first Malaysian to win the Women's Amateur Asia-Pacific Championship in 2025, a victory which earned her further major championship starts, bringing an increasingly impressive international résumé to KLGCC. One-time Epson Tour winner and 2023 Epson Tour Rookie of the Year Natasha Oon makes her first appearance at the Maybank Championship since 2023, seeking to capitalise on her encouraging performance at the recent CPKC Women’s Open. The LPGA Tour rookie is rebuilding her momentum following a lengthy injury that saw her miss most of the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Completing the Malaysian line-up is two-time Olympian Kelly Tan, Malaysia's most successful LPGA Tour player. Tan recorded her career-best results on the LPGA Tour with runner-up finishes at the Dow Great Lakes Bay Invitational in 2022 and 2023, and returns to KLGCC for the third time, bringing over a decade of elite professional experience on the West Course.

title: 'IOI Properties Now Agrees to Buy Shenton House From Group CEO for S$1 and Settle S$217m Advance
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, which owns Singapore's Shenton House, from its group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng for a nominal S$1.00. Under the deal, announced in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, IOI Properties will also settle S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) worth of shareholder advances that Yeow Seng injected into Shenton 101 — the vehicle he incorporated to acquire the property. It will also consolidate the vehicle’s S$376.23 million borrowings into its accounts upon completion of the deal. Both figures were as of July 31, 2026. The transaction marks a reversal by the group’s non-interested directors, who rejected Yeow Seng's proposal to sell Shenton 101 to IOI Properties in August 2024, citing heavy capital commitments from several acquisitions at the time. Yeow Seng had proposed the sale to avoid a potential conflict of interest as he acquired the property in his personal capacity. To mitigate that, IOI Properties entered into project and property management agreements for the building instead. Shenton 101 won the tender to acquire Shenton House — a 25-storey strata-titled commercial development completed in the mid-1970s sitting on a 3,377-sq-metre site — for S$538 million in November 2023, with the purchase completed in June 2024. The acquisition, which will be funded through IOI Properties’ internal funds, does not require shareholder approval as it makes up just 3.79% of IOI Properties’ total assets, below the 5% materiality threshold under listing rules that would require a shareholder vote. However, it will require Bank Negara Malaysia's green light as the foreign currency investment exceeds the group's permissible limit, as well as consent from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority. IOI Properties said the acquisition will allow it to strengthen its presence in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and unlock synergies with its existing asset portfolio, given Shenton House's walking distance to IOI Central Boulevard Towers and the recently acquired Asia Square Tower 2. The group said it is revisiting the deal, on Yeow Seng's request, after its "circumstances and strategic position have evolved". It pointed out that IOI Central Boulevard Towers has achieved over 95% committed occupancy and is self-sustaining in debt servicing. It has also completed the acquisitions of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties Pte Ltd — which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach — and Asia Square Tower 2. It noted that its acquisitions in Malaysia have also continued to perform satisfactorily, and that shareholders had, on Sept 30, approved injecting W Kuala Lumpur hotel and Courtyard by Marriott Penang hotel into the upcoming IOI Properties REIT, in support of the group's capital recycling strategy. “Although the group’s gearing has increased, the increase is largely attributable to acquisitions of income-generating assets in Singapore that have enhanced the quality of the group's investment property portfolio and strengthened its position in key gateway markets,” it said. IOI Properties' net gearing, which stood at 0.70 times as at June 30, 2025, is projected to hit 1.03 times after its recent acquisitions and REIT listing, and rise further to 1.10 times following the Shenton 101 deal. The group plans to redevelop Shenton House into a 35-storey mixed-use landmark featuring 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 10-storey luxury hotel (165 keys), a retail basement and three carpark levels. This will expand its total net lettable area from 20,276 sq metres (218,246 sq ft) to 36,528 sq metres (393,185 sq ft). The underlying land tenure, which has a remaining lease of about 42 years, is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year term. Savills appraised the market value of Shenton House as a redevelopment site at S$585 million, with an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion against total redevelopment costs of S$973.65 million. Maybank Investment Bank is the principal adviser for the exercise, which is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Although not mandated by listing rules, IOI Properties also appointed Affin Hwang Investment Bank as an independent adviser to advise non-interested directors on the deal's fairness and reasonableness. Yeow Seng and his brother Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is a non-independent non-executive director, are deemed interested parties and have abstained from all board deliberations and voting on the proposal. The Lee family's private vehicle, Vertical Capacity Sdn Bhd, holds a controlling 65.673% stake in IOI Properties, while Yeow Seng directly holds 3.768% and Yeow Chor has 0.012%. The Employees Provident Fund is the largest institutional shareholder in IOI Properties, with a 7.496% stake. Shares of IOI Properties closed six sen or 1.73% lower at RM3.40 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM18.72 billion. title: 'Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market
body: 'Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 FOR engineering outfit owner John, using artificial intelligence (AI) in his work has been a game changer. He “trains” the AI to write codes in the company’s style and now merely checks to ensure that the codes are written correctly. “I use AI to write more routine codes and it has helped me cut down coding time significantly, where a few days of work can be accomplished in 20 minutes. But I still need a few employees because engineers need to be at the physical location to make sure hardware is properly installed and conduct test runs,” he says. These days, the use of AI is prevalent in all aspects of life, in various sectors of the economy and professions, and more so among white-collar workers. Early research has shown that AI has, by some measure, improved the productivity of workers, but it still depends on the complexity of tasks and the user’s ability in AI prompting. Even so, AI is increasingly becoming part of everyday life. As a result, companies will soon be able to achieve the same outcomes with fewer workers — or, in some roles, none at all. The concern among white-collar workers about AI displacing jobs is real. Jobstreet’s Workplace Happiness Index found that while only around one-third of Malaysian workers feel “very” or “extremely” concerned about AI affecting their job security, the score is even higher among professional services workers, coming in at 47%. While there is no evidence of massive job loss as a result of AI at this juncture, recruitment agencies observe that job postings for certain roles have been declining. Jobstreet by SEEK in Malaysia managing director Nicholas Lam says AI is certainly putting pressure on some forms of white-collar work, particularly roles involving repetitive, standardised or administrative tasks, many of which are being automated. Current data points, however, more towards roles being redesigned than entire professions being replaced. “The clearest early signs of pressure are in selected content and administrative roles. Job ads for positions such as content writer, copywriter, secretary and graphic designer declined between 2024 and 1H2026. We see these trends as directional indicators that automation may be changing how these roles are structured, rather than proof of one-for-one job replacement,” Lam says. This observation is consistent with a May report by the International Labour Organization (ILO), which found that studies using job postings and online labour-platform data show a significant decline in demand for skills associated with routine writing and translation, following the diffusion of generative AI (GenAI) tools, alongside increased demand for AI-related skills such as machine learning and natural language processing. PwC Malaysia managing partner Soo Hoo Khoon Yean argues that the gradual redesign of work does not necessarily imply that workers will be displaced. Instead, he says, it points to a gradual shift in the mix of capabilities and skills required in those roles. “There may be a growing divide between workers who are able to integrate AI into their workflows and adapt to evolving skill requirements, and those who are unable to,” Soo Hoo says. “As AI becomes more capable, competitive advantage will increasingly come from areas where human strengths like context, judgement and accountability matter most. This includes making high-stakes decisions, solving nuanced problems, managing stakeholder relationships, and bringing together insights from different disciplines to create solutions that AI alone cannot deliver.” Such expectations are starting to show up in the hiring landscape in Malaysia, with AI or digital tools becoming more common in the workplace. Randstad Malaysia associate director, emerging technology recruitment Dylan Long sees a clear shift in Malaysia’s hiring landscape, where employers are increasingly prioritising talent who are adept in AI and digital tools. “This trend is no longer confined to specialised tech departments; instead, having basic knowledge and practical experience with AI has rapidly evolved into a fundamental, baseline requirement for almost any professional role. There is an immense demand for individuals who demonstrate high digital agility,” Long says. He adds that a proactive willingness to embrace self-directed learning and integrate AI into one’s routine work has become a powerful, highly attractive differentiator in the current market. Statistics from Jobstreet confirm this change in the hiring landscape. According to Lam, the recruitment agency’s data shows that 70% of employers factor AI knowledge into hiring decisions, while one in three treat AI capability as a core hiring requirement. At the same time, demand for dedicated AI hiring is also increasing rapidly, notes Lam. AI-labelled job ads grew by 131% year on year in 2025. In 1H2026, the number of AI-labelled job ads was already 24% higher than the total for the whole of 2025, he says. One question that has often been raised is whether junior hiring will be reduced as a result of AI proliferation. A Gartner Inc survey carried out late last year found that 22% of chief human resources officers in the US reported that at least one business leader in their organisation has stopped hiring for entry-level roles as a result of AI automation. Some argue that removing the routine or repetitive tasks traditionally assigned to junior staff — often a training ground for developing judgement and gaining crucial experience — could ultimately hurt organisations by weakening their future talent pipeline. According to Soo Hoo, however, PwC’s global research shows that the bar is now higher for junior talent, with emotional quotient, judgement and leadership skills — qualities normally expected of senior hires — being prioritised. “Organisations will need to rethink how early-career talent is developed, including creating new pathways through which early-career employees can learn through application and experience,” he says. “Traditional apprenticeship models built largely around repetitive tasks may need to evolve into more structured experiences that accelerate the development of these broader capabilities.” Sufficient AI talent in Malaysia? While employers today want workers who can use AI in ways that help create value, there is also a need for AI developer roles in the country, notes Soo Hoo. “Malaysia needs to strengthen both the depth and breadth of its AI talent base. Findings from our 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer indicate that AI-related roles in Malaysia are currently concentrated in roles that apply AI in business functions (AI user roles) rather than roles focused on developing core AI technologies (AI developer roles),” he says. Soo Hoo cautions that the pipeline of specialised AI talent in Malaysia may not be sustainable for the country’s long-term ambitions, given the pace at which AI is evolving. “Malaysia needs both AI user and AI developer roles in our journey towards realising our AI Nation 2030 aspirations. We need to expand the pool of highly specialised engineers, data scientists and technical experts who can develop and commercialise homegrown digital innovation. At the same time, we must equip workers across sectors with AI literacy, applied skills and judgement to use these technologies productively and responsibly,” he explains. Having said that, every paradigm change will have its drawbacks. Human resources practitioners are reporting that, because of the speed at which the AI world is moving, employees are starting to experience AI fatigue, or “AI brain fry”, as they try to keep pace with the changes. “Companies need to think about the pace at which and direction in which they are adopting AI in their systems and processes. AI fatigue is a real issue and it’s not because employees are not eager to learn. This could result in a decrease, instead of an increase, in efficiency and productivity,” says an HR practitioner. A human resources director with a local company says some employees might not want to go down the AI rabbit hole. “We have reskilling programmes where we reassign certain affected roles to other areas in the company. But some of our employees, typically those who are closer to retirement, say they would rather opt for an early retirement plan, instead of reskilling,” notes the director. State of the labour market Minister of Economic Affairs Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said last Friday that a total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs from January to Sept 16, representing an increase of 15,196 over the same period last year. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. title: 'AKPK Celebrates 20 Years with Strategic Partnership Program
body: 'Accra:The Credit Counselling and Debt Management Agency (AKPK) marked its 20th anniversary by hosting the 'Rencah Kita Pelbagai Rasa, Satu Makna' programme, aimed at strengthening relationships with strategic partners. According to BERNAMA News Agency, AKPK's chief executive officer, Azman Hasim, highlighted that the cooking challenge, organized in collaboration with M Resort and Hotel, included 30 agencies such as financial service providers, media partners, and other strategic partners. The event symbolized the blending of diverse strengths and expertise to enhance financial resilience among Malaysians. Azman emphasized that the agency's anniversary reflects the collective success of various parties working towards a unified goal. He likened the impact of their work to a well-prepared dish, underscoring the importance of understanding each component's role in achieving meaningful outcomes. He also noted that each AKPK undertaking involves real people with lives that need support and rebuilding. The event underscored the importance of strategic partnerships in providing the necessary guidance and confidence to help individuals overcome financial challenges. The primary focus of the day was the relationships and communication fostered through the challenge, rather than the competition itself. Azman reiterated that while participants have different perspectives, they share a common goal of improving the wellbeing of Malaysians. The annual event, which introduces new activities each year, serves as a platform to honor the strategic partners that have contributed to AKPK's success over the past two decades. Notable participants included Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), CIMB Bank Berhad (CIMB), Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, and AmBank (M) Bhd.

title: 'Maybank Matches Up To RM250 In ASNB Units
body: '7th September 2026 - 3 min read Maybank and Amanah Saham Nasional Berhad (ASNB) are running the ASNB Invest & Win Campaign 2026, letting eligible customers who invest in ASNB funds stand a chance to win ASNB units worth up to RM250. The campaign runs from 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, split into five monthly phases. To earn an entry, you’ll need to make at least two ASNB investments, in any fund, within the same phase. There’s no cap on the number of entries you can earn. To stand a chance at the full RM250, your total investment within that phase needs to reach at least RM250. If your total is lower, the prize you could win matches that lower amount instead. Each phase draws 148 winners, adding up to 740 across the whole campaign. Each customer can only win once during the entire campaign period, even if they qualify for multiple entries. Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) units, or ASB 2 or ASB 3 Didik units if their ASB limit has been reached. Non-Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Nasional Equity 5 or Amanah Saham Nasional Sukuk units, depending on fund availability. If a winner has reached the investment limit across all applicable funds, they’ll receive cashback of the same value instead. Winners are selected through a randomiser system on Maybank’s data platform, with witnesses present to verify the process. Only investments made through the MAE app or Maybank2u website count toward this campaign. Investments made at Maybank branches or through the standalone myASNB app don’t qualify, even though they’re valid ways to invest in ASNB. You can start investing in ASNB funds from as low as RM10 on the MAE app (download via Apple or Google Play) or visit Maybank2u. Via the MAE app: Via Maybank2u: There’s no fixed lock-in period, though redemptions are subject to standard settlement timelines. Winning units are credited within 90 days after the campaign ends, and your ASNB account needs to remain active, not dormant or closed, for the prize to be paid out. title: 'FBM KLCI Rebounds Slightly on Fed Pause Hopes
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The FBM KLCI opened higher on Monday, rising 4.53 points to 1,635.39 at 9.05am, supported by weaker U.S. jobs data that eased inflation concerns and strengthened expectations of a Federal Reserve rate pause. FBM KLCI Rebounds Banking stocks led gains, with Maybank up four sen to RM10.06, Hong Leong Bank adding six sen to RM22.70, Public Bank climbing four sen to RM4.70 and AMMB rising six sen to RM6.45. Among actively traded counters, VS Industry gained three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTech rose 4.5 sen to 75 sen, and GB Bond added 1.5 sen to 24.5 sen. title: 'Maybank raises Malaysia and ASEAN-6 growth forecasts as Invest ASEAN 2026 opens in Singapore
body: 'Around 200 institutional investors are gathering in Singapore for Maybank's flagship Invest ASEAN conference, as the bank lifts its 2026 GDP growth outlook for Malaysia and the wider ASEAN-6 region. Around 200 institutional investors and prime brokerage clients with a combined $23 trillion (MYR93 trillion) in global assets under management are convening at Maybank Investment Banking Group's ("Maybank IBG") flagship event, Invest ASEAN, on 7-8 July in Singapore. The event connects investors with 54 companies including a sovereign wealth fund, alongside meetings with key government bodies in Singapore. The companies are from ASEAN-6 markets (Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam) and India, representing total market capitalisation of $553 billion. Spanning banking, technology, consumer, healthcare, manufacturing and renewable energy sectors, the companies were selected based on clients' preferred names, a mix of mid and large caps, readiness to engage with global investors and Maybank IBG's research views. Michael Oh-Lau, chief executive officer, Maybank Investment Banking Group said, "Now in its 13th edition, Invest ASEAN reinforces Maybank's long-standing commitment to connecting investors with companies while providing the insights and conviction needed to navigate today's evolving global landscape. This year's attendance surpassed our expectations, highlighting sustained interest from both global and local investors in ASEAN as the region continues to demonstrate resilience amid global uncertainties. Energy transition, supply chain reconfiguration and AI-led digital transformation are key themes at this year's Invest ASEAN, and we expect these trends to continue over the next few years." Reflecting improved conditions, Maybank's research has revised its ASEAN-6 GDP growth forecast upwards to +4.7% from its estimate of +4.5% in March (2027E: +4.7%). Oil prices have fallen from their peak to near pre-war levels and tanker traffic via the Strait of Hormuz is recovering. In Malaysia, Maybank has revised its full-year 2026 GDP growth forecast upwards to 4.9% from 4.4%, reflecting resilient economic momentum in the first half of the year despite the heightened geopolitical risks. Economic indicators for April and May point to another quarter of growth above 5%, underpinned by robust manufacturing activities and stronger net exports as Malaysia benefits from the AI-driven technology upcycle, and being a net energy exporter amid higher commodity prices. Outlook for the second half of 2026 remains healthy, especially amid the sustained momentum in investment approvals, particularly in technology, renewable energy, industrial real estate and infrastructure segments. Maybank also remains positive on the market, with a year-end FBM KLCI target of 1,750 based on 7.5% earnings growth, sustained investment upcycle effects, stable consumer essentials spending and steady foreign participation. The expansion of KLCI to 50 constituents, from 30 currently, promises to reinvigorate broader sectoral picks whilst benefitting from the momentum of the MY Value Up initiative. As AI and data centre themes take centre stage, Maybank has upgraded its view on the technology sector, which is expected to benefit from these long-term structural growth drivers. title: 'Expedite political will to guarantee people’s right to know
body: 'On the International Day for Universal Access to Information on 28 September, the Centre for Independent Journalism (CIJ), Article 19 and the Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Center) call on the Malaysian government and Parliament to make the right to access information a meaningful and accessible right, and not merely a promise of reform. The UN has designated this year’s theme as ‘Upholding information integrity in the digital age: the role of access to information in addressing information disorder’. Reliable, timely and credible public information is essential to informed participation, accountability and trust in public institutions. Malaysia stands at a critical juncture. Parliament is considering the nation’s first federal freedom of information law, while serious questions remain about the transparency, legal basis, and implementation of Najib Razak’s conditional pardon and house arrest. These are not separate transparency failures. They expose the same problem: Malaysians cannot hold institutions accountable when the government makes decisions behind a wall of secrecy. We acknowledge the government’s decision to introduce a federal Freedom of Information Bill and welcome its referral to a parliamentary special select committee following its first reading in July 2026. However, as our organisations have stated, the bill, as tabled, falls far short of what ordinary people should expect from landmark transparency legislation. The Centre for Law and Democracy’s assessment subsequently gave the bill 47 out of 150 points under its right to information rating methodology, highlighting the extent to which the proposed framework needs improvement. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member The bill must be strengthened into an enforceable right to know act, consistent with Article 10(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution, international law and standards and the recommendations of Malaysian and international civil society. Malaysia must end the culture of secrecy that continues to shield the exercise of power from public scrutiny. The government cannot credibly champion transparency while limiting the public’s access to information about decisions of profound public interest, including from the laws governing access to information itself. The government must demonstrate its political will and commitment to transparency by applying these principles across the board and not letting them remain mere lip service to garner votes. On this International Day for Universal Access to Information, we call on the government and Parliament to act. The government and Parliament must: Strengthen the bill, currently under the purview of the special select committee, into an enforceable right to know act, consistent with international laws and standards and the recommendations from civil society groups. It must: - Uphold the constitutional guarantee under Article 10(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution and guarantee freedom of information as a pre-condition to the realisation of the freedom of expression and speech - Make disclosure the rule and secrecy the exception, with narrowly defined exemptions based on demonstrable harm and subject to a strong public-interest override - Ensure the freedom of information law cannot be undermined by existing secrecy provisions, including the Official Secrets Act - Remove unnecessary restrictions on who can request information and ensure everyone can exercise the right without having to demonstrate a particular interest or purpose - Establish a freedom of information commission as an independent oversight body, with the power to review refusals, order disclosure and monitor the implementation of the freedom of information law - Require proactive disclosure of information and documents of significant public interest - Make the parliamentary freedom of information process transparent and participatory, including publication of submissions, recommendations and the revised bill Guarantee prompt disclosure and publication of the documents necessary for the public to understand the decision regarding the conditional pardon of Najib Razak, as demanded by CIJ and other civil society organisations, including: - The relevant pardons board minutes - The Attorney General’s written submission, subject only to narrowly justified redactions - The full conditions governing the house arrest arrangement - The legal basis for implementing house arrest and its relationship with existing laws - The mechanisms for monitoring and enforcing compliance - Significant public expenditure associated with the arrangement. These demands do not challenge the constitutional existence of the power of pardon. They demand transparency about the exercise and implementation of authority’s power. Constitutional powers are not a licence for institutional secrecy. The Government has repeatedly committed itself to institutional reform, good governance and restoring public confidence. The test of those commitments is whether transparency is upheld when disclosure is difficult, politically sensitive or institutionally consequential. We believe that a freedom of information law that leaves the underlying culture of secrecy intact will not deliver meaningful reform. In the spirit of this international day, we call on Malaysia to move from promises of transparency to a legally enforceable culture of openness. Ordinary people have the right to know. Disclosure of information held by government and public authorities is necessary to scrutinise the exercise of public power. This ensures that no institution is beyond legitimate public accountability. The right to information is not a concession from government. It is a foundation of accountable government. This legislation is essential to guarantee the public’s collective right to be informed by public authorities about important aspects of their functioning; the right to seek or request information; and the right to be informed and to receive information about various aspects of the public sphere. We are also pleased to launch our campaign demonstrating the level of support from our MPs for the guarantee of a robust bill. Look out for more information on our social media in the coming days. Issued by: - Wathshlah Naidu, Centre for Independent Journalism - Nalini Elumalai, Article 19 - Prishanth Linggaraj, C4 Center The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'Bursa dibuka rendah pada pagi ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah pada Khamis, menjejaki prestasi bercampur-campur Wall Street berikutan hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS yang lebih tinggi serta ketegangan berterusan di Asia Barat menjejaskan minat belian. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) susut 3.74 mata atau 0.22 peratus kepada 1,647.43 daripada paras 1,651.17 ketika ditutup pada Rabu. Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 1.30 mata lebih rendah pada 1,649.87. Di pasaran meluas, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 200 berbanding 142, manakala 307 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,124 kaunter tidak diniagakan dan 12 kaunter digantung. Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 246.59 juta saham bernilai RM118.14 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata Wall Street ditutup bercampur-campur apabila inflasi yang lebih rendah mengurangkan jangkaan terhadap satu lagi kenaikan kadar faedah oleh Rizab Persekutuan AS, meskipun hasil bon yang kekal tinggi terus menjejaskan sentimen. Di peringkat domestik, beliau berkata, indeks penanda aras pasaran mungkin cenderung diniagakan berhati-hati, dengan sentimen keseluruhan pasaran yang lemah dan jualan asing baru-baru ini menunjukkan pelabur terus mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati. “Justeru, bagi hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks kekal dalam mod pengukuhan dalam julat 1,640-1,660, dengan aktiviti pembelian ketika harga rendah dijangka mengehadkan penurunan,” katanya kepada Bernama. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank dan IHH Healthcare masing-masing tidak berubah pada RM9.90 dan RM7.83. Public Bank susut tiga sen kepada RM4.67, CIMB berkurangan satu sen kepada RM7.78 dan Tenaga Nasional turun dua sen kepada RM12.94. Dalam dagangan aktif, saham yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE, GB Bond susut setengah sen kepada 24.5 sen, manakala VS Industry tidak berubah pada 28 sen. Astro Malaysia menambah setengah sen kepada enam sen, Jaks Resources meningkat satu sen kepada 21.5 sen dan Divfex menokok dua sen kepada 11 sen. Antara kaunter untung utama, Keck Seng meningkat 11 sen kepada RM5.14 dan Petron Malaysia menambah tujuh sen kepada RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining dan Spritzer masing-masing naik enam sen kepada RM3.62 dan RM3.67, manakala Jati Tinggi mengukuh lima sen kepada RM1.44. Kuala Lumpur Kepong mendahului kaunter rugi apabila susut 18 sen kepada RM22.02. UWC pula berkurangan 15 sen kepada RM6.92, manakala Insights Analytics dan MISC masing-masing turun sembilan sen kepada RM1.20 dan RM7.55. Petronas Dagangan susut lapan sen kepada RM19.20. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 susut 42.26 mata kepada 17,532.41, Indeks FBM Emas berkurangan 26.32 mata kepada 12,265.69, manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 turun 27.82 mata kepada 12,056.62. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah susut 22.09 mata kepada 12,154.26, manakala Indeks FBM ACE berkurangan 6.31 mata kepada 5,527.97. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian susut 0.10 mata kepada 180.31, manakala Indeks Tenaga meningkat 1.41 mata kepada 847.11. Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan turun 27.47 mata kepada 19,189.02, manakala Indeks Perladangan merosot 33.34 mata kepada 9,163.33. — BERNAMA

title: 'Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities
body: 'Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 25): Malaysian plantation companies with sizeable operations in Indonesia face greater regulatory uncertainty following the country’s new agrarian reform law, with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG), Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KL:KLK) among those with the largest exposure, according to CIMB Securities. The potential impact, however, remains unclear as key details — including maximum landholding limits for companies and affiliated entities, and how a provision requiring at least 20% of certain land to be made available for agrarian reform and redistribution — have yet to be finalised through implementing regulations. As such, CIMB has not made any adjustments to its earnings forecasts or the land banks of plantation companies under its coverage, saying it sees higher regulatory uncertainty rather than an immediate loss of land or earnings. “We do not expect an across-the-board 20% cut in existing land,” the research house said in a note on Friday. Indonesia’s parliament approved the Agrarian Reform Law on Tuesday, creating a broader framework to address land ownership concentration, redistribution and longstanding agrarian conflicts. The law also provides for a dedicated body under the president to oversee implementation, supervision and conflict resolution. However, the Indonesian government still needs to draw up implementing rules that will, among other matters, determine minimum and maximum landholding limits. Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning Minister Nusron Wahid said such details would be provided through subsequent regulations. The development was reported earlier this week, including by Bloomberg, which highlighted broader risks to Indonesia’s plantation and property sectors. CIMB’s latest assessment focuses on the potential implications for Malaysian-listed plantation companies. Among CIMB’s Malaysian plantation coverage, SD Guthrie, Genting Plantations and KLK have the largest absolute plantation exposure to Indonesia. IOI Corp Bhd (KL:IOICORP) has a smaller relative exposure, while Johor Plantations Group Bhd (KL:JPG), Ta Ann Holdings Bhd (KL:TAANN) and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd (KL:HSPLANT) have plantation operations entirely in Malaysia. CIMB said the impact will depend on the final land limits, whether the 20% rule applies to existing plantations and how it will be implemented. Bloomberg consensus as at Friday showed analysts remaining broadly positive on SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations, while views on KLK were more mixed. For SD Guthrie, 17 analysts had "buy" calls and three had "hold" calls, with a 12-month target price of RM7.68. Genting Plantations had 10 "buy" calls and two "hold" calls, with a target price of RM6.81. KLK had nine "buy" calls, 10 "hold" calls, and one "sell", with a target price of RM24.57. Separately, India’s decision to lower import duties on major edible oils could provide some support for crude palm oil (CPO) demand, although CIMB expects the benefit to Malaysian planters to be modest. India cut the basic customs duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil to 5% from 10%, while eliminating the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil, effective Thursday. The Indian government said the move was aimed at reducing import costs and easing domestic edible oil prices. CIMB said the lower CPO duty should reduce landed costs and support Indian palm oil imports, although the larger tariff reduction for sunflower oil could make it more competitive against palm oil and limit the increase in demand. India accounted for about 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025. CIMB said the main benefit for Malaysian planters would likely come through firmer CPO prices rather than a significant direct increase in export volumes. CIMB maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 per tonne for 2027. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. Refer to the original content for accurate info. title: 'CIMB Could Raise RM2 Bil Capital Return Commitment, Says MBSB Research
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) could potentially raise its RM2 billion capital return commitment to increase the chances of its share buyback programme garnering investor acceptance, according to MBSB Research. A higher capital-return commitment could help offset potential disappointment among investors who are expecting a larger portion of the RM2 billion to be returned via special dividends, the research house said. “To increase its chances of success, we think there is a likelihood of CIMB positively revising to the RM2.0 billion figure, and that CIMB is confident enough on its ability to garner sufficient capital before signalling to the market via share buybacks,” MBSB Research said in a note on Thursday. “We would not put it past CIMB’s management to pull off such a manoeuvre — they’ve surprised us positively multiple times in the past,” it added. MBSB Research noted that share buybacks have historically not been successful in Malaysia. CIMB’s share buybacks make up a portion of its RM2 billion capital return scheme, of which RM700 million has already been returned via special dividends. The primary purpose of the share buybacks is for CIMB to further drive its earnings per share, return on equity (ROE) and dividend per share figures, MBSB Research noted, particularly as the bank is slightly behind on its ROE target for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026). The research house noted CIMB has been buying back shares every day, tallying up to 20.76 million shares for RM163 million since Sept 21 thus far. CIMB’s share buyback programme is also being watched for its potential implications on other banks, according to MBSB Research. The research house described the programme as the first major share buyback scheme by a Malaysian bank for capital management purposes in many years, and said a successful outcome could encourage other large banks to consider similar measures. It listed Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) as possible candidates. Public Bank, it noted, has already received shareholder approval for a share buyback of up to 10% of its shares, although it has not done any yet. Its management has maintained that this is a capital optimisation option rather than a set path they want to go down, the research house added. RHB Bank, meanwhile, has high capital ratios and historically releases excess capital via larger payouts in the fourth quarter, MBSB Research noted. It is currently preparing a new capital release plan, which is scheduled to be announced by the first quarter of FY2027, the research house added. MBSB Research maintained its “buy” call on CIMB but with a lower target price of RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times. At the time of writing, shares of CIMB were down three sen or 0.39% at RM7.76, valuing the lender at RM84 billion. title: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Oil and gas, Sorento Capital Bhd, Bermaz Auto Bhd, UMedic Group Bhd
body:
'

This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026

Oil and gas

OVERWEIGHT

HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Brent has returned above US$100 per barrel as risks rise across Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and Saudi’s East-West Pipeline, while Middle East supply disruptions have widened the global oil deficit. China crude imports are also recovering, adding further upside risk to prices. We now expect Brent at US$95-US$100 per barrel towards end-2026 and raise our 2026 assumption to US$90 per barrel from US$80 per barrel.

While we retain “buy” calls on most names, we remain selective and favour companies with earnings drivers that can sustain beyond near-term Brent volatility.

We advocate positioning for our 2027 thesis of a recovery in Petroliam Nasional Bhd’s (PETRONAS) upstream capital expenditure (capex) alongside rising regional energy-security investments. We believe the sector remains supported by a recovery in offshore support vessel-related names such as Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd (KL:DAYANG), Keyfield International Bhd (KL:KEYFIELD) and Perdana Petroleum Bhd (KL:PERDANA), while improving oil and gas services and equipment order flows and longer-term demand for storage, pipelines and broader energy infrastructure should continue to support Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) and Wasco Bhd (KL:WASCO).

Dialog remains our top pick. We expect Dialog’s earnings to remain well supported in FY27-FY28 by growth across its three key segments. Upstream will be supported by the new Cendramas production sharing contract and Baram Junior Cluster (both commencing from 2QFY27), which are expected to shift the upstream earnings mix higher to 30% to 40%. Meanwhile, Dialog’s downstream earnings visibility remains well supported by several ongoing engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning projects.

PETRONAS Chemicals Group Bhd’s (KL:PCHEM) (PetChem) share price has risen around 25% after we upgraded it to “buy” in our end-June report. We are seeing early signs of stabilisation in key product prices, while elevated Brent prices could support further improvement in overall average selling prices in 4QFY26. We expect utilisation rates to improve with minimal turnaround activities at Methanol 2 for 60 days and Fertiliser Sabah for 10 days in 3QFY26, while no scheduled plant turnaround is expected in 4QFY26. PetChem remains attractive, with recovery of urea prices in 2HFY27 as seasonal planting demand returns, and potential divestment of its Pengerang Petrochemical Co Sdn Bhd stake, which could remove significant earnings drag and reduce the group’s foreign exchange (forex) exposure.

We view Dayang as a key beneficiary of a potential PETRONAS upstream capex recovery in 2027. Dayang delivered a stronger performance in 2024, when PETRONAS’ upstream spending was relatively elevated at around RM21.5 billion across 2023-2024, while upstream capex remained subdued at only RM9 billion in 1HFY26.

Sorento Capital Bhd

Target price: 77 sen BUY

TA SECURITIES (SEPT 14): Sorento Capital Bhd’s (KL:SORENTO) FY26 gross profit margin reached 45.2%, the highest in the company’s history, despite challenging market conditions arising from the US-Iran war. Management attributes the margin expansion to a reduction in original equipment manufacturing cost in China late last year, which contributed to a stronger 47% gross profit margin in 4QFY26.

According to management, global brass prices rose by 50% following the onset of the US-Iran war, leading to higher production cost for bathroom and kitchen taps. However, prices of ceramic bathroom products have been undergoing price cutting. As China’s exports of ceramic products to the Middle East has been disrupted by the war, these products have been redirected to Asian markets, creating downward price pressure. As such, management is confident of sustaining its gross profit margin above 40% for FY27.

As far as project sales are concerned, the group has seen an uptick in orders for its Sorento-series sanitary ware. It order book has increased to RM150 million from RM120 million, and we expect the company to secure new orders of RM80 million each in FY27 and FY28.

Bermaz Auto Bhd

Target price: RM1.35 BUY

MAYBANK INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Bermaz Auto Bhd’s (KL:BAUTO) recovery trajectory continues to outperform market expectations, and we see further upside should the momentum sustain.

Near-term margins should improve with stronger support from XPeng China, while Mazda volumes remain resilient. Key considerations include completely built-up (CBU) supply and evolving earnings mix as completely knocked-down (CKD) ramps up.

Mazda CBU volume now contributes about two-thirds of sales, which we expect to sustain over the next few quarters until the all-new CX-5 CKD is launched in mid-2027. We expect 5,000 CBU units by year-end, while forex hedging should support CBU margins in FY27.

Overall, BAuto’s outlook is underpinned by new Mazda and XPeng model launches, supporting its FY27 sales target of 16,000 units (+23% y-o-y, ex-Kia sales in FY26). Associate earnings are also improving, with Inokom Corp Sdn Bhd returning to profitability and further supported by potential additional assembly contracts. Mazda Malaysia should benefit from CKD expansion, with export volume for the new CX-5 from 2027 (targeting 7,000 units per annum) providing an additional volume boost, while Kia exposure is now minimal. Near-term earnings visibility remains solid, combined with an attractive dividend yield of more than 9%.

UMedic Group Bhd

Target price: 43 sen BUY

MBSB RESEARCH (SEPT 15): The RM47 billion allocated under Budget 2026 and the 13th Malaysia Plan promise of RM40 billion until 2030 continue to support UMedic Group Bhd (KL:UMC).

We believe with the upcoming Budget 2027 — which is expected to continue prioritising citizens’ welfare — UMC is positioned for sustained long-term growth by leveraging key industry tailwinds, including hospital overcrowding, medical tourism and an ageing population projected to reach 21% by 2044.

To capitalise on these trends, UMC is expected to further expand into ambulatory care by growing its ambulance fleet, scaling its integrated learning and community health centres, and diversifying into the laboratory market and specialised verticals via its Akiteck and Ateria subsidiaries.

Additionally, UMC is reinforcing its manufacturing foundation by acquiring three acres of industrial land, expanding clean room capacity and adopting advanced automation to meet rising domestic and global demand across its product portfolio.

By incorporating UMC’s FY26 results into our valuation, we revised FY27-FY28 earnings forecasts upwards by 2%. We like UMC for its stable distribution business, paired with its high-margin proprietary manufacturing operations. UMC’s key drivers remain the government’s fiscal support and long-term demographic tailwinds in terms of care demand and medical tourism.

title: 'Hong Leong Bank shines at Asian Banking and Finance Awards
body:
'

PETALING JAYA: Hong Leong Bank’s (HLB) business and corporate banking segment achieved a significant benchmark at the recent Asian Banking and Finance Awards, clinching four major accolades that solidify its standing as a regional industry leader.


Highlighted by its fifth consecutive win as Best SME Bank in Malaysia and securing Malaysia Domestic Technology & Operations Bank of the Year, the awards validate HLB’s distinct entrepreneurial DNA and reinforce its position as a regional leader for business and SME banking.


Adding to this regional momentum, HLB was also named the Singapore International Foreign Exchange Bank of the Year and won the Initiative Award for SME Cross Border Finance Innovation in Singapore.


Rooted in a 120-year entrepreneurial heritage, the bank’s approach to business banking stems from a lived understanding of tenacity, risk management, and commercial agility, positioning itself as an entrepreneurial bank, and not just a bank that builds entrepreneurs.

title: 'Stock Today: Maybank Falls 1.2% After RM1.56 Billion AT1 Sukuk Redemption
body: 'Maybank shares fell 12 sen or 1.18% to RM10.04 at 3.35pm, with the banking counter trading below its previous close amid broader caution in the financial sector.  The stock opened at RM10.16 and rose to an intraday high of RM10.20 before easing to a low of RM10.02. Some 7.9 million shares changed hands based on the reported volume of 79,022 (’00).  The counter’s previous close was RM10.16, while the current best bid stood at RM10.02 for 642,000 shares and the best offer at RM10.04 for 494,700 shares.  The share price movement comes after Maybank fully redeemed its RM1.56 billion Additional Tier 1 (AT1) Sukuk Mudharabah on Sept 25, its first call date seven years after the securities were issued.  The sukuk was originally issued on Sept 25, 2019 and formed part of Maybank’s AT1 capital instruments.  Meanwhile, Bank Negara Malaysia Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the central bank was reviewing whether financial institutions could be given greater flexibility to take on higher risks within acceptable limits to support Malaysia’s energy transition.  The move could have implications for how banks assess and finance green energy projects, particularly those that are technically feasible but not yet commercially viable.  At the time of writing, Maybank remained 1.18% lower for the session.
