title: 'Over 9,000 building owners required to appoint FSMs, FSOs from April 1, 2027
body: 'Starting April 1, 2027, owners of over 9,000 designated buildings in Malaysia must appoint Fire Safety Managers and Officers under the Fire Services Act. KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. “In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said. Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide. He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony.

title: 'World Bank Supports Malaysia’s Possible Integration of GST Elements Into SST
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): The World Bank has agreed that certain elements of the goods and services tax (GST) should be implemented into Malaysia’s sales and service tax (SST) to address its distortionary features. World Bank lead economist for Malaysia Apurva Sanghi said the government should address the SST’s nature as a cascading tax and, in turn, an embedded tax. The SST is a single-stage tax with no input credit mechanism. In other words, tax can become embedded in prices as goods and services move through the supply chain. “We believe what is required is neutral tax reform that relieves cascading and embedded effects on businesses, for example through input tax credits, while also broadening the tax base to bolster revenues," he said during a briefing on the October 2026 Malaysia Economic Monitor report. There has been much industry and policy discussion on what an integration of GST elements into the SST, or a formulation of a better SST, could look like. Discourse began after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the government is studying improvements to the existing SST, including whether it can incorporate elements of the GST, following a Budget 2027 engagement session in August. Malaysia implemented the GST in 2015 at a 6% rate under the administration of Datuk Seri Najib Razak. The implementation led to soaring inflation and widespread complaints of slow tax refunds that created a cash crunch for small- to medium-sized businesses. The tax was suspended on June 1, 2018, after Pakatan Harapan took over the federal government, and was subsequently abolished and replaced with the current SST on Sept 1, 2018. While Apurva agreed the SST can be improved if the cascading tax aspect is addressed, he did note the World Bank has held the view that the GST is a better solution, should its regressivity be offset with cash transfers to those vulnerable. “Trying to integrate GST elements with SST, I think of it as trying to integrate efficiency with empathy. “And, when you fuse both together, the risk is you may get neither,” he warned. GST, all being equal, is favourable to SST, Apurva noted. He said GST avoids cascading and embedded tax. “One of the stumbling blocks of GST 1.0, the previous GST regime, was the delay in issuing refunds. If that is addressed, then that definitely is yet another argument to think about GST,” he said. World Bank economist Deisigan Shammugam also highlighted that it has been a decade since then and that technology has improved since then. title: 'Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card: Everything you need to know before applying
body: 'Maybank has officially introduced its limited edition Maybank Visa BTS World Tour Arirang Debit Card in Malaysia. With initial physical branch allocations selling out rapidly across the country, fans looking to secure the card should now stand by for the official Maybank2u online rollout on 28 September 2026. What is the Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card? The card is an exclusive limited edition Visa debit card released in collaboration with Visa for the BTS World Tour Arirang. It links directly to any existing or new Maybank current or savings account, including popular options like a standard Savings Account i. Maybank has capped total nationwide issuance to 200,000 cards. Following the instant sell out of physical branch quotas, remaining card stock will be made available strictly through online applications. Additional features compared to a standard Maybank debit card While core banking functions mirror standard Maybank debit cards, the BTS edition includes several exclusive perks and modern payment integrations. Cardholders can add the Maybank Visa BTS World Tour Arirang Debit Card to Apple Pay and Samsung Wallet. This allows users to make contactless mobile payments directly from an iPhone, Apple Watch, or compatible Samsung Galaxy device without needing the physical card on hand. Beyond mobile wallet support and limited edition artwork, getting the card grants an immediate advantage in Maybank and Visa’s official concert ticket giveaway. While standard debit cardholders must accumulate spending to qualify, obtaining this limited edition card automatically awards an entry into the prize draw. In terms of banking capabilities, the card operates on the Visa network with smart chip security, contactless highway toll support, and standard fee structures, including the standard RM12 replacement fee. How to win BTS World Tour Arirang concert tickets in Kuala Lumpur Maybank and Visa are running a contest from 23 September 2026 until 1 November 2026, offering cardholders a chance to win pairs of tickets to the BTS World Tour Arirang concert at National Stadium Bukit Jalil on 12 December 2026. To participate, cardholders must first register by sending an SMS with the word BTS to the number 66628, or register through the dedicated Maybank2u promotion page. Once registered, users can earn entries through multiple qualifying actions: - Automatic entry: Successfully applying for or replacing an existing card with the limited edition BTS debit card awards one automatic entry. - Cumulative spending: Every cumulative RM400 spent on eligible retail transactions using any Maybank Visa debit card during the campaign period earns one entry. - Additional spending: Every subsequent RM400 spent yields additional entries to boost winning chances. Transactions involving eWallet top ups, government payments, and charity donations are excluded from eligible spend. Winners will be selected through Maybank’s randomiser system, with each cardmember eligible to win a maximum of one pair of tickets. How to apply for the Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card? With physical branch allocations fully exhausted, all remaining card requests must be submitted online when portal access opens on 28 September 2026. Existing Maybank customers Existing Maybank debit cardholders do not need to visit a branch or collect cards in person. You can request a card replacement online via Maybank2u starting 28 September 2026. To place an order, log in to Maybank2u on the web, navigate to Settings, select Cards, go to Manage Debit Cards, and click Replace or Renew Card. Select the BTS card, enter your mailing address, and confirm the request using Secure2u or SMS TAC. The card will be delivered directly to your home address for a standard RM12 replacement fee. Delivery times may exceed thirty days during periods of high demand. If card allocations run out completely before your request processes, Maybank will issue a full refund of the replacement fee. Non-Maybank customers If you do not currently hold a Maybank account, you cannot directly order a card replacement online as a first time applicant. New customers must first open an account with Maybank. You can set up an account online through the MAE app or visit any Maybank branch with your MyKad or passport and a standard RM250 deposit, or RM50 with an employment letter. Once your account is active and registered on Maybank2u, you can stand by to request the BTS debit card replacement via Maybank2u starting 28 September 2026. Transaction limits and security settings The card comes with a default daily purchase limit of RM3,000, which can be increased up to RM10,000 via Maybank2u or adjusted at any Maybank ATM. Each card carries a validity period of seven years from issuance. Cardholders planning to use the card for online shopping or overseas ATM cash withdrawals must manually activate ecommerce and overseas transaction features inside Maybank2u prior to making transactions.

title: 'Autopsy Confirms Yong Peng Schoolgirl Died From Head Injury — Police
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): An autopsy on 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, who was believed to have been murdered at a school in Yong Peng, Johor, on Saturday, found that she died from blunt trauma to the head. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the post-mortem was conducted on Sunday by a pathologist from the Forensic Department of Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital in Batu Pahat. “A 16-year-old boy was arrested on Oct 3 and has been remanded for six days until Oct 9 to assist investigations,” he said in a statement Monday. title: 'Existing taxes key to 2027 Budget, expect few major changes: Expert
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is likely to focus on improving tax collection and fine-tuning existing taxes rather than introducing major new levies in 2027 Budget, according to KPMG senior tax policy adviser Dr Veerinderjeet Singh. He said stronger enforcement, better use of tax agency analytics and broader tax bases could provide additional revenue while supporting the government's fiscal consolidation efforts. Speaking at a forum hosted by CIMB Securities, Veerinderjeet said the government should "sweat our assets". This is by improving collection efficiency, with scope to gradually raise Malaysia's tax-to-gross domestic product ratio towards 15 per cent through stronger personal, corporate and indirect tax bases. He expects few major tax changes in the upcoming budget, given the continued focus on cost-of-living support and social spending. Recent measures such as the dividend and capital gains taxes reflect a more progressive tax system, although he does not expect the two per cent dividend tax to be raised or capital gains tax extended to listed shares in the budget. A further increase in the 30 per cent top personal income tax rate also appears unlikely. On the sales and service tax (SST), Veerinderjeet estimates coverage has reached about 78-80 per cent of goods and services, bringing it closer to the breadth of the former goods and services tax (GST). He sees scope for broader input exemptions under SST to reduce cascading effects and business costs, although this would mean some revenue loss. GST reinstatement is not expected in thr 2027 Budget, with improving SST efficiency likely to take precedence. Wider e-invoicing participation could also help uncover unreported taxable activity, although exemptions for smaller businesses may be gradually reduced as economic conditions improve. On other measures, Veerinderjeet expects limited additional revenue from the global minimum tax until the first filing cycle provides clearer evidence of collections. A carbon tax remains on the policy agenda but could be delayed to 2028 or later amid business cost pressures. The budget may reaffirm the government's intention to introduce it, potentially at a low initial rate. He also sees only a slight possibility of modest excise duty increases on alcohol and tobacco, while no new windfall levy is expected. For real estate investment trusts, he does not expect the former 10 per cent final withholding tax on distributions to return, although he supports withholding mechanisms to reduce filing and monitoring costs.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia rebounds in early trade, investors remain cautious
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia rebounded in early trade on Friday, tracking Wall Street’s overnight recovery, although analysts expect investors to remain cautious and selective amid lingering concerns over US bond yields and oil prices.  Overnight, US stocks recovered from early losses to close slightly higher on Thursday as a global bond selloff eased, pulling Treasury yields back from multi-decade highs.  The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.04% to 50,926.74, the S&P 500 gained 0.20% to 7,666.48 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.04% to 26,871.60.  Back home, the FBM KLCI rebounded in early trade, gaining 5.37 points, or 0.33%, to 1,635.73 at 9.27am, supported by gains in selected heavyweights including banking, healthcare, energy and industrial stocks. title: 'FBM KLCI Rebounds at Midday, Driven by Utilities Stocks
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) saw a rebound at midday, gaining 10.18 points to reach 1,654.14, up from Tuesday's close of 1,643.96, driven by bargain hunting in selected heavyweight stocks, particularly in the utilities sector, although overall market breadth remained negative. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the index opened 2.53 points higher at 1,646.49 and moved within a range of 1,645.03 to 1,656.87 during the session. Utilities stocks were at the forefront of the gains, with Tenaga Nasional increasing by 32 sen to RM13.04, Petronas Gas rising by 20 sen to RM17.38, and YTL Corporation edging up by one sen to RM2.30. Despite the gains in the index, the broader market witnessed decliners outnumbering gainers by 603 to 350, with 521 counters remaining unchanged, 1,381 untraded, and 95 suspended. The turnover amounted to 1.92 billion shares valued at RM1.49 billion. Apex Securities Bhd noted in a statement that the energy sector, one of the only two sectors to gain, might experience a reversal of some gains following a dip in Brent crude oil prices overnight amid ongoing US-Iran talks. At the time of reporting, Brent crude had risen by 0.48 percent to US$103.08 per barrel. In terms of heavyweight stocks, Maybank increased by five sen to RM10.04, while Public Bank decreased by two sen to RM4.70. CIMB added one sen to RM7.79, and IHH Healthcare rose by three sen to RM7.90. Among active traders, Zetrix AI remained flat at 16.5 sen, V.S Industry increased by 1.5 sen to 25 sen, and Gamuda recovered by 20 sen to RM5.18. Jaks Resources and Tanco each rose by half a sen to 19.5 sen and 16.5 sen, respectively. Top gainers included Nestle, which rose by RM1.20 to RM90.12, United Plantations, which gained 28 sen to RM31.60, and UMS Integration, which added 20 sen to RM8.81. Ayer edged up by 18 sen to RM7.78, and Allianz Malaysia advanced by 14 sen to RM21. Hengyuan Refining led the decliners, falling by 57 sen to RM3.77, and its trading was suspended for the remainder of the day after breaching the prescribed price limit. Malaysian Pacific Industries dropped by 44 sen to RM40.36, Eurospan by 25 sen to RM2.99, Kuala Lumpur Kepong by 22 sen to RM22.28, and MI Technovation by 17 sen to RM5.22. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased by 48.14 points to 17,561.95. In contrast, the FBM Emas Index rose by 40.32 points to 12,305.79, and the FBM Top 100 Index gained 46.83 points to 12,098.37. The FBM Emas Shariah Index increased by 69.56 points to 12,197.17, while the FBM ACE Index fell by 33.86 points to 5,494.72. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index saw a slight rise of 0.32 points to 181.18. However, the Energy Index fell by 18.32 points to 850.38. Meanwhile, the Financial Services Index gained 10.75 points to 19,271.60, and the Plantation Index added 16.55 points, reaching 9,232.89.

title: 'Optimistic outlook for equities in fourth quarter
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Malaysia’s resilient domestic economy, alongside Budget 2027, should support the local stock market in the fourth quarter of 2026 (4Q26), although geopolitical uncertainty and elevated global yields could keep a lid on valuations, says MBSB Research. In a strategy report, the research house said it remained “optimistic but cautious” on Malaysian equities, favouring defensive sectors while selectively taking on growth exposure. The research house said market direction in 4Q26 would depend on whether the Strait of Hormuz begins to reopen, oil and freight costs moderate, and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) September rate hike proves to be an adjustment rather than the start of a prolonged tightening cycle. It said Malaysia’s resilient economic growth, corporate earnings and domestic liquidity should provide downside support, while Budget 2027 could bring renewed attention to domestic catalysts. However, sustained oil prices above US$100 a barrel, further Fed rate hikes and persistently elevated bond yields could continue to weigh on valuations and foreign fund flows. Despite heightened external uncertainties, MBSB Research said growth should remain well anchored, with the strong first-half (1H26) performance providing a solid base for the rest of the year, “which we expect to remain reassuring in 3Q26”. Even under more adverse scenarios, the research house said full-year growth should remain above 4%, given the strong 1H26 performance. “Into 2027, we favour sectors combining near-term catalysts with recurring demand, pricing power and resilience against prolonged external disruption,” it said. “Preference should remain with companies offering visible earnings, recurring demand, balance-sheet strength, dividend support and direct exposure to Malaysia’s domestic investment cycle.” Against this backdrop, the research house favours utilities, telecommunications, consumer staples and healthcare for their resilient earnings, while construction and technology offer exposure to growth. MBSB Research also recommended retaining exposure to plantations and energy-related stocks as protection against external uncertainty in 4Q26. Plantations could benefit from firm crude palm oil prices, biodiesel demand and ringgit weakness, while energy infrastructure and shipping should remain relevant amid normalising trade and potential supply disruptions, it said. MBSB Research expects Malaysia’s economic growth to moderate to 4.6% in 2027 from a forecast 5.1% this year, having expanded 5.7% year-on-year in 1H26. It said the moderation largely reflected normalisation from a relatively high base rather than a material weakening in underlying economic conditions. The research firm said domestic demand should remain supportive, underpinned by healthy labour market conditions, positive wage growth and continued investment activity, while external trade should continue to benefit from resilient electrical and electronics (E&E) demand. Still, MBSB Research said the outlook for 2027 remained clouded by geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties, including the US midterm elections, conflicts involving the United States, Iran and Israel, risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, inflation and the path of monetary policy. “A change in any one of these variables could materially alter the direction of energy prices, interest rates, global growth and financial markets, making a single-point forecast inadequate,” it noted. The research house said the next major political event to watch was the US midterm elections on Nov 3, which will determine control of the US House of Representatives and Senate. The research house said the election would not directly determine the actions of Iran, Israel or the Houthis, but could affect areas including war funding, sanctions, congressional oversight, the legal basis for military operations and the political cost of sustaining the blockade. Under its baseline scenario, where Malaysia’s economy grows 4.6% in 2027, MBSB Research expects corporate earnings to expand 6.6% and has set a preliminary FBM KLCI target of 1,850 points. The target is based on a forecast 2027 price-to-earnings ratio (PER) of 15.4 times, compared with the FBM KLCI’s current 2026 PER of 14.8 times. “Underpinned by our baseline expectations of resilient macro performance along with healthy earnings growth next year, we expect equity valuations to improve going forward,” it said. It expects the local equity market to benefit from an anticipated easing of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, with Brent crude oil prices expected to decline towards US$75 to US$85 per barrel. Under a more adverse scenario, MBSB Research sees GDP growth slowing to 3.2%, with earnings growth moderating to 4.5%. In this scenario, it has set a lower FBM KLCI target of 1,730 points based on a PER of 14.7 times. Separately, CIMB Research said changes to the rules governing the expanded FBM KLCI should give the 50-stock index a wider buffer against frequent changes in its constituents. The FBM KLCI is set to expand to 50 constituents from 30, with the new structure taking effect from the December 2026 semi-annual index review. FTSE Russell, which manages the index, has revised the entry and exit thresholds to reduce the frequency of stocks moving in and out of the index. Under the new rules, a stock must rank among the top 40 by full market capitalisation to qualify for inclusion, compared with the top 25 previously, while existing constituents will only be removed if they fall to 61st or below, compared with 36th previously. CIMB Research said the wider gap between the inclusion and deletion thresholds should reduce index churn. FTSE Russell has also lowered the fast- entry threshold to 1% of FBM Emas market capitalisation from 2%. Based on Aug 28 data, CIMB Research said this translates into an estimated market capitalisation threshold of RM18.1bil, compared with RM36.3bil previously. The research house said the lower threshold should allow large newly listed companies to enter the KLCI more quickly if they meet the other eligibility requirements.

title: 'S P Setia Launches 100-acre Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines
body: 'S P Setia Bhd on Monday officially launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines, Kepala Batas, marking a significant milestone in the group’s continued placemaking and township development efforts in Penang. From left: Penang state executive councillor for tourism and creative economy Wong Hon Wai, Penang state secretary Datuk Dr Jafri Abdul Jalil, Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Penang Tun Ramli Ngah Talib, S P Setia president and CEO Datuk Zaini Yusoff and member of the Penang state legislative assembly Bukhori Ghazali. KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 21): S P Setia Bhd (KL:SPSETIA) officially launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines in Kepala Batas, Penang — marking a significant milestone in the group's placemaking and township development efforts in Penang. According to a press statement on Monday, the launch was graced by Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Penang Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, alongside state representatives, government agencies, strategic partners, invited guests, residents and members of the public. Also present was Penang state executive councillor for tourism and creative economy Wong Hon Wai. "This effort not only enhances the value and appeal of Setia Fontaines as a premier township development but also contributes meaningfully to the broader socio-economic growth and development of Kepala Batas and the Northern Seberang Perai region," Wong said. He added that the project reflects the important role private-sector investment plays in creating sustainable communities, strengthening local economies and supporting the state's long-term development aspirations. Set within the wider Setia Fontaines development, the 100-acre Heritage Park incorporates a 63-acre man-made lake and a musical fountain to support quality living, recreation, wellness and community engagement. S P Setia president and CEO Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the launch reflects the group's long-term commitment to Penang and its belief that successful townships must be built around people, community and shared experiences. "Setia Fontaines Heritage Park represents our continued commitment to building beyond homes. Through thoughtful placemaking, green public spaces and community-led experiences, we are shaping Setia Fontaines into an integrated township that contributes to Penang’s growth while creating long-term value for residents, visitors and the wider community," Zaini said. He added that Heritage Park is envisioned as more than a township amenity, serving as a lifestyle and recreational attraction with potential to support visitation, public engagement and destination appeal for Seberang Perai Utara and the wider northern region. The official launch was followed by the Jom Mai Setia Fontaines Carnival, a large-scale community activation featuring family activities, Malaysia Day-themed programmes, cultural and entertainment performances, and tourism-related activations. Strategic collaborations with Tourism Malaysia, Penang Global Tourism and Maybank further supported the destination-branding direction of the programme. Setia Fontaines is planned as an integrated township in Kepala Batas, incorporating residential, commercial, recreational, lifestyle and future employment components within a single development. title: 'F1 Singapore Grand Prix value proposition still strong after 18 years
body: 'SINGAPORE – For 18 years, Singapore has marketed its Formula 1 Grand Prix not just as a motor race, but as a showcase of what the Lion City can do when it turns several kilometres of floodlit roads along the waterfront at dusk into a global stage.  Since September 2008, the Marina Bay Street Circuit has become one of the most iconic events on the F1 calendar, offering something no other city did – the first-ever night race.  The spectacle helped establish Singapore as a distinctive stop on the F1 calendar, while giving the city-state a high-profile platform to promote its hospitality industry, infrastructure, business environment and ability to stage a complex international event.  Now, a few countries in the region are seeking to replicate Singapore’s success and join the F1 bandwagon in hopes of global attention and attracting high-spending visitors.  After a nine-year hiatus, Malaysia is set to host an F1 race in Sepang again in October, while Thailand is targeting a street race in Bangkok’s Chatuchak area as early as 2028.  The emergence of new Asian contenders raises questions about whether the Singapore Grand Prix can continue to distinguish itself or if fans will be drawn away to rival races.  Market observers and economists believe it can.  “F1 is still delivering benefits to Singapore that outweigh the cost of hosting the event,” said Brian Lee, an economist at Maybank.  “While the direct tourism benefits may face diminishing returns, the race remains valuable as a platform for attracting high-spending visitors, business events and global capital,” he added.  He noted that the 2025 F1 race weekend drew a sell-out crowd of more than 300,000 fans. That was the second-highest attendance in the event’s history and an almost 12 per cent jump from 2024, suggesting the novelty remained.  Guy Llewellyn, academic director for Asia-Pacific at EHL Hospitality Business School, said it would be hard for other cities to replicate Singapore’s experience after it has run the event for 18 years, coordinating different stakeholders and building a strong international reputation.  “Singapore’s strategy has gradually evolved from hosting a sporting event to hosting a citywide festival. The concerts, entertainment zones, dining experiences, and new Barge Stage programming mean that visitors can spend an entire day in Marina Bay without focusing exclusively on racing,” the assistant professor said.  The Barge Stage waterfront amphitheatre will be unveiled in 2026 along with a line-up of international DJs.  “Few destinations can offer a Formula 1 circuit, internationally branded hotels, fine dining, nightlife and entertainment venues all within walking distance of one another,” Llewellyn said.  However, while being the first night race was once a powerful differentiator, the novelty naturally fades over time, making the broader ecosystem increasingly important in setting the experience apart, he added.  Faizal Yahya, senior research fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies at NUS’ Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, also believes the race should go on.  The returns have been “a massive net positive”, as Singapore has gained a lot economically, strategically, and in terms of its global image, Yahya said.  From the inaugural night race in 2008 until 2024, the event generated around $2.2 billion in incremental tourism receipts, mostly for accommodation, attraction tickets, food and beverage, shopping and airfares. It also attracted more than 720,000 visitors over the period.  Lee said that this is equivalent to $129 million a year in incremental spending from tourists attending the race. That is 0.4 per cent of Singapore’s 2025 aggregate tourism receipts.  While this may be close to the $140 million annual cost of organising the race, there are other beneficiaries that are not captured by the tourism receipt figures.  These include companies involved in the track and venue setup, advertising and others that support the event, ranging from raw material suppliers, equipment rental, logistics and even laundry and cleaning services, Lee said.  Beyond grandstand ticket sales, F1’s ripple effect extends to drawing other high-profile events around the race period.  Every year, about 25 to 30 international conferences – including the Forbes Global CEO Conference, the Milken Institute Asia Summit and TOKEN2049 – have been held around race week, bringing in around 90,000 C-suites to Singapore.  High-net-worth travellers, who make up 30 per cent of F1 visitors, account for 40 per cent of tourist spending during race week, pushing up occupancy rates and hotel room rates even outside the race vicinity.  A large share of the race’s contracts is subcontracted to Singapore-based small and medium-sized enterprises, including firms in engineering, construction and hospitality, the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) said.  About 30,000 staff, contractors and stakeholders work on each race. More than 1,000 students from the Institute of Technical Education and polytechnics are also trained each year for roles around the circuit, giving them exposure to the organisation of a major international event.  “This creates temporary employment for over 30,000 workers and students across logistics, advanced engineering, hospitality and specialised event staging,” Yahya said.  With millions of people around the world watching the Singapore race on television and online, the event is a global advertisement for the Republic, showcasing its infrastructure, safety, business environment and city life, he added.  The 2019 Singapore Grand Prix was estimated to have generated $70 million to $75 million in media value, according to a McKinsey study cited by METI.  Maintaining the head start  In 2026, Singapore will host its first-ever F1 Sprint race, on Saturday, Oct 10 – a two-day, 100km race that is hosted by just six circuits this season.  The Sprint format alters the dynamic of the traditional Marina Bay Street Circuit weekend, and could make the Singapore race weekend feel like two big race days instead of one, said Llewellyn.  Saturday gets its own race, giving fans another reason to come earlier and stay longer.  For hotels, it offers an opportunity to earn more if more guests arrive on Thursday and stay longer.  It remains to be seen whether fans will see the Sprint as a must-attend event, since this is Singapore’s first time hosting a Sprint, Llewellyn said.  To keep its competitive edge, experts said Singapore must continue to convert more F1 race visitors into long-term tourists and business connections by linking race week with high-value conferences, business-cum-leisure packages, and MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, and exhibitions) events.  Regional travel partnerships can encourage onward trips across ASEAN, while digital matchmaking connects delegates with local businesses. Hosting networking events in Marina Bay and Orchard Road can further showcase Singapore’s commercial ecosystem.  The Singapore Grand Prix was never just a sporting event from the start. It is being used as a tourism draw, a business-networking platform, a showcase for local companies and a recurring global advertisement for the city.  “The issue is less about whether Singapore should continue hosting F1, and more about whether it can continue extracting scarcity value from the event as competing cities replicate the street-race model,” Lee said.

title: 'Senior Citizens’ Bill: Give older people a fairer deal
body: 'V Thomas The women, family and community development minister has said the Senior Citizens’ Bill will be tabled in Parliament in early 2027. The public is still being asked for input and feedback. Here are my suggestions for the bill. Dedicated hospital wings Major government hospitals should have a separate wing for older adults. It would focus on treatment, surgery and medication. At present, older people wait with everyone else until their name or number is called. Many are frail, in wheelchairs or ill. They should not have to wait so long for treatment. A separate wing would help the government judge whether it needs bigger budgets and more geriatricians. It would also be easier to manage well, as it would handle fewer patients. Better EPF returns Major banks in India offer older adults deposit interest rates of up to about 7-8%, depending on the bank and tenure. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Likewise, the Employees Provident Fund in Malaysia could pay older people a higher dividend on their savings. A rate of 10% on up to RM200,000 in savings would help. (The current rate is about 6.15%, declared for 2025.) A separate EPF scheme for older people could achieve this. At 10%, RM200,000 would earn about RM20,000 a year, or roughly RM1,666 a month. At present, members can deposit up to RM100,000 a year in aggregate across EPF’s voluntary contribution schemes. But the EPF voluntary contribution scheme now stops at age 75. That age limit could be extended to 80. More older people could then cope with the cost of living, medical bills and other expenses. Many older people would no longer have to seek help from the Social Welfare Department. Harnessing experience The government should use older people’s experience through incentives in residents’ associations and other local groups. Local authorities could help in these programmes. Town hall sessions would benefit from older people’s knowledge, particularly of local government. Local authorities should register older people’s associations freely and tell older people about programmes in their areas. Some light duties could be reserved for older people who can work. Older people are a vital asset, and the government should make full use of what they can contribute in their later years. Many capable older people could serve as local councillors and village development and security committee (JKKK) members because they know local needs well. A quota for older people among councillors could be considered. Older people should also have their own associations at state and national level. This would let them voice their needs, especially when the yearly budget is drawn up. The government would then understand their needs better and allocate the right funds for their wellbeing. The number of older people is rising fast. It is time for the government to plan soundly and strategically for this growing issue. V Thomas follows the Aliran website. title: 'HLB Islamic fund lifts Langkawi entrepreneurs’ income
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Aligned with its commitment to deepening its value-based intermediation (VBI) ecosystem, HLB Islamic has channeled RM138,600 in social financing towards social enterprise SURI Inspirasi under Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) iTEKAD framework, which has led to a 94% average surge in monthly income and over RM14,000 in total new earnings for participating entrepreneurs of SURI’s Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) programme.   The SRI programme empowers underserved communities to upcycle discarded fabrics into unique fashion items, creating sustainable jobs and encouraging entrepreneurship while promoting zero-waste fashion and community empowerment. As part of the programme, the participating entrepreneurs, predominantly underserved single mothers, produced 1,000 school uniforms for students across five schools in Langkawi, generating RM30,000 in savings for local families.

title: 'The Legacy of Great Towers
body: 'Passport to Nature, Heritage and Culture After five hectic days of talking about towers, visitor experiences and the future of some of the world’s most iconic landmarks, what does a tower person do to chill out? Climb another tower? Get close to nature? Or immerse themselves in a different culture? For the delegates of the World Federation of Great Towers (WFGT) Conference, which ended at the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur on Sept 18, the answer was — all three. But not necessarily in that order. First, they went looking for elephants About 20 WFGT delegates, accompanied by their Malaysian hosts, left Kuala Lumpur after the five-day conference for a post-conference journey into Pahang. Their first stop was the National Elephant Conservation Centre (NECC), Kuala Gandah. And suddenly, the language of towers gave way to the language of nature. There were no observation decks, city skylines or glass elevators. Instead, there was jungle, water and the unmistakable presence of elephants. About a dozen delegates ventured down to the river and had a splashing great time bathing with a young elephant. Some got wet. Some got wetter. And almost everyone came away with a broad smile. The delegates were also given a video presentation, briefing and tour of the centre by Perhilitan personnel, gaining a closer understanding of Malaysia’s elephant conservation efforts. NECC head Muhammad Fadlli bin Ab Yazi and also his team also played a video of Perhilitan's conservation, research and elephant translocation efforts. It was perhaps the moment when everyone truly let their hair down after five intensive days of conference sessions. Kuala Lumpur Tower CEO Khairil Faizal came all the way to join in the fun Even Jean-Yves Ghazi, executive director of the World Federation of Great Towers, joined in the experience. At one point, he fed sugar cane to an elephant — with his back facing the animal. It was one of those moments that could never be fully captured in a conference room. It had to be experienced. Video 1: CELEBRATION OF CULTURE: WFGT delegates even joined the performers for joget as they sampled warm Malaysian hospitality at the Garden Terrace of Kuantan 188. Hyperlink: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/g1smui/AGtS8XXEWhOeZpLwpOS3WbW-9FciXuJn0GGimgXVPIt8-0eoVSV1r7YO7nd7=s294-w294-h294-k-p-v1-no Pahang for nature, culture and hospitality If the elephants had provided the delegates with a taste of Malaysia’s natural side, Pahang and Kuantan 188 delivered culture and warm Malaysian hospitality. At the Sky Terrace overlooking the Kuantan River, the evening turned into a garden party. The delegates were treated to cultural performances by Anak Kayan Pahang, with performers spanning three generations. The delegates joined the performers for a joget, turning the evening into an informal celebration of friendship and Malaysian hospitality. Before that, there was singing at the restaurant deck where dinner was hosted. After some urging, Dato Zulkifli Mohamad — WFGT member and managing director of Kuantan 188 — took to the floor and sang the Bee Gees classic To Love Somebody. The irrepressible Dato “One More” Zul Zulkifli soon called on Randy Stancik, general manager of Willis Tower Skydeck in Chicago, to join him on stage with the emcee. And no one wore a broader smile than Zul when everything turned out splendidly well. He had stitched the evening together — including lobbying the WFGT to host the conference in Kuala Lumpur. The WFGT duly presented an Appreciation Award to him with these fondly crafted words: “To Dato ‘One More’ Zul for being Dato Zul” — with love from Your Distinguished Guest. Zul, being his warm and jovial self, joked: “Now, please tell me, how do I say ‘one more’ to my wife?” And everyone erupted in laughter. The Dato Bandar Kuantan Dato Zaliza bin Zulkipli and members of Majlis Bandaraya Kuantan, Tourism Pahang and MOTAC Pahang also turned up to support this event and extend their hospitality. The trio who made the climb As for climbing, Miguel Amerlink and Mariana Ferruzca of Torre Latino México, together with Daniel Cecetka of UFO Bratislava in Slovakia, made it a point to scale the antenna of Kuantan 188. Not by lift. Not by stairs. But with ropes and safety harnesses, with the help of climbing guides. For people whose professional lives revolve around great towers, perhaps this was the ultimate way to start the morning. Three tower people, looking down from above, before the rest of the group headed on to the next destination. It was another reminder that a tower can be experienced in more ways than simply looking out from its observation deck. Visiting the historic royal town of Pekan From Kuantan, the delegates continued to Pekan, the historic royal town, where they were introduced to history, craftsmanship, music and royal tradition. At Perkampungan Kraf Diraja Tunku Azizah, they watched a weaving demonstration at Pusat Tenun Che Minah Sayang. They also visited the birthplace of Malaysia’s second prime minister, Tun Abdul Razak, the Pahang Silk Weaving Centre, Karyaneka Centre and Serambi House Pahang. Then came the music. A gamelan performance filled the space with the calming and distinctive sounds of traditional Pahang music. Caryn Stancik from the United States, who tried her hand at playing the gamelan, said: “It’s like a cultural awakening. I just love the music. It feels so nice and relaxing like the rustling of wind chimes. “When I go back to the US, I will definitely look out for gamelan music CDs to explore it further.” That is perhaps what a meaningful travel experience does. It leaves you curious enough to continue the journey after you have gone home. A sumptuous lunch beside the river at Gerabak Jaman Tory completed the Pekan experience before the delegates began their journey back to Kuala Lumpur. Trinidad Hospitality Group CEO Dato Sri Naresh Mohan and YB Leong Yu Man, Pahang Exco for Unity, Tourism and Culture took time off to greet and host the delegates. Building a towering experience for visitors In his closing remarks, Zul said he hoped that the staging of the WFGT conference in Kuala Lumpur would leave something meaningful behind. “Every tower has its unique offering,” said Zul, who had also thoughtfully arranged a WFGT visit to Menara Merdeka Maybank. “Each tower not only offers its unique view of the city but also connects to people, landscape, businesses, surroundings and nature in different ways.” A visitor could climb a tower, discover nature, cruise a river, experience local food, listen to traditional music or explore heritage and culture — thus creating a much richer journey around the country’s towers. In many ways, the WFGT delegates had already experienced the concept before they left for home. At the opening of the WFGT conference, Ghazi had reminded delegates: “Our responsibility is not simply to operate great towers.” “It is to ensure that these extraordinary places continue to inspire, educate, connect and create memorable experiences for generations to come.” That was precisely what had happened during their journey to Malaysia. The towers had not been left behind after all. They had simply become gateways to something much bigger. Zul hopes that the proposed Malaysian Tower Passport can carry that idea forward as one of the meaningful outcomes of the WFGT conference in Kuala Lumpur, in line with the aspirations of Visit Malaysia 2026. Before they left for home, a bus full of WFGT delegates sang Rasa Sayang, urged on by award-winning guide Jasmine Leow, who incidentally holds both City and Nature guide badges. After five days of talking about towers, everyone had discovered that a great tower can be much more than a place to look at a city. It can be a gateway to the city, nature, its people, its heritage, its culture — and to experiences visitors remember long after they have gone home. title: 'RHB Completes Five-Year Anti-Corruption Plan
body: 'RHB Banking Group has completed all 27 initiatives under its five-year Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan. The plan ran from 2022 to 2026 and focused on strengthening governance, managing corruption risks and improving accountability across the group. Achievements under the plan included the first phase of the Corporate Integrity System Malaysia Assessment. During Integrity Week 2026, RHB also held anti-corruption training and promoted the reporting of potential misconduct. Tan Sri Ahmad Badri Mohd Zahir, Chairman of RHB Banking Group, said, “The successful completion of our Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan is an important milestone, but it is only one step in our broader journey to strengthen trust and accountability across the organisation. As expectations continue to evolve, integrity must remain at the heart of how we serve our customers, engage our stakeholders, and create long-term value.” RHB is now developing an Organisational Anti-Corruption Strategy aligned with Malaysia’s National Anti-Corruption Strategy 2024–2028. Dato’ Mohd Rashid Mohamad, Group MD and Group CEO of RHB Banking Group, said, “The completion of our Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan is not the end of the journey, but the beginning of the next chapter. As we develop the Organisational Anti-Corruption Strategy, our focus is on embedding integrity, accountability, and ethical conduct more deeply into every decision, every interaction, and every outcome.” Featured image: (From lef): Azman Shah Md Yaman, Group Chief Legal & Governance Officer, RHB Bank Berhad; Tan Sri Ahmad Badri, Non-Independent Non-Executive Chairman, RHB Bank Berhad; and Dato’ Mohd Rashid Mohamed, Group Managing Director/Group Chief Executive Officer of RHB Banking Group

title: 'Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Longer-term financing secured much earlier is now providing Axis REIT (KL:AXREIT) cushion against rising interest rates as the real estate investment trust pursues deals, an analyst said. A 25-basis-point increase in policy rate would potentially raise its cost of borrowings by just 0.1 percentage-point to 4.06%, Maybank Investment Bank said, noting that Axis REIT has locked in 10-year and seven-year financing facilities over the past 12 months when rates were more favourable. “With the completion of signed acquisitions, gearing is expected to rise to around 39%, still having ample headroom before any equity raising is required,” the research house said. Axis REIT owns and manages more than 70 office and industrial assets worth over RM5 billion in Klang Valley, Penang, Johor, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Kedah. The trust is in the midst of acquiring a distribution centre, a warehouse, and an industrial complex for RM193 million combined. The stated aim is to nearly double the asset under management to RM10 billion by 2030, driven by high-growth sectors and key industrial hubs throughout Peninsular Malaysia. In the near term, Axis REIT has a RM250 million acquisition pipeline currently under negotiation, of which one or two transactions could be announced before year-end, Maybank Investment said and maintained its “buy” call on the trust. “We believe its acquisition pipeline should provide further income visibility” with most ongoing transactions fully occupied and carrying weighted average lease expiry of five years or longer, the research house said. Axis REIT has rebounded from its September lows when the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, sending global bond yields higher and triggering concerns of rising borrowing costs. Still, 10 out of 12 research houses tracked by Bloomberg recommend investors to “buy” Axis REIT and two are on “hold” calls. full_text: 'Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst. 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Longer-term financing secured much earlier is now providing Axis REIT (KL:AXREIT) cushion against rising interest rates as the real estate investment trust pursues deals, an analyst said. A 25-basis-point increase in policy rate would potentially raise its cost of borrowings by just 0.1 percentage-point to 4.06%, Maybank Investment Bank said, noting that Axis REIT has locked in 10-year and seven-year financing facilities over the past 12 months when rates were more favourable. “With the completion of signed acquisitions, gearing is expected to rise to around 39%, still having ample headroom before any equity raising is required,” the research house said. Axis REIT owns and manages more than 70 office and industrial assets worth over RM5 billion in Klang Valley, Penang, Johor, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Kedah. The trust is in the midst of acquiring a distribution centre, a warehouse, and an industrial complex for RM193 million combined. The stated aim is to nearly double the asset under management to RM10 billion by 2030, driven by high-growth sectors and key industrial hubs throughout Peninsular Malaysia. In the near term, Axis REIT has a RM250 million acquisition pipeline currently under negotiation, of which one or two transactions could be announced before year-end, Maybank Investment said and maintained its “buy” call on the trust. “We believe its acquisition pipeline should provide further income visibility” with most ongoing transactions fully occupied and carrying weighted average lease expiry of five years or longer, the research house said. Axis REIT has rebounded from its September lows when the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, sending global bond yields higher and triggering concerns of rising borrowing costs. Still, 10 out of 12 research houses tracked by Bloomberg recommend investors to “buy” Axis REIT and two are on “hold” calls. The average target price is RM2.22, a potential gain of up to 21% in the next 12 months from current price of RM1.84.

title: 'Equal work, equal pay
body: 'I guess Lim Guan Eng, the former finance minister and now adviser to the Democratic Action Party (DAP), has a soft spot for employers. His call to exclude migrant workers from the minimum wage and the paltry 2% contribution to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) repeats a position he took in early August 2025. Even then, labour groups criticised it. Since he has chosen to lend his voice to employers, be they micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) or others, it is apt to remind him of three fundamental issues. It said Malaysia should promote and guarantee equality of opportunity and treatment between migrant workers and nationals. Referring to the convention, the court said: - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Based on the above reasons we take the view that all workers should be treated with fairness, dignity and equality without distinction whether they are locals or foreigners. This is also consonant with Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution which essentially provides that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to the equal protection of the law. his judgment alone should put to rest the flawed argument that Malaysia should adopt discriminatory standards against migrant workers to protect employers. Legislative protection Section 69F of the Employment Act 1955 empowers the director general of labour to inquire into and decide any dispute over discrimination in employment. An employer who fails to comply with the director general’s order faces, on conviction, a fine of up to RM50,000. For a continuing offence, there is a further fine of up to RM1,000 for each day it continues. Where an employer has signed a collective agreement with a trade union, section 17(1)(b) of the Industrial Relations Act 1967 makes it binding once the Industrial Court takes cognisance of it. It covers all worker employed in the undertaking, now or later. Industrial Court and other judicial decisions have affirmed that such agreements apply to migrant workers. International standards From the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, one fact stands unchallenged – there is no room for discriminatory employment practices against migrant workers. Full stop! No reasonable person would dispute that people doing the same work must receive the same pay. The right to equal pay for equal work should never be compromised. Doing so would destroy the foundation of equality, good conscience and fair treatment of workers, whether migrant or local. Working people need greater protection against the ever-rising cost of living, low and stagnant wages and inadequate retirement savings in the EPF. They do not need more protection for employers. Seeking such protection for employers is like asking workers to wallow in a vicious low-wage ecosystem so that employers can profit from staying in business. To even entertain the thought that businesses should be protected by treating migrant workers as second-class employees is heartless, an affront to human dignity and devoid of any sense of justice. title: 'Maybank Offers Up to RM388 Off New iPhones
body: '15th September 2026 - 3 min read Maybank cardholders can get up to RM388 off selected new iPhone models from 12 September to 31 December 2026, while stocks last. The promotion covers the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. To qualify for the rebate, the purchase must either be paid in full or placed on a Maybank 0% EzyPay or EzyPay-i instalment plan of 6 or 12 months. The Maybank Visa Infinite Diamanté Card and The Platinum Card qualify for RM388 off, while all other Maybank credit and charge cards qualify for RM288. The rebate cannot be combined with other promotions. The promotion is available at Apple The Exchange TRX and seven authorised resellers, though the rebate is not paid out the same way at each. At Apple The Exchange TRX, you pay the full purchase price first, and Maybank credits the rebate back to your card after the campaign ends. The authorised resellers deduct it from your bill at the point of purchase. Some retailers also offer an accessories voucher: The rebate applies to in-store purchases only. Online orders, including purchases from Apple’s own website, do not qualify. You can pay in full, or spread the cost over a Maybank 0% EzyPay or EzyPay-i instalment plan of 6 or 12 months. title: 'CIMB Share Buyback, Market Watching
body: 'CIMB Group Holdings Bhd’s ongoing share buyback programme could mark a significant shift in how Malaysian banks manage excess capital, although investor acceptance will depend on how the programme is balanced against expectations for special dividends, according to MBSB Research.  The research house maintained its Buy call on CIMB but trimmed its target price to RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times.  MBSB said CIMB has been buying back shares daily since Sept 21, acquiring 20.76 million shares for about RM163 million, implying a weighted average purchase price of RM7.85 per share.  The shares, equivalent to about 0.192% of CIMB’s issued share capital, are currently being held as treasury shares and have not been cancelled.  The buybacks form part of CIMB’s RM2 billion capital return programme, of which RM700 million has already been distributed through special dividends.  If the remaining RM1.3 billion were used entirely for share repurchases, MBSB estimated CIMB could buy back around 1.5% of its total share base.  The research house said the programme is aimed at improving earnings per share, return on equity and dividend per share, particularly as CIMB remains slightly behind its FY2026 ROE target.  Share Buybacks Face Malaysian Investor Test  MBSB cautioned, however, that share buybacks have historically received a mixed response in Malaysia, where many local investors tend to favour direct cash dividends.  This differs from markets such as Singapore, where share repurchases are more established as a capital-management tool.  MBSB said CIMB’s relatively high level of foreign investor participation could help support acceptance of the strategy, although market expectations for further special dividends remain high.  The research house noted that the impact of buybacks would also be less permanent if the treasury shares are eventually reissued rather than cancelled.  Its scenario analysis showed that a 1.5% share buyback could lift FY2027 forecast EPS to 75.7 sen from 74.5 sen, ROE to 11.1% from 10.9%, and DPS to 49.2 sen from 48.4 sen, assuming a 65% dividend payout.  Under that scenario, MBSB estimated the implied target price could rise to RM9.46.  Capital Return Could Be Revised Higher  MBSB said there is also a possibility CIMB could eventually revise its RM2 billion capital return programme higher if additional capital becomes available.  Potential sources could include capital repatriation from subsidiaries, restructuring of less profitable businesses and changes arising from Basel requirements.  The research house said the market will be watching whether CIMB’s approach succeeds, as it could encourage other larger banks to consider similar capital-management strategies.  MBSB identified Public Bank and RHB Bank as potential candidates, given their mature dividend payout levels, relatively strong capital positions and exposure to foreign investors.  Earnings Outlook Remains Supportive  MBSB expects CIMB’s FY2027 core net profit to reach RM8.05 billion, rising 4% from FY2026, with ROE at 10.9% and dividend yield at 6.2%.  The research house continues to view CIMB positively on the back of strong non-interest income growth, wealth management momentum, cost discipline and improving profitability.  However, it flagged potential net interest margin compression, dividend disappointment and weakness in the Indonesian business as key downside risks.  At RM7.79 as of Sept 30, CIMB was trading at about 1.13 times FY2027 forecast book value, with MBSB projecting a total return of about 24.3%, including dividends.

title: 'Draft Penang Structure Plan 2040: Who are they building for?
body: 'This plan, the draft Penang Structure Plan 2040, is already well in progress. It has been put up for public display and feedback – but chances are, most people in Penang are not even aware of it. Look at it closely, and you will see that it looks like a developers’ and contractors’ dream. Plenty of ‘jobs for the boys’. Lot of land reclamation sites all over – about 12 from the looks of it. That includes the ‘Penang Gateway’ (no. 9 on the map) reclamation project somewhere in Batu Ferringhi. The SRS-proposed Islands B and C in the south are still on the map – despite previous reports that the project would be scaled down to just one island (Island A or the ‘Silicon Island’). There’s another large reclamation site on the southeast of Penang Island. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member And look at the half a dozen reclamation sites on the mainland. In the Penang channel, there appears to be a conflict in putting an earmarked reclamation project inside a zone that is supposed to be gazetted as a marine sanctuary – the unique Middle Bank seagrass strip in the Penang channel. Who are they building for, when the birth rate in Penang has shrunk well below population replacement level? Seems to me that Greed has taken over. Check out a new coastal ring highway on the east coast (no. 1). The third crossing (the tunnel?) is still on the map (no 6). They never give up, do they? And look at all the reclamation and ‘development’ slated for the area around Jerejak Island (no 9). Why are they indicating a 150-metre contour line above sea level, when at present there is a limitation on development above 76 metres about sea level? It seems they want to allow development on hill slopes even exceeding 300 metres above sea level, almost all the way up, subject to risk assessments and conditions. More multi-billion ringgit LRT links here and there but I don’t see much in the way of a “better, cheaper, faster” bus rapid transit and tram network. And where are the water taxi routes? Remember, after 18 years since the change in government in 2008, we still don’t have a more detailed local plan, which governs the permissible development and zoning densities allowed in your neighbourhoods. Why is that? And all this while, most of the Penang public remain blissfully in the dark about what is in store for them. title: 'RHB to charge merchants up to 0.60% on DuitNow QR payments
body: 'RHB Bank is revising the fees it charges merchants for accepting DuitNow QR payments, with the new rates taking effect on 26 October 2026. The bank informed its business customers of the change in a notice dated 3 October.  Under the revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), merchants will be charged 0.35% of the transaction value when a customer pays using a current or savings account, or an e-wallet. Payments funded by a credit card, on the other hand, will come with a higher MDR of 0.60%.  To put that into perspective, a merchant receiving a RM100 payment through DuitNow QR from a customer’s bank account or e-wallet will see RM0.35 deducted. If the same amount is paid using a credit card, the deduction goes up to RM0.60.  The new rates apply to DuitNow QR payments processed across RHB’s card terminal devices, DuitNow QR Sound Box and Sound Box+, as well as Reflex Mobile and Tent Cards. Consumers will not be affected by the change, as the fee is charged directly to merchants rather than end-users.  RHB stated that the revision aligns with the evolving payment landscape and ongoing servicing requirements, ensuring it can continue providing consistent service quality. Merchants seeking further details on the new rates are advised to contact their RHB home branch.

title: 'Maybank Fully Redeems RM1.56 Billion AT1 Sukuk On First Call Date
body: 'Maybank has fully redeemed its RM1.56 billion Additional Tier 1 (AT1) Sukuk Mudharabah on its first call date, seven years after the Islamic capital securities were issued.  The banking group said the redemption was completed on the same day, Sept 25, 2026.  The AT1 Sukuk Mudharabah was originally issued on Sept 25, 2019, under Maybank’s sukuk programme, which has since been upsized from RM10 billion to RM30 billion in nominal value.  The securities were structured based on the Shariah principle of Mudharabah, a profit-sharing arrangement, and formed part of the banking group’s Additional Tier 1 capital instruments.  Maybank Investment Bank Bhd made the announcement on behalf of Maybank’s board of directors.

title: 'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network accounts
body: 'THE High Court here today fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.   Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.   Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

title: 'Lindung 24 Perkeso tidak jejaskan industri insurans secara ketara — CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 29 Sept - Skim Lindung 24 Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (Perkeso) dijangka meluaskan perlindungan kemalangan kepada pekerja tanpa menjejaskan industri insurans dan takaful swasta secara ketara, menurut CIMB Securities. Skim yang berkuat kuasa pada 1 Jun 2026 itu memberi perlindungan kepada pekerja yang layak bagi kemalangan yang tidak berkaitan dengan pekerjaan, termasuk ketika berada di rumah, melakukan perjalanan peribadi atau menyertai aktiviti riadah. Ia melengkapi Skim Bencana Pekerjaan Perkeso yang melindungi pekerja bagi kemalangan berkaitan kerja. Menurut firma penyelidikan itu, Lindung 24 terutamanya memberi manfaat kepada pekerja yang kurang mendapat perlindungan, manakala insurans perubatan, hayat dan hilang upaya swasta masih mempunyai peranan tersendiri. Memetik Perkeso, firma itu berkata kira-kira 48% rakyat Malaysia mempunyai perlindungan insurans selain insurans motor. Dalam kalangan kumpulan berpendapatan 40% terendah (B40), kadar perlindungan dianggarkan hanya 4%. Menurut laporan berkenaan, kira-kira 38,000 tuntutan ditolak antara 2015 hingga 2025 kerana kemalangan yang dialami pekerja tidak memenuhi syarat bagi faedah bencana pekerjaan. Perkeso menganggarkan Lindung 24 boleh memberi perlindungan kepada kira-kira 250,000 pekerja setahun bagi kemalangan yang sebelum ini berada di luar skop skim sedia ada. Setakat 9 September, seramai 8.5 juta pekerja, bersamaan 87.6%, kekal menyertai Lindung 24 selepas tempoh memilih untuk tidak menyertai skim itu berakhir pada 31 Ogos. Kira-kira 1.2 juta pekerja memilih untuk tidak menyertainya, dengan 52% daripada mereka berpendapatan kurang RM3,500 sebulan. Caruman meningkat secara berperingkat Caruman yang ditanggung sepenuhnya oleh pekerja ditetapkan pada kadar 0.75% daripada gaji bulanan bagi tempoh 1 Jun 2026 hingga 31 Mei 2028. Kadar itu meningkat kepada 1% mulai 1 Jun 2028 dan 1.25% mulai 1 Jun 2031, tertakluk kepada siling gaji bulanan RM6,000. Penyertaan adalah secara sukarela bagi pekerja tempatan, tetapi mandatori bagi pekerja asing yang layak. Faedah skim ini merangkumi rawatan perubatan, bayaran bagi hilang upaya sementara atau kekal, pemulihan, faedah kepada orang tanggungan dan faedah pengurusan mayat. Anak tanggungan yang layak juga boleh memohon faedah pendidikan dalam bentuk pinjaman, tertakluk kepada syarat Perkeso. Kadar bayaran hilang upaya bergantung pada taksiran dan peraturan yang berkuat kuasa. Polisi kemalangan diri paling berpotensi bertindih Menurut CIMB Securities, pertindihan paling ketara dengan produk insurans swasta mungkin berlaku pada polisi kemalangan diri yang dibeli secara individu atau disediakan oleh majikan. Majikan boleh menilai semula faedah kemalangan yang bertindih dan mengalihkan sebahagian perbelanjaan kepada perlindungan perubatan atau manfaat pekerja yang lain. Bagaimanapun, polisi swasta kekal relevan, khususnya bagi pekerja yang pendapatannya melebihi siling gaji RM6,000 yang digunakan bagi Lindung 24. Produk swasta juga menawarkan pilihan perlindungan perubatan, hayat, penyakit kritikal dan pendapatan yang lebih luas. CIMB Securities berkata peningkatan kesedaran tentang jurang perlindungan dalam jangka panjang boleh mendorong permintaan terhadap produk insurans dan kesihatan lain. Firma itu mengekalkan pandangan `Neutral' terhadap sektor insurans, sambil menyatakan pandangan yang lebih positif terhadap LPI Capital berbanding Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga. — DagangNews.com

Perkeso menganggarkan Lindung 24 boleh memberi perlindungan kepada kira-kira 250,000 pekerja setahun bagi kemalangan yang sebelum ini berada di luar skop skim sedia ada. Setakat 9 September, seramai 8.5 juta pekerja, bersamaan 87.6%, kekal menyertai Lindung 24 selepas tempoh memilih untuk tidak menyertai skim itu berakhir pada 31 Ogos. Kira-kira 1.2 juta pekerja memilih untuk tidak menyertainya, dengan 52% daripada mereka berpendapatan kurang RM3,500 sebulan. Caruman meningkat secara berperingkat Caruman yang ditanggung sepenuhnya oleh pekerja ditetapkan pada kadar 0.75% daripada gaji bulanan bagi tempoh 1 Jun 2026 hingga 31 Mei 2028. Kadar itu meningkat kepada 1% mulai 1 Jun 2028 dan 1.25% mulai 1 Jun 2031, tertakluk kepada siling gaji bulanan RM6,000. Penyertaan adalah secara sukarela bagi pekerja tempatan, tetapi mandatori bagi pekerja asing yang layak. Faedah skim ini merangkumi rawatan perubatan, bayaran bagi hilang upaya sementara atau kekal, pemulihan, faedah kepada orang tanggungan dan faedah pengurusan mayat. Anak tanggungan yang layak juga boleh memohon faedah pendidikan dalam bentuk pinjaman, tertakluk kepada syarat Perkeso. Kadar bayaran hilang upaya bergantung pada taksiran dan peraturan yang berkuat kuasa. Polisi kemalangan diri paling berpotensi bertindih Menurut CIMB Securities, pertindihan paling ketara dengan produk insurans swasta mungkin berlaku pada polisi kemalangan diri yang dibeli secara individu atau disediakan oleh majikan. Majikan boleh menilai semula faedah kemalangan yang bertindih dan mengalihkan sebahagian perbelanjaan kepada perlindungan perubatan atau manfaat pekerja yang lain. Bagaimanapun, polisi swasta kekal relevan, khususnya bagi pekerja yang pendapatannya melebihi siling gaji RM6,000 yang digunakan bagi Lindung 24. Produk swasta juga menawarkan pilihan perlindungan perubatan, hayat, penyakit kritikal dan pendapatan yang lebih luas. CIMB Securities berkata peningkatan kesedaran tentang jurang perlindungan dalam jangka panjang boleh mendorong permintaan terhadap produk insurans dan kesihatan lain. Firma itu mengekalkan pandangan `Neutral' terhadap sektor insurans, sambil menyatakan pandangan yang lebih positif terhadap LPI Capital berbanding Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga. — DagangNews.com

title: 'Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 25): Malaysian plantation companies with sizeable operations in Indonesia face greater regulatory uncertainty following the country’s new agrarian reform law, with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG), Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KL:KLK) among those with the largest exposure, according to CIMB Securities.

The potential impact, however, remains unclear as key details — including maximum landholding limits for companies and affiliated entities, and how a provision requiring at least 20% of certain land to be made available for agrarian reform and redistribution — have yet to be finalised through implementing regulations.

As such, CIMB has not made any adjustments to its earnings forecasts or the land banks of plantation companies under its coverage, saying it sees higher regulatory uncertainty rather than an immediate loss of land or earnings.

“We do not expect an across-the-board 20% cut in existing land,” the research house said in a note on Friday.

Indonesia’s parliament approved the Agrarian Reform Law on Tuesday, creating a broader framework to address land ownership concentration, redistribution and longstanding agrarian conflicts. The law also provides for a dedicated body under the president to oversee implementation, supervision and conflict resolution.

However, the Indonesian government still needs to draw up implementing rules that will, among other matters, determine minimum and maximum landholding limits. Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning Minister Nusron Wahid said such details would be provided through subsequent regulations.

The development was reported earlier this week, including by Bloomberg, which highlighted broader risks to Indonesia’s plantation and property sectors. CIMB’s latest assessment focuses on the potential implications for Malaysian-listed plantation companies.

Among CIMB’s Malaysian plantation coverage, SD Guthrie, Genting Plantations and KLK have the largest absolute plantation exposure to Indonesia. IOI Corp Bhd (KL:IOICORP) has a smaller relative exposure, while Johor Plantations Group Bhd (KL:JPG), Ta Ann Holdings Bhd (KL:TAANN) and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd (KL:HSPLANT) have plantation operations entirely in Malaysia.

CIMB said the impact will depend on the final land limits, whether the 20% rule applies to existing plantations and how it will be implemented.

Bloomberg consensus as at Friday showed analysts remaining broadly positive on SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations, while views on KLK were more mixed.

For SD Guthrie, 17 analysts had "buy" calls and three had "hold" calls, with a 12-month target price of RM7.68. Genting Plantations had 10 "buy" calls and two "hold" calls, with a target price of RM6.81. KLK had nine "buy" calls, 10 "hold" calls, and one "sell", with a target price of RM24.57.

Separately, India’s decision to lower import duties on major edible oils could provide some support for crude palm oil (CPO) demand, although CIMB expects the benefit to Malaysian planters to be modest.

India cut the basic customs duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil to 5% from 10%, while eliminating the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil, effective Thursday. The Indian government said the move was aimed at reducing import costs and easing domestic edible oil prices.

CIMB said the lower CPO duty should reduce landed costs and support Indian palm oil imports, although the larger tariff reduction for sunflower oil could make it more competitive against palm oil and limit the increase in demand.

India accounted for about 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025. CIMB said the main benefit for Malaysian planters would likely come through firmer CPO prices rather than a significant direct increase in export volumes.

CIMB maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 per tonne for 2027.
