body: 'KUALA LUMPUR,. Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang KUALA LUMPUR,. Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), berkata agihan pendapatan akhir bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 Sept 2026 adalah sebanyak 2.1 sen seunit, dengan tambahan agihan bonus sebanyak 0.4 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan PHB selaku penaja dana itu. “Edaran bonus itu akan diberikan bagi 1,000,000 unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Dengan mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.5 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan pada April 2026, jumlah keseluruhan agihan pendapatan AHB bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 2026 adalah lima sen seunit,” menurut kenyataan itu. PHB berkata sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan pada pusingan akhir, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan tahunan sebanyak RM236.41 juta. Pengarah Urusan kumpulan PHB Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan pendapatan bagi setahun penuh itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB yang berterusan serta kekuatan portfolio hartanah asasnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan yang berdisiplin oleh PHB. “Prestasi AHB tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit. “Pada masa sama, kami kekal memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan yang dinamik serta pengoptimuman portfolio yang berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan yang mampan danpenciptaan nilai jangka panjang,” katanya. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM Zulkifli Ishak berkata pengurus dana itu kekal fokus menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB berkata agihan pendapatan itu akan dibayar dalam bentuk unit AHB yang dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun AHB pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Okt 2026. Agihan tersebut akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, sekali gus membolehkan pemegang unit menambah pegangan unit serta berpotensi menikmati kesan pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. “Pelabur Bumiputera yang ingin melanggan AHB boleh berbuat demikian pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. “Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd,” katanya. — BERNAMA

title: 'CIMB IB says Malaysia could widen corporate tax base for Budget 2027, cut old deductions
body: 'CIMB IB says Malaysia could widen corporate tax base for Budget 2027, cut old deductions KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Malaysia could widen its corporate tax base by reviewing special and double deductions that have been in place for two to three decades, and remove deductions that no longer serve their original purpose, said CIMB Investment Bank. CIMB IB said, citing KPMG senior adviser on tax policy Dr Verrinderjeet Singh during a discussion, that the removal of selected deductions could lead to the government collecting more revenue while creating room for a lower headline corporate tax rate. “His [Verrinderjeet] proposal is selective: investment incentives remain important for attracting businesses, but their benefits need closer scrutiny. He links Malaysia’s shift towards outcome-based incentives to its response to Global Minimum Tax,” said CIMB IB. It added, “Their effectiveness will depend on monitoring whether investors deliver the intended economic benefits”. Malaysia’s headline corporate income tax rate is currently 24%, but the amount of tax companies ultimately pay is also affected by deductions, exemptions and investment incentives. On major tax changes, CIMB IB said Malaysia is unlikely to introduce new tax changes in Budget 2027, with stronger collection from existing taxes and a wider tax base offering the main scope for raising government revenue. The government is expected to focus on improving tax collection, particularly by bringing more businesses into the tax net and identifying income that is not fully reported. Smaller businesses are likely to offer more room for additional collections, as larger companies are already more visible to the tax authorities, said CIMB IB. “His central message was that stronger collection and targeted refinements to existing taxes offer the main near-term revenue opportunities. Against a continued focus on cost-of-living support and the social agenda, he expects few substantial tax changes in the coming budget,” said CIMB IB. E-invoicing could help identify unreported taxable activity, although smaller businesses face additional compliance and technology costs. CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet expects participation to broaden as economic conditions improve. CIMB IB also sees scope for greater use of data analytics by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) and Customs to identify businesses and income outside the existing tax net. On indirect taxes, CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet does not expect the goods and services tax (GST) to return in Budget 2027. Instead, the focus is likely to remain on improving the existing sales and service tax (SST). SST is estimated to cover about 78% to 80% of goods and services, approaching the breadth of the former GST regime. CIMB said broader exemptions for business inputs could reduce the cascading of tax costs through supply chains, although this would come at the cost of lower tax receipts. Veerinderjeet also does not expect an increase in the 2% dividend tax on annual dividend income above RM100,000, an extension of capital gains tax to listed shares or a further increase in the 30% top personal income tax rate in Budget 2027, according to the note. “Dr Veerinderjeet argues that the government should ‘sweat our assets’ through better collection, supported by greater investment in tax agency analytics. These efforts can deliver incremental gains, while broader personal, corporate and indirect tax bases offer scope to lift tax-to-GDP towards 15% over time,” said CIMB IB economists. Veerinderjeet estimates only 15% to 16% of the workforce currently pays personal income tax, with low wages limiting the number of taxpayers. Higher wages would therefore be important in expanding the personal income tax base. Budget 2027 is expected to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Maybank Commits RM10 Billion to Technology and Growth Under ROAR30
body: 'Maybank is committing RM10 billion in investment through 2030 as it expands its ROAR30 strategy across technology, regional banking, payments, wealth management and sustainability. The banking group plans to spend RM1.5 billion on technology during FY2026 alone. Its investment programme will cover core system modernisation, artificial intelligence, cloud adoption, resilience improvements and stronger risk and compliance capabilities. Maybank expects those investments to help it increase productivity while providing more personalised services across its regional operations. The programme comes as the group reported RM5.17 billion in net profit for the first half of FY2026. Technology Becomes Central to Maybank ROAR30 Maybank is positioning technology as an important enabler of its next phase of regional growth. The group intends to modernise core banking infrastructure while expanding the use of AI and cloud technologies. It is also investing in systems designed to improve operational resilience and strengthen compliance capabilities. President and Group CEO Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli said technology was already helping Maybank deepen customer engagement, scale its businesses and improve productivity. The ROAR30 strategy will place greater emphasis on businesses where Maybank believes it can establish or extend regional leadership. These include Islamic finance, wealth management, transaction banking, payments, corporate and investment banking, and SMEs. Wealth and Investment Banking Fees Rise Several of Maybank’s targeted growth areas recorded stronger performance during the first half of FY2026. Wealth fee income increased 49.6% year-on-year to RM925.4 million. Corporate and investment banking fee income rose 15.6% to RM1.51 billion. Cross-border payments volume increased 15.8% to RM465.2 billion. Maybank also continued expanding its Islamic financial services business. Islamic corporate and investment banking income increased 3.9% year-on-year to RM896.8 million. Takaful net written contribution rose 10.2% to RM1.72 billion. The figures support Maybank’s strategy of increasing revenue from fee-based and regional businesses alongside traditional lending. Maybank Declares 31 Sen Interim Dividend Shareholders will also receive a higher first interim dividend following Maybank’s resilient first-half performance. The board declared 31 sen per share, compared with 30 sen per share for the first half of FY2025. Five sen per share will be electable under Maybank’s Dividend Reinvestment Plan. The dividend represents an estimated total payout of RM3.75 billion. That amount is equivalent to approximately 72.5% of Maybank’s first-half net profit. The payout highlights the group’s attempt to balance shareholder returns with continued investment in technology, growth and balance-sheet resilience. Maybank maintained a Common Equity Tier 1 ratio of 14.92% as of June 2026. Its total capital ratio stood at 18.68%. Sustainable Finance Reaches RM31.81 Billion Sustainability remains another major component of Maybank’s longer-term strategy. The group mobilised RM31.81 billion in sustainable finance as of June 2026. It also mobilised RM12.86 billion in social finance and RM30.96 million through social empowerment initiatives during the same period. Maybank said these programmes benefited more than 268,000 people. More than 238,000 people were reached through financial inclusion initiatives, while approximately 30,000 participated in financial literacy programmes. Maybank has refreshed its long-term sustainable finance ambition to RM300 billion by 2030. It is also targeting RM24 billion in annual social finance, with programmes intended to economically empower three million people. Maybank Cuts Operational Carbon Emissions The group reported a 58.9% reduction in carbon emissions against its baseline. That places Maybank close to its 2026 target of a 61% reduction. Its longer-term goals include achieving carbon neutrality by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2050. Maybank also reported continued progress across six priority sectors within its financed emissions portfolio. Physical emissions intensity has declined 23% in power, 13% in palm oil and 10% in commercial real estate since the baseline year. Automotive emissions intensity declined 8%. Steel and aluminium remained below their respective emissions glidepaths. Maybank said those improvements reflected portfolio management, client engagement and increased exposure to lower-emitting assets. ROAR30 Targets Regional Leadership Maybank Chairman Tan Sri Dato’ Sri Ir. Zamzamzairani Mohd Isa said the group’s capital and liquidity positions provide a strong foundation for navigating changing market conditions. He also emphasised the group’s commitment to responsible growth, shareholder value and sustainability. Khairussaleh said Maybank would continue sharpening its focus on businesses where it can lead while strengthening capabilities across the region. The strategy combines several priorities that traditionally compete for capital. Maybank intends to continue paying meaningful shareholder dividends while investing heavily in technology and pursuing regional growth. At the same time, the group is increasing sustainable finance commitments and working towards progressively tighter emissions targets. Its RM10 billion investment programme therefore represents more than a technology upgrade. It forms part of a broader attempt to position Maybank for the next phase of Southeast Asian banking, where digital services, regional scale, fee income and sustainability are becoming increasingly important sources of competitive advantage.

title: 'AirAsia’s Hunt for Cheaper Debt Won’t be Easy With US$100 Oil
body: '(Sept 24): AirAsia Group Bhd’s (KL:AAGB) Tan Sri Tony Fernandes is fed up with private credit and the exorbitant interest rate they charge. “I don’t want to take any more private credit debt because it’s expensive,” the co-founder of one of the biggest Southeast Asian budget carriers said at a briefing last week. “I don’t want more debt. I don’t like debt.” While Fernandes is seeking to reduce interest payments — some as high as 11% — through a US$1 billion (RM4.09 billion) refinancing package, it may be tough for a company that sells cheap flight tickets to make money when oil prices are above US$100 a barrel. AirAsia’s finances are so strained that it loses money, has more liabilities than assets, and has a cash-to-revenue ratio that’s well below the industry standard. “AirAsia likely needs either a real improvement in operating cash flow or credit enhancement,” said Linus Benjamin Bauer, founder of aviation consultancy BAA & Partners. “Without that, cheaper money is difficult to justify.” Like most airlines, the Iran war hit AirAsia hard but the carrier, which doesn’t hedge its fuel costs, has been grappling with soaring prices to such extent that it went through two straight quarterly losses. Its total debt had surged to a record US$4.1 billion at the end of June, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. While the jump largely reflected Fernandes’ consolidation of all its airline businesses into AirAsia from sister firm Capital A Bhd (KL:CAPITALA), AirAsia’s liabilities exceeded assets by RM606 million as of end-June, according to the company’s first-half financial report. It also shows it had RM954 million in cash and RM18.4 billion in current liabilities due over the next 12 months, suggesting coverage of only 5%. The cash represents 4.3% of AirAsia’s annualized revenue of RM22 billion and “normal airline practice is to have cash and facilities of at least 10%-20% of annualized revenue”, said independent aviation analyst Andrew Light. Fernandes has received an offer for US$1 billion of financing from Middle East banks to refinance existing debt, but he’s holding off on a final sign-off while he searches for cheaper alternatives. AirAsia, which is also seeking RM700 million in local credit facilities, aims to complete the refinancing by December or January. AirAsia declined to comment on its recent fundraising efforts and whether talks with creditors reflected liquidity pressures or raised concerns about its ability to meet obligations without additional financing. “Unless Tony can present a credible business plan to get the airline back to positive cash flow, raising the money AirAsia needs on commercial terms will become increasingly difficult,” said Gerry Soejatman, an independent aviation analyst based in Jakarta. “That challenge will only get harder if oil prices stay elevated or rise further.” Highlighting its financial strain, AirAsia fell behind on dues to some suppliers and asked lessors to defer rental payments on more than 16 aircraft after fuel costs surged, Bloomberg reported in June. It had also asked private-credit lenders Ares Management Corp and Indies Capital Partners Pte Ltd to allow aircraft lessors to share revenue from routes pledged to their US$200 million facility. And since the start of 2025, it sold six brand new Airbus planes without ever putting them into service. Fernandes denied renegotiating with Ares, and said the jet sale reported by Bloomberg was inaccurate, adding the company was returning planes it didn’t need “in this crisis”. The planned US$1 billion in refinancing debt would save AirAsia around RM200 million a year in interest expense if it’s able to lower the interest rate on debt raised during the Covid pandemic and private credit to 7%-8% from around 11%, said Samuel Yin, associate director for equity markets research at Maybank Investment Bank. “The debt isn’t maturing this year, but the airline wants to prepare ahead of upcoming obligations. title: 'HLB Islamic fund lifts Langkawi entrepreneurs’ income
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Aligned with its commitment to deepening its value-based intermediation (VBI) ecosystem, HLB Islamic has channeled RM138,600 in social financing towards social enterprise SURI Inspirasi under Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) iTEKAD framework, which has led to a 94% average surge in monthly income and over RM14,000 in total new earnings for participating entrepreneurs of SURI’s Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) programme.  The SRI programme empowers underserved communities to upcycle discarded fabrics into unique fashion items, creating sustainable jobs and encouraging entrepreneurship while promoting zero-waste fashion and community empowerment. As part of the programme, the participating entrepreneurs, predominantly underserved single mothers, produced 1,000 school uniforms for students across five schools in Langkawi, generating RM30,000 in savings for local families.  HLB Islamic commemorated the milestone through the handover of high-grade sewing machines to the participating entrepreneurs, marking the transition from classroom learning to active enterprise ownership.  According to HLBIslamic CEO Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, “Our vision of financial stewardship is grounded in our Hayat @ HLB Islamic framework, which views wealth building as a purposeful journey across life stages, starting with wealth creation. Through our partnership with SURI, we are providing the community with the essential tools and training to unlock their entrepreneurial potential, and we hope this will catalyse a lifelong trajectory of building wealth towards financial independence that will enrich the community for generations to come.”  This success marks a significant milestone in HLB Islamic’s ongoing collaboration with SURI, who first entered the bank’s ecosystem as a participant of the HLB Jumpstart initiative. Launched to incubate high-impact Malaysian social enterprises through commercial mentorship, branding, and digital capacity building, HLB Jumpstart provided SURI with the early framework to scale its operations, illustrating the bank’s long-term strategy of nurturing social ventures into self-sustaining implementation partners capable of delivering widespread impact.

title: 'Religion is not a political tool: Due process must follow Noorazli’s remarks
body: 'Community Action Network (CAN) Malaysia views with grave concern the recent conduct of Sepang Umno chief Noorazli Said, who misquoted sacred biblical scripture Psalms 129 while making inappropriate remarks during the recent Umno general assembly. Faith is sacred – not a political punchline: Religion should never be weaponised, trivialised or used as a tool for political posturing. In a multi-religious society like Malaysia, leaders across the political spectrum must treat all sacred texts and religious communities with absolute respect. Exploiting faith and sacred traditions on political platforms damages the delicate fabric of social harmony. The rule is simple: all religions must be respected equally and just like the commandments we subscribe to, we must treat thy neighbours as how we want to be treated. Ignorance is no excuse for political leaders: CAN is deeply appalled that a senior political leader could recklessly misquote the Bible to deliver a crude and sexual analogy that is completely devoid of the original text. Leadership demands accountability, precision and basic literacy regarding the diverse beliefs of the electorate. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member If a leader lacks knowledge on a matter – especially one involving sacred texts, the standard must be simple: if you do not know, do not say it. Misinformation masked as political rhetoric sets a dangerous precedent. Apologies do not preempt the law – due process must take place: While CAN acknowledges that Noorazli has issued a public apology, an apology alone does not erase legal responsibility or mitigate the impact of inﬂammatory speech. A healthy democracy relies on the consistent application of the rule of law. Apologising cannot serve as a free pass to bypass statutory oversight. Authorities must handle this matter with complete impartiality. Due process must take its course, and a thorough investigation by the relevant enforcement bodies must be conducted to determine whether legal standards were breached. Equal enforcement of the law is necessary to signal that religious provocation will carry consequences, regardless of political affiliation. A reconciliation mechanism is much needed in Malaysia, particularly in the context of the religious rhetoric and controversies that have taken place over the years. Too often, there is no clear or meaningful process through which harm, hurt and grievances arising from statements or actions concerning religion can be acknowledged and addressed. A nation that moves forward is one that is courageous enough to acknowledge when words or actions have caused hurt, disrespect or oﬀence to another person’s religion, beliefs or place of worship. Reconciliation is not about assigning blame or suppressing diﬃcult conversations. It is about creating a constructive space for acknowledgement, dialogue, accountability and, where appropriate, an apology. In the light of this, CAN calls on all political leaders to elevate the standard of public discourse and refrain from dragging religious texts and ﬁgures into political theatrics and to advocate for a meaningful reconciliation mechanism that will provide a space, allowing grievances to be heard and addressed before they deepen existing divisions. At the same time, CAN applauds and commends the political leaders, civil society organisations and concerned people across party and religious lines who promptly called out this unacceptable behaviour. Their swift condemnation demonstrates that ordinary people are united in refusing to normalise religious disrespect, setting a necessary standard for interfaith courtesy and national unity. In this regard, it is also opportune for us to wish everyone a Happy Malaysia Day! May this day be remembered for the commonality we share as true-spirited people who care about a greater Malaysia. – CAN, 17 September The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

title: 'Mesiniaga Wins Two-year RM32.3m Contract Extension From Customs Dept
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MYGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. According to the company’s bourse filing on Tuesday, the agreement does not include an automatic renewal clause. The MyGST system is the Customs Department's legacy online system for administering goods and services tax (GST), which was Malaysia's broad-based consumption tax from April 2015 until its abolition in September 2018. Malaysia's current sales and service tax (SST) system is administered through MySST, but MyGST system remains in operation as the agency maintains it to support other tax administrative matters, fulfil statutory/legal requirements and work procedures. Mesiniaga said the contract is expected to contribute positively to the group’s earnings and net assets for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026) and subsequent periods until completion. For the first half of FY2026, Mesiniaga’s net loss narrowed to RM0.95 million from RM2.13 million in the previous period, while revenue was up by 22.4% to RM113.2 million. The group said it saw higher revenue from projects and services deliveries. Shares of Mesiniaga were down by one sen or 0.9% to RM1.16 at market close on Tuesday, giving the group a market value of RM70.1 million. body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The public are annoyed and are questioning why Malaysian Hockey League (MHL) matches will be played on Nov 8, Deepavali Day. title: 'Player fatigue threatens TNB campaign as MHL resumes
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The second round of the Malaysian Hockey League (MHL) begins on Monday, and it has caused havoc for league leaders Tenaga Nasional (TNB) and their season campaign. TNB will face the Armed Forces on Wednesday at the National Hockey Stadium in Bukit Jalil but 11 of their players will only be arriving on Monday from the Asian Games. Malaysia were defeated 5-1 by defending champions India in the Asiad final in Nagoya on Saturday. The first round of MHL ended on May 17 with TNB leading the standings on 19 points from six wins and a draw, followed by Maybank and Terengganu Hockey Team with 17 and 14 points respectively. TNB coach Madzli Ikmar said the 11 national players would be tired after playing three consecutive tournaments at the Nations Cup in South Africa in June, the World Cup in Belgium in August and the Asian Games, which ended on Saturday. "The 11 players need a good rest after playing so many international matches. I have to use the other 12 players in the training squad in the MHL. "I am having a headache as I also need to use national players to play in the league to do well. I have decided that players who played a few matches in the Asian Games would play in the match against Armed Forces," said the former national captain Madzli. Madzli added that the other issue was that the national team would also feature in the six-nation Asian Champions Trophy in Punjab, India from Oct 27 to Nov 5. "Again, national players from TNB would be released to play in the tournament. I know that the priority is the national team, but if all 11 players feature in the tournament, then how are we going to play with the remaining 12 players in MHL? "I will leave it to the team management to decide whether they want to release national players for the tournament," said Madzli. The MHL will break on Nov 14 as the national team prepares for the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup in Ipoh from Nov 22-29 before the national league resumes for the knockout stage on Dec 2.

title: 'India’s Palm Oil Tax Cut Could Boost Earnings For Local Planters, CIMB
body: 'India’s decision to halve import duties on crude palm oil (CPO) could support demand for Malaysian palm oil and provide some relief to plantation companies, although stronger competition from sunflower oil may limit the upside, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest plantation sector report, CIMB said India reduced the basic import duty on CPO to 5% from 10%, effective Sept 24, as the country seeks to ease domestic edible oil prices ahead of its September-to-November festive season.  India also cut the duty on crude soybean oil to 5% and eliminated the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil.  The changes are particularly relevant to Malaysia, with India accounting for approximately 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025, making it an important market for the country’s plantation industry.  Higher CPO Prices Could Benefit Malaysian Planters  CIMB said lower import duties should reduce the landed cost of CPO in India, potentially encouraging higher palm oil consumption and imports.  However, the research house cautioned that the larger duty reduction for sunflower oil could improve its competitiveness against palm oil, limiting any significant shift in Indian demand towards CPO.  Before the announcement, CPO was already trading at a price advantage in the Indian market. As at Sept 18, its landed price stood at approximately US$1,265 per tonne, compared with US$1,314 for soybean oil and US$1,380 for sunflower oil.  CIMB expects the benefits for Malaysian plantation companies to come primarily through firmer CPO prices rather than a substantial increase in export volumes.  Upstream producers such as Johor Plantations Group, Genting Plantations, Hap Seng Plantations, Ta Ann Holdings and United Malacca have greater earnings sensitivity to higher CPO prices.  Integrated plantation groups, including SD Guthrie, IOI Corporation and Kuala Lumpur Kepong, could also benefit from stronger upstream margins.  Crude Palm Oil Retains Advantage Over Refined Products  CIMB noted that India has maintained a sizeable import duty differential between crude and refined palm oil, which continues to favour CPO imports for processing by Indian refiners.  The basic import duty on refined palm oil was reduced to 27.5% from 32.5%, compared with the new 5% duty on CPO.  As a result, CIMB expects the impact on Malaysian downstream refiners to remain broadly neutral.  The research house maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 for 2027, alongside its Overweight rating on the Malaysian plantation sector.

title: 'Tenaga Nasional Tells Analysts Extra Subsidy Is One-off, Mulls Permanent Solutions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 23): Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA) said the extra subsidy earmarked for households is a one-off measure, and the national electric utility is mulling tweaks to its charges to better shield consumers. The initial estimate of up to RM150 million in costs to subsidise consumers from rising electricity bills is conservative and the actual cost may be lower for the company, according to several analysts that attended an investor briefing by Tenaga Nasional on Tuesday. Tenaga Nasional stressed that “this is a one-off corporate contribution outside the regulatory framework, rather than a change to the revenue-cap or price-cap mechanism”, BIMB Securities said in a post-briefing note. The briefing follows a decline in Tenaga Nasional’s share price as investors priced in earnings impact after the company agreed to absorb the impact from the electricity tariff fuel surcharge exemption that has been expanded to more households up until the end of this year. Consumers are seeing relatively higher electricity bills from soaring temperatures and work-from-home policy and other seasonal factors. Last week, the government announced that households consuming 800 kilowatt-hour of power or less monthly will now be spared from surcharges under the automatic fuel adjustment. The exemption is previously provided only to those using under 600 kilowatt-hour each month. More importantly, Tenaga Nasional and the government are working on a more permanent solution for 2027 onwards to address elevated fuel price, CIMB Securities said. One possible approach could be differentiated rates versus the current uniform rate, and similar to how the imbalance cost pass-through, or ICPT, was previously implemented with residential users paying a lower rate against large-scale commercial users, the house noted. While there is no clarity on the new structure, the previous framework under ICPT mechanism allowed “cross subsidisation and potentially greater protection” for residential consumers and even small and medium enterprises, TA Securities added. Under the previous mechanism that was replaced in June 2025 with the automatic fuel adjustment system, the final tariff to be paid by consumers was adjusted every six months in the form of rebates or surcharges on top of the base tariff. title: 'RHB, The Makeover Guys Offer Flexi Loan for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: 'RHB Bank has partnered with renovation firm The Makeover Guys to offer financing that covers both a property purchase and renovation costs. The Makeover Flexi Loan provides eligible customers with financing of up to 120% of the property’s value. This comprises up to 90% for the home purchase and an additional 30% for renovation work, mortgage insurance or takaful, legal costs and documentation fees. Borrowers can repay the loan over a maximum of 35 years or until they reach the age of 70, whichever comes first. Its Full Flexi features allow them to make additional repayments and redraw funds when needed. Renovation funds will be released progressively as contractors reach project milestones. The facility is designed for homeowners and property investors. Customers can access consultation, interior design, project management and construction services through The Makeover Guys. “We have seen customers delay moving in, renovate room by room over several years or compromise on what they originally wanted because the renovation budget was not available upfront. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one,” said Gavin Liew, Founder & CEO of The Makeover Guys. “As homeownership needs evolve, financing solutions must evolve as well. Traditionally, property financing and renovation financing have been treated as separate decisions, even though both are fundamental to creating a home. We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing these financing needs together under a single solution,” said Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, Group Community Banking, RHB Bank Berhad. title: 'Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.   Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).   "From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises," he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank today.

title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.  Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.  Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.  He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.  Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer was that of debtor and creditor.  In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.  According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.  On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.  The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines had allegedly been breached.  The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.  The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.  The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.  Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.  The company asserted that this conduct amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.  It also claimed that the bank’s conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests.

title: 'Inside the UN tunnel
body: 'Guillermo R Barreto In September, like every year, the UN General Assembly commences. Heads of state take the floor to send messages to the world. These messages are broadcast on TV, transcribed, and recorded in official documents and the press. We have heard denunciations of violations of international law, calls for peace and coexistence, and also cynical remarks from leaders of genocidal entities. It is a month of speeches that surely generates revenue for the media and benefits the local economy of New York City. It is month that also entails significant expenses for the delegations of the 193 UN member nations, in addition to the numerous NGO delegations present at or around the event. The UN was founded in 1945 following the end of the Great Anti-Fascist War, referred to as World War Two, by the Eurocentric narrative. Its purposes, principles and structure are set forth in the UN Charter, signed on 26 June 1945, in San Francisco and enforced since 24 October of that same year. As stated in Article 1, its purpose is to maintain international peace and security and to promote friendly relations among nations, based on respect for the principle of equal rights and the self-determination of peoples. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Fundamental freedoms, respect for human rights, and universal peace – these are legitimate principles worth fighting for. The history of the UN, however, does not show that it has been capable of defending the principles for which it was created. Let’s look at three examples of this. In 1993 amid the war in the former Yugoslavia, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 819, which required the parties to the conflict (in this case, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina) to treat the city of Srebrenica and its surrounding areas as safe areas, free from armed attacks or any other hostile acts. At that time, Bosnian Serb forces were carrying out an operation to displace and exterminate the Muslim population of Bosnia, thousands of whom sought refuge in Srebrenica, where they expected protection from the UN through its protection force Unprofor. This protection never materialised, and the Bosnian Serb army attacked, resulting in the massacre of 8,372 people. Even today, hundreds of bodies have not been located. Rwanda is another tragic case. There, the United Nations Assistance Mission (Unamir) was established to mediate the conflict that had been brewing and that led, in 1994, to the massacre of the Tutsi population by the Hutu army and militias. The reality is that, while the Security Council debated whether to use the term ‘genocide’ to describe what was happening, Unamir’s blue helmets were restricted in their actions, their personnel reduced to 250 troops, and the slaughter continued, leaving hundreds of thousands of people unprotected; they were ultimately murdered before the eyes of a world that watched without reacting. The words of the peacekeeping force commander, Romeo Dellaire, speak volumes: “I know that the mourning for all those Rwandans who placed their faith in us and believed that the UN Peacekeeping Force was there to stop the extermination, to stop the killings, and to guide them toward peace will never end. That mission, Unamir, failed.” Another UN failure is reflected in the United Nations Stabilisation Mission in Haiti (Minustah). A blue helmet intervention was launched to “maintain peace and security and support a political process leading to elections in 2010”. The mission remained in place until 2017, when its continued presence was deemed unsustainable. The conduct of Minustah soldiers has been heavily criticised, with numerous cases of rape and abuse of women and children. The introduction of a cholera epidemic (due to negligence in the management of wastewater from the blue helmets’ camps), caused some 9,792 deaths and affected about 820,000 people between 2010 and 2019. To date, the UN has not provided any form of compensation, and there has been no restorative justice for these cases. These are just three examples. The reality is that the UN was born with fundamental flaws: - A General Assembly where all parties have a voice and a vote and pass resolutions that are merely deliberative in nature and not legally binding - A Security Council composed of five permanent members with veto power and 10 non-permanent members – five of whom are elected each year for a two-year term – who, although they can make decisions, are severely limited by the veto power of the permanent members This is a self-perpetuating structure that, day by day, seems to be turning into an empty shell, powerless to transform an increasingly cruel reality. Twenty years ago, in an iconic speech before the UN General Assembly, the then-president of Venezuela, Hugo Chávez, said: “The United Nations system that emerged after World War Two has collapsed, shattered, it does not work anymore.” In that speech, Chávez called for the re-founding of the UN and put four proposals on the table: - The expansion of the Security Council in both the permanent and non-permanent categories - The implementation of effective methods for addressing and resolving conflicts - The immediate abolition of the veto power - The strengthening of the role and powers of the secretary-general Chávez added that it was necessary to move the organisation’s headquarters to another country that, unlike the US, would respect the host country’s norms by not imposing visa restrictions on delegations that are entitled to participate in the General Assembly and in the organisation’s own meetings and activities. For this year’s 2026 Assembly, the State Department is preventing the Palestinian delegation from attending. title: 'Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas
body: 'PETALING JAYA – Bayi hidrosefalus, Muhammad Mateen Aryan Muhammad Hanif, 15 bulan, dari Sungai Petani, Kedah, kini semakin aktif namun pergerakannya terbatas disebabkan kepalanya yang berat. Bapanya, Muhammad Hanif Zakaria, 32, berkata, Mateen kini cuba menggerakkan badan dan memusingkan badan, tetapi sukar berbuat demikian dengan kepala yang mencecah ukuran 90 sentimeter (cm). “Perkembangan dia okey. Dia pun cuba bergerak, nak pusing badannya, tetapi tak boleh sebab kepala dia berat,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo!. Menurut Muhammad Hanif, keadaan Mateen kini semakin baik apabila sawan yang dialaminya semakin berkurang, namun apabila serangan berlaku, saiz kepala anaknya boleh kembali membesar. “Sejak kami mendapatkan rawatan alternatif, Mateen semakin kurang diserang sawan dan saiz kepala dia turun sedikit ke 89cm. Tapi apabila kena sawan, automatik saiz tu boleh naik balik,” ujarnya. Muhammad Hanif berkata, keperluan asas Matten kini mencukupi dan berterima kasih kepada pihak yang pernah membantu, namun dia dan isteri kini merancang untuk mendapatkan kereta sorong (stroller) khas bagi memudahkan pergerakan Mateen. Bagaimanapun dia menjelaskan, ia perlu ditempah khas mengikut keperluan Mateen, dengan anggaran kos sebanyak RM8,000 dan akan berbuat demikian apabila jumlah itu mencukupi. Orang ramai yang ingin membantu keluarga itu mendapatkan kereta sorong berkenaan, boleh menyalurkan sumbangan ke akaun bank CIMB bernombor 7632966954 di atas nama Muhammad Hanif. Terdahulu Kosmo! melaporkan, Muhammad Hanif yang bekerja sebagai pemandu lori bersyukur kerana anak bongsu daripada tiga beradik itu tidak pernah menangis kesakitan sejak lahir. Dia dan isteri, Habidah Nasruddin, 31, bagaimanapun berdepan kesukaran mengangkat Mateen disebabkan kepalanya yang makin membesar. The post Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas appeared first on Kosmo Online.

title: 'Ex-secretary to PM's Graft Case: Temporary Passport Release for Shamsul Iskandar
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, a former senior political secretary to the prime minister, has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month. The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption. According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties. He said he intends to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11. “Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities. “Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the Madani principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit. Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14. He said the summit aims to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices. Shamsul Iskandar also said he plans to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December. During Monday's proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport. He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month. Deputy public prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online. However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release. Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective from Monday, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16. The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249 respectively, from Tei for the same purpose. The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024. In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei's company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction. title: 'Lelaki bebas tuduhan tipu RM108,500
body: 'Kota Kinabalu: Seorang lelaki bekerja sendiri berusia 50 tahun dilepas dan dibebaskan daripada pertuduhan menipu seorang lelaki membabitkan RM108,500 berkaitan beberapa projek di Kinabatangan dan Semporna. Majistret Wan Farrah Farriza Wan Ghazali memutuskan demikian selepas mendapati pihak pendakwaan gagal membuktikan kes prima facie terhadap Abdillah Hamzah. Abdillah dilepas dan dibebaskan tanpa dipanggil membela diri. Abdillah didakwa menipu Chong Kong Fah dengan memperdayakannya sehingga mempercayai bahawa tertuduh mengurus beberapa projek iaitu pembinaan jalan konkrit ke SMK Bukit Garam, Kinabatangan; menaik taraf sistem perparitan di Taman Perumahan Bukit Permata, Kinabatangan; membaiki jeti terapung di Dataran Lepa-Lepa, Semporna; menaik taraf jalan di kawasan Dolton Town, Semporna; dan membaiki rumah di Semporna. Pertuduhan menyatakan Chong memasukkan wang berkenaan ke dalam akaun syarikat bernama Dilwani Enterprise, yang tidak akan dilakukannya sekiranya tidak diperdayakan sedemikian. Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan antara 23 Jun 2016 dan 5 Disember 2018 di Maybank cawangan Semporna. Pertuduhan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan memperuntukkan hukuman penjara sehingga 10 tahun dan sebatan serta boleh didenda jika sabit kesalahan. Pihak pendakwaan memanggil enam saksi sepanjang perbicaraan. Timbalan Pendakwa Raya (TPR) Noor Hafizah Anggu hadir bagi pihak TPR Arfa Anchal Khan manakala peguam Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip mewakili Abdillah. Sementara itu seorang lelaki berusia 64 tahun mengaku bersalah menyebabkan kecederaan parah terhadap seorang lelaki menggunakan parang. Bagaimanapun Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen Marlina Ibrahim menangguhkan hukuman terhadap Paul Akang ke 28 Oktober ini sementara menunggu laporan perubatan dan forensik. Sementara menunggu tarikh berkenaan, Paul direman lanjut. Paul didakwa menyebabkan kecederaan serius terhadap lelaki berusia 45 tahun itu menggunakan senjata berkenaan pada jam 5 petang, 21 September lalu di hadapan sebuah rumah di Kampung Kelansatan, Kuala Penyu. title: '13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty honours real estate excellence - Newswav
body: 'Top developers celebrated the 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia in partnership with iProperty, presented by Lim Soh & Goonting Advocates & Solicitors, at The St. Regis Kuala Lumpur. Guided by the theme “Defined by Excellence,” the 2026 PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty recognised the country’s best in real estate across 62 categories. From township developers to breakthrough companies, this year’s awards were comprehensive, honouring the best in different real estate segments and regions. Timber Land Group won the evening’s top honour, Best Developer, marking its first-ever win in the category, in addition to Best Developer (East Malaysia). CPI Land was named Best Developer (Central Malaysia) alongside award-winning project Tuan Straits. Tanah Sutera took both Best Developer (Southern Malaysia) and Best Landed Homes Developer, buoyed by winning project The Seed. JLand Group, named Best Township Developer, collected the most awards of any company, covering Developer, Development, and Design categories for projects including Arena Larkin; Bandar Tiram; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – Aspiration Park; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – STeP West; and Medora One. JRK Holdings Berhad won both Best Breakthrough Developer and Best Boutique Developer. Keck Seng (Malaysia) Berhad was named Best Mixed Use Developer, also winning for the project Daya 1 Residences, Taman Daya. Penang developers also made their mark at this year’s awards, with PTL Properties, Aspen and Pinnacle Group among the winners. PTL Properties was named Best Lifestyle Developer, with The Rimbun also winning Best Mass Market Landed Development (Northern) and Best Townhouse Development. Aspen’s Aspen Vision City received the Best Township Development (Northern) award, while Pinnacle Group won Best Premium High-Rise Development (Northern) for Pinnacle Bukit Gambier. Other companies with winning projects include Amalan Setar (M) Sdn Bhd, which won for Ixora Garden – Sari Alamanda 4 Phase 2; Armani Group (Armani Hallson Bukit Bintang); Astaka Kimlun Sdn Bhd (Amora Serviced Residence); BCB Land Sdn. Bhd. (Straya Heights); Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd (Coronation Square; Coronade Twins – Serviced Residences); CTC Development Malaysia Sdn Bhd (CTC Skyone @ Bukit Chagar); Faire Development (bée); Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd (Taman Impian Emas); Infra Park Sdn Bhd (MLIMA Kiara); KEB Berhad (Residensi Cove @ Kota Syahbandar); Matrix Concepts (Levia Residence Puchong); OCR Templer Sdn Bhd (D’Templer Hilltop Residences); Peter’s Group (Cherita Residences); Puncak Concept Sdn Bhd (Puncak LakePark City @ Cyberjaya); R&F Development Sdn Bhd (R&F Princess Cove); Steadfast Properties (Laguna Residences); Tiram Industrial Park Sdn Bhd (Akasia Business Park); Tropicana Corporation Berhad (Clarissa Serviced Suites, Tropicana Cenang); UEM Sunrise Berhad (Intrika, Serene Heightshase s); and Worldwide Holdings Berhad (Pavonia Worldwide, Bukit Bandaraya Shah Alam). Outstanding real estate figures The 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty celebrated some of the impactful figures in Malaysian real estate. Tan Sri Dato’ Seri Dr. Jeffrey Cheah KBE AO, founder and chairman of Sunway Group, received the Life Achievement Award. Dato’ Seri Azmir Merican, group managing director and chief executive officer of Sime Darby Property, was named Real Estate Personality of the Year. Dato’ Sri Edwin Tan Pei Seng, executive chairman of Paragon Globe Berhad, was honoured as Rising Star, while Ms. Maggie Ng Mui Kit, chief executive officer of Kuok Group Property Division (Southern), received the Woman Changemaker Award. Consumers, catalysts, and consistency The Consumer Demand Award continued this year, recognising the property that captured the strongest genuine interest from Malaysian property seekers. Determined by consumer views and leads across PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com.my, Leisure Farm Resort by Mulpha International was named Most In-Demand Bungalow/Villa, in addition to winning Best Resort-Style Township Development. The People’s Choice Awards also continued the tradition of tapping consumer opinion to identify the nation’s 10 favourite developers. This year, 15,383 votes were cast for developers that consumers in Malaysia admire and trust. The winners of the People’s Choice Awards in 2026 are: Berinda Group; Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd; CPI Land; Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd; JLand Group; KEB Berhad; Matrix Concepts; Pinnacle Group; Tropicana Corporation Berhad; and UEM Sunrise Berhad. In addition, PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com.my presented several titles for the first time this year. IIB Experience Centre (IIBEX) by Iskandar Investment Berhad received the inaugural Real Estate Ecosystem Catalyst Award. The Consistency Excellence Awards also made their debut, recognising companies with consecutive years of wins at the awards. Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd won the 4-Year Consistency Excellence Award. Meanwhile, the 3-Year Consistency Excellence Awards were presented to Armani Group; Astaka Padu Sdn Bhd; Berinda Group; Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd; Iskandar Investment Berhad; JLand Group; R&F Development Sdn Bhd; and Tropicana Corporation Berhad. Live selection process Winners of the competitive categories were selected during the Live Judging Days from 30 June to 2 July 2026 at the Amari Hotel Kuala Lumpur. The evaluation process, independently supervised by HLB Ler Lum Chew, saw a multi-disciplinary panel from Malaysia’s leading professional bodies assess an expanded lineup of categories. This year’s panel was chaired by Datuk Ar. Ezumi Harzani Ismail, president of the Malaysian Institute of Architects (PAM) from 2020 to 2022, and included Ir. Ashwin Thurairajah, executive director, GreenRE Sdn Bhd; YBrs. Sr. Haji Ishak Ismail, president, Malaysian Institute of Property & Facility Managers (MIPFM) 2023–2027; Ms. Janice Chin, senior director, Capital Markets, JLL Appraisal & Property Services Sdn Bhd; Prof. Dr. Ir. Jeffrey Chiang Choong Luin, president, The Institution of Engineers Malaysia (IEM) 2024–2026; Dato’ Sr. Lau Wai Seang, president, Royal Institution of Surveyors Malaysia (RISM) 2017–2018; TPr. Mazrina Dato’ Abdul Khalid, president, Malaysian Institute of Planners (MIP) 2025–2027; Assoc. Prof. LAr. Dr. Nor Atiah Ismail, president, Institute of Landscape Architects Malaysia (ILAM) 2024–2026; Adj. Prof. IDr. Norshafina Ibrahim, president, Malaysian Institute of Interior Designers (MIID) 2024–2026; Mr. Oliver Wee, president, Master Builders Association Malaysia (MBAM) 2024–2026; Ar. Sarly Adre Sarkum, chief executive officer, Green Building Index (GBI); Ar. Dr. Serina Hijjas, president, Malaysia Green Building Council (MGBC) 2023–2027; and Ms. Tan Hui Yin, partner, Tan Chap & Associates. Datuk Ar. Ezumi Harzani Ismail said: “Good design is the product of discipline, clarity of intent, and an understanding of how people inhabit space. What struck me most among this year’s winners was a shared design intelligence: sensitivity to context and climate, thoughtful handling of landscape and light, and a commitment to sustainability that goes beyond token gestures. From the elegant restraint of landed homes to the confident lines of high-rise towers, these projects show that Malaysian design has matured into something both internationally credible and distinctly our own. And with quality consistent across every tier, good design is not a privilege of the few but a standard we can deliver for all. On behalf of the judging panel, I congratulate every winner for raising the bar for Malaysian real estate.” Jules Kay, managing director of PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards and Events, said: “This year’s awardees share a commitment to thoughtful placemaking, sustainable design, and creating developments that enhance the way people live, work, and connect. From transformative township masterplans to beautifully crafted landed homes, this year’s winners show that excellence equals lasting value for communities. We are proud to celebrate developers that deliver value and quality to homebuyers. We also celebrate the individual leaders whose passion and foresight continue to inspire the industry. Together, these achievements set a benchmark for Malaysian real estate.” Winners may advance to the PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards Grand Final, recognising the Best in Asia on 11 December 2026 at The Athenee Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Bangkok. The PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty is supported in 2026 by platinum sponsor Lim Soh & Goonting Advocates & Solicitors; official portal partners PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com; official ESG knowledge partners Green Building Index (GBI), GreenRE, and Malaysia Green Building Council (MGBC); official magazine Property Report by PropertyGuru; strategic media partner Out of Home Media; media partners The Grid Asia, The Iskandarian, The Malaysia Voice, Niaga Times, Penang Property Talk, and Top 10 of Malaysia; official AI photo experience partner Gump; and official supervisor HLB. For more information, email awards@propertyguru.com or visit the official website: AsiaPropertyAwards.com. COMPLETE LIST OF WINNERS DEVELOPER AWARDS

title: 'Building on a legacy of Art and Community: Maybank returns for the third edition of CASB 2026 | Maybank
body: 'Since inception, CASB has attracted over 10,000 visitors and generated more than RM460,000 for artisans and cultural practitioners, championing cultural expression and economic empowerment Celebrating the people at the heart of CASB 2026 - Participating artisans proudly receive their Certificates of Appreciation in recognition of their talent, dedication and contribution to Malaysia’s creative and cultural landscape. Joining them are (L-R middle row, standing): Mr. Surin Segar A/L Gnanasegaram, Head, Group Tax Maybank & Chief Financial Officer of Maybank Foundation (in a blue, short-sleeve batik shirt); Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer (in a blue, long-sleeve batik shirt); Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in purple kebaya); Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin of Tanoti from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme (in black and floral kebaya); Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN) (in pink kurung batik); Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property (in a black and floral ensemble) & Datuk R. Karunakaran, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in a purple batik shirt). Maybank Foundation, the social impact arm of Maybank Group, celebrates the return of the Cultural Art Showcase and Bazaar (CASB) 2026, reaffirming its continued commitment to preserving Malaysia’s rich cultural heritage and creating meaningful opportunities for local artisans and cultural practitioners. Now in its third edition, CASB 2026 is being held from 20 August to 20 September 2026 at KLGCC Mall, Kuala Lumpur, bringing together artisans, cultural practitioners, performers and creative communities in a month-long celebration of Malaysia’s diverse cultural identity. The showcase is held in conjunction with the nation’s Hari Kebangsaan and Hari Malaysia celebrations. The official the launch of CASB 2026 - Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer and Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property took centre stage, officiating the month-long celebration of Malaysia’s rich cultural heritage and creative talent at the Cultural Art Showcase and Bazaar (CASB) 2026. They are joined by (from L-R): En. Ahmad Hilmi Hashim, Head of Technical Management and Governance, Group Sustainability Maybank (in brown batik shirt); Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir; member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation; Mr. Surin Segar A/L Gnanasegaram, Head, Group Tax Maybank and Chief Financial Officer of Maybank Foundation; Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN); Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation (in light blue kebaya batik); Datuk R. Karunakaran, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation & Rizqan Helmi Mohd Ariff, Head, Asset Management, Sime Darby Property (in a dark purple batik shirt). Visitors to CASB 2026 can experience cultural performances featuring traditional music, dance, theatre and contemporary interpretations of Malaysia’s diverse cultural heritage, Artisanal workshops led by participating practitioners, Artisan showcases and booths featuring a diverse range of Malaysian craftsmanship, including weaving, beading, batik, wau-making, indigenous art and other traditional crafts and Local F&B offerings, showcasing regional flavours that provide a platform for homegrown culinary talents. The 2026 programme features cultural groups such as Sanggar Seni Malaysia, Nyala Dance Theatre, Persatuan Kompang Cahaya Murni, Iron Gang Puppet Theatre, KRATE Creative Space and Sri Dasmesh Pipe Band. It also features two rotating groups of artisans and artisanal brands throughout the showcase, allowing more creative entrepreneurs to participate while refreshing the visitor experience, exposure and market access across the month. The launch came alive with a vibrant Borneo-fusion performance by Nyala Dance Theatre, inspired by the Ngajat of Sarawak and Sumazau of Sabah. Bringing movement, rhythm and tradition to the stage. The performance set the tone for CASB 2026, a lively celebration of the diverse cultural expressions that makes Malaysia unique. The Artisan Appreciation Ceremony, which marks the halfway point of the showcase was graced by Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir and Datuk Karunakaran A/L Ramasamy, Members of the Maybank Foundation Board of Trustees; Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer; Dr Yasmin Binti Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property; Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN) and Puan Anita Ahmad, CEO, Yayasan MySDG. From celebration to participation - Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property (in white dress) gets hands-on with traditional weaving, guided by Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin of Tanoti from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme, one of the 40 artisans featured at CASB 2026. Against a vibrant backdrop of woven textiles, the moment reflects CASB’s role in bringing heritage closer to the community while creating meaningful platforms for artisans to share their knowledge and craft. Speaking at the Artisan Appreciation Ceremony, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer, said, “CASB reflects what it means to impact society positively by creating opportunities for communities, celebrating our shared heritage and bringing people together through culture and creativity. Initiatives such as CASB demonstrate how cultural programmes can create impact beyond the arts by supporting livelihoods, strengthening community connections and providing greater visibility for the people who keep Malaysia’s traditions alive.” Connecting Artisans, Partners and Community - Engaging with the people at the heart of CASB 2026, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer (in a blue, long-sleeve batik shirt), Datuk Karunakaran A/L Ramasamy, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in a purple batik shirt), along with Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation (in light blue kebaya batik), engaging with Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin, a fellow weaver from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme, showcasing her artisanal products from Tanoti. Also pictured is Miss Elvina, Tanoti’s programme coordinator (in black shirt, with glasses). The exchange reflects the spirit of CASB, connecting artisans, partners and audiences to create greater visibility and opportunities for Malaysia’s creative communities. “More importantly, CASB represents something much bigger than a cultural showcase or bazaar. It is aligned with Maybank Group’s ROAR30 aspiration, particularly our commitment to Impacting Society Positively (ISP), which seeks to ensure that Maybank’s growth translates into meaningful and lasting benefits for the communities we serve. Under this pillar alone, the Group has mobilised more than RM30 million towards Social Empowerment initiatives and positively impacted over 466,000 individuals. As part of this journey, Maybank remains firmly on track towards its aspiration of empowering three million lives by 2030. CASB is part of this broader commitment, demonstrating how arts and culture can inspire learning, strengthen community bonds and create opportunities for greater social inclusion, and contribute meaningfully to this shared goal,” added Datuk Shahril. The showcase continues to be supported through Maybank Foundation’s partnership with Kakiseni, while Maybank MAE serves as the digital payment platform for the initiative. CASB 2026 is also made possible through collaboration with Sime Darby Property as the strategic venue partner, which hosts the showcase at KLGCC Mall, its third wholly-owned mall. Building on the momentum of its first two editions, CASB has welcomed more than 10,000 visitors and generated over RM460,000 in cumulative income for featured artisans and cultural practitioners since its inception in 2024. This year, CASB continues to strengthen its role as a platform for cultural expression and economic empowerment, providing artisans with opportunities to reach new audiences, showcase their craft and connect with potential customers. Turning skills into opportunities - En. Azmi bin Taha, representing the seven participants from the Reach Independence & Sustainable Entrepreneurship (R.I.S.E.) programme, received a Certificate of Appreciation from Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer witnessed by Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation. The recognition underscores CASB’s commitment to creating inclusive platforms where talent from various skillsets can be showcased, valued and translated into meaningful economic opportunities. As a key programme under the Balai Seni Art Series (BSAS), CASB is part of Maybank Foundation’s longstanding commitment to making arts and culture more accessible to communities, creating platforms for artists and cultural practitioners to thrive. Since the inception of BSAS in 1988, the programme has supported over 9,300 artists and beneficiaries through exhibitions and cultural initiatives. CASB builds on this legacy by bringing art, culture and community directly into spaces where people live, work and gather. The continued growth of CASB reflects Maybank Foundation’s broader commitment to catalysing positive and sustainable change, particularly through its three key pillars of Community Empowerment, Empowering Education and Environmental Diversity. By creating platforms for cultural participation and economic opportunity. The public is welcomed to visit CASB 2026 at KLGCC Mall, Level 1, Main Atrium, Kuala Lumpur till 20 September 2026. Showcases and activities will commence from 10.00am – 10.00pm daily. Visit www.maybankfoundation.com for more information on CASB 2026.
