Joining them are (L-R middle row, standing): Mr. Surin Segar A/L Gnanasegaram, Head, Group Tax Maybank & Chief Financial Officer of Maybank Foundation (in a blue, short-sleeve batik shirt); Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer (in a blue, long-sleeve batik shirt); Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in purple kebaya); Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin of Tanoti from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme (in black and floral kebaya); Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN) (in pink kurung batik); Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property (in a black and floral ensemble) & Datuk R. Karunakaran, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in a purple batik shirt). Maybank Foundation, the social impact arm of Maybank Group, celebrates the return of the Cultural Art Showcase and Bazaar (CASB) 2026, reaffirming its continued commitment to preserving Malaysia’s rich cultural heritage and creating meaningful opportunities for local artisans and cultural practitioners. Now in its third edition, CASB 2026 is being held from 20 August to 20 September 2026 at KLGCC Mall, Kuala Lumpur, bringing together artisans, cultural practitioners, performers and creative communities in a month-long celebration of Malaysia’s diverse cultural identity. The showcase is held in conjunction with the nation’s Hari Kebangsaan and Hari Malaysia celebrations. The official the launch of CASB 2026 - Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer and Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property took centre stage, officiating the month-long celebration of Malaysia’s rich cultural heritage and creative talent at the Cultural Art Showcase and Bazaar (CASB) 2026. They are joined by (from L-R): En. Ahmad Hilmi Hashim, Head of Technical Management and Governance, Group Sustainability Maybank (in brown batik shirt); Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir; member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation; Mr. Surin Segar A/L Gnanasegaram, Head, Group Tax Maybank and Chief Financial Officer of Maybank Foundation; Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN); Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation (in light blue kebaya batik); Datuk R. Karunakaran, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation & Rizqan Helmi Mohd Ariff, Head, Asset Management, Sime Darby Property (in a dark purple batik shirt). Visitors to CASB 2026 can experience cultural performances featuring traditional music, dance, theatre and contemporary interpretations of Malaysia’s diverse cultural heritage, Artisanal workshops led by participating practitioners, Artisan showcases and booths featuring a diverse range of Malaysian craftsmanship, including weaving, beading, batik, wau-making, indigenous art and other traditional crafts and Local F&B offerings, showcasing regional flavours that provide a platform for homegrown culinary talents. The 2026 programme features cultural groups such as Sanggar Seni Malaysia, Nyala Dance Theatre, Persatuan Kompang Cahaya Murni, Iron Gang Puppet Theatre, KRATE Creative Space and Sri Dasmesh Pipe Band. It also features two rotating groups of artisans and artisanal brands throughout the showcase, allowing more creative entrepreneurs to participate while refreshing the visitor experience, exposure and market access across the month. The launch came alive with a vibrant Borneo-fusion performance by Nyala Dance Theatre, inspired by the Ngajat of Sarawak and Sumazau of Sabah. Bringing movement, rhythm and tradition to the stage. The performance set the tone for CASB 2026, a lively celebration of the diverse cultural expressions that makes Malaysia unique. The Artisan Appreciation Ceremony, which marks the halfway point of the showcase was graced by Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir and Datuk Karunakaran A/L Ramasamy, Members of the Maybank Foundation Board of Trustees; Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer; Dr Yasmin Binti Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property; Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN) and Puan Anita Ahmad, CEO, Yayasan MySDG. From celebration to participation - Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property (in white dress) gets hands-on with traditional weaving, guided by Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin of Tanoti from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme, one of the 40 artisans featured at CASB 2026. Against a vibrant backdrop of woven textiles, the moment reflects CASB’s role in bringing heritage closer to the community while creating meaningful platforms for artisans to share their knowledge and craft. Speaking at the Artisan Appreciation Ceremony, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer, said, “CASB reflects what it means to impact society positively by creating opportunities for communities, celebrating our shared heritage and bringing people together through culture and creativity. Initiatives such as CASB demonstrate how cultural programmes can create impact beyond the arts by supporting livelihoods, strengthening community connections and providing greater visibility for the people who keep Malaysia’s traditions alive.” Connecting Artisans, Partners and Community - Engaging with the people at the heart of CASB 2026, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer (in a blue, long-sleeve batik shirt), Datuk Karunakaran A/L Ramasamy, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in a purple batik shirt), along with Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation (in light blue kebaya batik), engaging with Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin, a fellow weaver from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme, showcasing her artisanal products from Tanoti. Also pictured is Miss Elvina, Tanoti’s programme coordinator (in black shirt, with glasses). The exchange reflects the spirit of CASB, connecting artisans, partners and audiences to create greater visibility and opportunities for Malaysia’s creative communities. “More importantly, CASB represents something much bigger than a cultural showcase or bazaar. It is aligned with Maybank Group’s ROAR30 aspiration, particularly our commitment to Impacting Society Positively (ISP), which seeks to ensure that Maybank’s growth translates into meaningful and lasting benefits for the communities we serve. Under this pillar alone, the Group has mobilised more than RM30 million towards Social Empowerment initiatives and positively impacted over 466,000 individuals. As part of this journey, Maybank remains firmly on track towards its aspiration of empowering three million lives by 2030. CASB is part of this broader commitment, demonstrating how arts and culture can inspire learning, strengthen community bonds and create opportunities for greater social inclusion, and contribute meaningfully to this shared goal,” added Datuk Shahril. The showcase continues to be supported through Maybank Foundation’s partnership with Kakiseni, while Maybank MAE serves as the digital payment platform for the initiative. CASB 2026 is also made possible through collaboration with Sime Darby Property as the strategic venue partner, which hosts the showcase at KLGCC Mall, its third wholly-owned mall. Building on the momentum of its first two editions, CASB has welcomed more than 10,000 visitors and generated over RM460,000 in cumulative income for featured artisans and cultural practitioners since its inception in 2024. This year, CASB continues to strengthen its role as a platform for cultural expression and economic empowerment, providing artisans with opportunities to reach new audiences, showcase their craft and connect with potential customers. Turning skills into opportunities - En. Azmi bin Taha, representing the seven participants from the Reach Independence & Sustainable Entrepreneurship (R.I.S.E.) programme, received a Certificate of Appreciation from Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer witnessed by Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation. The recognition underscores CASB’s commitment to creating inclusive platforms where talent from various skillsets can be showcased, valued and translated into meaningful economic opportunities. As a key programme under the Balai Seni Art Series (BSAS), CASB is part of Maybank Foundation’s longstanding commitment to making arts and culture more accessible to communities, creating platforms for artists and cultural practitioners to thrive. Since the inception of BSAS in 1988, the programme has supported over 9,300 artists and beneficiaries through exhibitions and cultural initiatives. CASB builds on this legacy by bringing art, culture and community directly into spaces where people live, work and gather. The continued growth of CASB reflects Maybank Foundation’s broader commitment to catalysing positive and sustainable change, particularly through its three key pillars of Community Empowerment, Empowering Education and Environmental Diversity. By creating platforms for cultural participation and economic opportunity. The public is welcomed to visit CASB 2026 at KLGCC Mall, Level 1, Main Atrium, Kuala Lumpur till 20 September 2026. Showcases and activities will commence from 10.00am – 10.00pm daily. Visit www.maybankfoundation.com for more information on CASB 2026.

title: 'CIMB could raise RM2 bil capital return commitment, says MBSB Research
body: 'CIMB could raise RM2 bil capital return commitment, says MBSB Research KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) could potentially raise its RM2 billion capital return commitment to increase the chances of its share buyback programme garnering investor acceptance, according to MBSB Research. A higher capital-return commitment could help offset potential disappointment among investors who are expecting a larger portion of the RM2 billion to be returned via special dividends, the research house said. “To increase its chances of success, we think there is a likelihood of CIMB positively revising to the RM2.0 billion figure, and that CIMB is confident enough on its ability to garner sufficient capital before signalling to the market via share buybacks,” MBSB Research said in a note on Thursday. “We would not put it past CIMB’s management to pull off such a manoeuvre — they’ve surprised us positively multiple times in the past,” it added. MBSB Research noted that share buybacks have historically not been successful in Malaysia. CIMB’s share buybacks make up a portion of its RM2 billion capital return scheme, of which RM700 million has already been returned via special dividends. The primary purpose of the share buybacks is for CIMB to further drive its earnings per share, return on equity (ROE) and dividend per share figures, MBSB Research noted, particularly as the bank is slightly behind on its ROE target for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026). The research house noted CIMB has been buying back shares every day, tallying up to 20.76 million shares for RM163 million since Sept 21 thus far. Who could follow CIMB? CIMB’s share buyback programme is also being watched for its potential implications on other banks, according to MBSB Research. The research house described the programme as the first major share buyback scheme by a Malaysian bank for capital management purposes in many years, and said a successful outcome could encourage other large banks to consider similar measures. Public Bank, it noted, has already received shareholder approval for a share buyback of up to 10% of its shares, although it has not done any yet. Its management has maintained that this is a capital optimisation option rather than a set path they want to go down, the research house added. RHB Bank, meanwhile, has high capital ratios and historically releases excess capital via larger payouts in the fourth quarter, MBSB Research noted. It is currently preparing a new capital release plan, which is scheduled to be announced by the first quarter of FY2027, the research house added. MBSB Research maintained its “buy” call on CIMB but with a lower target price of RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times. At the time of writing, shares of CIMB were down three sen or 0.39% at RM7.76, valuing the lender at RM84 billion. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Creador acquires RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar
body: 'Creador acquires RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on August 31, 2026 - September 6, 2026 SOUTHEAST Asian private equity firm Creador, through its philanthropic arm Creador Foundation, is understood to have recently added at least two more properties in downtown Kuala Lumpur to its growing city-centre portfolio — the historic RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar, according to sources familiar with the matter. The Edge reported in July that the RHB building, a 13-storey office block located at 75 Jalan Tun H S Lee, had been on the market with a reserve price of RM30 million. Sources familiar with the deal say the building has changed hands close to the reserve price. The property carries considerable heritage weight. It was originally the landmark headquarters of Kwong Yik Bank, Malaya’s first local bank, founded in 1913. The building was formally opened in 1965 by then prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj and became part of RHB’s lineage after Rashid Hussain Bhd took a 75% stake in Kwong Yik Bank in 1996, ahead of its merger with DCB Bank the following year to form RHB Bank. RHB has already announced that its branch at the address will cease operations in January 2027. Details on the Bangunan UOB deal at 10-12 Medan Pasar are limited, although the road itself sits in the same historic banking and commercial belt as Jalan Tun H S Lee, just north of Dataran Merdeka — squarely within the footprint of the areas Creador, together with its founders’ Alaka Holdings Trust, has been actively involved in restoration initiatives. According to sources, Creador Foundation bought Bangunan UOB and the two shoplots next to it for slightly less than RM40 million. During a visit to the area on a Friday afternoon, the transformation to the area was apparent with ongoing construction and restoration works. A source tells The Edge that of the 27 buildings in the Medan Pasar area, 17 of them are believed to have been acquired by Creador while the other 10 have been leased. On Aug 13, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh announced a collaboration between Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and Creador Foundation to revitalise Medan Pasar’s public space as well as improve rainwater management. The acquisitions of the buildings would extend a heritage-property push that Creador, through its philanthropic arm Creador Foundation, has been on since 2024, when it began restoration work around Medan Pasar and Central Market in Kuala Lumpur’s historic district. Its efforts have already delivered several visible wins, with the revival of a shuttered row of shophouses in Medan Pasar, including the Sin Seng Nam corner lot, now home to the popular KLCG Confectionery & Bakery. Creador Foundation’s most ambitious project to date is Muara Arts Gallery, a public art gallery dedicated to modern and contemporary Malaysian and Southeast Asian art. The gallery, with a total built-up of about 20,000 sq ft and is slated to open in November, sits across six Art Deco shophouses from the 1930s. The performing arts theatre, Muara Arts Theatre, is currently under construction and is expected to be completed in 2029. Established in 2018, Creador Foundation was founded by Creador founder and CEO Brahmal Vasudevan and lawyer wife Shanthi Kandiah, founder of SK Chambers. Creador, incorporated in 2011, is known for its investments in brands such as MR DIY, Hock Kee Kopitiam and BIG Pharmacy. The private equity fund has about US$3.1 billion (RM12.52 billion) in assets under management, according to its website. Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'A wage floor with a loophole
body: 'Charles Santiago On 26 September, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said workers were stuck on RM1,700 while productivity and profits kept rising. He was right. Four days later, Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim announced that the cabinet had agreed to exempt micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the next minimum wage increase for now. That is a direct contradiction. Two rules, one workforce MSMEs employ 8.1 million people, or 48.7% of Malaysia’s workforce. This exemption means two cleaners doing the same work could be legally entitled to different pay. One works for a large company and the other for a smaller firm. Can small firms afford it? The argument is that MSMEs cannot afford higher wages. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member But gross domestic product from MSMEs grew 5.7% in 2025, faster than the overall economy’s 5.2%. Labour productivity also rose 4.1% to RM85,299 per worker a year, or about RM7,100 a month. Low wages So where does that value go? For every RM100 Malaysia’s economy produces, workers receive about RM34. In the EU, workers get about RM48 and in Germany RM55. The government promised 40% of GDP to workers by 2025 under the 12th Malaysia Plan and missed it. People are already struggling with food, rent, transport, childcare and healthcare. Even RM2,000 is still far below a living wage. Bank Negara estimated a living wage for a single adult in Kuala Lumpur at RM2,700 about eight years ago. The benchmark used by government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies is now about RM3,100. A better way There is a better way to support small firms without sacrificing workers. When South Korea raised its minimum wage sharply in 2018, it kept one wage for everyone. It also gave small firms a monthly subsidy of 130,000 won for each low-paid worker. Firms that got the help kept their staff. Budget 2027 will be revealed on 9 October. The government should not be creating divides. It needs to lift the wage floor for every worker. Charles Santiago is a prominent Malaysian politician, economist and human rights advocate who served three terms as the MP for Klang and has twice chaired the National Water Services Commission. body: '马股周五随隔夜美股反弹，由于市场对美债收益率和油价的担忧挥之不去，投资者仍保持谨慎并采取选择性投资策略，综合指数收盘仅微幅走高。 截至下午闭市，综合指数涨0.51点或0.03%，至1,630.87点。 市场整体表现平衡，全场上涨股592只，下跌股554只，562只平盘，另1041只股无交易。全天成交量42.59亿股，总成交额27.11亿令吉。 综指成分股涨跌互见，IHH医疗保健集团（IHH，5225，主板保健股）涨10仙至7.80令吉，国油贸易（PETDAG，5681，主板能源股）、PPB集团（PPB，4065，主板消费股）和国油石化（PCHEM，5183，主板工业股）各涨8仙，分别收在19.20令吉、9.15令吉和4.21令吉。 下跌股，雀巢（NESTLE，4707，主板消费股）跌48仙至89.52令吉，吉隆坡甲洞（KLK，2445，主板种植股）跌42仙至21.00令吉，马国际船务（MISC，3816，主板交通与物流股）跌15仙至7.53令吉，国油气体（PETGAS，6033，主板公用事业股）跌12仙至17.20令吉。 银行股，马银行（MAYBANK，1155）涨7仙至10.02令吉，大众银行（PBBANK，1295）跌1仙4.66令吉，联昌国际（CIMB，1023）跌4仙至7.65令吉，兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066）跌4仙至7.43令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819）跌20仙至22.64令吉，大马银行（AMBANK，1015）持平于6.30令吉。 热门股方面，Zetrix AI（ZETRIX，0138，主板科技股）跌5仙至11.5仙，捷硕科技（JAKS，4723, 主板建筑股）持平于18仙，JCY国际（JCY，5161，主板科技股）涨10.5仙至66仙，威铖（VS，6963，主板工业股）涨2仙至29仙，迪耐（DNEX，4456，主板科技股）涨2仙至51.5仙。 其他重要股项，马太平洋（MPI，3867，主板科技股）涨1.28令吉至42.40令吉，UWC公司（UWC，5292，主板科技股）涨47仙至7.57令吉；ENRA集团（ENRA，8613，主板产业股）跌25.5仙至72.5仙，安联保险（ALLIANZ，1163，主板金融股）跌20仙至20.80令吉。 亚太主要股指，新加坡海峡时报指数跌 0.58% 至 5,634.83 点，香港恒生指数跌 2.60% 至 23,972.29 点，日本日经指255数跌 0.94% 至 68,309.46 点，韩国首尔综合指数起 0.46% 至 7,003.74 点。中国股市适逢国庆长假期休市。 The post 马股随隔夜美股反弹，但投资者仍保持谨慎，综指仅微幅收高 appeared first on 股票消息.

title: 'RHB tumbles 9% as foreign selling pressure persists
body: 'FOREIGN investors kept up the selling pressure on Malaysian equities for another week, with RHB Bank Bhd among the hardest hit after losing close to 9% over the past fortnight as the benchmark index slipped below 1,700 points.   RHB fell from RM8.68 on Aug 28 to RM7.90 on Sept 11, down 78 sen or about 9%, amid heavy selling pressure. The counter extended its decline in early trade today, falling to RM7.75.   Foreign investors remained net sellers for the week ended Sept 11, marking the sixth consecutive week of net foreign outflows.
